# Editor specification and conformance record

## Scope

The engine implements a declared subset of transitional WordprocessingML. It is
not a complete OOXML consumer or a reference-compatible layout implementation. Schema
validation, property semantics, editing behavior and visual geometry are checked
separately. Each new feature must extend this record and its fixtures.

The application license remains undecided. This work adds no AGPL dependency or
another editor's implementation. Standards archives are downloaded only into the
OS temporary directory for testing; they are not distributed in the app.

## Best-effort opening and read-only previews

The app and local playground open documents with unsupported features rather than
rejecting them. The strict `DocxPackage.open` codec remains available to validate
the editable subset; the UI opts into `bestEffort` through `openCanvasDocument`.
Earlier references below to rejection on import describe eligibility for editing,
not rejection of a best-effort view.

Relevant specification areas are ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.2 (document structure),
§17.3 (paragraphs and runs), §17.4 (tables), §17.6 (sections), §17.13.5 (revisions),
§17.16 (fields and hyperlinks), Part 2 (package preservation), and Part 3
(markup compatibility and alternate branches). This is an original display
fallback, not an expansion of the editable OOXML subset or a claim of full
OOXML conformance or native reference layout equivalence.

Supported blocks and runs use the existing reader and renderer. Unsupported
inline structures fall back to their visible text, and unsupported blocks or
tables become paragraphs. The projection keeps direct bold/italic, tabs and
line breaks, displays cached field results rather than instructions, includes
insertions and omits deleted/moved-from text. It chooses one alternate branch,
using the existing selector first, then a fallback (or the first choice if no
fallback exists) for otherwise unprocessable markup. This last recovery rule is
an approximation, not conforming MCE processing. No external content is fetched.
Unsupported page geometry uses default page settings. If font measurement or
image decoding prevents rendering, a simpler text projection is attempted.

Gaps include omitted headers/footers and unsupported artwork, flattened complex
tables, lost formatting in approximated fragments, approximate revisions/fields,
and layout that can differ substantially from the native reference. Unsupported content stays
in the original package. Previews disable editing and attach no save handler;
the download returns the exact original file bytes. Corrupt archives, invalid or
unsafe XML, and resource limits remain errors. Ordinary supported documents stay
editable with their existing round-trip behavior.

`tools/canvas_preview_fixture.py` independently authors `best-effort.docx` with
Python's standard library; it contains original text and no external assets.
Unit tests cover mixed supported/unsupported content, alternate branches,
nested tables, source retention and the export guard. Browser tests cover
read-only keyboard/paste/composition behavior, returning to editable documents,
and byte-identical original downloads, including the existing unsupported-feature
cases. The valid independent fixture and its browser download are checked with
`npm run check:conformance`; malformed regression inputs are intentionally not
claimed to pass the schema.

Preserve the original attributes rather than flattening inherited themes on export. |
| Theme lookup | Part 1 §§20.1.4.1.16, 20.1.4.1.24–25 supplemental, major and minor fonts; §§21.1.2.3.1, 21.1.2.3.3, 21.1.2.3.7 regional entries; [themeFontLang](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.themefontlanguages) | Locate the theme through its package relationship. Implement East Asian hint/language/charset exceptions and the Times New Roman compatibility rule. Keep combining sequences and emoji together under their base character's family. Complex-script slots are retained, but active RTL/complex-script overrides remain outside the editable subset. |

Available native families use Canvas font bounding-box ascent/descent; bundled Noto retains its independently checked font-table metrics. The toolbar reports the Latin family and a detected unavailable-family substitution. |

`tools/canvas_font_family_fixture.py` independently generates
`public/fixtures/font-families.docx` with python-docx and original XML. It covers
partial style overrides, theme precedence, empty marks, AutoFit cells, mixed
numbering, Unicode and an unavailable family. No font binaries or third-party
engine code were added. Unit regressions check inheritance, mutations, round
trips, caret geometry, malformed declarations and unused-style preservation.
The browser test compares widths and vertical bounds with native Arial, verifies
different Courier New advances, checks substitution reporting, and edits,
downloads and reopens the fixture. The conformance gate validates that export
and independently checks all original font declarations and unrelated parts.

**Remaining limits:** this resolves declared-family selection, not complete
reference typography. Availability checks use local FontFace loading and native
Canvas comparisons; sparse or metrically identical faces can be ambiguous.
Embedded fonts, alternative font names and the native reference's font-substitution algorithm
are not loaded/implemented. Missing faces fall back to bundled Noto and then the
browser's glyph fallback; stored declarations remain intact. Non-Noto underline,
strike and script-transform metrics still use the existing Noto-derived preview
policy. Font-native decorations, script metrics, advanced shaping, exact reference
line metrics and pagination require further work. DrawingML text's separate
font declarations and chart fonts are not covered by this WordprocessingML
change. The font picker authors the Latin ASCII/high-ANSI pair; East Asian and complex-script slots remain unchanged. Clipboard transfer remains plain text,
so font formatting is not transferred in either direction.

The first local birthday card now resolves Skeena from its theme, but that face
is unavailable to this browser. Its reference PDF uses Skeena. The card's
substitution, layout differences and extra blank page remain open; this change
does not establish visual equivalence. Its edit/export/reopen and complete-undo
package retention checks pass. A fresh reference for the independent font
fixture has not been obtained.

Validation: 2,785 unit tests and 248 browser tests passed (four optional corpus
cases skipped). Browser exports passed the conformance gate; production build
and license policy passed with the existing 199 packages and Noto OFL assets.
The font fixture and first birthday card also passed focused browser checks.

## Rotated shape text and upright frames

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.7.6 `xfrm`, 20.1.7.5 group transforms and
21.1.2.1.1 `bodyPr` define the retained shape/group orientation and upright text
flag. The supplied Part 1 PDF's page 3203 and the Open XML SDK
[UpRight documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.drawing.bodyproperties.upright?view=openxml-3.0.1)
specify that upright text remains horizontal regardless of accompanying
transforms. Shape text now accepts validated shape/group rotations and measures
its writing area after resolving the rotated physical axes. Insets and font
sizes stay physical under unequal group scaling; glyphs are not stretched to
compensate for the ancestor frame. Existing local-flip behavior is retained.

**Reference-specific layout behavior:** upright text keeps the transformed frame's
center, but uses a horizontal frame whose width/height exchange in [45,135) and
[225,315) degrees of the composed orientation. This discrete wrapping rule is
not prescribed by the clause's upright-orientation description. Independently
authored `rotated-shape-text` controls demonstrate it at quarter turns, interval
boundaries and composed parent/child rotations. Preview text bounds include its
frame, and upright painting preserves offsets of intermediate shadow surfaces.
No source transforms or text XML are rewritten by rendering.

The 24 native controls verify colored text bounds, physical type size, wrapping,
local flips, scaling, source preservation, edit/export/reopen and exact undo.
Text in reflected/collapsed groups, upright text with vertical reflection, flat
rotated preset-line text and nonzero independent bodyPr text rotation retain
their separate guards. Existing text-box table and field support is retained;
the controls do not establish arbitrary text-warp or three-dimensional text.

## SVG picture representations

### Local masks, matrix filters and embedded raster images

SVG pictures accept local luminance/alpha masks with user-space or bounding-box
coordinates, and `filter` resources containing bounded `feColorMatrix` chains.
Matrix, saturation, hue rotation and luminance-to-alpha values retain browser
SVG semantics; inputs can use SourceGraphic, SourceAlpha or preceding named
results. See [SVG 1.1 masking, §14.4](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG11/masking.html#Masking)
and [SVG 1.1 color matrices, §15.10](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG11/filters.html#feColorMatrixElement).
Other filter primitives remain guarded; active animation and external resources
are still unsupported.

Embedded `image` resources accept base64 PNG/JPEG data only, with matching MIME,
existing raster dimension validation and a cumulative 16-megapixel limit per
SVG. Conflicting href/xlink:href image values remain unsupported pending native
precedence evidence. Resource graphs have cycle, depth and expanded-size checks.
Original media bytes are preserved through body edits, export, reopening and
undo; only disposable previews apply the native reference's opacity/viewport corrections.

Independent `svg-masks` controls cover masks, embedded PNG/JPEG and sRGB inversion
in full/cropped/grouped/fill pictures. The native reference gives alpha 128 for
gray #808080 and 127 for 50% opacity; the existing opacity quantization correction
reproduces both. Interior alpha/color and editing workflows are verified.
Native mask-boundary rasterization still differs at narrow strip seams; broader
filter-mode and color-space equivalence is not established by the inversion
control. These remain fidelity gaps, not full reference pixel-equivalence claims.
Translucent-group flattening excludes masks, filters and their resource trees
so their authored compositing is retained.

| Area | Specification | Supported subset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Extension list | ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.8.13 `blip`, 20.1.2.2.14–16 extension containers; [MS-ODRAWXML §2.26.3.1 `CT_SVGBlip`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-odrawxml/68e0150d-6a01-4ba5-ac4d-5a18d685229b) | Multiple distinct `a:ext` entries may coexist. Accept the registered SVG representation alongside the existing local-DPI extension, in either order. Reject duplicate extension URIs, unknown extensions, missing/ambiguous relationships, linked SVGs and content-type mismatches. |
| Vector semantics | MS-ODRAWXML §2.26 SVG namespace; Part 1 §22.8.2.1 relationship IDs; SVG 1.1 geometry, painting and coordinate systems | Select the embedded SVG for painting while retaining its companion raster relationship and bytes. Support rectangular pictures, cropped pictures, pictures inside groups and shape picture fills. Original SVG bytes, CSS and XML survive export; no generated bitmap replaces them in DOCX. |
| Native display | [SVG 2 §2.2 processing modes](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG/conform.html); Canvas image drawing | Decode validated SVG in an isolated HTML image context and draw the vector at the requested canvas scale. The supported subset includes paths, basic shapes, groups, local gradients and clip paths, opacity, strokes, transforms and simple static CSS rules. Explicit positive intrinsic dimensions in px, pt, pc, in, cm or mm are required. Existing crops, flips, sizing and drawing transforms remain separate from source artwork. |
| Resource boundary | Application limits, existing package/image budget | Reject scripts, event handlers, animation, foreign content, external images, embedded formats other than PNG/JPEG, external stylesheets, CSS imports/escapes/variables and nonlocal resource references before decoding. Unsupported SVG stays in the original package and opens read-only. Limits are 10 MB, 8,192 px per side, 16 million intrinsic pixels, 20,000 elements and 64 levels; existing aggregate asset budgets also apply. |
| Editing and retention | Existing history, image-property and OPC contracts | Surrounding text edits, picture size/crop/alt edits, deletion and undo retain both source representations and their relationships. No-op/full undo retain every original part byte. Group contents and shape fills retain their existing immutable-content restrictions. Clipboard is still plain text: rich vector/image copy-paste remains unsupported in both directions. |

`tools/canvas_svg_fixture.py` independently authors original vector artwork and
an intentionally different magenta PNG fallback, using python-docx, lxml and
Python's standard library. It exercises both extension orders, CSS, a local
gradient and clip path, cropping, groups and shape fills. Unit tests cover
selection of the vector representation, editing/reopening, package restoration,
relationship failures and unsupported SVG. Browser pixel checks distinguish the
vector from the raster fallback at enlarged scale and inside groups/fills; an
unsupported external-resource SVG stays read-only, makes no external request,
and downloads byte-identically. The browser export verifier compares complete
drawing trees and all unrelated package parts.

The official [MS-ODRAWXML §5.24 schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-odrawxml/cc083f6d-bc38-4ff4-b32a-5bc97df8addc)
is hash-pinned in the temporary test cache and included in the conformance gate.
It validates the SVG relationship extension, not the entire SVG language or
the native reference's appearance. The SVG renderer is the browser; no external engine,
dependency or user artwork was added.

**Remaining limits:** no SVG insertion UI or artwork editing; no SVG
filter primitives other than color matrices, patterns or advanced CSS. Later sections document SVG text,
automatic intrinsic sizing and local use-elements. Unsupported content is not silently removed or replaced by the raster
fallback. Vendor-specific dynamic theme recoloring of SVG classes is not
implemented; supported CSS paints its stored values. Group previews retain the
existing two-times bitmap resolution policy. Browser rasterization, reference SVG
rendering and arbitrary large/complex artwork are not claimed equivalent.
The second local birthday card now passes SVG import and visibly renders its
vector artwork. Its temporary controls now support mailto hyperlinks and editable
round trips; see “Hyperlinks inside temporary content controls” below. Its
complete layout/typography/clipboard review remains pending.


Validation: 2,803 unit tests and 251 browser tests passed, with four optional
corpus cases skipped. The original second card was included. Full conformance,
production build and the existing 199-package license policy passed. Both
full-page SVG renders were inspected; no reference-equivalence claim is made.

## Drawing creation identities

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.2.2.14–16 provides DrawingML extension containers;
§22.9.2.4 defines `ST_Guid`. [MS-ODRAWXML §2.25.1.2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-odrawxml/f4da5f85-bb28-4ea4-859f-f1e23801f737)
and [§2.25.3.2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-odrawxml/7b70d634-1469-4275-bc1f-f77375d39641)
define `a16:creationId` as drawing identity metadata, with an optional `id`.
The shared nonvisual-property reader now accepts the registered creation-ID
extension in document drawing properties, pictures, shapes and nested groups.
It validates the GUID's braces, uppercase hexadecimal spelling and token
whitespace, without imposing UUID version/variant rules. An omitted ID remains
omitted. Duplicate extensions, unknown attributes, nested/text content and
incorrect namespaces remain errors before editing. Decorative metadata can
coexist in either extension order.

Identity has no painting or layout effect. The complete original drawing shell
retains the extension and namespace bindings through text edits, image-property
edits and deletion/undo/redo. No-op and full-undo exports preserve all package
part bytes. No identities are synthesized or reassigned for existing drawings.
The current plain-text clipboard does not transfer drawing objects; rich drawing
copy/paste and the identity rules for newly duplicated objects remain gaps.

`tools/canvas_creation_id_fixture.py` independently authors
`drawing-creation-ids.docx` using the original Python artwork generator, with
identities on inline/anchored pictures and nested shapes/groups. No user artwork
is redistributed. Unit tests check validation, unchanged geometry, editing and
package restoration. Browser tests check painting, deletion/undo and edited
download/reopen. The Python export verifier compares original drawing trees,
identities and unrelated parts. The official MS-ODRAWXML §5.23 schema is pinned
and cached only in the OS temporary directory; its split-schema `ST_Guid`
reference resolves to ECMA's unchanged shared-types definition. Validator
self-checks include malformed GUIDs and the permitted absent ID.
The macOS reference also opens the independent fixture and exports its pictures,
shapes and text to PDF; the reference render was inspected locally. This checks
interoperability of the metadata, not overall typography conformance.

This removes the creation-ID rejection in the second birthday-card specimen.
Group locks are now retained as described below; that file subsequently reaches
unsupported SVG picture extensions. Its complete fidelity is not established.

## Group transformation locks

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.2.2.6 and 20.1.2.2.21 define `cNvGrpSpPr` and
`grpSpLocks` (schema type `CT_GroupLocking`, Annex A.4.1).
The [published attribute definitions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.drawing.groupshapelocks)
cover restrictions on grouping, ungrouping, movement, resizing, rotation,
aspect ratio and selection. Omitted flags default to false; supplied values
must use XML Schema booleans, including XML whitespace normalization.

The reader now accepts transformation locks on top-level and nested WPG groups.
The existing retained-drawing model prevents geometry and group-structure
mutations, so it enforces `noGrp`, `noUngrp`, `noMove`, `noResize`, `noRot` and
`noChangeAspect`. Surrounding text edits may still reflow an anchored group;
its stored position and transforms remain unchanged. Locks do not affect
painting or prevent atomic deletion/undo. A future group editor must enforce
these flags when enabling those mutations. Active `noSelect` still fails before
editable attachment because group selection is currently supported. Unknown
attributes/extensions, duplicate locks, invalid booleans and non-whitespace
content also fail. No source locks are removed or rewritten.

`tools/canvas_group_locks_fixture.py` independently authors `group-locks.docx`
with top-level/nested flags, three placements and MCE alternatives. Unit tests
check unchanged scenes, prohibited mutations, surrounding edits, deletion/undo,
exact no-op/full-undo retention and malformed inputs. Browser tests cover
painting, object selection, the properties dialog, plain-text paste, reopening
and rejection without replacing the previous document/save handler. Drawing
copy/paste remains outside the current plain-text clipboard. The independent
Python checker compares complete drawing trees, both alternatives and unrelated
package parts in browser exports; the extension-aware official schema checks
include the locks. The macOS reference opens the fixture and its two reference
pages were inspected. Overall font/layout equivalence is not claimed.
The native reference's rasterized PDFs with and without the locks are pixel-identical on both
pages. This comparison also exposes an existing nested-group text-size mismatch:
the canvas scales the text with the group coordinate transform, whereas the native reference
keeps its requested point size. That separate layout gap remains open.
The native reference also opens the browser-edited export; the inserted text is present and the
unedited second page remains pixel-identical to its reference.

## Stretched picture fills in shapes

Part 1 §§20.1.8.14 (`blipFill`), 20.1.8.30 (`fillRect`), 20.1.8.55
(`srcRect`) and 20.1.8.56 (`stretch`) define image fills with independent source
and destination rectangles. Original WPS shape scenes now retain a validated
image reference and destination offsets. Source cropping is evaluated before
mapping the surviving pixels into the fill rectangle; negative source offsets
leave transparent space. Positive destination offsets inset the image, while
negative offsets extend it beyond the frame. The painter clips the mapped
image to each filled path, then draws its outline and text in the existing order.

Raster part validation, resource limits, PNG/JPEG decoding, shared image assets,
blip extensions and crop validation reuse the existing picture reader. Shape
fill XML is never substituted with the synthetic picture used by that reader.
The original drawing remains an atomic retained object for export, deletion
and undo. An explicit image fill can override an otherwise inactive theme fill
reference under the same existing no-text/no-outline/no-effect rules. Conflicting
fills, linked images, invalid percentages and unsupported fill children fail
before attaching the editable save handler. Destination rectangles, like the
existing source-crop subset, must retain positive width/height; percentage
offsets use signed 32-bit DrawingML thousandths of a percent.

The original `shape-picture-fills.docx` fixture covers full stretch, source
insets/outsets, destination insets/outsets, combined rectangles and polygon
clipping. Independent reference probes match these coordinates. Unit tests verify
mapping, resource sharing, direct theme overrides, rejection, editing/reopening
and package restoration. Browser tests inspect painted bounds and polygon
clipping, delete/undo a retained shape, edit text and reopen the export. An
independent Python verifier compares all drawing trees and unrelated parts;
both input and browser exports are checked against the standard and supported
extension schemas.

Tiled picture fills (§20.1.8.58), additional blip effects and rotated shape/group
transforms remain separate gaps. Native reference PDF probes of tiles ignore declared flip
and DPI overrides even in isolated documents, but the on-screen comparison is
not yet verified. A misleading high-DPI result in a combined PDF was isolated
to bitmap reuse at mismatched dimensions: a standalone 300-DPI image uses the
correct physical tile size. That export artifact is not a renderer rule.

## Page and margin drawing positions

Part 1 §§20.4.2.10–11 (`positionH`, `positionV`) separates each positioning base
from its alignment or signed EMU offset. §§20.4.3.1–5 define the alignments,
offset datatype and horizontal/vertical bases. The no-wrap subset now supports
page and margin bases on both axes, horizontal column offsets/alignment, and
vertical paragraph offsets. Horizontal left/center/right and vertical
top/center/bottom alignment use the retained drawing frame. Offsets remain
bounded to the editor's existing 22-inch coordinate limit.

Positioned objects have zero inline advance and ascent/descent. After pagination,
their coordinates use the anchor's page/section geometry, independent of text
indents and wrapping. Painting, hit testing and selection use that same frame;
behind-document order is retained. Resizing recalculates alignment against the
new frame dimensions. Text edits retain positioning XML, relationships, settings
and image bytes; complete undo restores the original package parts.

### Native reference compatibility difference

Independent reference probes on an 8-inch page found that compatibility mode 14 (and
an omitted mode) clamps a page-right-aligned picture's left coordinate to the
right edge of the writing area. Its position is
`min(pageWidth - pictureWidth, pageWidth - rightMargin)`. Numeric page offsets
are unaffected. Six combinations of picture widths and right margins confirmed
this rule. Mode 15 matches the specified page-edge alignment without the clamp.
The engine deliberately reproduces the legacy difference. Compatibility mode is
retained at document/section geometry level, so copied pictures use the
destination document's mode rather than carrying a source-document clamp flag.
Modes 11, 12, 14 and 15 are retained; missing mode uses legacy mode 12 semantics.
Other mode-specific reference layout differences are not claimed to be implemented.

`tools/canvas_anchor_position_fixture.py` authors original OPC/XML and PNG data
using Python's standard library. `anchor-position.docx` and
`anchor-position-legacy.docx` cover page/margin alignments and numeric offsets.
The modern fixture's eight image coordinates were independently measured in
native reference PDF output. Unit tests cover geometry, legacy dimensions, destination mode,
hit testing, resizing, reopening, no-op export and full undo. Browser tests check
actual painted coordinates, pointer selection, deletion/undo and exported files;
the independent Python verifier compares every retained anchor and package part.

Character/line bases, individual/inside/outside margins, inside/outside alignment,
aligned paragraph-relative vertical positions, arbitrary side wrapping and
page-relative top-and-bottom exclusion remain unsupported. Table-cell positioned
drawings still require the existing column/paragraph numeric no-wrap subset;
other cell bases are rejected before attaching an editable save handler. Rotation
and transformed positioned raster pictures retain their existing restrictions.

## Numbering Definitions part location

Part 1 §11.3.11 identifies Numbering Definitions through an internal implicit
relationship from the main document. Part 2 §§6.4, 6.5.2.3 and 6.5.3.4 define
target resolution relative to that document part. The same resolver now serves
styles and numbering: relative/absolute package paths and dot segments are
accepted, while duplicate, external, missing and malformed targets are rejected.
The numbering XML root must still use the supported WordprocessingML namespace.

Text edits preserve numbering bytes. Restarting or authoring lists appends to the
related numbering part without changing its location, relationship or content
type. Unrelated parts occupying `word/numbering.xml` are ignored and preserved;
new-list creation selects an unused filename. Existing numbering format, level,
override, inheritance and unknown-unused-definition rules are unchanged. General
OPC IRI normalization, arbitrary main-document locations and numbering images
remain outside the supported subset.

The independent `numbering-location.docx` fixture is authored from original XML
by `tools/canvas_numbering_location_fixture.py` and the standard-library OPC
shell in `canvas_first_section_fixture.py`. It starts a decimal list at 4 through
`../lists/numbering2.xml`. Unit tests cover paths, an unrelated conventional part,
text editing, restarting the second item at 1, new-list creation and exact undo.
The browser test edits/restarts/downloads/reopens it. An independent XML check
verifies that the original sequence and new restart instance coexist at the
original location; schema validation discovers numbering parts by content type.

## First-section start type

Part 1 §17.6.22 (`type`) defines placement relative to the preceding section;
§17.18.77 lists `nextPage`, `continuous`, `nextColumn`, `oddPage` and `evenPage`.
There is no preceding section for the first section. All five valid values are
therefore accepted there without introducing an empty page or column. This also
applies when the first section ends at a paragraph-level `sectPr` in a document
with later sections. The stored type is preserved through text edits, paragraph
splitting, single-section page setup, undo and export. Missing `type` defaults to
`nextPage`; missing/invalid `val` and duplicate type elements are rejected.
Later sections still require next-page transitions and equal paper dimensions.
Continuous, column and parity transitions between sections remain unimplemented.

Reference check: five independently authored OPC/XML probes differing only in
their first-section type were opened in the native reference. Every probe had one
page, with the first paragraph on page 1 at a vertical position of 72 points.
This agrees with the interpretation above; no reference/spec divergence was found.
`tools/canvas_first_section_fixture.py` authors the independent continuous-type
fixture with Python's standard library. Unit variants check every type in single
and multiple-section documents, preserved boundaries during paragraph splitting,
page setup, exact full undo, and rejected later transitions. The browser check
edits, downloads and reopens the fixture; an independent XML check verifies its
retained type and text, followed by schema validation.

This removes the first-section rejection from the first meeting-agenda specimen.
It does not claim that the remainder of that specimen is rendered correctly.

## Style Definitions part location

ECMA-376 Part 1 §11.3.12 identifies the main document's Style Definitions part
through an implicit relationship. Its example filename is not mandatory. Part 2
(2021) §§6.4, 6.5.2.3 and 6.5.3.4 resolve internal targets relative to the source
part, not the relationships file. The editor follows that relationship for both
paragraph/character style inheritance and table styles, accepting relative and
package-absolute paths, including dot segments. Main-document location remains
restricted to `word/document.xml`; other part readers have separate limitations.

Shared-style edits update the existing part in place without renaming it or
rewriting its relationships/content types. No-op and full-undo exports preserve
all original part bytes. An unrelated conventional `word/styles.xml` is ignored
and preserved; authoring a new styles part chooses an unused name. Duplicate,
external, missing, malformed and non-part style targets are rejected before
editing. General OPC IRI normalization and strict-namespace packages remain gaps.

`tools/canvas_styles_location_fixture.py` constructs the original minimal XML
fixture `public/fixtures/styles-location.docx` using Python's standard library.
Unit tests exercise inheritance, table styles, text edits, shared-style edits,
undo, malformed relationships and collision handling; the browser test edits,
downloads and reopens the fixture. Schema validation discovers style parts by
content type so nonstandard locations receive the same checks as conventional
ones. This corrects the loader assumption seen in meeting-agenda specimens
targeting `/word/styles2.xml`; it does not establish those specimens' complete
rendering fidelity or remove their other unsupported features.

## Hyperlinks inside temporary content controls

Proofing annotations (`w:proofErr`, ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.13.8.1) are accepted
inside supported temporary and persistent inline text controls and their text
hyperlinks. The four spelling/grammar boundary types are non-text annotations;
invalid types, extra attributes and child contents reject before editing.
Untouched control shells retain the original markers, while content edits
follow the existing temporary/persistent wrapper rules. Independent source and
native reference print evidence: `tests/fixtures/control-proofing`; regression tests:
`tests/control-proofing.test.js` and `tests/browser/control-proofing.spec.js`.

Completed body spelling (`w:proofState`, §17.15.1.65) now consumes saved
spellStart/spellEnd ranges on initial load. Each start matches the next end;
unmatched anchors are ignored. Whole words intersecting those ranges are checked
with the existing dictionary and noProof exclusions. An empty completed cache
does not load the dictionary. Dirty/omitted completion or changed body text,
language or noProof scope checks the full body; F7 and Recheck Document explicitly
bypass the cache. Undo may restore imported eligibility. Formatting that leaves
text and proofing scope unchanged retains source body markers and completion.
Exports invalidate existing clean flags after body proofing-scope changes as well
as the previously supported story-text changes. See
`tests/fixtures/cached-proofing`.
Grammar, other-story cached display, other-story property-only invalidation and
native reference dictionary/locale equivalence remain open. Recovered body text without
verified offsets is checked afresh. No new completion claims are authored.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.5.2.31, 17.5.2.36 and 17.5.2.38 define inline
`sdt`, its content and properties; §17.16.22 defines `hyperlink`, with
relationship references under §22.8.2.1. The inline content model permits
hyperlinks. The engine now applies its ordinary hyperlink reader to text-only
links inside unlocked temporary rich-text controls. External destinations,
internal bookmark anchors, tooltip/history attributes, mixed linked/plain runs,
adjacent controls and split formatting runs retain their existing semantics.
No-op and full-undo exports preserve every package part byte.

Formatting-only edits retain both the control wrapper and nested hyperlink
wrappers, including their targets and attributes. Hyperlink destination/removal,
text edits and paragraph splits unwrap the affected temporary control under the
existing §17.5.2.43 lifetime policy. Replacing a placeholder retains a destination
only when its hyperlink covers the entire expanded replacement range; a link
under the caret cannot spread across an otherwise partly linked prompt. Undo
restores control and link structure together.

`tools/canvas_control_hyperlinks_fixture.py` independently generates the original
`public/fixtures/control-hyperlinks.docx` using standard-library OPC/XML, without
external assets or editor code. Unit coverage includes export/reopen, partial
formatting, text/target edits, unlinking, splits, placeholders, graphemes, invalid
relationships and nested/empty links. Browser coverage formats and reopens links,
edits a target with undo, and copies/pastes source text. The independent browser
export verifier compares text, nested links, attributes and unrelated package
parts. The second local birthday card now opens for editing; its regression
formats a linked prompt, exports/reopens and verifies byte-identical full undo.

**Remaining limits:** links in these controls contain supported text runs only;
nested controls/links, inline bookmarks, pictures and fields inside their content
remain rejected before editing. Existing URI restrictions and hyperlink limits
apply. Clipboard interchange remains plain text; rich hyperlink/control metadata
is not transferred. This is structural and behavioral conformance for the stated
subset, not a claim of native reference layout equivalence or a fresh reference comparison of
linked-control editing.

| Inline rich-text controls | §§17.5.2.26, 17.5.2.31, 17.5.2.36, 17.5.2.38 | Unlocked temporary and persistent rich-text controls directly in ordinary body/cell paragraphs. An omitted type means rich text. Contents use supported text runs, tabs, breaks and text-only hyperlinks, retaining run formatting, alias/tag, signed 32-bit ID, placeholder reference, input properties and end properties. Controls occupy ordinary text offsets and do not alter layout. At most 2,000 controls; controls nested inside inline controls, empty temporary/plain-text/picture controls, row/cell wrappers, data-bound, locked, field and form-widget controls remain rejected before editable attachment. Imported control boundaries cannot divide a grapheme. |
| Block rich-text controls | §§17.5.2.29, 17.5.2.34, 17.5.2.43 | Unlocked temporary wrappers around body paragraphs/tables and cell paragraphs, including nested block wrappers and inline controls within their paragraphs. Nesting is bounded at 12 levels. Editing unwraps the nearest affected temporary control; formatting retains it. New table cells inherit formatting without copying cell-owned wrappers. Empty and multi-paragraph placeholders use their input formatting. Empty wrappers in vertical-merge continuation cells are preserved. Nested tables retain their enclosing block controls. Section properties inside wrappers and row/cell-level wrappers remain unsupported. |
| Temporary lifetime | §17.5.2.43 `temporary`; §17.17.4 booleans | Preserve the complete original wrapper until its contents change. Text edits, internal hyperlinks/bookmarks and splitting unwrap the entire affected control, retaining its surviving content. Formatting-only edits, including direct run formatting and character styles, retain the wrapper and serialize updated runs inside it. Unrelated edits and shared/paragraph style changes retain it. Undo/redo restores the wrapper with its text in the same transaction. A later manual change back to the old text does not recreate the wrapper. |
| Placeholder entry | §§17.5.2.24, 17.5.2.27 `rPr`, 17.5.2.39 `showingPlcHdr` | Show the stored prompt with its stored formatting. Clicking it selects the prompt; typing/pasting or composition within a single prompt replaces it using the control's input run properties. Without those properties, new text uses ordinary style inheritance, without inheriting prompt formatting. Selections extending beyond the prompt and literal search replacement retain their normal selection/matching semantics; inserted search text uses input formatting, and the changed control unwraps. End-boundary typing is outside the prompt unless it starts an adjacent prompt. Partial deletion unwraps while retaining unmodified text; direct formatting preserves the wrapper. |
| Appearance and namespaces | ECMA-376 Part 3 namespace scope; MS-DOCX §§2.5.3.7, 2.5.4.2, schema §5.2 | Accept omitted appearance or explicit `w15:appearance` hidden; preserve the extension and its namespace scope. Visible control adornments are outside this subset. Bind unambiguous local prefixes before serializing adjacent controls, retaining namespace aliases without reusing declarations outside their scope. |
| Export and clipboard | Existing OPC/mutation contract | No-op and full-undo exports retain every original ZIP part byte. Other edits retain unrelated package parts and unchanged controls (apart from invalidated renderer page-break hints). Clipboard support remains plain text: visible prompt/content text is copied without control metadata and pasted through normal text editing. Rich DOCX/HTML clipboard interchange, control authoring/navigation UI and real OS IME testing remain gaps. |

## Text geometry inside scaled drawing groups

Specification basis: ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.7.1–6 (child coordinates and
transforms), §21.1.2.1.1 (`bodyPr` insets, wrapping, anchoring and overflow),
§21.1.2.1.2 (`noAutofit`), and §17.3.2.38 (`sz` in half-points);
MS-ODRAWXML §2.16.3.2 (Wordprocessing groups). Reviewed against the published
[group transform definition](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.drawing.transformgroup)
and [no-AutoFit definition](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.drawing.noautofit).

Compose the ancestor transforms before laying out a shape's text. The resulting
physical frame determines wrapping and the free vertical space for top/center/
bottom anchoring. Font sizes, text insets and paragraph geometry retain their
physical units; they are not multiplied by the group coordinate scale. Painting
cancels that coordinate scale for text while retaining the transformed origin
and bitmap resolution. Visible overflow expands the session bitmap in the same
physical coordinates without changing the drawing's stored frame or wrap area.
This covers positive, axis-aligned uniform and nonuniform scales at arbitrary
supported nesting depth, including a drawing frame differing from scene extents.

Native reference comparison of `grouped-drawings.docx` found the original bug: its two nested
2× groups incorrectly painted nominal 8 pt text at 32 pt. The existing macOS
reference PDF paints all three copies at 7.92 pt (the native reference's output quantization),
not 32 pt. Its source package was rechecked byte-for-byte against the current
fixture. `canvas_group_text_fixture.py` independently generates
`group-text-scaling.docx`: equal physical frames, identity/double/nonuniform/
nested coordinates, asymmetric insets, wrapping and three vertical anchors.
Unit tests exercise physical layout, expanding/shrinking writing space, overflow
and source immutability. Browser tests inspect native paint transforms, wrapping,
insets, bitmap bounds, surrounding edits and export/reopen. The independent
Python export verifier compares the complete drawing trees and untouched parts;
`check:conformance` requires that browser export and validates the XML schemas.

The existing immutable-drawing editing and plain-text clipboard limits remain.
Rotation/flips, autofit, font-family resolution and full reference text metrics are
separate gaps. The fresh four-case reference PDF comparison remains pending while
the reference application's file-access dialog blocks automation; the broader typography must not be
described as matching the native reference perfectly.

Apply group child coordinate origins/extents at every nesting level. Reject rotation, flips, guide formulas, effects, theme fills, hidden shapes, linked text boxes, and unsupported drawing elements before editable attachment. Limit scene depth, node/path counts, image sizes and aggregate decoded pixels. |
| Drawing text | §21.1.2.1.1 `bodyPr`, §17.3 paragraphs/runs, §17.3.1.41 `textDirection`; MS-OI29500 §2.1.62 implementation note | Resolve ordinary text-box paragraph/run inheritance with the existing engine; support bold, italic, size, RGB text, paragraph spacing/indents/alignment, horizontal body flow, insets, top/center/bottom anchoring and default overflow with noAutofit. Retain WordprocessingML paragraph edge spacing regardless of spcFirstLastPara, following the independent reference controls below. Extend the preview bitmap for overflow without changing the stored drawing frame or its wrap area. Reject decorated/linked/list/field/table text-box content outside this subset. As documented by the MS-OI29500 implementation note, paragraph textDirection is inactive outside text frames; DrawingML body properties govern these boxes. This is an explicit reference compatibility choice, not a claim of implementing arbitrary vertical WordprocessingML paragraphs. |
| Floating objects | §§20.4.2.3 `anchor`, 20.4.2.10–11 positions, 20.4.2.15 `wrapNone`, 20.4.2.20 `wrapTopAndBottom` | Column-relative horizontal and paragraph-relative vertical numeric offsets. Behind/foreground ordering uses behindDoc and relativeHeight. Floating anchors consume no inline width or ascent. Top-and-bottom wrapping excludes the whole horizontal band from text flow; retain irrelevant horizontal text distances. Keep a wrapping anchor's host paragraph together and reject an oversized paragraph or negative top-and-bottom offsets. No-wrap objects may have negative offsets and are clipped at page edges. Existing full-column square wrapping remains supported. Pointer selection and selection rectangles use the floating frame independently of the text caret. |
| Section layout | §§17.6.17–18 `sectPr`, §17.6.22 section `type`, §17.6.11 `pgMar`, §17.6.13 `pgSz` | Next-page sections with equal paper dimensions and independently resolved margins. A paragraph's sectPr applies to the section ending at that paragraph; body sectPr applies to the final section. Numbering and document offsets remain continuous. Splitting a paragraph moves its section mark to the last resulting paragraph and preserves its XML once. Reject editing across section boundaries, section properties in tables, non-next-page breaks, differing paper sizes and multi-section page-setting edits. |
| Picture/numbering compatibility | §20.1.8.6 `alphaModFix`; §§17.3.2.2 `bCs`, 17.3.2.17 `iCs`, 17.3.2.39 `szCs` | Retain picture alpha modifiers (see Picture opacity below) and empty picture outlines. Retain validated complex-script marker declarations on Latin/numeric and the supported Unicode bullet labels, where those declarations have no visual effect. Unsupported complex-script numbering still fails. |
| Atomic editing and retention | Existing model/OPC contract; Part 3 preservation of alternatives | Groups and alternate drawings remain complete objects: surrounding body edits, selection, deletion and undo/redo are supported. Their contents/appearance and named-style definitions while groups remain present cannot be edited. The properties dialog explains this limitation. Retained drawings are never replaced with generated raster images in DOCX exports. No-op/full-undo saves retain every original package part byte; other edits preserve unrelated parts, including media, fonts, styles and relationships. |

Reviewed using the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),

Validation: 2,481 unit tests passed (`npm test -- --maxWorkers=2 --testTimeout=20000`);

`npm run check:conformance` checks both the standard fallback view against the
official ECMA transitional schemas and the understood extension view against the
published MS-ODRAWXML WPG/WPS schemas. The latter are hash-pinned and cached only
in the OS temporary directory. Split-schema imports in the published MS-ODRAWXML schemas are resolved to
the ECMA definitions; the unsupported legacy wne text-box and w14 contentPart
alternatives are removed, narrowing the published schemas. Negative self-checks
ensure incomplete group/shape definitions fail. Both views of the supplied
specimen also pass the checked XML schemas; that does not certify the package's
fallback images as visually equivalent to the selected groups.

**Remaining gaps:** internal shape/text-box editing, named-style changes while
groups are present, arbitrary shape/path/effect formats, general side wrapping,
page/margin/character-relative positioning, rotated groups, cross-page floating
objects, continuous/odd/even sections and mixed paper sizes. Drawing-text layout
uses the engine's bundled Noto Sans; original font references and embedded fonts
are preserved but not loaded. Narrow labels can therefore wrap and overflow,
and pagination can differ from the native reference. Group text is visible and retained but is
not exposed as editable body text or body search results. No reference application
was used for comparison. Schema validity is not full OOXML/OPC or reference layout
equivalence.

## Cached column charts and full-column floating pictures

### Cached-chart metadata, generated labels and constrained AutoFit content

The reader retains date-system, blank-display, disabled data-label/title,
roundedCorners=false, unique-series-ID and vendor NA-display metadata while
rendering complete finite caches with flat string categories. Relevant clauses
are Part 1 §§21.2.2.38, 42, 49, 63–64, 180, 197, 202 and 216; Part 3 governs
MCE branch selection. Internal embedded XLSX relationships with refresh disabled
are retained without fetching or evaluating formulas. External workbooks,
automatic refresh, sparse/error caches and unknown active extensions reject.

Generated Latin labels support inherited chart/axis text properties: explicit
point size, family or document-theme family, bold, italic, opaque solid color,
and kerning threshold. Chart-local theme overrides reject unresolved theme
colors/fonts. Rich/vertical/decorated labels remain unsupported. The native reference's
observed -60000000 rotation sentinel is accepted for the tested horizontal
short labels; this is not general automatic label rotation. Built-in/related
chart styles require explicitly supplied visible appearance and text defaults;
the implementation does not claim complete chart-style inheritance.

Five original controls and native reference PDFs in `tests/fixtures/chart-metadata`
check bars, tick strings, colors, fonts, emphasis and size. The negative
`chart-metadata-order.docx` reproduces the native reference accepting showDLblsOverMax after
extLst although the standard schema rejects the order. The reader retains that
source order; the schema self-check continues to reject it, and an in-memory
reordered control must validate. No source repair is silently applied.

For §17.18.87 AutoFit, indivisible content exceeding available width retains
its natural dimensions. In legacy compatibility modes, the solver compresses
to independently measured padding/indent floors and clips inline ink at the
cell edge. Legacy top-level AutoFit width limits include exterior cell writing
insets. In mode 15, indivisible-content floors can instead expand AutoFit with
a positive absolute preferred width beyond the writing area. Automatic,
omitted and percentage table widths retain their width limit and clip the
oversized inline content. Eight independent picture controls in
`tests/fixtures/autofit-picture-preferences` establish this distinction;
editing the preference reflows the table without rewriting picture dimensions.
Six paired original
reference controls in `tests/fixtures/table-unbreakable` cover a wide chart, picture
and glyph. Mode-15 controls independently retain a 7-inch drawing inside a
roughly 515.64-point table despite a 4-inch writing area; the legacy counterpart
stays about 299.60 points wide. Impossible legacy padding constraints still reject. The shared clipping
geometry also constrains carets, hit testing and selection. This is observed
reference behavior within the standard's layout guidance, not an asserted normative
contradiction. The automatic chart layout extension below covers explicit-font
axis placement; these table controls do not establish complete reference chart
equivalence.

### Explicit-font automatic chart plot layout

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§21.2.2.88–89 (`layout`, `layoutTarget`), 21.2.2.91
(`lblOffset`) and 21.2.2.216 (`txPr`) provide the layout/text vocabulary but
do not prescribe the native reference's automatic plot-padding algorithm. For the supported
explicit-font axis subset, plot margins now use native font-box metrics and
the widest value label. Chart frame resizing no longer changes the spacing
solely through a frame-height-derived font size. Numeric labels account for
internal leading when centered on ticks; category labels reserve their face
descent. Small bitmap-strike advance rounding is avoided by measuring and
painting chart labels at outline scale with kerning evaluated at the original
point size. Package chart XML and font declarations remain unchanged.

Twenty-four original reference controls in `tests/fixtures/chart-layout` vary five
font families, four sizes, frame dimensions and positive/mixed/negative caches.
When zero is above the plot bottom, the bottom inset accounts for value labels
while category labels remain next to the internal/top zero axis.
The controls compare absolute plot edges
and label origins/baselines within 0.2 point and exercise surrounding edits,
unrelated-part retention, exact undo and reopening. The README records the
measured geometry and reference provenance. This is matching observed consumer
defaults, not a claimed contradiction of the standard. Unformatted labels,
complete legend/title layout, long/wrapped labels and other custom chart
features still have the limitations described below.

### Chart DrawingML solid colors

Chart `spPr` (§21.2.2.197) now uses the existing DrawingML solid-color resolver
(§20.1.2.3) for series, chart/plot fills, outlines, gridlines and axis lines.
This adds scheme/preset/system/scRGB colors and the resolver's ordered color
transforms to the previous RGB-only subset. The document theme and its color
mapping apply; a chart-local theme-override relationship rejects scheme-color
resolution until that separate inheritance layer is implemented. Empty effect
lists are accepted; nonempty effects, alpha below one, conflicting colors and
unsupported transforms still reject before editing. No chart XML is rewritten.

The three original controls in `tests/fixtures/chart-colors` independently verify
theme remapping, shade/tint, preset/system/scRGB fills, grid/axis luminance and
empty effects against the native reference. Bar colors agree exactly. The native reference quantizes
the 50%-luminance gridline to #7f7f7f; the shared resolver produces #808080.
That measured one-level residual remains explicit, consistent with the earlier
shape-color quantization limitation. This does not establish a specification
contradiction or complete chart-layout equivalence. The metadata and generated
label extension above covers a further subset; full style inheritance remains open.

This iteration opens the supplied `file-sample_1MB (2).docx` while retaining its
chart, photograph, table, numbering and text. The implementation is original and
adds no dependencies or third-party engine. The supplied photograph/package is
not redistributed. Earlier drawing limitations below are superseded only by
the explicitly supported subset in this section.

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |

Read complete indexed string/number caches or literals; retain formulas without evaluating them. Respect point indices and series order independently of XML order. Reject missing/duplicate points, inconsistent categories or axes, external relationships/workbooks, unsupported content, nonfinite numbers and resource-limit excesses. Up to 20 series, 100 categories, 200 characters per label; values are zero or have magnitude between 1e-9 and 1e12. |
| Column-chart preview | §§21.2.2.16–17 `barChart`/`barDir`, 21.2.2.77 bar grouping, 21.2.2.75 `gapWidth`, 21.2.2.25/226 category/value axes, 21.2.2.34 axis crossing, 21.2.2.160 scaling | Inline clustered columns with matching string categories, positive/negative values, nonoverlapping bars, RGB/no-fill series, simple RGB grid/axis lines, a right-hand nonoverlaid legend and linear automatic axes crossing zero. `gapWidth` uses one bar's width, accepts whole percentages in both transitional forms, and retains its schema default. Automatic ticks, fonts and plot geometry are application choices, not native reference layout equivalence. The chart painter uses only parsed data and native canvas; no remote resources are loaded. |
| Chart editing and retention | §§20.4.2.7–8 extent/inline positioning; existing object-run, model and OPC contracts | Charts are atomic objects supporting surrounding text edits, splitting, deletion, undo/redo, frame resizing and alt text. Chart data/style editing, crop, flip and rotation are unavailable. Source chart XML, relationships and all unrelated parts remain byte-identical; resizing changes the drawing frame, not cached chart data. The preview is a session-only bitmap, never a replacement image in the DOCX. |
| Stacked-column data geometry | §§21.2.2.77 and 21.2.3.4 `grouping`/`ST_BarGrouping`, §21.2.2.131 `overlap`, §21.2.2.122 `numFmt`, §21.2.2.86 `invertIfNegative` | Extends the cached-column subset to `stacked` and `percentStacked`. Accumulate positive/negative values independently; normalize each percentage category by total absolute values, with zero totals producing no bars. Honor integer overlap from -100 to 100, including percent lexical forms and the zero default. Support General/whole-percentage value-axis labels. Twelve independent reference controls verify normalized bar/outline geometry, tick strings, negative inversion, no-fill and explicit-outline behavior. The native reference's default inversion uses white fill and a black fallback outline, retains explicit outlines, and leaves no-fill/no-outline series empty. Source XML is immutable. Absolute plot margins, fonts and text layout remain preview policy, not native reference equivalence; chart-local theme overrides, metadata and text formatting beyond the earlier subset remain unsupported. Document-theme colors are covered by the color extension above. |
| Full-column floating pictures | §§20.4.2.3 `anchor`, 20.4.2.10–11 horizontal/vertical positioning, 20.4.2.17 square wrapping | A single picture in a standalone body paragraph, centered relative to the column, top-aligned relative to its paragraph, with square wrapping and zero distances/effect extents/rotation. Its width must equal the column width within one EMU, leaving no side text area. Layout reserves an atomic full-width band independently of inline line spacing and paragraph indents/alignment. Reject side-wrapped/narrow pictures, table/list/shaded/bordered anchors, mixed paragraph text, other positioning/wrapping and pictures taller than the writing area. Reflow rejects edits that leave this subset and the editor restores selection/history. Original anchor XML remains an anchor after export. |
| Invisible outlines and drawing locks | §§20.1.2.2.24 `ln`, 20.1.8.44 `noFill`, 20.1.2.2.31 `picLocks` | Preserve explicit no-fill picture backgrounds/outlines and their inactive line metadata. Accept `noChangeArrowheads` because the editor offers no arrowhead mutation; retain the existing aspect-ratio lock. Active unsupported editing locks still fail before editing. Ordinary visible picture outlines are covered by the later picture-outline section. |
| Paired-off capitalization compatibility | §§17.3.2.5 `caps`, 17.3.2.33 `smallCaps`, 17.7.3 toggle semantics | Accept and preserve the unambiguous producer form with both properties explicitly false, resetting both forms for direct runs/marks and retaining separate style-toggle semantics. This is an intentional import exception: the normative prose forbids both elements on one run even when off, though the XSD allows them. Simultaneous declarations with either flag enabled remain rejected; ordinary capitalization edits continue to author one property. |
| Fragment namespace preservation | XML Namespaces prefix scoping; existing OPC retention contract | Bind chart references' relationship prefixes locally before detaching drawing/paragraph/table fragments. This prevents a generated relationship prefix from colliding with an existing chart prefix, without copying unrelated XML. Unedited/full-undo packages bypass reserialization entirely. |

Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 Part 1 and Part 4 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
including chart schema defaults, indexed-cache ordering, gap-width units,
floating positioning, invisible outlines and the capitalization prose constraint.

## Clear direct paragraph formatting iteration

| Paragraph declarations and inheritance | ECMA-376 Part 1 fifth edition §§17.3.1.26 `pPr`, 17.3.1.27 `pStyle`, 17.7.2 style hierarchy; Part 4 §A.2 `CT_PPr` / `CT_PPrBase` | Remove direct paragraph declarations, including explicit off/default values and opaque properties. Retain the paragraph style, paragraph-mark `rPr` and section structure, then resolve the existing style hierarchy again. A caret resets its current paragraph, including an empty one; a range covers selected paragraphs, excluding a final paragraph when the range ends at its start. Style-only paragraphs are no-ops that retain redo. |
| Numbering | §§17.3.1.19 `numPr`, 17.9.18 `numId`, 17.9.23 `pStyle`; Part 4 §A.2 `CT_NumPr` | Remove direct numbering references and level overrides, including `numId=0` suppression. Style numbering becomes effective again; a direct list disappears when no style supplies one. Recompute levels, geometry and counters using the existing numbering subset. Corrected serialization of new paragraphs so inherited numbering is not written as direct `numPr`, preserving later style changes after save/reopen. Numbering definitions remain untouched. |
| Paragraph layout | §§17.3.1.12 `ind`, 17.3.1.38 `tabs`, 17.3.1.33 `spacing`, 17.3.1.24 `pBdr`, 17.3.1.31 `shd`, 17.3.1.20 `outlineLvl`, 17.3.1.14–15 / .23 / .44 pagination | Restore inherited indents, tab stops (including removed clears), spacing, borders/fill, outline levels and pagination within the existing supported subsets. Built-in heading outline levels remain fixed. Reflow through the original layout/painter; all selected paragraphs reset in one transaction. | Retained text and structures | §§17.3.1.29 paragraph-mark `rPr`, 17.3.2.28 run `rPr`; existing OPC preservation contract | Retain run formatting, character styles, paragraph-mark formatting, pending typing choices, source text, links, bookmarks, breaks, pictures and table structure. The command finishes native composition before its own undo step. Later direct edits do not revive cleared shell properties. Untouched/full-undo exports preserve every original part; reset exports change only `word/document.xml`. |

Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 Part 1/4 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/ecma-376/),
especially paragraph properties, style precedence and the special zero numbering
reference. Clearing direct paragraph properties, including numbering, is the

command. The toolbar action has an accessible name and keyboard activation.
There is no Ctrl/Cmd+Q binding because it conflicts with application quit.

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Searchable source text | ECMA-376 Part 1 fifth edition §§17.3.2.25 `r`, 17.3.3.31 `t`, 17.3.3.1 `br`, 17.3.3.32 `tab`; Part 4 §A.2 `CT_Text` | Search literal main-story text within each paragraph, across formatting and hyperlink boundaries. Include table-cell source paragraphs; count a repeated header once. Paragraph boundaries, tabs, soft/page breaks and picture placeholders interrupt a match. Search/navigation do not alter the document, its pagination or undo history. Search state is not serialized. |
| Matching policy | Application behavior, not prescribed by OOXML; ECMA-262 Unicode RegExp case folding and ECMA-402 `Intl.Segmenter` | Case-insensitive by default, with Match case and Whole words. Query metacharacters are escaped; there are no regular expressions or replacement substitutions. Matches are nonoverlapping and must begin/end at complete grapheme boundaries. Whole words requires word-like start/end boundaries from the browser's English-locale segmenter, including multiword phrases. Rejected candidates do not hide later overlapping valid matches. |
| Replacement and inheritance | §§17.3.2.28 `rPr`, 17.3.3.31 `t`/`xml:space`, 17.7 style hierarchy; existing editing contract | Replace the selected current match, or batch all original matches in one transaction. Empty replacement deletes text. Inserted text takes the first matched character's style and direct formatting, retaining live inheritance; subsequent characters' different formatting is removed with the matched text. Pending typing formatting is ignored. Identical replacements are no-ops and retain redo. Ordinary text and significant leading/trailing spaces use the existing DOCX writer. |
| Links, bookmarks and structures | §§17.16.22 `hyperlink`, 17.13.6.1–2 bookmark markers, 17.4 table structures | Retain a hyperlink if the entire match is within it; a match spanning linked/unlinked text loses that link while surrounding fragments remain intact. Bookmark ranges and points follow the same boundary rules as ordinary edits, including overlapping ranges. Batch changes retain paragraph/cell boundaries, breaks, images, lists and table metadata. Untouched/full-undo packages preserve all source parts byte-for-byte; edits preserve unrelated parts. |
| Navigation, layout and rollback | Existing model, layout and painter contracts | Accessible toolbar action and Ctrl/Cmd+F open a nonmodal panel. Enter/Shift+Enter navigate and wrap; Escape closes and returns focus. Current results use the existing selection painter, caret geometry and scroll path, including zoom and page boundaries. Counts refresh on document edits and undo; search-field composition commits before navigating. Replace All builds each affected paragraph once, then reflows once. Invalid text, size limits, unsupported resulting formatting or failed pagination roll back the whole edit and retain history/selection. |

Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
especially literal text and whitespace handling. Matching behavior follows native
[Unicode case folding](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/text-processing.html#sec-runtime-semantics-canonicalize-ch)
and [Intl.Segmenter](https://tc39.es/ecma402/#sec-intl.segmenter), with the declared
application rules above; it is not a claim of matching the native reference's search
semantics. No third-party implementation or dependency was added. Licensing
remains undecided.

Editable minimums range from 0 to 31,680 twips (22 inches), in twentieth-point steps. Untouched unit spellings and ignored automatic values remain intact. |

An explicit auto still resets the minimum. Retain the engine's existing ordinary table-style height inheritance, including based-on chains. ECMA permits this style property, but the native reference does not; this is an engine extension, not a reference style-interoperability claim. Inherit removes the row override; absent any declaration, rows are automatic. |
| Editing and preservation | §§17.4.80, 17.4.84 `vMerge`; existing model/OPC contracts | Accessible Row height dialog edits every selected physical row, including rows covered by a vertical merge. Mixed selections remain unchanged until edited. Height edits, inherited resets, row insertion, merge splitting and deletion retain row metadata. Undo/redo restores formatting and selection; no-edit/full undo preserves every ZIP entry byte. Direct edits retain other row properties, source text and unrelated package parts. |
| Reflow and interaction | §§17.4.6 `cantSplit`, 17.4.59 `tblHeader`; existing original layout and painting contracts | Minimums feed existing row sizing, pagination, cell vertical alignment and repeated headers. Rows can grow past the minimum; tall rows can continue across pages. Carets, selection, pictures and pointer targets use the same resulting geometry as painting. A repeated header that leaves insufficient body space fails the editing transaction and restores document, history, selection and layout. |
| Import checks | Part 4 §A.2 `CT_Height` and `CT_TrPr`; declared engine limits | Reject unknown rules, malformed or oversized active measurements, duplicate properties, unknown WordprocessingML height attributes and nested/text content before editable open. Exact heights are covered by the later iteration above. Valid unsigned automatic values can exceed the editable minimum limit because they are ignored. Unsupported active table-style structures still reject; unused definitions remain preserved. |

Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 publication and Part 1/4 downloads](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/)
and the MS-OI29500 implementation notes above. The previous reader treated a
missing rule as automatic and could discard a reference-authored minimum. Imported
documents with that spelling now use the declared height, so their preview may
gain space or pages. Serialization preserves the original spelling until the
height itself is edited. No third-party implementation or dependency was added;
the application license remains undecided.

Declared preview policy: the minimum applies to the whole row, including cell
margins. It can extend over multiple page fragments. A keep-together row starts
on a fresh page when possible; an oversized row still splits. Existing cell
vertical alignment operates within each already allocated page fragment, so
short content stays on its original page. Repeated header copies use the same
edited height and redirect interaction to the original row. Height editing
changes vertical geometry without altering column widths or horizontal text
advances. These are engine policies, not claims of exact reference pagination.

Reviewed using the official [ECMA-376 publication and Part 1/4 downloads](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
especially §§17.3.1.37–38 and 17.18.85. No implementation was copied. The
application license remains undecided; no dependency or vendored library was added.

Reference-compatible leader ink uses a page-relative 600 dpi advance grid. Display
font size, glyph advance, custom spacing and the starting text coordinate round
to that grid; glyph advance and spacing round separately. Whole glyphs fit in
the resolved gap, leaving fractional remainders blank. Source run properties,
tab geometry, wrapping and carets retain their original measurements. Existing
font, color, script shift and text-width transforms remain in effect. Leaders do
not expand with paragraph justification. Centered/right paragraphs shift the
positioned leader with their text. Tables, AutoFit, soft breaks, continuations
and repeated headers retain their tab geometry and caret positions.

Native reference compatibility refinement (template 17): §17.18.85 requests complete filling
of tab spacing without specifying numeric phase or rounding. The native reference leaves blank
fractional remainders instead of clipping a partial glyph. Four original fixtures
from `tools/tab_leader_grid_fixture.py` and retained reference PDFs/coordinates in
`tests/fixtures/tab-leader-grid` establish this behavior. The 77 cases cover two
fonts, changed indents/margins, all leader kinds, font sizes, spacing, scaling and
alignment. Browser assertions match 76 cases. The retained Arial superscript
case exposes a separate existing generic script-transform approximation and is
explicitly excluded from reference-metric assertions. The TOC uses dots in the native reference too;
reduced-size images were not evidence for changing the character.
