## Saved invisible DrawingML outlines

MS-ODRAWXML §2.3.1.6 `hiddenLine` stores an inactive `a:CT_LineProperties`
(ECMA-376 Part 1 Annex A.4.1). It contributes no ink or layout extent and is
ignored when an outline is visible. The importer accepts the published extension
URI in picture and shape property lists, checks its identity/cardinality,
attributes and ordered property groups, and retains the dormant XML unchanged.
Its fill, dash, join and end subtrees stay opaque; unsupported active gradient,
compound or arrowhead rendering does not discard invisible saved settings.

Eight original controls retain a reference PDF and object coordinates under
`tests/fixtures/hidden-line`. Six are supported and browser-matched; two expose
the existing visible raster-outline gap and retain read-only rejection. Tests
cover unchanged scenes, malformed containers, image/text edits, reopening,
unrelated OPC parts and exact undo. Export validation loads the unchanged
published `hiddenLine` declaration with ECMA's complete line-property schema.
The feature follows the specification; no reference divergence was observed.

## Isolated inline objects and omitted paragraph defaults

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.4.2.8 (`inline`), 17.3.1.29 (paragraph-mark `rPr`),
17.3.1.33 (`spacing`), and 17.3.1.39 (`textAlignment`) govern this layout.
Automatic vertical alignment is consumer-defined. Original reference controls in
`tests/fixtures/inline-object-baseline` establish the following refinement:
image-only lines, including ordinary whitespace, use font metrics as a minimum
height without adding an invisible font descender below the inline objects.
Short objects bottom-align within that natural line; tall objects determine its
height. Automatic multiples retain the natural baseline and add space below;
at-least lines bottom-align, while exact lines place the baseline at 80% of the
assigned height and retain the existing clipping/hit-testing bounds. Visible
text, generated leaders and list markers retain text-baseline layout.

The minimum font height comes from the paragraph mark in the measured legacy
12/14 controls and from inline image runs in mode 15. Five original documents
cover 62 cases, including pictures/shapes, effect extents, font choices and
sizes, whitespace, multiple objects and spacing modes. Browser assertions match
61. The retained mixed-text exact-spacing control exposes a separate existing
text-baseline discrepancy; it is not included in the reference-fidelity claim.

The later `tests/fixtures/flat-line-baseline` controls refine the zero-reservation
case: an unshifted zero-height inline drawing on an otherwise image-only line
retains text ascent/descent from the paragraph mark and whitespace, including in
mode 15. Minimum line spacing still bottom-aligns; exact spacing is unchanged.
The 26 original controls cover fonts, run/mark size differences, body/table
contexts, positive heights, raised runs, effects and spacing modes. Twenty-five
object positions and all following-paragraph baselines match the native reference within
0.1 pt. The legacy mode-12 positive-effect-reservation control retains a separate
2 pt visible-frame offset gap, explicitly documented and excluded from that
fidelity claim. This is native reference consumer behavior under the same clauses above.

The footer regression controls exposed an additional default-category omission.
Part 1 §§17.7.5.1 and 17.7.5.3 specify application-defined defaults when the
document/paragraph-default category is absent. The native reference materializes
8pt after-spacing and a 278/240 line multiple in that case. The importer now
uses those consumer defaults only for an absent category (including no styles
part). An explicitly empty category/property set keeps single spacing and zero
after-spacing; inherited styles and direct formatting continue to override
defaults. New app documents already declare their existing defaults explicitly.
Eight independent controls and reference application COM/serialized-default references live in
`tests/fixtures/default-paragraph-spacing`. No-edit/undo preserve source package
parts; explicit edits serialize overrides rather than silently adding defaults.

## Justified paragraph iteration

Known reference-fidelity gap: line selection currently uses natural widths and then
expands spaces. The original `justified-line-fit` control demonstrates that the native reference
also contracts inter-word spaces to fit additional words. Three browser cases
retain this unresolved mismatch as expected failures; thirteen paired controls
match. §§17.3.1.13 and 17.18.44 specify inter-word adjustment but not its minimum
spacing or line-fitting algorithm. This is an implementation gap, not evidence
that the native reference contradicts a specified numerical threshold. See the fixture README.

Further native controls under `tests/fixtures/justification-contraction` isolate
175 native reference pages. Mode 15 contracts proportional-font ordinary spaces, including
final/manual-break lines; mode 14 does not in the paired controls. Mixed-size
spaces contract proportionally, while NBSP and Courier New retain their widths.
The single-space boundary agrees with a 25% limit, but a separate total-line
limit still needs a precise rule. Consecutive-space/word-length controls refute
using 25% alone or treating an approximate 5% line allowance as established.
Joining identical runs leaves the thirty cluster cases' line breaks intact.

The explicitly failing `tools/check-justification-contraction.mjs` currently
reports 65 mismatched pages; all 22 mode-14 cases match line text. Nine reference
tests verify the native evidence and hashes, and seven source packages pass
56 XML checks. Those passes do not certify contraction support. The separate
legacy `wpJustification` formula in the MS-OI29500 compatibility note must not
be substituted for the modern algorithm: these controls do not enable that flag.

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Alignment and inheritance | ECMA-376 Part 1 fifth edition §17.3.1.13 `jc`, §17.18.44 `ST_Jc`, §17.7.2 style hierarchy | Import and author `both` in direct paragraph formatting and ordinary paragraph styles, including based-on inheritance and direct overrides. Require one nonempty `val`; reject duplicates, nested/text content, unknown WordprocessingML attributes and unsupported active alignment values before editable import. Existing left/center/right and LTR start/end behavior remains supported. |
| Expansion and last lines | §§17.18.44, 17.15.3.5 | Expand inter-word spaces on nonfinal lines without changing inter-character spacing, source text or chosen line breaks. Leave paragraph-final and gap-free lines natural. Share the expanded measurements with glyph painting, color clips, backgrounds, underlines, strikes, carets, selections and image positions. Indents, list labels, cell margins, repeated headers and page fragments retain their existing geometry. |
| Soft returns | §17.15.3.5 `doNotExpandShiftReturn`, §17.17.4 boolean properties | Default false expands soft-break lines too. True exempts those lines while ordinary wrapped lines still justify. Read all legal on/off lexical forms; reject malformed declarations. Retain the source flag unchanged through edits and export; fresh package creation can emit it. No user-facing compatibility-setting editor is added. |
| Editing and preservation | Part 4 §A.2 `CT_PPr` order; existing model and OPC contracts | Accessible Justify toolbar button, Ctrl/Cmd+J, formatting input events and Style alignment control edit `both`. Mixed state, undo/redo, typing and paragraph splitting/merging use existing transactions. Display spacing belongs only to layout fragments and never enters run properties or source text. No-edit/full undo preserves every ZIP entry byte; ordinary alignment edits preserve unrelated package parts. |
| Browser text contract | [HTML Canvas text styles](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-wordspacing) | Use native Canvas word spacing in both measurement and painting, retaining whole-word shaping and kerning. Convert spacing through existing script/text-width transforms so its final page distance is constant. Reset native spacing on every style change. Reject justified imports when Canvas word spacing is unavailable; ordinary documents remain editable. Browser regressions compare native paint widths with Canvas and CSS references. |

Review used the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/)
and the clauses above, including the
[soft-return definition](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.donotexpandshiftreturn?view=openxml-3.0.1).
The review distinguishes word justification from `distribute`, which also expands
characters, and requires Arabic kashida behavior that this engine does not yet
implement. Arabic text in a justified paragraph therefore rejects on import or
rolls back an editing transaction.

Declared preview policy: expansion opportunities are interior U+0020 spaces and
U+00A0 nonbreaking spaces. Leading/trailing spaces and other fixed Unicode spaces,
including narrow NBSP, retain natural advances. The existing trailing-space
compatibility flags still govern wrapping, hanging and underlining. With tabs,
only the final left-aligned field expands; earlier fields stay anchored. Actual
expansion after center/right/decimal tabs rejects before a save handler attaches.
The local playground measures the incoming layout before replacing its current
editor, so geometry-based import failures preserve the open document.
Native advances are remeasured when rounding exceeds the writing edge, reducing
the added spacing without relaxing cell bounds. If the native shaper omits space
expansion at a fragment boundary, layout restores that advance and painting uses
the same offset; this includes small-caps size changes.
Internal page-break lines justify; a terminal page break that keeps its paragraph
mark on the old page is treated as final. These policies are covered by behavioral
tests and are not claims of exact reference layout.

Independent fixtures: `public/fixtures/justification.docx` and
`public/fixtures/justification-soft-breaks.docx`, generated by original
`tools/canvas_justification_fixture.py` using python-docx (MIT). Regenerate with
`python tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-justification-fixture`. This records
their source and provenance. They cover style chains, direct overrides, rich
runs, Unicode, soft/page breaks, hanging indents, left tabs, numbering, table
pagination and repeated headers. Browser exports of both fixtures and
`new-justification.docx` receive independent text, alignment, break, formatting
and ZIP-part checks, followed by official XSD validation.

Local milestone validation: 2,265 unit tests in 183 files, 148 browser scenarios,
81 independent export checks and 543 official schema part checks pass. The
production build and license audit pass (199 locked packages). Unit and browser
suites ran separately, with one and two workers respectively; existing test
timeouts remain unchanged. Native browser regressions include 72 combinations
of fractional cell widths, text scaling, character spacing and small caps with
superscript. Screenshots cover rich paragraphs, both soft-return policies and
continued tables with repeated headers.

**Remaining gaps:** distributed and Thai justification, Arabic kashida, expansion
after center/right/decimal tabs, language-specific justification rules and exact
reference spacing across compatibility versions. No reference application was available
for visual comparison. Browser checks cover current Chromium; other browsers
are capability checked but not visually certified. A schema pass is not full
OOXML/OPC or visual conformance. No dependency or third-party implementation was
added; licensing remains undecided.

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |

Missing vertical defaults are zero. The native reference diverges from the specified 115-twip leading/trailing defaults: ordinary resolved table styles start with zero side margins, the built-in Normal Table supplies 108 twips, and an unresolved/absent table style supplies 10 twips. See the independent table-margin-defaults controls below. Newly inserted tables retain their explicitly authored 108-twip horizontal padding. Empty containers do not clear inherited sides. |
| Measurements | §17.4.87 `CT_TblWidth`, §17.18.107 `ST_MeasurementOrPercent`; Part 4 §A.2 | Missing type means dxa; missing width means zero. Read nonnegative twips and absolute mm/cm/in/pt/pc/pi values; an explicit suffix overrides contradictory type. Round absolute values to whole twips. Percentage/automatic cell exceptions cancel earlier cell-style exceptions and resolve to table/row defaults (see the cell-margin reset controls below). Reject unknown units, malformed/negative values, duplicate sides, unknown WordprocessingML attributes and nested/text content before editable import. Active margins are limited to 31,680 twips (22 inches), an application limit. |

Table-level leading/trailing auto/pct declarations mean zero in the native reference; vertical table auto/pct declarations inherit, while cell exceptions reset to table/row defaults. Preserve ignored source declarations; the authoring UI writes explicit dxa zero for No padding and removes direct declarations for Inherit. |
| Logical aliases and preservation | Part 4 §A.2 `CT_TcMar`, `CT_TblCellMar`, `CT_TcPr`; [MS-OI29500 logical-side precedence](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/94be0b29-8284-4099-b9c6-0df1e3988a08) | In supported LTR tables, start/end supersede left/right within each declaration, including when the logical declaration is ignored. Editing or inheriting a physical side removes both aliases, then writes one dxa declaration in schema order. Keep unedited side spellings, ignored declarations, other properties and unrelated package parts intact. No-edit/full undo preserves original ZIP entry bytes. |
| Editing, reflow and geometry | §§17.4.17 `gridSpan`, 17.4.84 `vMerge`, 17.4.59 `tblHeader`, 17.18.87 layout guidance; existing model/layout contracts | Accessible Cell margins controls edit four point-valued sides, with mixed-field preservation, No padding and Inherit all. Apply to every selected cell and every physical member of a vertical merge. Existing original layout uses margins in fixed-cell wrapping, AutoFit demand, row heights, pagination, vertical alignment and repeated headers. Glyphs, paragraph fills, pictures, carets and hit targets share the resulting writing area. Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
the clauses above and the MS-OI29500 [table-measurement notes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/d9b4a6f6-8b07-43c5-87f2-34c1238911a4).

declarations or the source table grid. Margin edits can wrap text and increase
page count; undo restores the original geometry and selected text. Row insertion,
splitting and merged-owner promotion retain edited margins.

## Border raster coverage

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.1.24 (`pBdr`), 17.4.66 (`tcBorders`), 17.18.2
(`ST_Border`) and the `CT_Border` size/color attributes define the existing
paragraph/cell border declarations. Review of the cached official fifth-edition
text confirms line-border widths use eighths of a point. This correction changes
raster coverage only; it does not reinterpret declarations, border conflicts,
layout widths, source colors, dash periods, pagination or serialization.

The shared painter previously clipped every border fill through its own outline.
Native Canvas antialiasing then multiplied edge coverage, making thin strokes
lighter and sometimes nearly invisible at fractional positions. Straight bands
now fill their bounded rectangles directly. Paragraph corner polygons and exact
cell-row bounds intersect the ink geometry before a single fill. Double/triple
bands and dash fragments use the same path. Complete dots avoid redundant
clipping; partial dots crossing actual corner/end/cell boundaries retain native
curve clipping. This is original geometry code, without a third-party engine.

`tools/canvas_border_coverage_fixture.py` independently authors
`public/fixtures/border-coverage.docx` with standard-library OPC/XML. It combines
quarter/half-point strokes, unequal paragraph corners, all supported line
patterns, fractional page/paragraph coordinates and an exact-height row. Unit
coverage checks intersection areas, scaling, winding direction, circle tangency,
imported widths/patterns, border/text edits, export/reopen and full undo. Browser
pixel regressions compare against directly painted primitives across fractional
origins, horizontal/vertical strokes and zooms; they also check corner/cell crops,
multiple bands and whole dots. The independent export verifier checks unchanged
border declarations and table geometry after editing text.

The second local birthday card's blue cell borders now use one coverage pass.
Its regression also copies original mixed-case source text beneath uppercase
display formatting, pastes into an email placeholder and reopens the export.
Clipboard interchange remains plain text. Book Antiqua is unavailable to this
browser and substitutes Noto Sans; Impact is available. The existing reference embeds Book Antiqua and Impact, and its DOCX source matches the corpus
package part-for-part. Font metrics, remaining layout differences, rich clipboard
interchange and exact reference rasterization equivalence remain open. No font binary
was copied, installed or redistributed.

Validation: 2,828 unit tests and 258 browser tests passed, with three optional
corpus tests skipped and both reviewed cards included. Full conformance checks,
production build and the 199-package license gate passed. The fixture at normal
and enlarged zoom and the second card were visually inspected. A local Chrome
probe painting 120 strokes per batch showed comparable dotted timing (about
15 ms before/after) and slightly lower solid, double and dashed timings; this
small probe is not a general performance guarantee.

Mixed fields stay unchanged until that side is edited. No borders writes `nil`; Inherit removes direct sides. Review used the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),

`none` inheritance from the explicit empty `nil` side, and replaced double painting of shared
edges. Source theme provenance survives unrelated edits; authored sides use flat
RGB/automatic values. Supported patterns are symmetric, so the retained frame
flag does not change their appearance. Nonzero active border offsets and shadows
reject rather than silently losing their geometry.

The prior null-coalescing implementation incorrectly let transparent cell-style declarations fall back to the table fill; this is corrected. |
| `nil` compatibility | §17.18.78; [MS-OI29500 §2.1.550, 2017 edition](https://officeprotocoldoc.z19.web.core.windows.net/files/MS-OI29500/%5BMS-OI29500%5D-170919.pdf) | Follow the documented MS-OI29500 table/cell behavior: `nil` is equivalent to an absent shading declaration and permits inheritance. | Painting and geometry | §§17.4.32, 17.4.17 `gridSpan`, 17.4.84 `vMerge`, 17.4.59 `tblHeader`; existing canvas layer policy | Fill cell backgrounds before paragraph fills, table borders, run backgrounds, selections and glyphs. Vertically merged fills retain restart-cell padding at each page fragment as described in the merged-shading follow-up below. Automatic text/decorations use the visible fill. Shading does not change widths, wrapping, row heights, page assignments, carets or selection geometry. Repeated headers and continued/empty page fragments reuse the effective fill. |
| Editing and preservation | §A.1 `CT_TcPr` child order; existing transaction and OPC contracts | Accessible Cell shading dialog reports mixed selections and authors RGB, No fill, Automatic foreground or Inherit. An unchanged mixed dialog is a no-op. A vertical merged-cell edit updates every physical member; splitting or deleting its owner row retains the edited color. Horizontal merges use their surviving owner's properties. Undo/redo restores formatting and selection. Serialize only edited cell `shd` elements in schema order, preserving other properties and unrelated package parts. No-edit/full undo preserves the original ZIP entries byte for byte. |

## Table-cell vertical-alignment iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cell alignment | ECMA-376 Part 1 fifth edition §17.4.83 `vAlign`, §17.18.101 `ST_VerticalJc`, §A.1 `CT_VerticalJc`; Part 4 §A.2 | Import `top`, `center` and `bottom`. The page-only `both` value resets a cell to top as §17.18.101 requires; preserve its source spelling until the property is edited. Require `val` and reject unknown values, duplicate elements, nested/text content and unknown WordprocessingML attributes before editable open. The authoring API/UI accepts only top/center/bottom. |
| Inheritance and removal | §§17.7.2, 17.7.6 table styles; §17.4.70 cell properties | Resolve ordinary table-style based-on chains followed by direct cell declarations, falling back to top. A direct top declaration overrides inherited center/bottom. Inherit removes the direct declaration and restores the table-style value, including through repeated edits and reopen. Table-style editing and conditional regions remain outside the current editor subset. |
| Available height | §§17.4.68 `tcMar`, 17.4.80 `trHeight`, 17.18.101; original geometry policy | First allocate row heights, merged-cell rectangles and text page assignments. Then translate all lines/baselines in each cell fragment by half or all of its remaining vertical space. Respect unequal top/bottom cell margins, paragraph before/after spacing and paragraph-border extents. Do not change row heights, line heights, wrapping, horizontal alignment, AutoFit widths, source offsets or page assignments solely for vertical alignment. |
| Merges and continued cells | §§17.4.17 `gridSpan`, 17.4.84 `vMerge`, 17.4.59 `tblHeader`; declared preview policy | A merged owner aligns all its paragraphs within the combined rectangle. Repeated headers reuse the aligned source geometry. On continued cells, align the text already assigned to each physical page fragment; keep blank continuation fragments blank. Bottom alignment does not move short content to a later page merely because its cell continues there. This page-fragment policy is not a claim of exact reference pagination or cross-page positioning. |
| Painting and navigation | Existing layout/painting/source-offset contracts | Glyphs, pictures, paragraph fills/borders, selections and carets share the shifted lines. Image and text hit testing use the same moved geometry. Repeated headers retain one editable source; cell padding remains clickable through the existing owner mapping. Empty cells retain an aligned paragraph-mark insertion line. |
| Editing and preservation | §A.1 `tcPr` child ordering; existing model and OPC contracts | Accessible Cell alignment controls report mixed selected cells and allow Top, Center, Bottom or Inherit. Apply only to cells represented by selected paragraphs; non-cell paragraphs are unaffected. Selection, text and alignment participate in atomic undo/redo. Row insertion, cell splitting and merged-owner promotion preserve the relevant cell properties. Save only edited `vAlign` declarations in schema order; retain unrelated cell/paragraph data, continuation shells and package parts. No-edit/full undo preserves original ZIP entry bytes. |

Specification review used the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/)
and the fifth-edition clauses above, alongside [the MS-OI29500 cell alignment note](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/d42f12d5-178c-4a6f-8107-e15b5b27bce8).
The latter restricts the values to top/center/bottom; the importer additionally
follows ECMA's explicit top fallback for the page-only `both` token. The review
corrected an initial rejection of that token and closed the former silent
fallback for malformed or missing `val` attributes.

## Paragraph-border iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Declarations and patterns | ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.1.24 `pBdr`, 17.3.4 `CT_Border`, 17.18.2 `ST_Border`; Part 4 §A.2 | Read top/left/bottom/right/between sides with `single`, `double`, `triple`, `dotted`, `dashed`, `dashSmallGap`, `dotDash`, `dotDotDash`, `none` and `nil`. Reject other active styles, shadows, duplicate sides/containers, nested content, unknown WordprocessingML attributes and malformed values before editable open. Retain and ignore legacy `bar` ink as §17.3.1.4 permits. Frame reversal has no visible effect on these symmetric patterns; the asymmetric compound style and its frame behavior are documented below. |
| Width, distance and color | §§17.3.4, 17.18.23 `ST_EighthPointMeasure`, 17.18.68 `ST_PointMeasure`; MS-OI29500 notes linked below | Store width in eighths of a point; accept 2–96, plus zero (no ink except for the compound style below). Clamp positive imported widths outside that range as CT_Border permits, preserving source XML. Omitted size/distance/color use the native reference's 0/0/auto defaults. The authoring distance subset is whole points 0–31. Resolve RGB/automatic/theme colors with the existing color mapper and tint-over-shade policy. Retain unedited theme attributes; editing a side writes an explicit RGB/auto replacement. |
| Inheritance and reset | §§17.3.1.5, 17.3.1.7, 17.3.1.17, 17.3.1.28, 17.3.1.42; §17.7.2 | Resolve document defaults, ordinary table-style properties, paragraph-style chains and direct formatting per side. A present side replaces that side's entire declaration, including omitted attributes. Missing sides inherit. Explicit `none`/`nil` suppress inherited ink. Style editing can remove one side or the whole set to inherit again; later style edits preserve direct overrides. Unsupported unused styles remain preserved but unavailable for application. |
| Adjacent paragraphs | §§17.3.1.5 `between`, 17.3.1.7 `bottom`, 17.3.1.42 `top` | Compare every resolved side, including theme provenance, frame/shadow flags and distance. Identical sets join within a page and cell. A differing side, an intervening paragraph or a cell boundary interrupts the group. Draw top/bottom around each physical group and optional `between` at the preceding paragraph's allocated after-spacing. Honor the divider's distance on both sides as a documented reference divergence from §17.3.1.5; see the native paragraph-between-distance controls below. Missing `between` leaves the group without a divider. Different indents connect corresponding side edges with horizontal steps. |
| Layout and fills | §§17.3.1.12 `ind`, 17.3.1.31 `shd`, 17.3.1.33 `spacing`; original preview policy | Borders surround the available paragraph width, including hanging indents and outdented list labels. Reserve top/bottom ink and distance in pagination, keeps, widow calculations and table/header height checks. Borders do not change shaped text advances or horizontal caret positions. Reject borders outside the page/cell width; failed edits roll back. Extend paragraph fills to the inside edges of the physical border group. Automatic border color contrasts with the underlying page/cell. |
| Painting and continuation | Existing canvas, table and source-offset contracts; original pattern geometry | Paint paragraph borders after paragraph fills and table borders, before run backgrounds/selection/text. Clip corners to their joined edge polygons. Double/triple patterns divide the declared total thickness into equal ink/gap bands; dashed ratios are 3:2, short dashed 3:1, dot-dash 3:1:1:1 and dot-dot-dash 3:1:1:1:1:1. Dots have diameter equal to thickness and a two-thickness period. These are preview dimensions, not specified reference pixel geometry. Frame each page fragment, repeat header borders, and omit virtual trailing page-break caret lines. |
| Editing and serialization | §A.1 property/side ordering; existing preservation contract | Accessible direct and paragraph-style controls expose each side, width, distance and color, with Box/All/Bottom/None presets. Mixed values remain unchanged until edited; clearing mixed sides requires no disabled input. Undo/redo and paragraph split/merge retain formatting. No-edit/full undo preserves all source ZIP entries byte for byte; direct border edits touch only document.xml and retain other sides and unrelated package parts. |

Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
Part 1 fifth edition clauses above and transitional schemas. Published implementation references:
[adjacent border groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.betweenborder?view=openxml-3.0.1),
[omitted-attribute defaults](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/c2a35f23-1270-4ca6-9914-0fa440d56fdf),

## Flat paragraph-shading iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paragraph background | ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.31 `shd`, §17.3.5 `CT_Shd`, §17.18.78 `ST_Shd` | Import flat `clear` background fills and `solid` foreground fills. Support six-digit RGB, `auto`, theme colors/mappings and the existing HSL tint/shade resolver for both channels. Omitted channels mean `auto`; `clear` exposes the page/cell background; automatic `solid` paints black, as established by the later native percentage-shading reference. Percentage patterns resolve to native blended RGB and `nil` preserves inheritance (see below). Require the pattern attribute; reject unsupported hatch patterns, duplicate, nested or malformed active declarations before editable open, even if run highlighting would cover them. |
| Inheritance and reset | §§17.3.1.31, 17.7.2 style hierarchy | A shading element replaces the entire preceding declaration. Resolve document defaults, ordinary table-style paragraph properties, paragraph `basedOn` chains and direct `pPr` in order. An explicit `clear` with automatic/omitted fill suppresses an inherited fill. Named paragraph-style editing can set a fill, explicitly suppress it, or remove the declaration to inherit again. Direct paragraph overrides survive style edits. Unsupported unused style definitions remain preserved and unavailable for application. |
| Theme interpretation | §17.3.5; [Open XML SDK shading documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.shading); MS-OI29500 notes for §17.3.1.31 referring to §17.4.32(a,d) | Theme channels supersede RGB fallbacks. Follow the existing tint-over-shade policy if both are present. In the absence of `themeFill`, use `fill`, following the MS-OI29500 correction to the background-channel wording. Unrelated edits retain source theme attributes; authoring a new flat fill replaces its source pattern/theme channels explicitly. |
| Physical fill bounds | §§17.3.1.12 `ind`, 17.3.1.31 `shd`, 17.3.1.33 `spacing`; native reference spacing controls | Use the paragraph writing width, from the left indent (including a hanging first line or outdented list label) through the right indent. Positive first-line indents and center/right alignment do not shorten the band. Cover measured line boxes, including empty paragraphs. Isolated fills exclude surrounding spacing. Adjacent shaded paragraphs with equal horizontal bounds share only the allocated collapsed gap: the preceding fill owns its after-spacing and the following fill owns the remainder. Contextual spacing, page/column boundaries and cell clipping apply. Different horizontal bounds interrupt the shared gap. Border-frame bounds remain independent. See the 64 native pages in `tests/fixtures/shading-spacing/`; this establishes the tested reference behavior, not universal pixel identity. |
| Pagination and tables | Existing pagination, cell and repeated-header contracts | Shading does not participate in text measurement, wrapping, keep/widow constraints, AutoFit, caret or selection geometry. Split bands at page boundaries; virtual trailing page-break caret lines have no fill. Group each placed paragraph fragment so glyphs/decorations between its lines use the same background. Repeated table headers reuse the source fill at their placed coordinates; cell backgrounds remain visible in margins and through explicit no-fill paragraphs. |
| Paint order and contrast | §§17.3.2.6 `color`, 17.3.2.15 `highlight`, 17.3.2.32 run `shd`; original canvas policy | Paint page/cell fills, paragraph fills, table borders, run backgrounds, selection and glyphs/decorations in order. Run highlights retain precedence over run shading. Automatic foreground and automatic solid run shading use the paragraph fill underneath. Separate inside/outside clips keep automatic colors responsive to the underlying page/cell when ink extends beyond its paragraph band. Exact line-height clipping remains active. |
| Editing and preservation | §A.1 property order; existing model and OPC contracts | Accessible Paragraph shading controls author RGB fills, No fill and Automatic foreground for the selected paragraphs. The paragraph-style editor supports RGB/automatic/reset/inherit declarations. Undo/redo restores formatting and selections; paragraph splitting/merging retains paragraph formatting. No-edit and full undo exports preserve original ZIP entry bytes. Direct fill changes touch only the main document part; shared-style edits may rebuild affected paragraphs but retain unrelated parts. |

## Bookmark and internal-link iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paired range markers | ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.13.6.1 `bookmarkEnd`, 17.13.6.2 `bookmarkStart`, 17.18.10 `ST_DecimalNumber` | Preserve paired zero-width markers in main-story paragraphs, table-cell paragraphs and supported hyperlink wrappers. Support points, nested/overlapping ranges and ranges spanning paragraphs or tables. Match integer IDs by numeric value using arbitrary-precision integers, preserving their source spelling on export. Require one start followed by one end per ID. Reject unmatched, reversed, duplicate-ID or malformed markers before editable open. Marker offsets are separate from text and run formatting. |
| Names and duplicates | §17.13.6.2 `name`, §22.9.2.13 `ST_String`; [MS-OI29500 §2.1.356](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/da8b8f59-2af1-49d9-8553-f0c1ff2fb18d) | Import and retain arbitrary XML-valid names, including hidden underscore names, Unicode, spaces and empty strings. Resolve duplicate names to the first start in document order, following ECMA's rule; preserve subsequent markers. The native reference instead uses the last duplicate, a documented interoperability difference. New/renamed names use a declared ASCII authoring subset: 1–40 letters/digits/underscores, first character a letter or underscore, unique exact name. This UI subset does not restrict existing names. |
| Marker attributes and containers | §§17.13.6.1–2, 17.18.13 `ST_DisplacedByCustomXml` | Paired column hints outside tables are retained and ignored as specified. Within tables, collapsed markers in the same paragraph are accepted as point bookmarks with their column attributes preserved, matching the native reference. Validate this after pairing endpoints, not while reading the start alone. Noncollapsed column ranges use the active-column model below; incomplete or noninteger pairs remain guarded. Retain valid next/prev displacement hints; they have no effect because block custom-XML structures are not editable in this engine. Reject invalid hints, marker child content and unknown attributes. Body/cell/control block boundaries and direct table/row boundaries have the additional supported subsets below. |
| Internal destinations | §17.16.22 `hyperlink`, `anchor`, `r:id` | With no `r:id`, an anchor names a bookmark in the current document. Preserve explicit empty strings separately from omitted anchors. A missing bookmark or omitted anchor leads to the document start. `r:id` retains precedence over an accompanying anchor. Creating/editing internal links writes `w:anchor` without adding an external relationship. Switching between destination types retains character formatting and wrapper attributes. Nonempty `docLocation` remains unsupported. |
| Bookmark editing | Original editor policy over §§17.13.6.1–2 | Accessible Bookmarks controls add a point/range from the current selection, rename, remove or navigate. Rename updates internal links to the active named bookmark while leaving ignored anchors on external links unchanged. Removing a bookmark retains links, which then follow missing-target fallback (or the next duplicate). Undo/redo restores markers, names, references, source text and selections atomically. |
| Text edit tracking | Original editor policy | Interior insertion expands ranges; insertion at a range start/end stays outside. Point bookmarks move together after insertion at their position. Replacement retains a bookmark around replacement content; deletion collapses retained text bookmarks instead of orphaning an endpoint. Paragraph splitting/merging redistributes markers by source offsets. Native composition uses the same model and remains separately undoable. Source markers inside a grapheme retain their exact saved offset; navigation follows the existing caret policy by rounding forward to a complete grapheme. |
| Structural table edits | Original editor policy | New rows/columns and split cells do not clone bookmark IDs. Markers follow surviving paragraph content through merges/reordering. When cell movement makes originally bookmarked content discontiguous, retain the smallest contiguous range enclosing its surviving segments. Deletion trims ranges to surviving segments and removes bookmarks whose entire content/point paragraph disappears. Insertion between surviving endpoints is included by the retained range. Table structure and ordinary text offsets remain unchanged by bookmark metadata. |
| Layout and navigation | §§17.13.6.1–2, 17.16.22; existing layout/caret policy | Markers have no width or ink and do not change shaping, wrapping, AutoFit, selection rectangles or pagination. The manager shows target pages. Ctrl/Cmd+click and the link dialog navigate to the target's first editable occurrence, including targets/links in repeated headers. Internal navigation never invokes an external browser window. Existing styles, direct formatting and linked pictures use the same rendering paths. |
| Serialization and preservation | Existing package-part policy | Untouched/full-undo exports preserve every original ZIP entry byte. Rebuild changed paragraphs as ordered marker/run events, keeping markers within a contiguous hyperlink where applicable; serialization-only run splits do not affect layout. Preserve source marker XML/attributes, run properties, unused relationships and unrelated package parts. Validate paired ranges again before export. |

Milestone validation: 2,043 unit tests in 176 files, 113 browser scenarios,
66 independent export checks and 449 schema part checks pass, along with the
production build and license audit.

Sources: the official [ECMA-376 downloads](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
Part 1 fifth edition clauses above; [Open XML bookmark reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.bookmarkstart?view=openxml-3.0.1);
the linked MS-OI29500 implementation notes and [MS-DOC bookmark-name guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/openspecs/office_file_formats/ms-doc/a65c98b7-8ca6-4220-9850-51703696f3ee).

The later collapsed-column controls in `tests/fixtures/column-bookmarks` cover
cell-block and inline points with preserved `colFirst`/`colLast`, alongside
active single/multiple-column, single-cell and merged-cell ranges. The native reference
reports Column=false for collapsed points and keeps that behavior
after reopening a browser-edited package. Point validation therefore occurs
after both markers are read. Native selection shows why active column ranges
cannot use ordinary linear selection. The local Part 1 §17.13.6.2 defines
column attributes and their placement/ignored-value rules; collapsed-point
handling is native compatibility, not a claimed normative contradiction.

The twelve additional `merge-control.docx` native controls establish that the
first bookmarked row matters when resolving horizontal merges: a first-row
merged cell selected by `0..0` includes both underlying columns in later rows,
whereas a later merged cell does not expand selections in other rows. Starting
after or on a merged row changes the selected region accordingly. Inline and
table-level endpoints are also recorded. The hash-bound reference selection
references and source configuration checks are in
`tests/column-bookmarks-merged-native.test.js`. See the fixture README for the
complete observations and remaining geometry cases. This is evidence for
active-column support, implemented in the later iteration below.

### Active table-column bookmarks

Part 1 §17.13.6.2 `colFirst`/`colLast` now has a distinct column-range model.
The original marker interval remains available for XML pairing, while covered
cell IDs, paragraph ranges and the first navigation target are resolved
separately. Physical indices in the first bookmarked row determine grid spans;
later intersecting cells are included. Vertical owners are included once, and
owners starting before the first bookmarked row are excluded. Nested cell
content, omitted leading grid cells and unequal widths have independent native
controls. Collapsed points retain their existing semantics. Navigation places
the caret in the first covered cell, consistent with ordinary bookmark
navigation; it does not turn the enclosing linear interval into a selection.

Text edits retain source markers and column hints. Row/column insertion and
deletion, horizontal/vertical merges and splits update structural endpoints and
physical indices separately from ordinary text ranges. Insertions within the
covered region, including its trailing structural edge, extend that region;
deletions trim it and remove a bookmark when its whole row/column region or
table disappears. A merged first-row cell may expand the representable region
to its complete span. These are explicit editor mutation policies over the
OOXML range model. Rebuilt column hints preserve their original numeric spelling
when their value is unchanged. No-edit and full-undo ZIP preservation remain in
force. The source does not require a document-name or hidden-bookmark exception.

**Reference/spec divergence:** printed pages 911–913 require ignoring both hints for
reversed/out-of-range indices and applying the bookmark to the whole table.
The native reference instead clips an oversized last physical index, lowers a reversed
first index to the last, and retains an empty column selection when the first
index is beyond all physical cells. Negative indices disable column semantics.
`limits-control.docx`, generated independently by
`tools/column_bookmark_limits_fixture.py`, proves these cases. For example,
`Reversed` (`2..1`) selects only column two, not the entire three-column table.
The engine implements the recorded native reference behavior. Source/PDF hashes and complete
selected-cell records are in `limits-native-ranges.json`. The recorder uses
indexed COM access: enumerating Selection.Cells after an empty selection can
return stale cells despite Count=0.

`geometry-control.docx` and its native records cover six additional geometry
cases. `column-bookmarks-geometry.test.js` binds both new sources to the native reference's
PDFs and compares covered content and cell counts. Active-column unit and
browser tests cover text/structure mutations, navigation, export/reopen,
unrelated-part preservation and exact undo. The earlier general guard against
all active column bookmarks is removed.

Remaining gaps: authoring or visually selecting a new column bookmark, markers outside supported paragraph/
hyperlink containers, other document stories, fields/REF/PAGEREF updates, custom-XML
range displacement, visible bookmark brackets and native DOM anchor semantics.
New-name validation is a deliberate subset, not the complete reference binary naming
algorithm. Duplicate-name resolution follows ECMA rather than the native reference's last-wins
behavior. Schema validity does not prove full OOXML/OPC or reference layout equivalence.

## External-hyperlink iteration

The later bookmark iteration above supersedes this iteration's bookmark-only
import gate and adds an internal destination mode to its link dialog.

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Link structure | ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.16.22 `hyperlink`, 15.3 Hyperlinks, 22.8.2.1 `ST_RelationshipId`; Part 4 transitional namespaces | Read direct paragraph/cell `w:hyperlink` wrappers containing supported `w:r` text, tabs, line/page breaks and inline pictures. Keep link identity outside character formatting. Preserve distinct adjacent wrappers even when they share a target. Nested links, fields, revisions, bookmarks, content controls, empty wrappers and unknown wrapper attributes reject before attaching a save handler. Proofing hints follow the existing paragraph preservation policy. |
| External relationships | §§15.3, 17.16.22 `r:id`; ECMA-376 Part 2 relationship mechanism | Require one matching document relationship of transitional `/hyperlink` type with `TargetMode="External"`. Supported destinations are absolute HTTP(S), mailto and tel addresses; retain spelling, percent escapes, query and fragment. Reject missing/duplicate/wrong-type relations, package-internal targets, relative addresses, other schemes, whitespace, backslashes, invalid escapes and lone surrogates. Do not fetch destinations on import or export. Reuse matching relationships, append new IDs for changed targets, and preserve unused/source relationships. Image/style and hyperlink relationship writers compose without overwriting each other's additions. |
| Wrapper attributes | §17.16.22 `anchor`, `docLocation`, `history`, `tgtFrame`, `tooltip`; §22.9.2.7 `ST_OnOff` | With `r:id`, retain and ignore `anchor` as specified. Retain `tgtFrame`; the editor has no HTML frameset and opens explicitly invoked links in a new context. Display tooltip on hover, falling back to the target. Validate history's on/off lexical values and record invoked history-enabled targets for the current editor session. Nonempty `docLocation` and bookmark-only links reject. Do not synthesize fragments from either attribute. |
| Editing | Original editor policy, with §17.16.22 wrappers on export | Ctrl/Cmd+K and an accessible toolbar dialog insert a link around selected text or insert text at an empty caret. At a caret in or immediately after a link, edit/remove the entire contiguous wrapper; range actions affect only the selection. Keep source text and run formatting intact when linking/unlinking. Typing strictly inside a link extends it; ordinary edge typing is unlinked. Replacing text wholly inside one wrapper retains the link; crossing its boundary clears the replacement's link. Paragraph splits retain existing linked prefixes/suffixes, while newly inserted multiline text is unlinked. Undo/redo restores text, links, selections and formatting together. |
| Grapheme boundaries | Original caret policy; §17.16.22 supported subset | Link boundaries must coincide with editable grapheme boundaries. Reject imported wrappers that divide one combining sequence or joined emoji between different links/plain text; differently formatted runs within one wrapper may divide a cluster. During text edits, a newly joined cluster follows the link of its first character, so a combining mark typed after a linked base stays with that base. Preserve original UTF-16 source text and grapheme caret stops. |
| Rendering and interaction | §17.16.22; existing §17.7 style cascade | Hyperlinks do not imply blue or underlined text: render their existing character styles/direct formatting. Newly created links preserve selected/insertion formatting. Link metadata never splits shaping groups or changes intrinsic widths, wrapping, AutoFit, line metrics or pagination. Hit detection uses source caret/selection geometry, including wrapped lines, linked pictures and repeated table headers at zoom. Ordinary pointer selection remains available; Ctrl/Cmd+click and the link popover's Open link button explicitly open the target with `noopener,noreferrer`. |
| Preservation | Existing package-part policy | Untouched/full-undo exports preserve all original ZIP entry bytes. Edited paragraphs reconstruct hyperlink wrappers around their runs, retain wrapper attributes and source rPr declarations, and keep shared relationships unchanged when another wrapper changes target. Normalize relationship namespace bindings across assembled fragments. Unrelated package parts, styles, images and unused relationships remain intact. |

save/reopen. `check:conformance` independently checks `hyperlinks.docx` and

## Underline-pattern iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Patterns | ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.2.40 `u`, 17.18.99 `ST_Underline` | Support all 18 enum values: none, single, words, double, thick, dotted/dottedHeavy, dash/dashedHeavy, dashLong/dashLongHeavy, dotDash/dashDotHeavy, dotDotDash/dashDotDotHeavy, wave/wavyHeavy/wavyDouble. Reject unknown values (including literal `auto`), duplicate elements, nested content and unknown WordprocessingML attributes before editable open. |
| Attribute inheritance | §17.3.2.40; MS-OI29500 §2.1.99(a,c), also [MS-OE376 §2.1.101](https://learn.microsoft.com/id-id/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oe376/70728747-cf2d-4393-afb3-f5117faa27d5) | Omitted pattern and color inherit independently. Final defaults are no underline and automatic color, following the MS-OI29500 implementation notes. Correct the former assumption that a present `u` without `val` always meant single. Part 1's prose refers to a fallback `auto`, which is absent from ST_Underline; the documented reference fallback resolves that ambiguity. Underline is an ordinary value, not a §17.7.3 toggle. Cover defaults, unconditional table styles, paragraph/character styles, direct runs, marks and numbering levels. |
| Words only | §17.18.99 `words`; §17.15.3.8 `ulTrailSpace` | Underline non-space graphemes, including punctuation. Skip breaking/nonbreaking Unicode White_Space characters and tabs, including a combining sequence whose base is a space. Numbering labels use the same rule without gaining editable offsets. All other patterns cover internal spaces and tab gaps. Trailing ordinary spaces remain governed by `ulTrailSpace`; words-only skips them in either setting. |
| Stroke geometry | §17.18.99 shape definitions; [OpenType post metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/post) for the bundled Noto fonts | Use the existing post top-edge position −100 and thickness 50 at 1000 units/em; let `t` be thickness after script/baseline transforms. Double uses two `t` strokes separated by `t`; heavy uses `2t`. Dotted periods use ink/gap units [1,2], dashed [4,2], long dashed [8,3], dash-dot [4,2,1,2], dash-dot-dot [4,2,1,2,1,2], multiplied by stroke thickness. Waves have period `8t`, amplitude `t`, cubic control displacement `4t/3`, and double-wave separation `3t`. These dimensions are original preview choices; OOXML names the shapes without prescribing those numbers. |
| Layout and painting | Existing source-offset, typography, table and pagination contracts | Decoration changes do not split shaped text or alter advances, line metrics, wrapping, AutoFit widths, carets, selection or pagination. Continue dash/wave phase through color-only boundaries; restart at a new line, pattern/metric change or word gap. Clip partial periods to the span, hanging tails to the writing edge, and exact-height lines to their existing clip. Numbering, continued tables and repeated headers share the painter. Preserve properties on inline pictures without drawing on the bitmap. |
| Editing and persistence | §§17.3.2.28, 17.3.1.29, 17.9.24; Part 4 §A.2 | The existing toggle/native formatting shortcut clears any active pattern or enables single with automatic color. Accessible Underline options chooses any pattern and automatic/RGB color; mixed selections and future typing work. Named-style pattern and color can be changed or inherited independently. The legacy boolean style API retains its single/none plus automatic-color behavior. Pattern-only and color-only edits retain inheritance of the other attribute, including after reopening and later style changes; partial imported declarations stay intact for unrelated edits. No-edit/full undo preserve every source ZIP entry. |

Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
its underline and enum clauses, and the MS-OI29500 implementation notes linked above.
The original `tools/canvas_underline_fixture.py` uses python-docx (MIT) to generate
`public/fixtures/underlines.docx` via
`tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-underline-fixture`. It covers every pattern,
partial attributes, paragraph/character/table inheritance, explicit none, Unicode
spaces, color boundaries, scripts, width/spacing/position combinations, trailing
spaces, marks, numbering, AutoFit and repeated headers. Independent verification
checks changed declarations, unchanged source text/XML and unrelated package parts.
Unit regressions cover inheritance, exact undo, geometry, input, invalid values
and generated numbering. Browser checks compare actual rectangle and curve paint
calls with laid-out spans, operate keyboard controls, edit shared attributes and
save/reopen imported and freshly authored documents. Existing style-browser
regressions now select the explicit single enum instead of the former boolean UI.
No dependency, font asset or third-party implementation was added.

**Remaining gaps:** there is no reference pixel comparison for dash pitch, dot shape,
wave geometry, double gaps or underline positioning. Dots use rectangular ink;
patterns do not perform glyph-contour/descender avoidance. Decorations do not
increase line height and exact-height clipping can trim a low wave. Linguistic word
boundaries and Unicode case expansion do not change the space-based words-only
rule. Existing text-color/theme, font fallback, RTL/complex-script and layout
limitations still apply. Default/table-style/numbering patterns can be imported
and serialized but have no dedicated UI. Schema validity is not full OOXML or
reference rendering equivalence.

## Capitalization iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Display-only capitals | ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.2.5 `caps`, 17.3.2.33 `smallCaps`; §17.17.4 common booleans | Preserve original text and UTF-16 source positions. All caps displays uppercase letter equivalents. Small caps follows measured reference behavior: lowercase letters display uppercase at 80% of the stored size, rounded to the nearest half point with a one-point floor. This intentionally differs from the clause’s fixed two-point reduction. Uppercase letters, numbers and punctuation retain the stored size. Accept absent `val` as true and all six standard lexical booleans; reject malformed, duplicate, nested or unknown WordprocessingML attributes. Reject both properties in the same active property set, including false combinations. |
| Inheritance | §§17.7.2–17.7.3 and the existing MS-OI29500 toggle compatibility interpretation below | Both properties are toggles. Resolve the nearest declaration of each form in a same-type style chain; table and paragraph declarations reset, character declarations toggle relative to document defaults, direct declarations are absolute. Explicit false clears only its form. Later competing positive declarations choose one form; this cross-form precedence is a declared inference, without reference comparison. Cover defaults, unconditional table styles, paragraph/character styles, marks, direct runs and numbering. |
| Editing and serialization | §§17.3.1.29, 17.3.2.28, 17.9.24; Part 4 §A.2 ordered run properties | Accessible All caps/Small caps icon buttons switch modes or clear them, preserve selections, support mixed selections, future typing and undo/redo. Shared-style controls retain four distinct on/off declarations and Inherit. Direct clearing emits false for the inherited form, or caps false if neither is inherited. Switching removes the competing source property. No-edit/full undo preserve every original ZIP entry; other edits preserve unrelated XML and parts. Invalid unused styles remain intact but cannot be exposed by editing. |
| Text geometry | §§17.3.2.19 `kern`, 17.3.2.38 `sz`; existing source-offset/layout contracts | Build display spans without changing run text. Adjacent equal-size spans shape together, including color-only run boundaries. The kerning threshold compares stored `sz` before reducing small-cap display size. Measure each displayed span with the bundled font and paint those same spans; then apply script, baseline and width transforms. Spacing remains an absolute distance. Underline and strike metrics use the original run size; small-cap letters do not shrink those decorations. Widths feed wrapping, aligned tabs, caret/selection, AutoFit and pagination, including repeated table headers. Uppercase expansions such as ß→SS share one source grapheme selection interval. Inline pictures retain the property without transforming the bitmap. |

Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/)
and the Open XML SDK [small-caps clause reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.smallcaps?view=openxml-3.0.1).
The preview uses locale-neutral [ECMAScript uppercase mapping](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/text-processing.html#sec-string.prototype.touppercase)
on Unicode lowercase/titlecase letters, preserving other code points. Small-cap
size changes keep a combining sequence with its base letter. It does not use the
browser's synthetic CSS small-caps proportions or OpenType `smcp` alternates.

`public/fixtures/capitalization.docx` is independently generated using python-docx
(MIT), `tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-caps-fixture`, and the original
`tools/canvas_caps_fixture.py`. It covers direct/paragraph/character/table modes,
explicit false, competing forms, Unicode, color boundaries, script combinations,
kerning thresholds, tabs, empty marks, numbering, AutoFit and repeated headers.
Unit regressions cover source offsets, style/default inheritance, editing,
round trips, exact undo, rejection and transformed intrinsic widths. Browser
regressions compare actual canvas text, fonts and kerning with native reference
measurement, operate accessible controls, inspect selections and save/reopen
imported and fresh documents. Independent export checks inspect source text,
mutually exclusive declarations, styles, unrelated XML and package parts.
No dependency or font asset was added; the two toolbar outlines are original.

**Remaining gaps:** no language-sensitive casing (for example Turkish dotted I),
full contextual Unicode casing, font-native small-cap alternates or native reference layout
comparison. Other-lowercase symbols and alphabetic combining marks outside Unicode
letter categories retain their source form. The one-point floor and original-size
decoration placement are preview policies. Competing inherited forms use the
explicit precedence above, and the strict same-property-set gate can reject files
some consumers tolerate. Nonzero character spacing combined with an expanding uppercase mapping is rejected
before editing: native spacing would otherwise count displayed letters instead
of source characters (§17.3.2.35). This includes conservative rejection of mappings
that expand into combining sequences. There are no UI controls for default/table-style/numbering
capitalization. Existing RTL, complex-script, font fallback and pagination limits
still apply. Schema validity is not full OOXML or reference rendering equivalence.

## Strikethrough iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Single and double forms | ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.2.37 `strike`, 17.3.2.9 `dstrike`; §17.17.4 common booleans | Read single/double on and explicit false separately. Missing declarations inherit; absence throughout means no strikethrough. Accept missing `val` as true and `0/1/false/true/off/on`. Reject duplicate elements, malformed booleans, nested content and unknown WordprocessingML attributes. Reject both elements in the same active property set, including explicit false combinations, rather than silently choose a conflicting declaration. |
| Style inheritance | §§17.7.2–17.7.3; existing MS-OI29500 style-toggle compatibility policy recorded below | Single is a toggle; double is not in the §17.7.3 toggle list. Use the nearest declaration of each form in a same-type `basedOn` chain. Paragraph/table single declarations reset, character single declarations toggle relative to the document default, and direct declarations are absolute. Double on remains on through a child style declaring on. An off declaration affects its own form. Support document defaults, unconditional table styles, paragraph/character styles, empty marks, direct runs and numbering labels. |
| Cross-form precedence | Declared compatibility interpretation of the mutually exclusive appearance requirement | A positive declaration selects its form over the previously resolved form. Resolve nearest single/double declarations in their style-chain order, then continue through the hierarchy. This provides one visual form and supports direct switching over inherited formatting. ECMA does not explicitly prescribe competing forms across different property sets; this precedence is an inference, not verified reference behavior. |
| Editing and serialization | §§17.3.1.29, 17.3.2.28, 17.9.24; Part 4 §A.2 ordered run properties | Accessible icon buttons select single/double or clear the active form; mixed selections and future typing are supported. Native `formatStrikeThrough` input uses the same mutation/history path. Shared-style controls preserve four distinct on/off declarations and Inherit. A direct clear writes the false declaration for the inherited form, or single false when no inherited form exists. Switching removes the opposing source element; no new property set contains both. Explicit source declarations and unused invalid styles remain untouched until changed/exposed. |
| Stroke geometry and painting | [OpenType OS/2 strike metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/os2#ystrikeoutposition); declared double-line preview policy | Both bundled Noto faces have yStrikeoutPosition=322 and yStrikeoutSize=50 at 1000 units/em. Their MVAR `stro` record, after `avar` remapping, raises the position to 328.1000732198371 at bold weight 700; thickness remains 50. Position defines the top edge above the baseline; use that edge and thickness for a single stroke. For double, place two strokes symmetrically around the single stroke with one thickness of clear space between. Scale vertically for scripts, shift with manual position, retain thickness under horizontal scaling, and use text color over highlight/shading. Tabs and trailing spaces receive strokes; overflowing tails use the existing writing-edge clipping. Exact-height lines clip decorations with their text. |
| Layout and persistence | Existing source-offset, table, history and OPC preservation contracts | Decorations do not split shaping groups or change advances, caret stops, selection, AutoFit widths or pagination. Cover mixed-color runs, Unicode boundaries, tables and repeated headers; numbering labels paint strokes without editable source characters. Retain the property on inline pictures without drawing strokes over their bitmap. No-edit/full undo preserve every original package entry byte for byte. Other edits preserve unrelated XML and package parts. |

Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
primary [single-strike reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.strike?view=openxml-3.0.1)
and [double-strike reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.doublestrike?view=openxml-3.0.1),
and OpenType font metrics. Font-table values are also checked directly from both
existing font binaries, including the [MVAR variation adjustment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/mvar); source/provenance remains in `public/fonts/PROVENANCE.md`.
No dependency, external editor code or font binary was added.

The independent `public/fixtures/strikethrough.docx` is generated by python-docx
using `tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-strike-fixture` and original source
`tools/canvas_strike_fixture.py`. It covers both forms, explicit off, paragraph
and character style chains, cross-form precedence, default-off single toggles,
scripts, color/highlight/underline combinations, tabs, long space tails, empty
marks, numbering, AutoFit tables and repeated headers. Unit variants exercise
default-on toggles, rejection and exact undo. Browser checks compare expected
strokes against actual canvas paint calls, operate controls by keyboard, edit and
remove shared declarations, handle native formatting input, and save/reopen
imported and fresh text. Independent verification checks mutually exclusive
XML, expected direct/style declarations, text and unrelated source XML/parts.

**Remaining gaps:** cross-form inheritance precedence and the double-stroke
placement rule have no native reference rendering comparison. The strict
same-property-set gate also rejects documents containing both false declarations,
even though some consumers may tolerate them. There are no controls for document
defaults, table-style or numbering-level strikes; imported and generated supported
values render. Picture strikethrough is retained without a bitmap overlay. Source
font-family substitution, complex scripts and reference-exact decoration geometry
remain outside the supported subset. Schema validity is not full conformance.

## Trailing ordinary spaces iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wrapping | ECMA-376 Part 4 §14.8.3.58 `wrapTrailSpaces`; Unicode UAX #14 SP discussion, LB7/LB18 | By default, a sequence of plain U+0020 graphemes remains on the preceding line even past the writing edge; the next nonspace starts the next line. Leading/all-space lines and spaces before manual breaks remain source text. This fixes the prior fallback that placed an overflowing separator on a separate line and inflated pagination. Enabled `wrapTrailSpaces` treats spaces as ordinary wrapping characters. |
| Underlining | Part 1 §17.15.3.8 `ulTrailSpace`, §17.3.2.40 `u` | Suppress single underlines beneath trailing ordinary spaces by default, including across formatting runs. Preserve underlines under internal spaces. Enabled `ulTrailSpace` includes trailing spaces, subject to the preview's writing-edge clipping below. Both wrapping modes use the same underline rule. |
| Compatibility settings | §17.17.4 common booleans; Part 4 §A.2 `CT_Compat` | Import both flags, absent = false, missing `val` = true; accept `0/1/false/true/off/on`. Reject duplicates, malformed values, nested elements and unknown WordprocessingML attributes before editable open. Keep imported flags read-only and preserve their exact settings part. Fresh package creation can initialize flags in schema order. |
| Alignment and table demand | Part 1 §17.3.1.13 `jc`, §17.18.87 AutoFit algorithm; declared preview policy | Exclude default hanging tails from paragraph alignment and AutoFit minimum/maximum widths and indivisible-grapheme floors. Wrapped-space mode includes their width. Center/right tab fields exclude ordinary trailing spaces from their alignment width (see the native aligned-tab-tail follow-up below). Keep source font metrics, including taller trailing-space runs, for line height and pagination. |
| Carets and visible bounds | Application editing policy, not an OOXML print-layout requirement | Clip overflowing trailing caret advances, backgrounds, fragment bounds and enabled underlines at the paragraph writing edge, including table cells and repeated headers. Every source-space offset remains available to keyboard navigation. Pointer/vertical hits at collapsed tail stops choose the last offset; a selection containing only collapsed spaces receives a one-pixel strip inside the edge. Soft-wrap forward/backward affinity still distinguishes the next line from the preceding tail. |
| Source text and performance | Part 1 §17.3.3.31 `t` and `xml:space`; existing mutation/history contracts | Retain all spaces through typing, selection replacement, format/style changes, undo/redo and save/reopen. New/changed significant whitespace uses `xml:space="preserve"`; no-edit/full undo retain original package entries byte for byte. Measure visible prefixes normally; approximate only already-overflowing repeated-space advances, then measure each completed group once to remove native accumulation-rounding differences. Work remains linear in long clipped tails. |

Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
the Open XML SDK [wrapping reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.wraptrailspaces?view=openxml-3.0.1)
and [underline reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.underlinetrailingspaces?view=openxml-3.0.1),
and [Unicode UAX #14](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr14/).
This is original code; no dependency, external editor implementation or font binary was added.

The independent `public/fixtures/trailing-spaces.docx` and `wrapped-spaces.docx`
come from python-docx through `tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-spaces-fixtures`.
Original generation/verification source is `tools/canvas_spaces_fixture.py`;
this records fixture provenance. They cover explicit false/true settings, long
interstitial/leading/trailing spaces, styled underlines, italic highlighted tails,
left/center/right alignment, combining text and emoji, nonbreaking spaces, tabs,
manual lines, fixed/AutoFit tables and repeated headers. Browser acceptance edits
inherited and direct formatting, tests keyboard movement and replacement in
collapsed tails, saves/reopens imported and fresh text, and compares native Canvas
advances under kerning, scripts, width scaling and positive/negative character
spacing. Independent parsing verifies exact space counts, significant-whitespace
attributes, expected edits and unchanged package parts.

**Remaining gaps:** this iteration covers plain U+0020 graphemes only. Nonbreaking,
figure and narrow nonbreaking spaces retain the existing word treatment; a space
with a combining mark is not a hanging ordinary space. Other Unicode breaking
spaces and full UAX #14 are outside this subset. Writing-edge clipping, tail
selection display, paragraph alignment and tab-field interactions are declared
preview policies without a native reference rendering comparison. There are no
controls for changing these imported compatibility flags. Schema validity is not
full OOXML or reference layout equivalence.

## Font kerning iteration

Known native shaping gap: the independent `kerning-space-pairs.docx` native reference probe
shows that Edge Canvas omits Rockwell Bold space-leading kerning pairs even
with `fontKerning=normal`. The native reference applies the font's space–W pair, while Canvas
only applies W–o, making the centered title about 0.96pt too far left. Plain,
split-run and temporary-control cases isolate the same result. See
`tests/fixtures/kerning-space-pairs/README.md` for numerical evidence and the
retained reference. This remains unresolved; native Canvas checks alone
do not prove native reference kerning fidelity. No font-specific width adjustment is used.

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Threshold and default | ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.19 `kern`, §17.3.2.38 `sz`, §17.18.42 `ST_HpsMeasure` | Positive thresholds enable font kerning when the stored font size is at least the threshold. Missing declarations inherit; absence throughout a hierarchy with an explicit `rPrDefault` means no kerning. An absent run-default category invokes the reference application threshold described below. Compare stored size before script, width and baseline transforms. The previous preview ignored `kern` and used the browser's automatic choice; explicit modes correct that discrepancy. |
| Units and range | §22.9.2.12 `ST_PositiveUniversalMeasure`; Part 4 §A.2 transitional schemas; [MS-OE376 §2.1.84](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oe376/eca8e125-fc83-4a6d-884c-317d82698755) | Import numeric half-points and positive universal units (`mm`, `cm`, `in`, `pt`, `pc`, `pi`) with half-point precision. Support 0–3277 half-points (0–1638.5 pt), matching the MS-OE376-documented range. Explicit edits write integer half-points. Untouched lexical forms survive edits. |
| Zero compatibility policy | [MS-DOC §2.6.1 character properties, `sprmCHpsKern`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_file_formats/ms-doc/7022285b-9621-42e9-ad4d-4e02c115ef18) | Zero means off in this editor, including an explicit reset of inherited kerning. The [MS-DOC] binary format specification explicitly defines that convention. Applying it to DOCX is a compatibility inference: ECMA's `kern` prose describes a threshold without explicitly assigning zero an off meaning. This is not literal zero-threshold conformance. The independent punctuation-kerning reference controls verify the zero-off convention at 24 pt for Latin and punctuation pairs. Positive .5 pt enables kerning for every supported font size. |
| Inheritance and persistence | Part 1 §§17.7.2, 17.3.1.29, 17.9.24 | Resolve document defaults, unconditional table styles, paragraph/character styles, direct runs, empty marks and numbering labels. Thresholds replace inherited values; nearer valid declarations may mask an out-of-range ancestor. Shared edits/removal preserve direct zero. Unicode typing, split/merge, mixed selections and undo/redo retain thresholds. No-edit/full undo preserve every original package entry byte for byte. |
| Measurement and painting | [HTML Canvas text drawing styles](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#text-styles) | Set `fontKerning` to `normal` or `none` for measurement and painting, without changing the stored size. Effective kerning modes delimit shaping groups; different thresholds with the same effective mode, colors and highlights share shaping. Existing width, script and absolute character-spacing transforms compose afterwards. Inline images retain the property without changing image geometry. |
| Layout and controls | Existing source-offset, table and history contracts | Recompute advances, wrapping, AutoFit demand and pagination; caret/selection, underlines, backgrounds, aligned tabs and repeated-header hits follow those advances. Accessible Kerning dialog accepts points, zero Off and mixed selection; paragraph/character style dialogs also permit empty Inherit. Generated numbering definitions serialize their thresholds. |
| Rejection and capability checks | §A.1/Part 4 §A.2 element content; Part 1 §17.15.1.60 `noPunctuationKerning`; Part 4 §14.8.3.49 `useAnsiKerningPairs` | Reject invalid/missing threshold values, duplicates, nested content and unknown WordprocessingML attributes in active declarations. Preserve unused invalid styles; exposing them rejects atomically. Validate and preserve `noPunctuationKerning` for either Boolean value, following the native reference's measured behavior: normal run kerning remains active, including punctuation pairs. The six original punctuation-kerning controls document this divergence from §17.15.1.60. Reject enabled ANSI pair settings because the current Canvas path cannot reproduce them. Preserve explicit false ANSI settings. Reject browsers lacking Canvas font-kerning control before attaching an editor/save handler. |

Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
the primary [OOXML kerning reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.kern?view=openxml-3.0.1)
and the MS-OE376/HTML sources above. The default-off correction can change wrapping
in older preview documents; it does not rewrite absent source declarations.
No editor implementation or new dependency was used.

**Remaining gaps:** the zero-value interpretation noted above has no current
