## Contextual paragraph spacing iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Adjacent paragraph spacing | ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.9 `contextualSpacing`, §17.3.1.33 `spacing` | For adjacent paragraphs with the same effective paragraph style, subtract the first paragraph's after spacing if its flag is on, and the second paragraph's before spacing if its flag is on, from the ordinary collapsed gap. Floor at zero. The specification's 10 pt after / 12 pt before, first flag only, yields 2 pt. Stored before/after values remain unchanged. |
| Style identity and hierarchy | §§17.3.1.27 `pStyle`, 17.7.2 style hierarchy, 17.9.23 numbering `pPr` | Resolve document defaults, unconditional table styles, paragraph style chains, numbering-level properties and direct overrides. Omitted and explicit default paragraph styles match. Different style IDs remain distinct even with a common base. Direct numbering resolves after paragraph styles; style-inherited numbering resolves before them. Explicit false resets inherited true. |
| Boolean forms and validation | §17.17.4 common boolean properties; Part 4 §A.2 transitional schemas | Missing element inherits, default false; missing `val` means true. Accept `0`, `1`, `false`, `true`, `off`, `on`. Reject malformed values, duplicate elements, nested content and unknown WordprocessingML attributes in active declarations before editable open. Preserve unused unsupported styles and reject applying them atomically. |
| Table compatibility | Part 4 §14.8.3.2 `allowSpaceOfSameStyleInTable` | Normally apply contextual spacing within each owning cell. When this compatibility flag is true, ignore contextual suppression inside cells, including repeated headers and continued rows; retain stored paragraph flags. The document setting is read-only and preserved through edits/export. New package creation can initialize it in schema order. |
| Flow, pagination and source offsets | §17.3.1.9 and existing keeps, breaks and cell-flow contracts | Tables and cell boundaries interrupt paragraph adjacency. Same-paragraph line/manual-page-break segments never act as neighboring paragraphs. Kept-chain fitting uses the same contextual gaps as placement. Page advance discards the preceding after spacing; any before spacing retained at a new page is still subject to same-style suppression. Initial space-before and existing oversized-gap/manual-break compatibility rules remain. Carets, selections and repeated-header hits use the resulting line geometry. |
| Editing and persistence | Application behavior and ordered paragraph serialization | Accessible toolbar toggle supports mixed selections and keyboard use. Paragraph style dialogs expose On/Off/Inherit. Unicode typing, empty paragraphs, split/merge, shared edits and undo/redo preserve the flag. Changed properties serialize in paragraph schema order; generated numbering levels include their flag. No-edit/full undo retain every original package entry byte for byte; other edits preserve unrelated XML and parts. |

Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
Parts 1 and 4, and the primary references for
[contextual spacing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.contextualspacing?view=openxml-3.0.1)
and [table compatibility](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.allowspaceofsamestyleintable?view=openxml-3.0.1).
The review identified the subtraction rule and the table exception; simply
zeroing a flagged side before taking the maximum would fail the standard's
example. This is original implementation code, with no new dependency or binary.

The independent fixtures `public/fixtures/contextual-spacing.docx` and
`contextual-table-spacing.docx` are generated with python-docx by
`tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-contextual-fixtures`, using original source
`tools/canvas_contextual_fixture.py`. This records their source and provenance.
They exercise one-sided/both-sided flags, explicit default-style identity, distinct
child styles, false overrides, empty paragraphs, Unicode, numbering precedence,
tables spanning pages and repeated headers, with and without the compatibility
flag. Unit tests check numerical gaps, fitting, selection/hit geometry, history,
malformed inputs and package preservation. Browser tests observe actual painted
baselines, use keyboard controls, change shared declarations, and save/reopen
imported and fresh documents. Independent verification compares all source XML
except intended flag edits and equivalent text whitespace attributes, plus every
unrelated package part.

**Remaining gaps:** automatic and line-unit paragraph spacing, conditional table
style regions, paragraph borders and reference-exact pagination remain unsupported.
There are no dedicated document-default, table-style, numbering-level or
compatibility-flag editing controls. Existing editable-structure limits still
apply. Schema validity does not establish full OOXML, OPC or reference layout equivalence.

## Style-toggle interoperability correction

| Behavior | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nearest declaration | ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.7.2, 17.7.3, 17.7.4.3 | Resolve the nearest declaration within each same-type `basedOn` chain once. Absent properties retain the inherited value; direct formatting remains absolute. Keep defaults, style references and direct declarations separate. |
| Table and paragraph resets | [MS-OI29500 §2.1.246(b)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/14452bbe-be4d-4dbb-90e6-3d23ae9361bc), [§2.1.258(a)](https://learn.microsoft.com/lv-lv/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/bd62641d-7786-473f-872d-4b3205e91a82) | Follow the MS-OI29500-documented variation from the base-standard XOR rule: a declared table or paragraph toggle sets the inherited value explicitly. Thus a bold paragraph style inside a bold table stays bold, and an explicit non-bold paragraph clears table/default bold. An absent declaration keeps the previous level's value. |
| Character toggles and defaults | [MS-OI29500 §2.1.230(a–b)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/f7130225-2368-48f3-acae-a9d278d0fb25) | Character declarations equal to the document default keep the inherited value; opposite declarations reverse it. When defaults are off, character On reverses and Off keeps; when defaults are on, the effects reverse. An absent character declaration keeps the inherited value. The character-style dialog labels these effects for bold/italic while retaining the original boolean declaration values. Direct overrides still win. |
| Boolean classification and rejection | §§17.3.2.1 `b`, 17.3.2.16 `i`, 17.3.2.41 `vanish`; §§17.3.2.7 `cs`, 17.3.2.30 `rtl`, 17.3.2.44 `webHidden`; §17.7.3 toggle list | Apply toggle rules to bold, italic and hidden-text evaluation. Complex-script selection, right-to-left and web-hidden flags are ordinary absolute booleans; repeated true declarations cannot cancel them. Unsupported effective flags reject before save attachment. A later effective false remains allowed. This does not add hidden or complex-script rendering support. |
| Editing, painting and preservation | Existing history, source-offset, layout and OPC contracts | Shared edits, declaration removal, character references, empty marks, future typing, split/merge and direct toolbar toggles resolve consistently. Font changes remeasure and repaginate body/table text and repeated headers. Selection retains source offsets; caret hit testing follows new geometry. Save/reopen preserves declarations rather than flattening computed values. No-edit and complete undo keep every original ZIP entry byte for byte. |

The review used the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/)
and the MS-OI29500 notes above. It found that the prior resolver followed the base
standard's cross-level XOR and default-true rules even where MS-OI29500 documents
different behavior. It also incorrectly treated `cs`, `rtl` and `webHidden` as
toggles. These discrepancies are corrected in the shared style resolver.

Independent fixtures `public/fixtures/style-toggles-off.docx` and
`style-toggles-on.docx` are generated by
`tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-toggle-fixtures` using the original
`tools/canvas_toggle_fixture.py` helper and python-docx. They cover both document
defaults, nearest paragraph/character declarations, unconditional table styles,
direct false, Unicode, an empty styled mark, numbering and repeated headers.
The browser edits shared paragraph/character declarations and a direct override,
checks toolbar state and actual Canvas font arguments, types and undoes Unicode
text, and saves/reopens both documents. Independent verification compares all
source text and XML declarations except the three intended boolean changes, plus
unrelated package parts. Engine regressions also check declaration removal,
repagination, source selection/caret, hidden/script guards and byte-exact undo.

**Remaining gaps:** document-default editing, conditional table styles, linked
style automation, additional toggle decorations and hidden/complex-script layout
remain unsupported. This uses the documented modern reference rules; pre-2016 table
toggle bugs are not emulated. Exact reference font fallback, rasterization and page
layout are not claimed. Schema validity is not full OOXML/OPC or reference equivalence.
No external editor implementation or dependency was introduced.

| Direct highlighting | ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.15 `highlight`, §17.18.40 `ST_HighlightColor`, §A.1 `CT_Highlight` | All 16 named colors and explicit `none`, with the standard's sRGB values (including `darkBlue=00008B`, `darkGreen=006400`, `darkGray=A9A9A9`, `lightGray=D3D3D3`). The anchored Text highlight swatch palette applies to a selection, an empty paragraph mark or future typing. No highlight writes `none` and reveals the underlying background. Invalid/missing values, duplicate elements, nested content and unknown highlight attributes reject before editing. |
| Implementation-note restrictions | [MS-OI29500 §2.1.79](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/e07a90e2-76b5-47dd-8bf4-668a806177c7), referring to [§2.1.245](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/9f0ca7a0-5e6a-487e-bb52-2b74d4bb614a), [§2.1.248](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/d0244b61-fd96-45f0-ac84-7380d2b6d663), [§2.1.260](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/0f36799f-599e-449b-8d9d-cd42c9c6e41f), [§2.1.291](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/ffb4a990-b46f-4e38-8db3-96fc13d0b0f6) | Unlike the base schema, the native reference disallows highlight in document defaults, named styles, conditional table styles and numbering-level run properties. The supported subset therefore authors direct highlighting only. Active default/style/level declarations reject; unused definitions remain preserved and cannot be applied. Style-edit APIs reject highlight patches. Existing direct highlighting survives supported paragraph/character style changes. |
| Background precedence and shading | §17.3.2.32 run `shd`, §17.3.5 `CT_Shd`, §17.18.78 `ST_Shd`, §17.7.2 hierarchy | Highlight supersedes run shading. Import flat `clear` fill and `solid` foreground, including RGB, Automatic, mapped themes and HSL tint/shade. Shading declarations inherit atomically through defaults, table/paragraph/character styles and direct properties. The existing theme resolver handles `themeFill`, `themeFillTint` and `themeFillShade` independently of foreground attributes. `clear` Automatic exposes the page/cell background; `solid` Automatic chooses contrasting black/white. Patterned and `nil` run shading reject, including when a highlight would hide them. Paragraph shading is supported by the later flat paragraph-shading iteration above. |
| Geometry and paint | Existing source-offset/layout contracts; §17.3.1.33 line spacing | Background rectangles use measured source advances and the run's font/image ascent and descent. Include spaces, aligned tab gaps and inline-image reserved slots; transparent image pixels reveal the highlight. Exact line spacing clips backgrounds with text. Color/highlight boundaries share shaped text and do not change advances, AutoFit demand, caret stops, selection, line breaks or pagination. Repeated header copies share source formatting. Empty marks and undisplayed breaks have no artificial background width. |
| Foreground and selection | §17.3.2.6 automatic foreground; application selection policy | Automatic foreground/underlines respond to run shading and the underlying paragraph/cell/page fill, ignoring highlight overlays as confirmed by the independent page-background reference controls. Paint page/cell fills, run backgrounds, translucent selection, then text/images/underlines. Selection remains visible over highlighting without washing out automatic white text on a dark background. List-label backgrounds follow paragraph-mark formatting and supported level shading; no highlight is written into numbering definitions. |
| Serialization and history | §A.1 run-property ordering and existing OPC contracts | Write edited highlight values in schema order, retain explicit `none`, and leave original shading/theme/image/style declarations intact. Model shading edits serialize as flat `clear` or automatic `solid`; style shading can be removed back to inheritance through the engine API. No-edit and full undo preserve all original package entries byte for byte. Highlight edits change only `word/document.xml`; rebuilding text may add semantically equivalent `xml:space="preserve"` attributes. |

Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/)
and the MS-OI29500 notes above. The review identified the restrictions on default and
style-based highlights before implementation. No external engine code or new
dependency was introduced.

`public/fixtures/text-highlights.docx` is generated independently with
`tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-highlights-fixture` and the original
`tools/canvas_highlights_fixture.py` helper, using python-docx/lxml and Python's
standard library. Its RGBA PNG pixels are original and generated from source.
The fixture covers all palette values, explicit removal, inherited/theme/solid
shading, dark backgrounds with automatic and explicit foreground, aligned tabs,
mixed sizes, exact-line clipping, Unicode, empty highlighted marks, a marked list,
a transparent inline image and highlighted repeated headers across pages.

Browser exports `text-highlights.docx` and `new-text-highlights.docx` cover import,
keyboard controls, mixed selections, removal, future typing, undo/redo, repeated
header editing and save/reopen. Pixel checks inspect palette RGB, automatic white
glyphs inside a black background, selection compositing, shading exposed by
removal and the background through an image's transparent center. Independent
verification checks exact highlight declarations, unchanged run properties and
text, original media, styles, theme parts and other package entries. Unit
regressions check inheritance and overrides, theme-fill semantics, shaping across
highlight boundaries, tab geometry, source navigation/selection, clipping,
invalid imports, implementation-note restrictions, marks and byte-exact undo.

**Remaining gaps for run backgrounds:** no run-shading dialog, arbitrary highlight
colors, patterned/nil run shading or default/named-style/numbering highlight
support. The engine API can edit supported flat run shading; the toolbar edits
highlights. Paragraph fills are covered by the later paragraph-shading iteration. The palette follows ECMA values, without claiming every reference version
uses identical display colors. Background height follows bundled-font metrics;
reference-specific glyph/ligature segmentation, hidden formatting-mark backgrounds,
list-suffix backgrounds and exact rasterization are not claimed. Existing theme,
font substitution and layout limits remain. Schema validity is not full OOXML,
OPC, accessibility or reference layout equivalence.

Validation on 2026-09-15: all 1,706 unit tests across 163 files passed. All 51
browser scenarios have passing results: 50 in the full run and all three highlight
scenarios in the focused rerun after correcting a pixel probe that stopped at a
foreground glyph. The independent verifier accepted 38 browser exports; official
XSD validation passed 265 part checks. The production build and license check
passed with 199 locked packages and existing Noto OFL assets. The rendered sample
was visually inspected. No dependency or application-license change was made.

## Text color iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Foreground declarations | ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.6 `color`, §17.18.38 `ST_HexColor`, §17.18.97 `ST_ThemeColor`, §17.18.98 byte modifiers | Direct six-digit sRGB and `auto`; theme color takes precedence over the cached RGB value. Absent elements inherit as one declaration through defaults, table/paragraph/character styles and direct overrides. `themeColor="none"` leaves the RGB/automatic value in effect; tint/shade without a theme do not modify that RGB. The transitional schema requires `w:val` even when a theme supersedes it; theme-only examples in the prose do not waive that requirement. Missing, invalid, duplicate or unresolved active declarations reject before editing. |
| Theme resolution | §14.2.7 Theme part, §20.1.6.2 `clrScheme`, §20.1.2.3.32 `srgbClr`, §20.1.2.3.33 `sysClr`, §17.15.1.20 `clrSchemeMapping` | Follow the internal document theme relationship, with package-relative target normalization. Support sRGB scheme entries and system colors using their saved `lastClr`. Map accents, hyperlink colors and text/background aliases. Missing text mappings use dark1/dark2 per [MS-OI29500 §2.1.395](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/1be23913-3f88-40ab-9cb2-2790be8c549d). Referenced missing entries, external themes, alternate color spaces and nested DrawingML color transforms reject. Unused theme data stays untouched. |
| Tint/shade interoperability | §17.3.2.6; [MS-OI29500 §2.1.72](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/8229a077-7fc8-4fba-96cc-c77b6a4fc768) | Follow the documented MS-OI29500 HSL behavior: shade multiplies lightness by the stored byte/255; tint uses `L*t + 1-t`. Tint wins when both are present. Hue and saturation remain unchanged. Compute at full precision and round final sRGB channels to the nearest byte. This deliberately differs from the base clause's channel-wise formulas. Known unresolved precision gap: `C0504D` with shade `BF` resolves to `953735` here, but the native reference resolves it to `943634`, matching the implementation note. The independent 128-case `theme-color-precision` fixture confirms the native RGB values through both saved XML and PDF. A final-rounding-only change is insufficient; `node tools/check-theme-color-precision.mjs` is an explicitly failing diagnostic until the generic conversion is corrected. |
| Underlines and markers | §17.3.2.40 `u`, §17.3.1.29 paragraph-mark `rPr`, §17.9.24 level `rPr` | Single underlines support RGB/theme declarations; automatic underline follows text color, including tab gaps. Numbering-level colors override paragraph-mark colors. Color affects painting only. Decorative forms were rejected at this iteration; the underline-pattern iteration above supersedes that limit. Re-enabling underline creates a single automatic-colored declaration. |
| Editing and display | Supported style hierarchy §17.7.2 and existing source/history contracts | The anchored Text color palette edits RGB or Automatic for selected text, empty marks or future typing. Paragraph/character style dialogs edit RGB/Automatic or remove a declaration with Inherit. Imported theme declarations remain live in the file unless explicitly replaced with RGB/Automatic. Color spans share shaped text, measurement, caret stops and pagination; clipped painting changes color without restarting kerning. Automatic chooses black or white against the supported page/cell background. Repeated headers use the same source formatting. |
| Serialization | §A.1 run-property types and existing OPC preservation contracts | Replace only edited color elements/attributes in schema order; preserve untouched themes, settings, numbering, assets and unused style markup. Preserve all original package entries byte for byte on no-edit and full undo. Extended w14 text fills/outlines reject because they would supersede this renderer's foreground colors. |

Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
its run-color and underline clauses, and the MS-OI29500 implementation notes above.
No external rendering implementation or dependency was added.

`public/fixtures/text-colors.docx` is generated independently with
`tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-colors-fixture` and the original
`tools/canvas_colors_fixture.py` helper using python-docx/lxml. It covers document
defaults, paragraph/character inheritance, mapped themes, conflicting cached RGB,
tint/shade precedence, explicit Automatic, colored/automatic underlines, a colored
numbering level, an empty colored mark, Unicode and repeated headers over six
preview pages, including automatic white text in a dark cell.

Browser exports `text-colors.docx` and `new-text-colors.docx` exercise accessible
controls, selection/mixed values, style edits, future typing, undo/redo and
save/reopen. Pixel samples check actual foreground colors, list labels, dark cells
and repeated headers. Independent checks inspect color/theme declarations and
compare unrelated package parts. The conformance validator also checks declared
theme parts against the official DrawingML schema and rejects a deliberately
invalid theme in its self-check. Unit tests verify hierarchy, style inheritance
restoration, source metadata, Unicode editing, exact undo, invalid inputs and
unchanged shaping/line geometry/caret/selection/pagination after color-only edits.

**Remaining gaps:** no theme editor or theme-color chooser; new color edits use
RGB or Automatic. System colors use saved fallback RGB rather than the host OS
palette. No scRGB/HSL/preset scheme entries, theme-entry transforms, extended text
fills/outlines. Decorative underlines and flat paragraph shading are covered by later iterations above. Highlighting
and supported flat run backgrounds are added by the later highlighting iteration.
Automatic contrast uses supported rendered backgrounds; other retained background
markup is outside the preview subset. Color boundaries inside a shaped ligature
are painted through source-advance windows; reference glyph-level color segmentation
and exact platform rasterization are not claimed. Schema validity is not full
OOXML, OPC, accessibility or reference layout equivalence.

Validation on 2026-09-15: 1,692 unit tests across 162 files and all 48 browser

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Associated level | ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.20 `outlineLvl`, §17.18.10 `ST_DecimalNumber`, §A.1 `CT_DecimalNumber` | Stored levels 0–8 represent displayed levels 1–9; 9 is Body text. The level does not change text appearance or numbering. Absent declarations fall back through the supported style hierarchy and then to 9. Valid signed/zero-padded integer spellings are read and preserved unless edited. Missing, duplicate, fractional and out-of-range active declarations reject before editing. |
| Inheritance and overrides | §17.7.2 hierarchy, §17.7.4.3 `basedOn`, §17.7.8.2 style `pPr` | Resolve document defaults, supported table defaults, paragraph style ancestors, direct paragraph properties and user overrides. Explicit Body text masks an inherited heading. Use style level removes a direct declaration; Inherit in the style editor removes the style declaration. Custom style outline levels remain independent of list levels, fonts, paragraph keeps and following styles. |
| Built-in heading exception | [MS-OI29500 §2.1.51](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/d102191b-957b-471a-b062-7af071ec8e52) | The native reference fixes effective levels for associated paragraph-style IDs `Heading1` through `Heading9`, regardless of conflicting declarations. The engine applies that rule after resolving ordinary formatting. Existing conflicting XML is preserved; ineffective level edits are blocked, and controls explain that a different paragraph style is needed. Custom IDs, including styles based on heading styles, keep ordinary declaration inheritance. New Heading1/Heading2 definitions explicitly include their levels. |
| Editing and navigation | §17.3.1.20 permits additional application behavior; existing source-offset/history contracts | Outline level selector handles the current paragraph or selected paragraphs, including mixed values and selection endpoint rules. Document outline lists each source heading once, with nesting indentation and preview page number, including empty headings and table-cell headings. Repeated table headers do not create extra entries. Keyboard/pointer activation focuses the heading's source start, clears stale page affinity and scrolls to its first source page without creating a document edit or history entry. |
| Export and preservation | Paragraph/style child ordering and existing OPC contracts | Edited declarations serialize as `w:outlineLvl` in schema order; clear-to-style removes the element. Style edits affect only requested declarations. Original style IDs, numbering, runs, table structure and unrelated parts remain intact. No-edit and full-undo export retain every original package entry byte for byte. |

Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
the [Open XML outline reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.outlinelevel?view=openxml-3.0.1),
and the MS-OI29500 implementation note above. The implementation-note review identified the

## Picture rotation and extra extents iteration

Ordinary positioned rectangular pictures now retain source crops and horizontal/
vertical reflections in the editable import path. Their floating painter maps
the source viewport before reflection without changing the anchor frame, wrap
bounds or source image. Negative offsets leave transparent frame space. The
original `positioned-picture-crop` native reference control checks opaque and translucent
pixels, crop outsets and both reflection axes, plus edit/export/undo retention.
This follows §§20.1.8.55–56 and §20.1.7.6; no reference divergence was observed.
Unwrapped floating-picture rotation is added below. Text-wrapped rotation and
wrapping-extra-extent guards still apply.

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rotation and transform order | ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.7.6 `xfrm`, §20.1.10.3 `ST_Angle`, Annex L.4.7.3 and L.4.7.3.2; §A.4.1 `CT_Transform2D` | Signed 32-bit integer angles in 1/60,000 degree units. Source cropping and scaling precede center flips, which precede clockwise rotation about the center of the unrotated frame. Rendering normalizes signed and multi-turn angles; untouched source spellings survive export. New/edited angles are written in the range 0–359.999983… degrees. |
| Base dimensions and reserved space | §§20.4.2.6–8 `effectExtent`/`extent`/`inline`; §20.1.7.6 `xfrm`; [MS-OE376 §2.1.1416](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oe376/9a6e4fd2-659e-4541-95c6-c2505ad110d7) | The declared import subset uses a zero inner origin and equal inner/outer dimensions when the rotated inner extent is present. Absent optional transforms/extents use the inline dimensions. Nonnegative `effectExtent` values add left/right advance and top/bottom line-height space to the native orientation frame described below. Saved effects need not enclose rotated corners. Negative effect extents and rotated pictures with different inner/outer dimensions retain their guards. |
| Rotation editing | Existing image properties, snapshot history and atomic layout contracts | Accessible degrees input accepts −360 through 360 and rounds to 1/60,000 degree. Width/height describe the unrotated picture. Rotating or resizing recomputes nonnegative padding to contain the rotated frame while preserving additional authored padding on each side. Crop, flip and alt-text edits leave that reservation intact. Undo/redo restores metadata, layout and selection; an edit that cannot fit rolls back the full transaction. |
| Fill and rendering boundaries | §20.2.2.1 `blipFill/@rotWithShape`, §§20.1.8.55–56 crop/stretch; [MS-OE376 §2.1.1366](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oe376/a9897c2b-0404-4676-aa5c-8f25bc6d66ca) | Omitted `rotWithShape` follows the MS-OE376-documented default of true. Explicit false is accepted only at zero rotation; the rotation control is disabled and nonzero rotation rejects. Crop outsets rotate with the full frame. Exact-height paragraph clipping remains in page coordinates. Following text and selection overlays are painted after restoring the picture transform. |
| Flow, tables and package preservation | §§17.3.1.33 line spacing, 17.4 table layout; existing package and source-position contracts | Inline advance, AutoFit minimum width, line height, pagination, rectangular selection and hit testing include reserved extents. Repeated table headers share their source picture. Rotation keeps media bytes, relationship IDs, crops, flips, DPI metadata and unrelated parts intact; missing transforms and extra extents are inserted in schema order. No-edit export and full undo retain every original package entry byte for byte. |

The spec review used the official [ECMA-376 publication](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/)
and the MS-OE376 implementation notes linked above. The MS-OE376 note corrects the
standard's left/top/right `effectExtent` descriptions so each applies to its
named side. Review also replaced the old permissive zero-origin check with
validation of the required `x`/`y` integer zero coordinates; boolean values,
missing coordinates, extra axes and child elements now reject. Extra extents
participate in inline layout even when no visual effect is present; this does not add support for shadow, glow or other effects.

**Updated inline rotation behavior:** Native reference controls supersede the former
conservative union-of-rectangles reservation and rotated-corner import guard.
The inline frame exchanges width/height at normalized angles [45,135) and
[225,315), then adds the declared effect extents. Missing effects are zero.
Painting rotates the original physical rectangle about the reserved frame's
center. The native reference clips vertical overflow to the complete line box, including
descent; horizontal overflow remains visible. Hit testing and selection respect
those visible bounds. Ordinary unrotated interaction remains unchanged.
Floating pictures retain their existing center/anchor convention.

Geometry edits recompute nonnegative rotated-ink padding relative to this
orientation frame while preserving extra authored padding. Quarter turns need
no additional inline rotation padding. This authoring choice avoids clipping
newly rotated ink; imported zero-effect geometry is preserved without padding
normalization. The 22-inch dimension limit and paragraph/page checks remain.

The local Part 1 §§20.1.7.6 and 20.4.2.6–8 specify transform rotation, drawing
size, effects and inline line-height participation, but do not prescribe these
45-degree orientation bands. We implement the independently measured reference
compatibility behavior without claiming an explicit normative contradiction.
`tests/fixtures/inline-picture-extents` has 24 independently authored controls
over seven reference pages, with boundary angles, signed/multiple turns, flips, crops
and absent/asymmetric/large effects. Native text positions, image matrices and
stable pixels bind to source/PDF hashes. Matrix-only observations initially
missed clipping; native PDF paths and pixel comparisons corrected that inference.

`public/fixtures/rotated-images.docx` is independently generated by
`tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-rotated-images-fixture` with python-docx and
the existing original four-color PNG generator. Python computes padding from
transformed corner coordinates independently of the JavaScript engine. Cases
include arbitrary, negative and multi-turn angles, asymmetric extra extents,
crops, flips, transparency, shared media, an absent transform, inherited styles,
repeated headers and AutoFit. No external artwork, dependency or license change
is introduced.

Browser exports `rotated-images.docx` and `new-rotated-images.docx` cover rotation,
resize, crop/flip order, asymmetric transparent space, pointer selection,
adjacent typing, repeated-header edits, undo/redo, deletion and save/reopen.
Pixel tests locate source colors independently of engine layout state, then check
transformed quadrant positions and visible bounds. Independent DOCX checks verify
base dimensions, corner padding, preserved extra spacing, angle spellings,
transform child order and unchanged bitmap/package parts. Unit tests cover
inheritance, exact-line clipping, AutoFit, repeated-header caret/selection,
invalid imports, stationary fills, failed-layout rollback and byte-exact undo.
A rejected import in the playground leaves the previous document editable;
the rejected package never receives a save handler.

**Remaining gaps:** negative/clipping extra extents, differing rotated inner and
outer dimensions, translated inner origins, rotated stationary fills, floating
positioning/wrapping, visual effects, other drawing extensions and interactive
transform handles remain unsupported. Hit targets and selection use the full
reserved rectangle, including transparent space. Native reference layout/rendering equivalence,
browser interpolation and color management remain unverified. Schema validity is
not full OOXML or reference layout equivalence.

Validation on 2026-09-15: all 1,663 unit tests passed across 160 files; the final
origin-validation regressions also passed with all 28 image tests. All 42 browser
scenarios passed. Conformance passed 32 independent browser-export checks and the
official transitional schemas for every fixture/export. Production build and
license policy passed (199 locked packages). Rotated/cropped pixels, transparent
outsets, the table header and the scrolling properties dialog were visually
inspected. No dependency or application-license change was made.

## Picture flips iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Horizontal and vertical flips | ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.7.6 `xfrm`, Annex L.4.7.3 shape transformation pipeline; §A.4.1 `CT_Transform2D` | Independent `flipH` and `flipV` XML booleans (`true`/`false`/`1`/`0`), both defaulting to false. The cropped and scaled picture reflects about the center of its existing frame. Two flips can be combined. Rotation is added in the iteration above; translated inner origins, additional transforms and active unsupported editing locks remain unsupported. |
| Crop order and clipping | §§20.1.8.55–56 `srcRect`/`stretch`; §20.4.2.7 outer `extent`; §17.3.1.33 exact line spacing | Crop percentages still address the original source edges. Mirroring applies to the whole displayed frame, including asymmetric transparent outsets. Frame width/height, baseline, source offsets, caret/selection, AutoFit and pagination remain unchanged. Exact-line clipping applies in page coordinates; following text and selection overlays are outside the picture transform. |
| Editing and preservation | Existing picture properties, history and package contracts | Accessible horizontal/vertical checkboxes work on imported and authored pictures, including cropped pictures and repeated headers. Flips support undo/redo, deletion restoration and transactional rollback together with other image properties. Changed axes write explicit `1`/`0`; untouched axis spellings, crop declarations, sizes, descriptions, compression extensions, source media and unrelated parts remain intact. An absent optional `xfrm` is created in schema order with zero origin and the saved dimensions. |

Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 publication and schemas](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/)
and the [DrawingML transform reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.drawing.transform2d?view=openxml-3.0.1).
The shape-transform review establishes reflection around the sized frame's
center. Crop edges are not exchanged or rewritten to implement a flip. Import
validates XML booleans rather than applying WordprocessingML on/off spellings to
DrawingML flags. Rotation support is recorded in the later iteration above.

outset position within an unchanged frame. Independent verification checks flip
attributes, untouched boolean spellings, preserved crop and extension metadata,

caret/selection, shared media isolation, invalid booleans, failed-size rollback

or reference layout equivalence.

license change was made.

## Picture cropping and local-DPI metadata iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source crop rectangle | ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.8.55 `srcRect`, §20.1.10.40 `ST_Percentage`; Part 4 transitional integer percentage representation | Four offsets from the original bitmap edges. Positive offsets inset; negative offsets outset. Omitted edges default to zero. Integer thousandths of a percent and percentage literals are accepted at 0.001% precision. The source viewport must have positive width and height; each offset fits the signed 32-bit transitional integer representation. A viewport wholly outside the source paints transparent space and retains its editable frame. |
| Stretch and frame geometry | §20.1.8.56 `stretch`, §20.1.8.30 `fillRect`, §20.4.2.7 `extent`, §20.2.2.1 `blipFill` | Cropping changes the sampled source, keeping outer EMU dimensions, inline advance, baseline, line spacing, AutoFit minimum, pagination and caret/selection geometry fixed. The source viewport is intersected with the actual bitmap; outsets leave transparent space in the destination frame. Nonzero destination `fillRect` offsets and tiling remain unsupported; flips and rotation are added above. |
| Compression preference extension | [MS-ODRAWXML §2.3.1.13 `useLocalDpi`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-odrawxml/c05c287f-f63e-4fa9-8163-e3e106b4105f) and [§2.3.3.42 `CT_UseLocalDpi`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-odrawxml/2d5944fe-ef10-4a1e-8c47-3bcee2917930) | Accepts the reviewed BLIP extension URI `{28A0092B-C50C-407e-A947-70E740481C1C}` with one `a14:useLocalDpi` element, optional XML boolean `val` (default true), and no child elements. This flag controls whether the BLIP compression preference overrides the document default; it does not replace the authored frame dimensions. Compression preferences and original bitmap bytes are preserved; the editor does not recompress media. Other drawing extensions still reject. |
| Editing and preservation | Existing atomic image, history and package contracts | Four accessible percentage inputs and Reset crop in Image properties. Crop edits replace metadata, preserve shared binary assets, and support undo/redo. Resizing a cropped picture respects aspect locks and updates only transform extents. Untouched crop attribute spellings and extension content survive neighboring text edits. Reset removes the source rectangle; full undo restores every original package entry byte for byte. |

Reviewed against the official [ECMA-376 publication and schemas](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/).
The spec review distinguishes source outsets from destination fill offsets and
compression preferences from display dimensions. Extension-bearing pictures
revealed an ambiguous `a:ext` lookup during resize; the writer now addresses
`a:xfrm/a:ext` explicitly, preserving the unrelated extension record.

`public/fixtures/cropped-images.docx` is generated independently by
`tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-cropped-images-fixture`, using the existing
python-docx tooling and original procedural PNG generator described below. It
covers integer/fractional percentage spellings, positive crops, transparent
outsets, an off-bitmap viewport, shared media, inherited line spacing, repeated
headers, AutoFit and local-DPI flags with true, false and omitted values.
No third-party code, binary codec or artwork is added.

Browser exports `cropped-images.docx` and `new-cropped-images.docx` exercise
crop/resize/alt-text editing, invalid geometry, reset, undo/redo, text insertion
and save/reopen. Pixel checks distinguish blue/orange source regions and verify
outset size and placement within a fixed frame, including browser interpolation
at crop edges. The independent verifier checks crop attributes, untouched
percentage spellings, inner/outer extents, compression metadata, image bytes and
unrelated package parts. Unit tests cover pagination and inherited spacing,
repeated-header selection, source positions, blank viewports, defensive metadata
copies, deletion and byte-exact full undo. Official transitional schemas validate
the source and exported DrawingML; extension payload semantics are checked by the
explicit importer and independent verifier, not certified by that base schema.

**Remaining gaps:** interactive crop handles, destination fill offsets,
floating wrapping, image effects, other vendor drawing
extensions and rich image clipboard remain unsupported. Browser resampling and
color management are not verified against the native reference. The signed 32-bit / 0.001% crop representation limits
are application limits, not full `ST_Percentage` limits. Schema validation is
not full OOXML or reference layout equivalence.

## Inline pictures iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inline drawing structure | ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.3.9 `drawing`, §20.4.2.8 `inline`, §§20.1.2.2.16–17 `graphic`/`graphicData`, §20.2.2.5 `pic` | Embedded rectangular PNG/JPEG pictures in ordinary paragraphs and table cells. Pictures occupy one source position, affect line height, wrap as indivisible objects and sit on the line baseline. Repeated headers project the same picture without adding document content. Floating anchors, non-picture graphics and unsupported drawing children reject before editable open. |
| Dimensions and fill | §20.4.2.7 `extent`, §20.2.2.1 `blipFill`, §20.1.8.56 `stretch`, §20.1.10.19 EMU coordinates | Stored integer EMUs remain authoritative: 914,400 per inch, 9,525 per CSS pixel. Resizing updates outer and present inner extents. Full-image stretch is supported, including transparent PNGs; source cropping and flips are added in the iterations above. Nonrectangular geometry, effects and alternate fills reject; rotation and supported extra extents are added above. Inline `distT/B/L/R` declarations are preserved and correctly ignored for inline layout. |
| Identity, descriptions and locks | §20.4.2.5 `docPr`, §20.2.2.3 `cNvPr`, §20.1.2.2.19 `graphicFrameLocks` | Drawing IDs are unique; new IDs avoid live drawings. Name/title and source non-visual properties remain intact. The alt-text control edits `docPr@descr`. Imported aspect-ratio locks constrain resizing and disable unlocking in the dialog. Other active editing locks reject. |
| Media relationships and preservation | §20.1.8.13 `blip`; Part 2 package parts, content types and relationships | Embedded relationships resolve only to existing internal package parts. PNG/JPEG types normally match the encoded payload; native compatibility also accepts validated PNG/JPEG bytes under the other format's part extension and matching declaration (see image-content-types controls). Linked/external images reject and are never fetched. Shared source media is stored once; original bytes, relationships and unrelated parts survive edits. New assets receive noncolliding media paths, relationship IDs and explicit content types. Deleted source media is retained as an untouched package part. |
| Editing and geometry | Existing paragraph spacing, source-offset and history contracts; §17.3.1.33 exact line spacing | Insertion, image selection, resizing, alt-text edits and deletion undo/redo. Typing beside a picture cannot inherit the picture object. Grapheme boundaries keep pictures separate from adjacent combining marks. AutoFit includes image width in its indivisible-content minimum. Exact-height lines clip pictures and restrict image hit targets to the visible area. Font/style changes affect surrounding text/line spacing while picture dimensions remain fixed. |
| Decode and rollback | Application import/editing limits | PNG/JPEG signatures and dimensions are checked before decoding. Every imported asset is materialized with the browser's bitmap decoder before save attachment. Decoder failure leaves the original downloadable. Failed geometry changes restore model, selection, layout and history. Decoded images are view resources; immutable binary assets stay outside text history snapshots. |

Reviewed against official [ECMA-376 Part 1, fifth edition](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
especially §§17.3.3.9, 20.2.2 and 20.4.2.5–8. Original picture primitives,
package serialization, document mutations, measurement and painting remain
separate. The specification review corrected treating inline distance attributes
as potential padding: they have no inline layout effect. Round-trip testing
found generated namespace prefixes whose declarations were scoped to sibling
fragments; export now binds image relationship attributes at document scope.
Browser rejection testing also found that an HTML image element could report a
successful load/decode for corrupt compressed pixels. Creating a bitmap verifies
actual decoding before the editor enables save. Metadata edits replace picture
records so rejected changes cannot mutate previously computed layout objects.

`public/fixtures/inline-images.docx` is generated independently with python-docx

`tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-inline-images-fixture`. Its two PNGs are

The browser's native canvas encoder independently generates the authored JPEG
test pixels in `tests/browser/inline-images.spec.js`. No image-codec dependency,

Browser exports `inline-images.docx` and `new-inline-images.docx` cover imported
and authored PNG/JPEG pictures, clicking, resize/alt-text controls, adjacent
typing, failed-size rollback, deletion undo/redo and save/reopen. Independent

spacing, exact-line clipping, source-byte undo and unsupported imports.

**Remaining gaps:** floating positioning/wrapping,
effects, vector/animated images, linked images, other vendor drawing extensions and
nonrectangular pictures remain unsupported. Plain-text clipboard output uses

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Header declarations | ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.49 `tblHeader`, §17.17.4 common boolean properties | Leading, contiguous marked rows repeat at the top of each later page occupied by the table. Empty/true flags enable repetition; explicit false disables it. Flags after the first unmarked row are ignored for layout and preserved in the package. A table consisting entirely of header rows renders once if it fits a page. |
| Inheritance and serialization | §17.7.6.11 style `trPr`, §17.4.49 | Unconditional table-style row properties resolve through the based-on chain before direct row declarations. Direct false overrides inherited true. Unchanged declarations and style parts retain their source bytes; edited flags write explicit true/false without expanding repeated display copies into DOCX rows. |
| Pagination | §17.4.49; §17.4.6 `cantSplit`, §17.4.80 `trHeight` | The header is measured once and reserves space on each occupied table page. Body cells keep their independent text flow, row keeps, minimum heights, margins and vertical merges. A first body row moved by its keep carries the first header with it. Fixed and AutoFit tables use the same repeated-header placement. Header-only tables remain one placement unit. |
| Merged headers | §17.4.17 `gridSpan`, §17.4.84 `vMerge` | Horizontal and vertical merges wholly inside the header are supported. Authoring a header region extends it to include whole vertical merges. Imports or subsequent merges crossing the header/body boundary reject before save attachment, or roll back the edit. The complete header must fit a page and leave room for body text lines. These restrictions are application limits. |
| Editing and navigation | Existing source-offset, history and geometry contracts | Repeat rows through selection sets a leading header region; remove repeated headers writes false where needed. Row insertion inside the region extends it; insertion at its boundary creates a body row, including under an inherited header style. Display copies share source positions. Clicking, typing and arrow movement retain the clicked page as a view preference; copy/paste, undo and exported text contain the header once. Selection highlights all visible copies. |

Reviewed against official [ECMA-376 Part 1, fifth edition](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
especially §§17.4.49 and 17.7.6.11. The specification requires ignoring a marked
row after a gap; such a row is neither a new header group nor an import error.
`src/engine/table-headers.js` prepares and places header projections separately
from mutations, DOCX serialization and painting. Canonical source lines remain
distinct from repeated display lines, and the clicked-page preference is view
state rather than document content.

## Table rows whose first content is postponed

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.6 (`cantSplit`), 17.4.80 (`trHeight`),
17.3.1.14–15 (`keepLines`/`keepNext`) and 17.3.1.33 (`spacing`) govern row and
paragraph constraints. A row without `cantSplit` may split, but the standard
does not prescribe the precise first-content boundary behavior tested here.
Nine original `empty-table-fragment` controls exported by the native reference establish
that the entire row moves when an owning cell postpones its first printable
line, even if another cell could start. Paragraph after-spacing, keeps and cell
margins participate. Once every cell has started, later paragraphs may split
normally. No explicit normative contradiction was identified.

The row paginator now checks actual first-line placement after cell pagination,
moving borders with the row instead of retaining an empty border fragment.
Exact-height allocations, existing row keeps, continuation reflow and fresh-page
overflow retain their existing paths. Source formatting is not rewritten.
The original fixture includes minimum/exact-height controls and a genuine split;
tests cover edits to each cell's spacing, export/reopen, exact undo and native
browser border placement on all eighteen reference pages.

## Tables and vertical merges across pages iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vertical merge flow | ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.84 `vMerge`, §17.4.17 `gridSpan`, §17.18.57 `ST_Merge` | The one-page restriction is removed. Each owning cell paginates its paragraphs independently. Its last covered row extends to include all text; cell fragments share one source owner across pages. Staggered merges, rectangles, fixed widths and AutoFit remain editable. Page placement changes no saved merge declarations. |
| Row keeps and inheritance | §17.4.6 `cantSplit`, §17.7.6 table styles | Resolved row keeps apply individually, including inherited keeps and direct false overrides. A kept row that cannot fit the remaining space starts on a fresh page; an oversized kept row can then span pages. Continuing merges extend the preceding row's boxes to the page edge when a later kept row moves. Flexible height shared with future rows does not by itself force an otherwise fitting row forward. The whole connected group is no longer kept together. |
| Row heights | §17.4.80 `trHeight` | Automatic and `atLeast` heights remain supported; minimum heights larger than a page now flow across pages for ordinary and merged tables. Minima, ordinary-cell text and merged-cell remaining extents determine row boundaries. Height already consumed on earlier pages is credited before allocating remaining space. Exact heights are covered by the later iteration above. |
| Cell paragraph pagination | §17.3.1.14 `keepLines`, §17.3.1.15 `keepNext`, §17.3.1.44 `widowControl`; existing paragraph contracts | Each cell uses the existing paragraph pagination path, preserving line keeps, widow/orphan behavior, list markers, line breaks and cell margins across pages. Mixed font sizes do not require aligned line endings in adjacent cells. Heading keep chains include at least the first visible line of a fully merged table. |
| Selection and navigation | Existing source-offset and cell geometry contracts | Selection paints only real text lines. Arrows continue through an owner cell across pages and then leave its full extent. Clicking a blank fragment locates the nearest owner text using page-aware coordinates; no phantom continuation offset is created. Text/format/style edits and row/column/merge/split operations repaginate, undo and save/reopen without changing ownership. The existing 200-page guard remains transactional. |

The review used official [ECMA-376 Part 1, fifth edition](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
especially §§17.4.6, 17.4.80 and 17.4.84. `cantSplit` permits oversized rows to
flow after starting on a new page; `atLeast` is a minimum, not a reason to reject
a tall row. The new original `src/engine/table-pagination.js` places measured
cells and row boundaries separately from text mutation, DOCX writing and painting.
Visual review corrected counting consumed page space again as future merged-row
height. A heading regression also corrected fully merged tables contributing zero
height to the preceding paragraph's keep chain.

`public/fixtures/vertical-pages.docx` was independently generated with python-docx
(MIT, test tooling) and app-authored XML using
`tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-vertical-pages-fixture`. This is its source
and provenance record. It contains overlapping vertical spans, a full-table
AutoFit rectangle, long text, 11/17-point type, inherited italic and row keeps,
direct false keep overrides, a numbered paragraph with contextual spacing
explicitly disabled, shading, combining text/emoji and a 4-inch minimum-height
row on a 3-inch page text area. Browser exports `vertical-pages.docx` and
`new-vertical-pages.docx` test imported and authored long merges, formatting,
continuation-row insertion, undo and save/reopen. Independent checks inspect
physical merge markers, paragraph text, shared/direct properties and row heights.
Geometry tests check every text line's cell containment, non-overlapping boxes,
continuous fragments, source offsets, page-aware navigation, width/style changes,
heading keeps, structural edits, exact undo and unchanged package parts.

**Remaining gaps:** row-height distribution is an original approximation and does
not claim reference-exact pagination. It uses natural demands for not-yet-started cells
and actual remaining extents for started cells; different font metrics, spacing,
row allocations and border edge choices can produce different page breaks.
At that milestone, repeated headers, non-top alignment and exact heights were
still gaps; later iterations above add them. Nested/floating tables, nonempty
merge continuations, cell page breaks and the other declared table limitations
remain unsupported. Schema validity is not full OOXML
or reference layout equivalence.

## Vertical merged cells iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vertical ownership | ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.84 `vMerge`, §17.18.57 `ST_Merge`, §17.4.17 `gridSpan` | `restart` begins a group; `continue` and omitted `val` continue it. Continuations must cover exactly the same grid columns. Omitted `vMerge` closes a group; a new restart begins another. Orphan continuations are ignored as required by §17.18.57, including their text remaining visible. Invalid values and mismatched continuation spans reject. Vertical merges declared in table styles remain unsupported. |
| Cell content and preservation | §17.4.65 `tc`, required block content; existing OPC contracts | Each effective merge has one editable owner. Physical continuation cells retain their required empty paragraph XML without creating extra text offsets or Tab stops. Continuations containing text, breaks or numbering reject before editable open. Unrelated edits retain source merge spelling, continuation paragraph properties, cell shells and unrelated package parts; no-edit and full undo retain every original entry's bytes. Newly authored continuations serialize a required empty paragraph. |
| Merge and split editing | `vMerge`/`gridSpan` semantics plus application operations | Merge with cell below joins cells or existing groups covering identical grid columns. It appends all lower-cell paragraphs to the top cell, retaining formatting and mapping selection through paragraph identity as source offsets move. Split into grid cells restores every physical grid cell in a vertical/horizontal rectangle; all visible text stays in the top-left cell and new editable cells receive empty paragraphs. Each operation undoes in one step. Horizontal merging rejects selections that touch a vertical group or cross a hidden continuation. |
| Row and column editing | §17.4.17, §17.4.84; application behavior | Row insertion is below the active cell's final row. When this lies inside another group, the new row continues that group; otherwise it contains ordinary blank cells. Deleting a group's starting row promotes its text and cell appearance to the next row. Deleting an interior continuation leaves the remaining group connected. Column edits apply the same grid interval to every physical cell, preserving matching spans and retaining text when only part of a span is removed. Tab from a fully merged table appends a usable row. |
| Geometry and page placement | §17.4.80 `trHeight`, §17.4.6 `cantSplit`; declared layout subset | Fixed and AutoFit measurement includes merged content once. Ordinary cell content and `atLeast` heights establish row minima; spanning content distributes additional height across its covered rows. Connected vertical spans form one placement unit, moved to the next page if needed. The whole unit must fit a page; larger groups reject before save attachment, or edits roll back with history and selection intact. Normal rows retain their existing splitting behavior. Source row-keep declarations are preserved; this preview additionally keeps connected vertical groups even when individual rows allow splitting. This is a pagination limitation, not full `cantSplit` or native reference layout equivalence for vertical groups. |
| Painting, navigation and inheritance | Existing layout/painting/style contracts | A merged cell has one full rectangle, using the top cell's fill, margins and formatting. Internal horizontal and vertical borders disappear within that rectangle. Clicks in its lower blank area map to the owner's text. Tab skips physical continuations; vertical arrows follow owner lines and then move beyond the merged rectangle. Selected row-keep controls cover all spanned rows. Direct and inherited text changes reflow the table; undo restores text, selection and geometry. |

Reviewed against official [ECMA-376 Part 1, fifth edition](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
especially §§17.4.6, 17.4.17, 17.4.65, 17.4.80, 17.4.84 and 17.18.57.
Spec review corrected the previous blanket rejection of orphan continuations:
the standard requires ignoring them, while retaining ordinary cell content.
Behavioral review also corrected horizontal selections crossing a hidden
continuation and arrow navigation entering a neighboring row inside the current
merged rectangle. Mutations, package serialization, measurements, page placement
and painting remain separate. The implementation is original code; no other
editor's implementation or new dependency was incorporated.

**Remaining gaps at this iteration:** connected vertical groups cannot split across pages, and

uses the owner's appearance. Split creates blank editable cells using the

## Merged AutoFit preferred widths

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.18.87 describes AutoFit sizing from grid/cell preferences and
measured content, enlarging a merged cell's combined columns when necessary.
§§17.4.17, 17.4.48, 17.4.63 and 17.4.71 define its grid span, table grid and
preferred table/cell widths. Review used the official fifth-edition text cached
in temporary storage, including its distinction between required semantics and
non-normative layout guidance.

The former solver found one allocation at the minimum possible table width,
then incorrectly treated those individual column widths as lower bounds at the
larger final width. A merged cell constrains an interval's sum, not each column
in that particular allocation. The corrected solver computes the minimum total
without committing to an allocation, determines the final table width, and then
fits interval constraints around the preferred column proportions. Feasible
preferences stay intact. Overlapping intervals share their space; actual content
pressure still redistributes columns, expands the table within available page
space, or forces wrapping subject to indivisible-character/margin floors. Layout
never rewrites saved grid or width preferences.

`tools/canvas_merged_autofit_fixture.py` generates the original independent
`public/fixtures/merged-autofit.docx` using only standard-library OPC/XML. Its two
tables combine staggered spans, equal/unequal preferred columns and long text
that already fits those preferences. Unit tests cover varied/mirrored intervals,
scaling, genuine growth, overlapping constraints, page limits, caret hits,
export/reopen and byte-identical full undo. Browser tests check native font
measurements, long-text reflow, clipboard text and pasted replacement, and export
without changing grid/cell properties. The independent export verifier checks
text, spans, preferences, borders, margins and unrelated parts.

The first local birthday card now retains its feasible saved grid and its text
and entry-line horizontal positions move toward the existing reference.
Its original prompt-edit/full-undo test and an additional cell-edit round trip

open; this table correction is not a font or pagination compensation. A fresh reference
PDF export is still unavailable (`-1708`). The fixture establishes the
stated sizing invariants, not reference-exact AutoFit under every competing constraint.

## Horizontal merged cells and grid spans iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Grid spans | ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.17 `gridSpan`, §17.4.48 `tblGrid`, §17.4.65 `tc` | Positive spans up to the 32-column table limit; omitted span means one. Rows may have different cell counts while covering the same grid. Staggered spans, fully merged rows and multiple paragraphs per cell are supported. Grid columns implied beyond a declared grid are added to the effective model (one-inch defaults for fixed layout, automatic zero for AutoFit); source grid XML stays intact until the grid itself is edited. Missing/zero/negative/excessive span values and omitted cells reject before attaching save. |
| Fixed and AutoFit sizing | §17.18.87 table layout guidance, §17.4.71 `tcW` | Merged cell width is the sum of its grid columns. Later fixed-width requests enlarge the final spanned column; table preferred widths still constrain proportional reduction. AutoFit measures merged content once and enforces interval constraints across its spanned columns. Overlapping spans share available space; they do not each demand a separate allocation. At the final table width, allocation follows column preferences where interval constraints permit (see the merged AutoFit correction above). Forced wrapping still observes merged-cell grapheme/margin floors. |
| Merge and split editing | §17.4.17 and required cell content in §17.4.65; application editing behavior | Table actions provides Merge cells in row and Split into grid cells. Merge applies to all cells touched by a text selection within one row, including empty cells; it retains every paragraph/run and selection offset, using the first cell's properties. Split restores cells along existing grid lines, keeps all content in the first cell and creates required empty paragraphs in the others. Newly created cells retain the source cell's appearance and paragraph-mark formatting; their source XML IDs are removed. Each action undoes in one step. |
| Row, column and width editing | Grid-span semantics plus application operations | New rows copy the source row's span pattern. Column insertion after the active cell adds a cell at matching row boundaries and enlarges any spanning cell that crosses that position. Column deletion removes the grid columns covered by the active cell, removes cells wholly inside that range, and shrinks partially overlapped cells while retaining their text. Fixed preferences are recomputed from the grid; AutoFit retains remaining preferences. Table properties addresses grid columns independently of cell count. |
| Layout and navigation | Existing cell geometry contracts; §17.4.6 `cantSplit` | Merged cells use combined widths for painting, selection, hit testing and text wrapping. No internal vertical border is painted inside a merged cell. Oversized merged rows flow across pages with synchronized cell fragments and the existing row-keep fallback. Tab visits actual cells; arrow navigation uses cell bounds across different span patterns. Text/format changes and shared styles repaginate merged cells; undo restores selection and geometry. |
| Preservation and inheritance | Existing OPC and style hierarchy contracts | Direct cell spans are distinct from table-style text/appearance inheritance. Save only changes requested spans/widths and structure; unrelated parts and shared styles retain their bytes. No-edit and full-undo export preserve original entry bytes. Grid spans declared in table styles reject rather than being interpreted as editable structure. |

The implementation was reviewed against official [ECMA-376 Part 1, fifth edition](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
especially §§17.4.17, 17.4.65, 17.4.84 and 17.18.87. `gridSpan` spans columns;
`vMerge` links rows and requires matching column coverage. This iteration supplies
the common grid mapping and horizontal editing needed before vertical merges.
AutoFit uses original prefix-width constraints, with no other editor's source or
implementation. Review covers implicit grid augmentation, shared space for
overlapping spans, actual cell boundaries in caret movement and column operations
that intersect a merged cell. The independent fixture also covers adding `tcW`
after retained `cnfStyle` flags, correcting cell-property schema order when the
source omitted a preferred width.

`public/fixtures/merged-cells.docx` was generated independently using python-docx
(MIT, test tooling) and app-authored XML via
`tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-merged-cells-fixture`. This is the fixture's
source/provenance record; its content is app-authored. It includes staggered fixed
spans, a fully merged row, an oversized kept merged row, a derived italic table
style, direct bold, shading, retained cell flags without a direct width,
combining text/emoji, and overlapping AutoFit spans
on a zero-width grid. Browser export `merged-cells.docx` exercises text edits,
merge/split, formatting, grid width changes and save/reopen. `new-merged-cells.docx`
covers creating merged cells, column insertion/deletion, copied merged rows and
AutoFit. Independent validation inspects physical `tc` elements, span values,
paragraph contents, style declarations and summed cell/grid preferences, avoiding
the repeated references exposed by a grid-based table API.

**Remaining gaps at this iteration:** vertical `vMerge`, legacy transitional `hMerge`, omitted cells,
nested/floating tables, repeated headers and other table limitations below remain
unsupported. Merge is limited to one row; rectangular multi-row selection and
vertical merge/split follow next. Split uses existing grid boundaries and does not
arbitrarily create new grid lines. Preferred table/cell widths retain the existing
22-inch limit; column edits that would exceed it in a merged cell reject atomically
to keep exports reopenable. The width and border algorithms are a declared
subset; reference-exact layout and full Unicode line breaking are not claimed.

## AutoFit sizing and table properties iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Layout choice and inheritance | ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.52 `tblLayout`, §17.18.87 `ST_TblLayoutType`, §17.7.6 table styles | Fixed or AutoFit, including an omitted layout resolved through a table-style chain and then the AutoFit default. Zero or omitted widths on explicit grid columns are accepted for AutoFit; fixed layout still requires positive widths. Rectangular tables require an explicit grid and one cell per column. Direct layout changes preserve shared styles. |
| Content measurements | §17.18.87 AutoFit guidance | Measure each cell with resolved run/paragraph formatting, margins, indents, list markers, tabs and explicit line breaks. Use widest wrap chunk and unwrapped line for minimum/maximum content demand, plus an indivisible-grapheme floor for forced wrapping. Complete shaping groups avoid measuring every growing prefix during unwrapped width calculation. NBSP, narrow NBSP and figure space do not create ordinary wrapping opportunities. |
| Width distribution | §17.18.87, §17.4.63 `tblW`, §17.4.71 `tcW` | Start from fixed grid/cell preferences. The first explicit preferred cell width bounds its column's maximum content preference. Redistribute available width subject to cell minima, expand beyond the preferred table width when necessary up to available page space, then force grapheme wrapping. Percentage table widths use the page text width; percentage cell widths use the table width. Left indentation reduces available space. Layout measurements never overwrite stored width preferences. |
| Width lexical forms | §17.4.87 `CT_TblWidth`, §17.18.90 `ST_TblWidth` | Nonnegative integer twips/fiftieth-percent, explicit decimal percentages and `mm`, `cm`, `in`, `pt`, `pc`, `pi` measurements. An explicit measurement unit overrides a contradictory type; physical measurements normalize to rounded twips in the model. Original XML lexical forms survive unrelated edits. Fractional fiftieth-percent values serialize as explicit percentages. Existing width limits remain. |
| Properties and fitting | §17.4.28 `jc`, §17.4.50 `tblInd`, the width/layout clauses above; application editing behavior | Accessible Table properties dialog edits layout, preferred width, alignment, left indent and individual column preferences. Fit to contents clears table/cell preferences; Fit to page sets 100% table width and automatic cells. Both retain the declared grid. Switching a zero grid to fixed layout materializes positive displayed widths, rounded up to keep individual glyphs fitting. AutoFit column insertion adds an automatic zero-grid column; deletion removes its column while preserving other width preferences. Unchanged dialog submission creates no history entry. Invalid geometry rolls back atomically. |
| Editing and preservation | Existing mutation, layout, painting and OPC contracts | Text and inherited font changes recompute column widths and row pagination. Undo/redo restores selection, width preferences and geometry. DOCX save/reopen retains the chosen layout and only rewrites changed properties in schema order. Unrelated package parts and shared table styles retain their bytes; full undo restores all original entry bytes. |

The review used the official [ECMA-376 Part 1, fifth edition](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
especially §§17.18.87 and 17.4.87. Its AutoFit algorithm is guidance; this engine
uses an original proportional distribution subject to the measured constraints.
No other editor's implementation was inspected or incorporated. Review corrected
nonbreaking spaces being treated as ordinary breaks, contradictory width types
winning over explicit units, and fixed conversion rounding a measured column
below its single-glyph minimum. Measured widths stay separate from source width
declarations. Column editing was also corrected to accept automatic
zero-width grids without forcing them through fixed layout. Browser retry testing
found and corrected a dialog baseline changing during a rejected edit; retrying
now retains all requested settings.

`public/fixtures/autofit-tables.docx` was independently generated with python-docx
(MIT, test tooling) and app-authored XML via
`tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-autofit-fixture`. This records the fixture's
source/provenance; it contains no third-party document content. It includes an
omitted AutoFit declaration, explicit AutoFit, 100% width, unequal preferences,
a zero grid, empty cells, bold text, long wrapping content, a nonbreaking space,
a decimal tab, combining text and emoji. Browser export `autofit-tables.docx`
changes cell text, alignment, fractional percentage and column preferences.
`new-autofit-tables.docx` covers insertion, fixed/AutoFit changes, fitting and
indentation. Independent checks inspect these properties and their cell text;
unit tests additionally cover shared-style layout inheritance, content-driven
font/text reflow, caret/selection geometry, forced wrapping, full undo and
package preservation.

**Remaining gaps at this iteration:** omitted cells, nested/floating tables, repeated headers
and the other table limitations below remain unsupported. Width controls edit
preferences; pointer dragging to resize columns is not implemented. Wrapping uses
whitespace opportunities and forced grapheme breaks; full Unicode line breaking,
language-specific hyphenation, CJK breaking and reference-exact AutoFit widths are not
claimed. Table-style and cell-property editing remain future work. An AutoFit
table whose margins/indents and indivisible characters cannot fit is rejected
before save is attached, or its edit is rolled back. Schema validity is not full
OOXML or reference layout equivalence.
