## Fixed-width table editing iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Table structure | ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.37 `tbl`, §17.4.65 `tc`, §17.4.78 `tr` | Rectangular body tables with one cell per grid column and one or more paragraphs per cell. Paragraphs retain UTF-16 source offsets in row/cell order; separate table, row and cell records retain their boundaries. See the merged-cell, sparse-grid, block-control and nested-table sections below for extensions to this initial structure. Missing editable cell paragraphs and tracked table structures remain unsupported. |
| Fixed column layout | §17.4.16 `gridCol`, §17.4.48 `tblGrid`, §17.4.52 `tblLayout`, §17.4.63 `tblW`, §17.4.71 `tcW`, §17.18.87 `ST_TblLayoutType` | Positive explicit grid widths; fixed layout with integer-twip, integer-fiftieth-percent, auto or nil preferred widths. Resolve all row requests before proportional reduction. An explicit single-column request replaces a share inferred from a merged cell; complete span requests remain constraints on the unreduced grid. Reduction reserves each cell's horizontal margins plus one point of writing space, taking the maximum cell requirement across rows and retaining merged-cell constraints. A smaller table preference cannot reduce below that combined minimum. Omitted columns retain their independent gaps. These behaviors follow independent reference controls rather than literal whole-column scaling during each row of the clause's optional guidance. See `tests/fixtures/fixed-table-reduction/README.md`. Unshrunk grids and AutoFit retain their existing allocation. |
| Placement and appearance | §17.4.28 `jc`, §17.4.38 `tblBorders`, §17.4.42 `tblCellMar`, §17.4.50 `tblInd`, §17.4.68 `tcMar`, §17.4.31–32 `shd` | Left/center/right alignment, nonnegative twip indent for left alignment, inherited table margins and per-cell margin overrides. `start`/`end` override legacy `left`/`right`. Single/none/nil table-level borders and explicit RGB clear shading. Cells align at the top. Nonprinting dashed grid guides show otherwise borderless cells. |
| Table style inheritance | §17.7.2 hierarchy, §17.7.3 toggles, §17.7.6 table styles, §17.7.4.3 `basedOn`, §17.4.62 `tblStyle` | Same-type table-style chains supply unconditional table, row, cell, paragraph and run properties. Resolve text defaults, table style, paragraph style, character style and direct formatting separately. Unused definitions stay intact. Conditional table styles reject. Newly inserted tables use a new empty table style plus explicit geometry, keeping their appearance independent of an imported default table style. |
| Row pagination | §17.4.6 `cantSplit`, §17.4.80 `trHeight` | Automatic and minimum row heights. **Keep table row together** applies an explicit on/off override to selected rows. A kept row moves to a fresh page if necessary; a row taller than a page still flows across pages. Each cell paginates its own lines; row fragments share page boundaries and border heights. Paragraph keeps/widows operate within each cell. Trailing paragraph space at a page boundary is clipped to available space. |
| Editing and navigation | Application behavior; §17.4.65 required cell content | Insert at a caret; add/delete rows and columns; delete a table; insert body paragraphs before/after a table. Enter splits within a cell. Tab/Shift+Tab move through cells; Tab from the last cell adds a row. Insert tab still inserts a literal tab. Arrow navigation uses column-aware geometry. Backspace/Delete cannot merge cell boundaries. Cross-cell text replacement clears selected text within each cell, preserving the table and one paragraph per cell, and inserts replacement text in the first selected cell/body region. |
| Transactions and serialization | Existing mutation/codec/layout/painting and OPC contracts | Row/column, row-keep and text operations have undo/redo snapshots including cell boundaries and selection. Column insertion preserves total width; column deletion reduces it. Export writes table/row/cell shells around the existing preservation-aware paragraph writer. No-edit and full-undo export retain original entry bytes. Cell text edits retain unrelated ZIP parts, styles, widths and shading. |

The review used the official [ECMA-376 Part 1](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
especially §§17.4, 17.7.6 and 17.18.87, with the Open XML SDK
[table reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.table)
and [table width reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.tablewidth)
as secondary element references. The specification's `cantSplit` exception for
oversized rows is implemented. Indentation with `pct`/`auto` is ignored as
specified. Review also corrected cross-cell deletion creating empty undo
transactions, trailing cell spacing crossing the page bottom, column deletion
leaving obsolete preferred widths, percentage cells using different width bases
within one row, and run inheritance omitting the table-style layer. Cell geometry rejects indents or glyphs that would extend outside their
supported writing area. No other engine implementation was used.

`public/fixtures/tables.docx` is independently generated with python-docx (MIT,
test tooling) and app-authored XML in
`tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-tables-fixture`. It contains unequal
columns, a derived table style, inherited italic text, direct bold, shading,
multiple paragraphs, a literal tab, combining text/emoji, an oversized kept row,
minimum row height and an empty cell. Browser export `tables.docx` changes cell
text, paragraph formatting and row splitting. `new-tables.docx` covers insertion,
Tab-created rows, adding/removing columns and rows, deleting/restoring a table,
and save/reopen. Independent validation checks cell boundaries, text, references,
preferred/grid widths, row flags, shading and unflattened text inheritance. Puter
mock save/reload includes table text and navigation to its next cell.

**Remaining gaps at this iteration:** merged/omitted cells, nested/floating tables, repeated
headers, row property exceptions, conditional styles, exact heights, non-top
vertical alignment, per-cell border conflicts, other border/shading styles,
nonzero cell spacing and negative table indents remain unsupported. AutoFit and
additional width lexical forms are covered above. Manual page breaks and page-break-before inside cells reject.
There is no pointer column resizing, rectangular cell selection, rich table clipboard,
table-style editing or semantic screen-reader table view. Cross-cell text editing
preserves structure; structural deletion uses explicit row/column/table actions.
Inter-row paragraph keep constraints and reference-exact row splitting, border
placement and table layout are not claimed. Current limits are 32 columns, 1,000
rows per imported table, 100,000 source characters and 200 pages; insertion UI
starts with up to 16 columns and 100 rows. Schema validity is not full OOXML/OPC
or reference equivalence.

## Character style selection and editing iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Character references | ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.29 `rStyle`, §17.7.9 character styles | Apply or remove a character-style reference on selected text without changing paragraph styles or direct run formatting. Mixed selections are identified. Partial runs split at source offsets; grapheme boundaries prevent splitting a surrogate pair or combining sequence. References inside a character definition's `rPr` are ignored. Duplicate document-run or paragraph-mark references reject before attaching a save handler. |
| Shared character definitions | §17.7.4.3 `basedOn`, §17.7.4.9 `name`, §17.7.4.17 `style`, §17.7.9.1 `rPr` | Create, rename, change a same-type base, and edit size/bold/italic/single underline. Inherit removes a declaration. Recompute uses of the definition and descendants while retaining direct overrides. New documents include Emphasis and Strong. Paragraph properties and `next` are not character-style editing controls. |
| Hierarchy and defaults | §17.7.2 hierarchy, §17.7.3 toggles, §17.7.4.17 `default` | Resolve character styles after paragraph styles and before direct run formatting. Keep nearest declarations within a based-on chain and combine toggles across hierarchy levels. Missing or wrong-type references remain unresolved; removing a reference allows the declared character default to apply. Preserve unused unsupported definitions; unavailable preview formats are disabled in the selector. |
| Empty paragraphs and marks | §17.3.1.29 paragraph-mark `rPr`, §17.3.2.29 `rStyle` | Resolve and edit references on paragraph marks, including character defaults. Applying to a selected paragraph separator changes its mark; applying at an empty paragraph changes that mark persistently. Typing and Enter carry the character reference into new text/marks, while paragraph-style transitions still resolve separately. Save styles as references, without flattening inherited sizes into direct formatting. |
| Future typing and native input | Application behavior and UTF-16 position contract | A collapsed choice in nonempty text affects future typing without changing existing text or adding an undo step. Creating a definition still changes the document. Pending choices are captured by the next edit's undo snapshot and reset on selection movement. Native input and composition retain pending style/direct-format choices. Replacing a selection uses its first selected character's formatting; collapsed insertion retains the existing left-side caret affinity. |
| Layout, undo and preservation | Existing geometry and OPC preservation contracts | Shared size edits repaginate text and empty paragraphs without changing source offsets. Undo restores definitions, references, selection and geometry. Character selection leaves numbering definitions intact. Only changed `rStyle` references/declarations are written; unrelated run properties, definitions and ZIP parts remain preserved. Full undo and no-edit export preserve all original entry bytes. |

The review used [ECMA-376 Part 1](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
especially §§17.3.1.29, 17.3.2.29, 17.7.3 and 17.7.9. The Open XML SDK
[character reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.runstyle)
and [parent style](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.basedon)
references corroborate the hierarchy and type restrictions. The paragraph-mark
clause requires each child at most once, a condition its schema does not fully
express; behavioral rejection tests cover duplicate references. The review also
corrected missing character-style resolution on paragraph marks, lost pending
formatting during native input, and replacement inheriting from the unselected
character immediately before a styled selection. No other engine was used.

python-docx (MIT, test tooling) and app-authored XML declarations in

text, direct overrides and retained list. Puter mock save/reload verifies a
character reference alongside paragraph and list state.

**Remaining gaps:** Linked paragraph/character style automation, style deletion,
updating a definition from selected direct formatting, editing document defaults,
automatic style redefinition, additional font/decorative properties and

Off declaration depends on document defaults; see the later interoperability
correction above. Clipboard and text
mode remain plain text; pending choices without inserted text are not stored in

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported subset and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List references and definitions | Part 1 §17.3.1.19 `numPr`, §17.9.1–3, §17.9.6, §17.9.15–18 | Resolve `numId` and zero-based `ilvl` through defaults, based-on paragraph styles and direct properties. `numId=0` removes inherited numbering. Abstract definitions are reusable; each numbering instance has its own counters. Nine levels are supported. |
| Style associations | §17.9.23 `pStyle`, §17.7.2 hierarchy; MS-OI29500 §2.1.50 | Follow the native reference's explicit paragraph-style `ilvl`, otherwise level zero. Reciprocal style bindings govern inherited marker activation; a direct `numId` selects numbering explicitly. Suppressed inherited markers retain the style level’s geometry. See “Paragraph-style numbering bindings” below for native controls and the standards divergence. |
| Counters and restart | §17.9.8 `lvlOverride`, §17.9.10 `lvlRestart`, §17.9.25–26 `start`/`startOverride` | Counters advance in document order and continue across intervening ordinary paragraphs. Deeper levels restart after the designated or any earlier level; zero means never restart. Missing starts default to zero. Full level overrides replace abstract levels; `startOverride` wins over a level's start, including later restarts. |
| Label formats | §17.9.4 `isLgl`, §17.9.11 `lvlText`, §17.9.17 `numFmt`, §17.18.59 `ST_NumberFormat` | Literal text survives for bullet and none as well as numeric formats. Expand `%1`–`%9`; none/bullet references contribute no numeric text, including under legal numbering. Other legal references use decimal. Following the native divergence documented below, a deeper-level reference suppresses the whole label. Latin letters repeat after Z (AA, BB, …), as specified for English. |
| Label placement | §17.9.7 `lvlJc`, §17.9.22 `pPr`, §17.9.24 `rPr`, §17.9.28 `suff`, §17.18.84 `ST_TabJc` | Left/center/right labels at the first-line anchor; suffix tab, space or nothing. Level paragraph properties currently cover physical indents and custom tabs. Legacy `num` tabs apply to the label suffix, not ordinary text tabs. Wrapped lines use the continuation indent. Marker size/bold/italic/single underline contribute to line metrics and painting. |
| Editing | Application behavior | Accessible Bulleted list and Numbered list toggles, level changes through indent buttons or Alt+Shift+Left/Right, and Restart numbering at 1. Restart allocates a separate instance for the contiguous remainder, preserves current ancestor values, and stops before a shallower level. Enter continues a list; Enter on an empty item or Backspace at its start removes numbering. Mixed selections, split/merge, undo/redo and selection restoration are tested. |
| Geometry and save | Source-offset and package preservation contracts | Labels have no editable offsets and appear once per paragraph, including across page breaks. Clicking a label resolves to the first text position. Formatting and text changes retain caret/selection and pagination. Text-only edits leave numbering bytes intact; restarts clone original instance XML so unused overrides survive. New definitions append using unused IDs; missing numbering parts receive relationships and content types. |

Native numbering divergence: Part 1 §17.9.11 says to ignore references to levels
deeper than the current level, illustrating retention of surrounding literals.
The native reference instead suppresses the entire label, whether that deeper level is
defined or absent. A suppressed level also contributes no numeric substitution
when another level references it. The renderer follows the native reference. The native reference drops the
suppressed level's paragraph geometry but retains paragraph/style geometry,
uses a tab suffix irrespective of the authored suffix, and supplies an 18pt
numbering-only fallback tab. An earlier custom tab can still win. Equality at
the fallback tab or body indent does not advance to another stop. Stored
numbering definitions, counters and package parts are unchanged by projection.
The independently authored `tests/fixtures/none-numbering/control.docx` and
hash-bound three-page native PDF establish 58 items covering literal none,
legal and bullet references, defined/undefined deeper references, nested
suppression, direct/style indentation, custom tabs and suffix overrides.
Unit tests exercise text insertion, splitting, list toggling, export/reopen and
exact undo; browser tests check native marker presence and body positions.

The original implementation follows [ECMA-376 Part 1](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/),
including the current clause numbering above. The Open XML SDK element references cover
[numbering properties](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.numberingproperties),
[level restarts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.levelrestart)
and [start overrides](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.startoverridenumberingvalue).
The preview retains U+F0B7 with a readable U+2022 fallback when the level names the
Symbol font; this font-specific mapping is described by a font vendor's text-team
engineer in the [Unicode archive](https://www.unicode.org/mail-arch/unicode-ml/Archives-Old/UML022/0292.html).
Other private-use labels now retain their literal text and selected font; see
Font-encoded numbering labels below. No font or third-party code was added.

### Spec review corrections

The hierarchy review found an existing run-style discrepancy affecting list text
and labels. Part 1 §17.7.3 (2016) takes the nearest declaration inside a `basedOn`
chain before combining toggles across distinct hierarchy levels. The old resolver
toggled at every link. That correction followed the base specification, including
direct off overrides and its document-default true rule. Tests cover two italic-on
styles, a nearest italic-off style, and a character style applied on top. The
independent list fixture includes the two italic-on declarations. The MS-OI29500
implementation deviations for defaults, paragraphs and tables are now implemented
by the later style-toggle interoperability correction above. Exact reference layout
is still not claimed.

Review also corrected list-only tab scope, direct-geometry precedence, nearest
style-level associations, UTF-16 numbering input and preservation of unused
unsupported level overrides when restarting an imported sequence. The existing
explicit-zero character-indent regression remains covered; layer bookkeeping
must not reject a property that is disabled by a later direct override.

### Fixtures, preservation and limits

`public/fixtures/numbering.docx` is generated by the app-authored
`tools/verify-canvas-docx.py --generate-numbering-fixture` using python-docx (MIT,
test tooling). Its numbering definitions are authored independently of this
engine. It includes inherited and nested lists, non-one starts, independent
instances, a start override, a Symbol bullet, wrapped text, an explicit `numId=0`
and an empty item. Browser acceptance exports `numbering.docx` after a text edit,
restart and level change; `new-lists.docx` exercises creating definitions from a
blank document. Independent checks inspect text, references, levels, starts,
styles and geometry. Conformance validation now includes `word/numbering.xml`
in every fixture and export. Puter mock save/reload also preserves list state.

This is a body-paragraph subset, not complete numbering or reference equivalence.
Picture bullets, linked numbering styles, custom/other numbering formats,
non-geometry level paragraph properties and unsupported decorative symbol
formatting reject when referenced. Unused definitions remain
preserved. Alphabetic output currently uses English A–Z; locale-specific
alphabets remain a gap. Roman values are limited to 1–3999, starts to 0–1,000,000,
and label templates to 128 UTF-16 units. Large labels that leave no text space
reject transactionally. The existing Noto substitution and native reference layout limits
remain. Plain-text clipboard and text mode expose paragraph text without generated
labels; semantic screen-reader list announcements remain future work. There is
no automatic conversion of typed list prefixes or arbitrary numbering-definition
editor yet. Schema validity is not full OOXML/OPC or reference layout equivalence.

Validation on 2026-09-15: `npm test -- --maxWorkers=2` passed 1,547 tests across
147 files; `npm run test:browser` passed 14 scenarios; `npm run check:conformance`,
`npm run build` and `npm run check:licenses` passed. Browser list rendering and
toolbar screenshots were inspected. No dependency or application-license change
was made.

The next priority at this checkpoint was style selection and editing; paragraph
styles are now covered above. Character styles, tables and images remain next.

## Paragraph pagination iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Supported behavior and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keep lines together | ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.14 `keepLines` | Move all measured lines to the next page when they cannot fit the remaining space. An oversized paragraph starts on a fresh page and then splits. No leading blank page is added. |
| Keep with next | Part 1 §17.3.1.15 `keepNext` | Resolve complete chains including the final paragraph. A fitting chain stays together, including collapsed internal paragraph gaps. An oversized chain starts on a fresh page once, then permits breaks; its suffix is not repeatedly moved as another chain. |
| Widow/orphan control | Part 1 §17.3.1.44 `widowControl` | Defaults to on. Choose page fragments with at least two lines when the measured heights permit it. Look ahead across variable-height lines to avoid leaving a final singleton; include paragraph-mark metrics. Explicit off allows ordinary line-by-line pagination. |
| Inheritance and boolean values | Part 1 §17.7 style hierarchy, §17.17.4 common boolean properties | Resolve each property through document defaults, paragraph based-on styles, then direct formatting. These paragraph booleans are absolute, including in styles. Omitted `keepNext`/`keepLines` default off; omitted `widowControl` defaults on. Empty elements and `1`/`true`/`on` enable; `0`/`false`/`off` disable. Invalid values reject import. |
| Explicit breaks | Part 1 §17.3.1.23 `pageBreakBefore`, §17.3.3.1 `br` | Paragraph page-break-before overrides keep-with-next. Authored page breaks split constraint groups, including leading and terminal breaks. Apply keep-lines/widow rules to the portions between authored page breaks. Manual line breaks remain lines of their paragraph. Terminal paragraph-mark and leading-break spacing compatibility behavior is retained. |
| Editing and geometry | Application behavior | Three icon buttons expose names, titles, keyboard activation and `aria-pressed` true/false/mixed states. Selected paragraphs change in one transaction; a selection ending at the next paragraph's start excludes it. Splits inherit flags; merges retain the first paragraph's flags. Undo/redo restores selection and page geometry. Moved lines retain source offsets for caret affinity, hit testing and cross-page selection. |
| Save and reopen | Part 1 paragraph-property order; OPC preservation contract | Write only edited properties as direct boolean overrides in schema order. Retain style references, style bytes, untouched paragraphs and unrelated ZIP parts. Full undo restores every original package part. Browser downloads and Puter mock save/reload reopen with the same flags and page geometry. |

Specification review used the official [ECMA-376 Part 1](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/)
and the Open XML SDK's published element semantics for [keepLines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.keeplines),
[keepNext](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.keepnext),
[widowControl](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.widowcontrol)
and [pageBreakBefore](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.pagebreakbefore).
The review corrected the previous omission of default widow control and covered
oversized-chain fallback and explicit-break precedence. Behavioral regressions
also cover variable-height look-ahead and before-spacing after terminal breaks.
No engine implementation was copied or translated.

`public/fixtures/paragraph-pagination.docx` is generated independently by the
app-authored `--generate-pagination-fixture` mode of
`tools/verify-canvas-docx.py`, using python-docx (MIT, test tooling only). It has
short pages, a two-heading inherited chain, eight kept lines, a five-line widow
case, manual line breaks, bold text and an empty paragraph. It renders as four
pages initially; turning off the headings' keeps produces three. Unit tests
verify per-line page assignments, preservation, defaults and edit transactions.
Browser tests click lines before/after movement, edit across a page boundary,
activate the icons with mouse and keyboard, undo/redo and export `pagination.docx`.
`npm run check:conformance` requires that browser export, independently checks its
text/flags/styles with python-docx, then validates its document/styles/settings
XML against the official transitional XSDs.

**Limits:** When page height and line sizes make two-line fragments impossible,
placement makes progress and relaxes the widow constraint. Oversized keeps split
as specified. Explicit authored breaks take precedence over automatic constraints;
these interactions are behavioral tests, not a claim of reference-exact layout.
Only the supported single-section body paragraphs participate; tables, unsupported numbering,
floating objects, alternate stories and other unsupported editable structures
still reject before attaching a save handler. Font substitution, additional reference
compatibility flags and full reference layout equivalence remain gaps. Schema validity is
not full OOXML, OPC or reference equivalence.

Validation on 2026-09-15: `npm test` passed 1,524 tests across 146 files;
`npm run test:browser` passed 12 scenarios; `npm run check:conformance`,
`npm run build` and `npm run check:licenses` passed. Browser page and toolbar
screenshots were inspected. No dependency or application-license change was made.
The next priority at this checkpoint was bullets and numbering, now covered by
the iteration above. Style editing, tables and images remain next, retaining the
new page-placement contracts.

## Paragraph indents and tab-stop iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Implementation and checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Physical paragraph indents | Part 1 §17.3.1.12 `ind`, §17.7 style hierarchy | Left/right inherit independently. `start`/`end` are LTR aliases, preferred over `left`/`right` at the same level. First-line and hanging are mutually exclusive forms of one signed distance; the nearest declaration replaces that distance, and hanging wins when both forms occur in that declaration. |
| Distances and first lines | Part 1 `ST_TwipsMeasure` / `ST_SignedTwipsMeasure` | Integer twips in the model, including negative left/right indents inside the physical page. Numeric or unit-suffixed distances import. First-line offsets apply once per paragraph; wrapping, manual line breaks and page continuation use the ordinary indent. Empty paragraphs have the same geometry. |
| Custom tab stops | Part 1 §17.3.1.37 `tab`, §17.3.1.38 `tabs`, §17.18.84 `ST_TabJc` | Sets add through defaults, based-on styles and direct formatting. A position replaces the same inherited position; `clear` removes it. Left/start, center, right/end and decimal are implemented. Export emits explicit clears for removed inherited stops, leaving style definitions unchanged. |
| Automatic tabs | Part 1 §17.15.1.25 `defaultTabStop` | Absent setting means 720 twips. Custom stops take precedence; automatic stops resume on multiples of the document interval after the last custom stop. They remain anchored to the text margin, not the previous custom stop or paragraph indent. |
| Hanging-indent tab | Part 1 §17.3.1.38; Part 4 §14.8.3.31 `noTabHangInd` | A hanging indent supplies an implicit left tab at the paragraph's continuation edge, unless the retained compatibility flag disables it. An explicit stop at that position keeps its alignment. |
| Alignment after tabs | Part 4 §14.8.3.21 `forgetLastTabAlignment` | Shape tab fields before aligning the whole line. With this retained flag enabled, omit the gap from the last non-left tab when computing the paragraph-alignment shift. |
| Decimal fields | Part 1 §17.18.84; MS-OE376 §2.1.589 | Align around the first period, including across formatting runs. Without a period, use the end of the first number (before a suffix), or the field's end if there is no number. Other decimal separators/locales remain a stated gap. |
| Character-unit overrides | MS-OI29500 §2.1.43 | Zero character-unit indents disable earlier character-unit indents in the native reference; retain those explicit zeros on edit. Effective nonzero character-unit indents are rejected instead of being approximated as physical distances. |
| Editing and geometry | Application behavior | Tab is one source character and one real layout gap. Carets, selection, hit testing, underline gaps and line metrics use its geometry. Aligned fields reshape as text grows; wrapping resumes at the continuation indent. Indents/custom tabs and the document default can change in one undo transaction. Unchanged mixed fields and exact imported twips survive the dialog. |

Primary references:

- [ECMA-376 publication, Part 1 and Part 4 downloads](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/).
- [Paragraph indentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.indentation?view=openxml-3.0.1).
- [Custom tabs and inheritance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.tabs?view=openxml-3.0.1).
- [Default tab interval](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.defaulttabstop?view=openxml-3.0.1).
- [MS-OE376 decimal-tab interpretation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oe376/8eb0e728-345f-4f7b-bbfa-f37bde9c542e).
- [MS-OI29500 implementation notes, §2.1.43](https://officeprotocoldoc.z19.web.core.windows.net/files/MS-OI29500/%5BMS-OI29500%5D-170919.pdf).

### Preservation, scope and corrections

`public/fixtures/indents-tabs.docx` is generated independently using python-docx.
It includes based-on styles, all four alignments, an inherited tab clear, mixed
bold/italic decimal text, first-line/hanging indents, manual continuation and an
empty paragraph. Browser acceptance edits the first paragraph's indents and tab
positions plus the document interval, checks atomic undo/redo, keyboard Tab,
pointer placement and mixed no-op dialogs, then downloads and reopens the file.
The independent parser verifies the edited XML and untouched style/run semantics.

No-edit exports still preserve every entry's uncompressed bytes. Updating the
default interval changes `word/settings.xml`, preserving its other settings.
If that part is absent, export adds it and its content-type and relationship,
using an unused relationship ID. Paragraph changes preserve unrelated package
parts. XML children are written in schema order; clearing all stops never writes
an empty `<w:tabs/>`, which the transitional schema disallows. The importer
tolerates an existing empty set as adding no stops, without claiming that the
source is schema-valid. Tests reject both empty sets and missing tab positions
as validator self-checks.

The editor supports up to 64 custom stops per paragraph, distances within ±22
inches and a positive default interval up to 22 inches. These are application
limits. Indents must leave writing space inside the physical page. Tab advances
are bounded by the indented right edge; an oversized aligned field cannot move
backwards over its preceding field, and overflow wraps at word/grapheme boundaries.
Exact reference behavior for overflowing/overlapping fields has not been verified.
Tab leaders are supported by the later iteration above. Bar tabs, mirrored
indents and effective nonzero character-unit indents are rejected. Locale-specific decimal separators are not implemented;
the dialog explicitly identifies period alignment. Other existing typography and
pagination gaps below still apply.

The toolbar uses the existing Lucide icons with accessible names, titles and
pressed/mixed states. Tab inserts a tab in canvas and text modes; Shift+Tab, or
Escape followed by Tab, leaves the input. The toolbar also has an Insert tab
button. No new runtime dependency or license file was introduced.

## Page geometry and explicit-break iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Implementation and checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Single-section dimensions | Part 1 §17.6.13 `pgSz`, §17.6.17 body `sectPr` | Import physical width/height in twips (1/1440 inch), with separate orientation metadata. Never rotate dimensions again on import. Letter, A4, Legal and custom sizes; the orientation control swaps the physical dimensions. |
| Margins and gutter | Part 1 §17.6.11 `pgMar`; Part 4 `ST_TwipsMeasure` / `ST_SignedTwipsMeasure` | Independent top/right/bottom/left margins; preserve header/footer distances. Gutter adds to the left, or the top when the source enables `gutterAtTop`. Signed top/bottom distances use their magnitude for body layout because headers/footers are outside this subset. Numeric twips and unit-suffixed mm/cm/in/pt/pc/pi are read. |
| Manual page and line breaks | Part 1 §17.3.3.1 `br`, §17.3.3.4 `cr` | Run-level breaks preserve paragraph identity and text/run formatting. `br` with type `page` advances the page; absent type or `textWrapping`, and `cr`, advance a line. Editing a paragraph may normalize `cr` to equivalent `br`. Column and text-clearing breaks are rejected. |
| Paragraph page breaks | Part 1 §17.3.1.23 `pageBreakBefore`, §17.17.4 on/off properties | Resolve through defaults, paragraph-style chains and direct overrides. Explicit false overrides an inherited true. Already-first-on-page paragraphs do not add a blank page. Undo and mixed selection are supported. |
| Cached pagination hints | Part 1 §17.3.3.13 `lastRenderedPageBreak` | Not treated as authored breaks. No-edit export preserves them; changed exports remove stale hints in the main document. |
| Terminal paragraph mark | Part 4 §14.8.3.38 `splitPgBreakAndParaMark` | Normally a trailing page break does not allocate a paragraph-mark line on the next page. With the flag enabled, that line is allocated. A virtual insertion caret after a trailing break remains available without displacing the following paragraph in the default case. |
| Leading-break before spacing | Part 4 §14.8.3.42 `suppressSpBfAfterPgBrk` | For a paragraph beginning with page breaks, before spacing moves to its first line after the breaks, unless the compatibility flag suppresses it. Both flag values have independently generated fixtures. |
| Editing and save | Application behavior plus ordered `CT_SectPr` / `CT_PageMar` serialization | Page setup is one undo transaction and preserves selection. Invalid or unrenderable settings roll back. Page and manual-line breaks retain one source offset each; keyboard, deletion, cross-break replacement, native input/composition, save and reopen are checked. |

Primary references:

- [Page size and orientation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.pagesize?view=openxml-3.0.1).
- [Page margins](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.pagemargin?view=openxml-3.0.1).
- [Run breaks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.break?view=openxml-3.0.1).
- [Start paragraph on new page](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.pagebreakbefore?view=openxml-3.0.1).
- [Paragraph marks after a trailing page break](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.splitpagebreakandparagraphmark?view=openxml-3.0.1).
- [Spacing after a leading page break](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.suppressspacingbeforeafterpagebreak?view=openxml-3.0.1).

### Preservation and limits

No-edit exports preserve each package entry's uncompressed bytes. A page-only
edit retains paragraphs, unrelated section properties and other package parts;
only changed page attributes are written. Creating `pgMar` initializes all seven
required attributes in schema order. Changing physical paper dimensions removes
an obsolete printer paper-size code. Existing compatibility settings and gutter
placement are retained rather than exposed as editing controls.

Unchanged measurements survive the page-setup dialog exactly, including A4 values
rounded differently by other producers. Imported universal measures are rounded
to the nearest integer twip for layout; their original XML values remain until
that measurement is edited. If page properties are missing, this application uses
Letter, portrait and one-inch body margins, with half-inch header/footer distances
and zero gutter. These defaults are application policy, not universal OOXML defaults.

Supported dimensions are 1–22 inches with at least 1/4 inch of body space in each
direction; these are application limits. Multiple sections, multiple/custom-width
columns, mirrored/book-fold margins, RTL gutters, vertical text, non-top vertical
page alignment, and header/footer references are rejected before editing.

`page-settings.docx` is generated independently with python-docx: landscape A4,
asymmetric margins, a gutter, a page break inside mixed-format text, a manual line
break, and an inherited paragraph page break. Browser acceptance changes it to
portrait Letter, edits margins and breaks, overrides inherited pagination, tests
undo/redo and selection, and downloads/reopens `pages.docx`. The independent parser
checks exact break positions/types, dimensions, margins, paragraph count, styles
and preserved font formatting. `page-breaks-default.docx` and
`page-breaks-compat.docx` independently exercise both compatibility flags.

Corrections from the spec review: distinguish authored breaks from cached hints;
keep paragraph boundaries separate from manual line/page breaks; avoid an extra
paragraph-mark line after a terminal page break by default; postpone before
spacing after leading breaks unless suppressed; preserve orientation separately
from dimensions; and initialize all required attributes when adding margins.

Schema validation now includes document settings. The independent generator fixes
the missing required `zoom/@percent` in python-docx's default template and orders
compatibility elements before `compatSetting`. The existing three fixtures were
regenerated with that settings-only correction; their content and formatting remain
unchanged. A 200-page preview limit stops excessive pasted breaks before canvas
allocation, rolling back the edit without losing the existing document/history.

## Font-formatting iteration

| Feature | Specification basis | Implementation and checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Font size | ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.38, `sz`; Part 4 `ST_HpsMeasure` | Non-complex-script size, 1–200pt in 0.5pt steps. Numeric OOXML values are half-points, so 13.5pt writes `27`. Inherited values resolve before direct formatting. Unit-suffixed universal measures and sizes outside this subset are rejected. |
| Italic | Part 1 §17.3.2.16, `i`, and §17.7.3 toggle properties | The nearest declaration in each based-on chain contributes one toggle at its hierarchy level; a nearest false overrides an earlier true within that chain. Direct false turns italic off. See the numbering iteration's 2016 specification correction above. Document defaults, paragraph-style chains, character-style chains, and direct overrides have regression fixtures. |
| Underline | Part 1 §17.3.2.40, `u` | Supports continuous single underline and explicit `none`. It is an enumerated value, not a toggle-style property. Decorative forms are rejected; RGB/theme single underlines are supported by the later text color iteration. Turning underline off writes `none`, preserving inherited style definitions. |
| Paragraph marks | Part 1 §17.3.1.29, paragraph `rPr` | Empty paragraphs retain size/italic/underline on their paragraph mark. This formatting survives download/reopen and supplies the format for new text. Paragraph mark formatting is separate from ordinary run formatting. |
| Mixed-size line layout | Font metrics and Part 1 §17.3.1.33 line spacing | Each line shares a baseline and takes the maximum ascent/descent of its runs. A terminal paragraph mark contributes to empty/whitespace-only lines, not text-containing lines. Auto spacing scales natural line height; atLeast expands to fit. Exact spacing follows the separately documented reference baseline and ink-overflow behavior. |
| Underline geometry | Bundled Noto `post` table | Position and thickness scale with point size. Underline-only changes do not split shaping groups or alter advance widths. |
| Editing | Application behavior; not prescribed by OOXML | Mixed toolbar states, selected text and future typing, grapheme-safe edits, undo/redo, page-boundary caret movement and repagination are tested. Failed changes that exceed page height roll back atomically. |

Primary references:

- [ECMA-376 official publication and schema downloads](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-376/).
- [Font size](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.fontsize?view=openxml-3.0.1).
- [Italic](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.italic?view=openxml-3.0.1).
- [Underline](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.underline?view=openxml-3.0.1).
- [Line spacing and exact-line placement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.spacingbetweenlines.line?view=openxml-3.0.1).
- [Paragraph mark run properties](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.paragraphmarkrunproperties?view=openxml-3.0.1).

## Corrections made during this iteration

1. Replaced the fixed 26px line box and 19px baseline with the bundled font's
   ascent/descent, scaled by each run's point size. The tests independently read
   the actual TTF tables to verify the constants used by the engine.
2. Corrected exact-height lines: oversized text is bottom-aligned and clipped;
   text with extra room is centered within the line box.
3. Replaced a bold-only style resolver with separate toggle and absolute-value
   rules for font size, italic and underline, including explicit off values.
4. Added paragraph-mark storage so formatting an empty paragraph is saved, rather
   than existing only in temporary typing state.
5. Preserved shaping across underline boundaries and scaled underline geometry
   from the font's `post` metrics.
6. Added rollback when a valid size/spacing combination would exceed a page;
   failed layout cannot leave unsaved model changes behind.

## Repeatable validation

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv-conformance
.venv-conformance/bin/pip install -r tools/requirements-conformance.txt
npm test
npm run test:browser
PATH="$PWD/.venv-conformance/bin:$PATH" npm run check:conformance
npm run build
```

CI installs the same pinned Python packages and runs the conformance command after
browser tests. These are test tools: python-docx (MIT) and lxml (BSD-3-Clause,
with libxml2/libxslt under MIT), not browser dependencies. No new npm dependency
is required. The Noto upright and italic fonts use OFL-1.1; see their provenance.

`check:conformance` requires the browser acceptance downloads registered in its manifest to exist and
checks their expected properties with python-docx. It then validates
`word/document.xml`, `word/styles.xml` and any `word/settings.xml`/`word/numbering.xml` in all fixtures and downloads against
the official, hash-pinned ECMA-376 Part 4 fifth-edition transitional XSDs. A
hash-pinned W3C `xml.xsd` supplies the imported XML namespace declarations. Intentionally invalid font-size and incomplete page-margin elements are rejected
as validator self-checks, along with empty tab sets and missing tab positions.

The validator handles declared `mc:Ignorable` namespaces used by these fixtures.
It does not implement general Markup Compatibility processing (such as
AlternateContent, ProcessContent or MustUnderstand), validate every OPC package
constraint, or certify all untouched package parts. It does not discard arbitrary
unknown namespaces to make validation pass.

### Independent acceptance fixture

`public/fixtures/font-formatting.docx` is generated with python-docx, not the new
engine. It contains an inherited 24pt italic heading with a directly applied
underline, a body line mixing 12pt, 18pt italic/underlined and 13.5pt text, and an
empty 18pt italic/underlined paragraph.

The browser edits the heading to 32pt and explicitly turns italic/underline off,
checks undo/redo, inserts text with the pointer, downloads and reopens the file.
The independent parser verifies the changed heading, unchanged original style,
unchanged mixed body runs, and retained empty-paragraph properties. Browser
geometry tests also compare canvas widths and baselines against native DOM text
and the browser's font bounding-box metrics; tolerances are 0.1px for widths and
1px for metric rounding. This is a browser/font comparison, not a reference comparison.

## Block-control reference probes

`tools/canvas_block_control_fixtures.py` builds the eight `block-control-*.docx`
fixtures using original standard-library OPC/XML, independently of the engine.
They cover body and cell wrappers, tables, nested block/inline controls,
vertical-merge continuation cells, and empty placeholders. The browser exports
are independently checked by `tools/check_block_control_exports.py`, then by
the transitional XSD checker. No third-party document engine is involved.

Native reference probes of these structures confirmed that text edits remove the nearest
temporary wrapper while preserving enclosing wrappers; direct bold and paragraph
alignment preserve wrappers. A body paragraph split removes its block wrapper.
Adding a table row removes a wrapper around that table, whereas a control inside
an existing cell survives and the new cell contains no copied control. Entering
text into an empty placeholder applies its input properties before unwrapping.
The saved reference XML was inspected independently of this engine. Section 17.5.2.43
does not specify the formatting-versus-content distinction in this detail; these
are measured reference behaviors, not a claim that the standard mandates every case.

The native reference rejected a paragraph split inside an intact inline control through both its
range and selection APIs. The editor retains its existing behavior of unwrapping
inline controls when splitting; the nested-inline split test establishes package
integrity and undo, not native reference equivalence for that operation. Block wrappers containing
section properties remain a separate implementation gap; actual nested tables are covered below.

## Block-level bookmark boundaries

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.13.6.1–17.13.6.2 define paired bookmark ends and starts,
including block-level placements in the body, table cells and structured document
tag content. The reader retains these placements and their control ancestry.
A marker after a paragraph includes its paragraph mark; a final-document marker
can therefore lie one position beyond the editor's visible text without creating
an extra paragraph. Markers enclosing a table follow its boundary when rows or
columns change. Markers owned by a cell follow their paragraphs when cells merge.
Formatting, text edits, paragraph splits, search replacement, bookmark rename and
removal, table changes and undo have round-trip tests. Empty block sequences with
no paragraph to anchor a marker remain unsupported.

`tools/canvas_block_bookmark_fixtures.py` authors the five
`block-bookmark-{body,cell,table,final,merged}.docx` fixtures directly as OPC/XML
using Python's standard library, without another document engine or third-party
content. Its independent export verifier checks paragraph-mark ranges, control
retention/removal, merged-cell structure and unchanged unrelated package parts.
The body, cell and merged cases also run through browser download and reopen;
their exports are required by the conformance gate and validated against XSDs.

Native reference probes confirmed that the body/cell bookmark includes the final paragraph
mark before and after typing in a temporary control. The native reference can relocate boundary
markers around the control and use `displacedByCustomXml`; the editor preserves
the range rather than requiring the native reference's rewritten XML arrangement. Directly
reading the browser exports in the native reference confirmed the same marked text and removed
temporary wrapper. Adding a row extends a bookmark enclosing the whole table.
Merging adjacent cells preserves both a cell-owned bookmark and its intact
temporary control; changing the cell containing the control alone is not a
content edit. These are independently measured reference editing behaviors, not
additional normative requirements inferred from the bookmark clauses.

## Bookmarks at table and row boundaries

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.13.6.1–2 allow zero-width bookmark markers directly in
`tbl` (§17.4.38) and `tr` (§17.4.79), as also listed in the Open XML SDK
[bookmark parent documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.bookmarkstart?view=openxml-3.0.1).
The reader now accepts these placements in XML order using the existing paired
marker model. It retains the row/cell boundary, container and original marker
attributes separately from the editable paragraph offset. Leading markers before
`tblPr` also retain that placement. Serialization emits the markers around rows
and cells, rather than moving them into unrelated paragraph content.

Supported cases include starts/ends before, between and after rows or cells;
points, overlapping ranges and ranges crossing between a paragraph and a table;
and boundaries around empty vertical-merge continuation cells or rows. Those
continuations contribute no editable paragraphs, so multiple physical boundaries
can share a text offset while retaining distinct XML positions. No marker
contributes width, ink, wrapping or pagination. Bookmarks *inside* continuation
paragraphs remain unsupported and reject editable open rather than silently
dropping their ranges. Active column-limited bookmarks now use the separate
column-range model described above. Other unsupported containers retain their
own guards.

Structural editing follows the existing editor policy for retained content.
Surviving row/cell boundaries follow their structural neighbor; inserting within
a retained row can extend its boundary, while appending a row after an end marker
leaves that row outside the range. Deleting the neighboring row/cell reattaches
the boundary beside its nearest surviving sibling. If a merge moves existing
paragraphs across a boundary, the marker follows the surviving text range instead;
discontiguous content uses the smallest enclosing contiguous range. A marker
between cells that are merged becomes a paragraph boundary inside the merged
cell. New cells never clone bookmark IDs. These mutation choices are editor
policy, not claims that ECMA prescribes the native reference's exact interactive behavior.

`tools/canvas_table_bookmark_fixture.py` independently generates the original
`table-bookmarks.docx` and `table-bookmarks-merged.docx` OPC fixtures with Python's
standard library. Unit regressions cover the placements above, zero-width layout,
format/text/search edits, paragraph splits, rename/link updates, removal, table
changes, empty continuation row/column edits, malformed markers and byte-identical
undo. A 512-row case checks every bookmark after editing and reopening; boundary
lookup and export use structural indexes instead of rescanning the table for each
marker. Browser tests cover plain-text clipboard interchange, bookmark navigation,
editing, export/reopen and exact undo. The conformance gate independently compares
marker parents/order/attributes, the expected text edit, table properties,
temporary controls and unrelated package parts, then runs schema validation.
Rich clipboard transfer of bookmark/table metadata is not implemented. A fresh reference attempt timed out, so no new reference-equivalence claim is made for
these fixtures or structural edit policies.

## Opposing borders at an explicit empty cell side

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.66 specifies that the opposing cell border is displayed
when either participant is `nil` or `none`. Independent reference probes agree for
horizontal and vertical shared edges, with the `nil` side in either position.
Two `nil` sides have no ink. An opposing omitted/`none` side first resolves its
inherited border, which can also win against `nil`. A `nil` declaration remains
an explicit empty side and does not itself inherit a table border.

This corrects the previous suppression rule taken from
[MS-OI29500 §2.1.169](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/7c791c5d-44c3-4fe8-abdd-8f136761bb93).
That implementation note says `nil` suppresses the conflicting border; the
tested reference behavior contradicts the note and agrees with the ECMA rule for
these cases. The fixtures explicitly request native reference compatibility mode 15.
The native reference's exported PDF contains the green visible or blue inherited shared edge;
its saved Flat OPC retains the original `nil` declarations. This is a measured
discrepancy with the published implementation note, not a claimed divergence
from the base standard.

`tools/canvas_nil_border_fixture.py` independently creates
`public/fixtures/nil-border-conflicts.docx` using standard-library OPC/XML.
Its twelve tables cover both orientations, reversed sides, both `nil`, and
opposing inherited sides. Unit tests check the resolved shared edges, text
editing, round-trip geometry and byte-preserving undo. Browser tests inspect
the actual green/blue pixels on all twelve pages and download an edited file.
The independent export checker preserves all cell/table border declarations,
the expected text edit and unrelated package parts; XSD checks validate the
fixture and browser export. Conflict weights and color tie breaks are unchanged.
Row allocation and compound-border thickness are addressed by the later row-geometry iteration below.

## Table row padding, borders and oversized pagination

This iteration supersedes the earlier row-allocation and oversized-pagination
limitations above. It changes computed layout only: stored row heights, margins,
border declarations, merge structure and compatibility settings remain intact.

| Behavior | Standard and implementation evidence | Supported interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Physical row insets | ECMA-376 Part 1 fifth edition §§17.4.2–5 bottom margins, 17.4.42 `tblCellMar`, 17.4.68 `tcMar`, 17.4.75–78 top margins, 17.4.80 `trHeight`; independent reference probes | Use each physical row's largest top and bottom cell margins, including vertical-merge continuation cells. The top writing inset reserves the row's own top-border width minus half the resolved shared stroke; the bottom inset reserves half the resolved stroke. See the later independent opposing-border probes. A merged owner takes its initial inset from its first physical row and its final inset from its last. These are layout values, not rewritten cell properties. |
| Exact heights | §17.4.80 `trHeight`, §17.18.37 `ST_HeightRule`; MS-OI29500 §2.1.180 and the exact-height probes | Retain the native reference's previously supported addition of the largest bottom margin to an exact declaration. For very short rows, the native reference also preserves a minimum extent for the top border and both vertical margins, as demonstrated by the independent probes under [Table continuation borders and merged-row allocation](#table-continuation-borders-and-merged-row-allocation). These layout calculations leave the stored exact declaration unchanged. Clip text, selections and caret geometry to the visible region, including the physical paper edge. Preserve all hidden source text for editing and export. |
| Border geometry | §§17.3.4 common border properties, 17.4.38–39 `tblBorders`, 17.4.66 `tcBorders`; single, mixed and compound-border probes | Resolve shared horizontal borders before row allocation. Double and triple table borders occupy three and five stroke widths respectively, including their gaps. Reuse the resolved cell borders for final layout; only horizontal edges participate in the preliminary row-height pass. Paragraph-border geometry is unchanged. |
| Fresh-page placement | §17.4.6 `cantSplit`, §17.4.80 `trHeight`; page-edge probes | A minimum-height row reserves the necessary fresh-page space even when splitting is permitted. An oversized minimum fills each physical fragment to the writing-area border, with text determining how many fragments are needed. An oversized exact row keeps one physical allocation, potentially extending beyond the paper, without creating pages solely for the hidden height. |
| Compatibility-dependent headers | §17.4.49 `tblHeader`, §17.4.80 `trHeight`; independently authored mode-14, mode-15 and omitted-setting probes | Modern compatibility omits repeated headers over a physical row whose declared height cannot share the body area with the header, then resumes them for following normal rows. Legacy compatibility keeps the header and lays an oversized minimum row unbroken, clipping overflow. Source headers are retained even when the first body row moves to a later page. |
| Continuing vertical merges | §17.4.84 `vMerge`, §17.4.49 `tblHeader`; merged-oversized and merged-later probes | Reserve a resumed header before flowing continuing merged text. Distribute the merge across its actual physical row rectangles. A normal row before an oversized row can end early on its page; its unused gap must not consume merged-cell text or become part of its painted/hit-test rectangle. Legacy compatibility clips remaining merged source in the first oversized fixed row without enlarging a later row. Modern compatibility can continue into later flexible rows after consuming the fixed row's declared extent, including hidden off-paper source positions; a span ending in an oversized fixed row keeps its remaining overflow there. Physical-page clipping applies to the visible text and editing geometry in both cases. |

**Observed reference deviations and refinements.** Section 17.4.49 specifies header
repetition on each new page occupied by a table; the modern oversized-row probes
demonstrate the native reference omitting those repetitions. Section 17.4.80 describes exact and
minimum row heights in terms of the declared height; the native reference's margin/border
allocation, bounded oversized minimum fragments, and compatibility-dependent
overflow cannot be reproduced by treating that declaration as a simple physical
rectangle across pages. The implementation follows the independently measured
reference behavior while preserving the original declarations. These observations
are specific to the tested features and compatibility settings, not a claim that
all reference pagination behavior is specified by ECMA-376.

`tools/canvas_row_geometry_fixtures.py` builds twenty-six original OPC/XML fixtures
using Python's standard library. The source generators, reproduction steps,
reference version and measurement date are in `tools/row_geometry/README.md`.
`tests/fixtures/row-geometry/provenance.json` records canonical XML-part hashes
of the actual source packages opened in the native reference. Reference JSON records text
baselines, page membership, border rectangles and clipping bounds from native reference PDF
exports; `tools/measure_native_row_geometry.py` independently reproduces it.
No reference measurements are derived from this engine's output.

Unit coverage compares those measurements, checks vertical-merge rectangles,
and exercises editing, export/reopen and package-entry-preserving undo. Browser
coverage includes resumed-header caret placement, merged-cell editing and undo,
physical-page caret clipping, rendering snapshots and a saved/reopened edit.
`tools/check_row_geometry_exports.py` checks the expected edit and preserves all
other paragraphs, table/row/cell/section properties and unrelated package parts.
The standard conformance command includes fixture provenance, this export check,
and the row-geometry fixtures in its XSD validation set.

The existing limits on oversized header groups, merges across a header/body
boundary and unsupported structures remain. These probes do not establish full
reference equivalence for horizontal table placement, arbitrary nested tables,
every combination of compatibility flags, or untested row structures. Schema
validity alone is not evidence of visual equivalence.

## Table continuation borders and merged-row allocation

Relevant ECMA-376 Part 1 clauses are §17.4.38–39 (`tblBorders`), §17.4.66
(`tcBorders`), §17.4.74 (`top`, cell border), §17.4.76 (`top`, table border),
§17.4.75/77 (top cell margins), §17.4.80 (`trHeight`), and §17.4.85
(`vMerge`). The row geometry and compatibility qualifications above still apply.

The following native reference layout choices were measured with independently authored
OPC/XML probes in the native reference, on 2026-09-17. The standard's
border and height definitions do not specify this complete pagination algorithm;
these are recorded native reference behaviors, not additional XML semantics:

- A physical continuation starts with the table's outer top border, overridden
  by the applicable physical cell's top border. It does not automatically use
  the logical internal row border or a merged owner's original top exception.
  Rows below repeated headers share the header boundary instead.
- Both the outer half of the top border and the interior inset contribute to
  text placement. When the physical top border differs from the logical row
  border, row allocation uses the replaced inset too. Unequal top and bottom
  border widths also affect exact-row centerline geometry.
- Physical vertical-merge continuation cells participate in row border insets
  even when their internal horizontal borders are hidden by the merge. Thin
  painted horizontal segments align with the leading edge of the row's widest
  border. Vertical edges reach the exterior corners of a table page fragment.
- Additional merged text extends the span's final flexible row; it is not
  distributed equally across earlier rows. When a following row moves to a new
  page, merged text flows through the actual preceding row boxes and leaves the
  unused page gap empty. It resumes using the continuation row's physical inset.
  A row containing only merge continuations does not move an already-started
  owner solely because of `cantSplit`; a kept heading stays with the first text.
  Existing fixed-height clipping and oversized-row compatibility behavior is
  retained and tested separately.

`tools/continuation_border_fixtures.py` uses only Python's standard library to
generate 25 independent DOCX files under `public/fixtures/continuation-borders`.
They cover borderless controls, equal and unequal outer/internal borders,
minimum and exact heights, repeated headers, owner/continuation border
exceptions, and merged text both within and across pages. No editor serializer
or layout code is used to author those fixtures.

`tools/continuation_heading_fixtures.py` independently authors two additional
fully merged, small-page tables under `public/fixtures/continuation-headings`.
They differ only in row keeping. The native reference keeps the heading and the first cell text
on the same page in both; these references check that relationship without
claiming identical line wrapping from the unit test's synthetic font metrics.

`tools/continuation_exact_fixtures.py` authors 18 short-row probes under
`public/fixtures/continuation-exact`. They demonstrate a reference qualification of
the exact-height wording in §17.4.80: even when `trHeight` requests less, the native reference
preserves enough extent for the top border and both vertical cell margins.
The declared edge extent is therefore the greater of (declared height plus
bottom margin) and (top border plus top and bottom margins). Converting to row
centerlines then subtracts half the top border and adds half the bottom border.
These layout calculations do not rewrite the stored `trHeight` or margins.
The probes cover 1-twip heights, zero and nonzero padding, unequal borders and
12-point ink. Text clipped by the resulting box remains editable and exportable.
This measured reference behavior is explicitly distinguished from the standard's
statement that an exact row has the requested height.
Four of these probes test page boundaries: automatic rows reserve their bottom
border's exterior half when deciding whether the first line fits; a constrained
row may collapse to zero height when its shared top border disappears at a page
cut. The latter still retains all source text in a zero-height clip. The page
probes compare table text and the following paragraph separately from the tall
spacer paragraph's font-dependent baseline distribution.

The references in `tests/fixtures/continuation-borders` come from native reference PDF text
matrices and filled border rectangles. `tools/measure_native_continuation.py`
reproduces them from externally exported `<fixture>-native.pdf` files, using
`pypdf`; it never calls this editor. To reproduce the fixture packages, run
`python tools/continuation_border_fixtures.py OUTPUT_DIRECTORY`, or invoke the
heading/exact generator with its own output directory. To reproduce
measurements, run `python tools/measure_native_continuation.py PDF_DIRECTORY
OUTPUT_DIRECTORY`. Keep those output directories separate from the committed
fixtures and references when checking provenance.

The unit probes compare every visible label's page and relative baseline,
painted border thickness and position, and vertical endpoints on both pages of
the direct-border probes. Layout must leave the table model unchanged. Browser
tests check page-two caret placement, typing, undo/redo, download and reopening.
`tools/check_continuation_exports.py` independently checks fixture provenance
and the seven browser exports, including collapsed-row edits, paragraph/run formatting, table/grid/
row/cell properties, section properties and byte-preserved untouched package
parts. The standard conformance command includes that check and the new source
fixtures in its XSD set. Schema validity is not proof of native reference visual fidelity.

Natural sizing, repeated-header placement and merged-cell reflow share prepared
paragraph segments and their border measurements within a single document
layout. This cache is discarded between layouts and distinguishes the
`suppressSpBfAfterPgBrk` setting. Physical fragment bounds are evaluated on
every pagination pass; editing and subsequent layout cannot reuse old line
measurements. The reflow tests cover changed fragment bounds, compatibility
switches and fresh standalone pagination after measured input changes.
Run formatting is normalized once per source run during paragraph measurement,
while font-slot selection remains per grapheme. Graphemes crossing a format-run
boundary retain the base character's formatting; the next layout recomputes
formatting after edits.

These probes use fixed line spacing and Noto Sans. They do not establish
equivalence for every border style, arbitrary combinations of row/column
exceptions, nested tables, all compatibility settings, or general font fallback.
## Hidden end-of-cell markers

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.21 (`hideMark`) excludes the end-of-cell marker from
row-height calculation. The supported direct `tcPr/hideMark` property uses the
§17.17.4 on/off lexical values: an omitted value enables it, and `0`, `false`
and `off` disable it. Malformed values, attributes, children and duplicates
reject editable attachment. [MS-OI29500 §2.1.134](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/c0865add-b937-497b-8bea-368b654b6329)
also disallows this property in table styles (the referenced §17.7.6.8(b) and
§17.7.6.9(a)); used styles containing it remain unsupported. The older 2007-era
behavior that enables false-valued declarations is not emulated.

Only the final paragraph's end marker loses its contribution to line ascent
and descent through `hideMark`. Independently, the native reference excludes terminal marks
from lines containing text (see paragraph-mark metrics below). Earlier empty
paragraph marks, visible runs, manual breaks, inline
pictures and numbering labels retain their normal metrics. For an entirely
empty hidden final paragraph, the native reference also suppresses before/after spacing and
explicit exact/minimum line height. These are suppressed only in measured
layout; their authored values remain available when text is inserted. Cell
margins and minimum/exact row heights still apply. Nonempty paragraphs retain
their paragraph and line spacing. An otherwise empty automatic row can collapse to zero height. Its
paragraphs and insertion positions remain in the model; the marker's formatting
still supplies the insertion caret and newly typed text. That caret may extend
beyond a collapsed row without allocating row height. This behavior also applies
to vertical-merge owners and repeated header content.

Unchanged cell-property XML is retained through edits and export, including
explicit false values. Inserted rows inherit the property; a new cell without a
source shell serializes the enabled property in schema order. There is no UI
control for authoring or toggling `hideMark` yet. The property does not alter
text copied to the plain-text clipboard; rich table clipboard interchange is
outside this subset.

`tools/canvas_hidden_cell_mark_fixture.py` independently creates
`public/fixtures/hidden-cell-mark.docx` using original OPC/XML and a generated
solid-color PNG, entirely with Python's standard library. Unit regressions cover
mixed text/mark sizes, empty and zero-height rows, earlier paragraphs, manual
breaks, pictures, numbering, vertical merges, repeated headers, margins, row
rules, Boolean values, malformed input, insertion, round trips and undo.
Browser coverage checks actual font geometry, typing into an empty short row,
plain-text copy/paste, export/reopen and byte-identical package parts after undo.
The conformance gate independently verifies the browser edit, table/row/cell
properties, drawing XML and unrelated package parts before schema validation.
Native references are retained in `tests/fixtures/hidden-cell-mark`.
The original fixture omits styles, so the native reference supplies 8pt after spacing and
278/240 multiple line spacing for nonempty paragraphs. The independent
`hidden-cell-spacing-controls.docx`, generated by
`tools/canvas_hidden_cell_spacing_fixture.py`, isolates eight empty hidden-cell
cases: automatic, exact and minimum line spacing with zero or 8pt before/after
spacing. All retain only their 3pt row minimum (plus borders) in the native reference. This
records the native reference's treatment of the empty paragraph under §17.4.21; it is not a
claim that the clause specifies every interaction with paragraph spacing.
Unit tests exercise all eight cases, insertion, export/reopen and exact undo.

## Bookmarks at row and column insertion boundaries

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.13.6.1–2 define `bookmarkEnd` and `bookmarkStart` as
zero-width range markers. The XML records their positions; it does not prescribe
an editor's insertion affinity. The native reference was independently
observed with `public/fixtures/bookmark-insertion.docx`, authored directly as
OPC/XML by `tools/bookmark_insertion_fixture.py`.

When inserting a row below or a column to the right, markers immediately after
the old sibling move past the inserted siblings. A range ending there includes
the new content; a range beginning there still begins at the original following
content. Paired point markers move together. For example, appending a row extends
the bookmark ending after the former last row; inserting a column between A1 and
B1 extends a bookmark from A1 to the start of B1 to include the new cell. Existing
marker IDs, source shells and unrelated package parts remain preserved.

`tests/fixtures/bookmark-insertion/native-ranges.json` records literal marker
positions from the native reference's saved FlatOPC, projected to UTF-16 paragraph-text offsets.
The reference application's automation API can expand a partial-cell bookmark selection to a whole
row; its `Range.Text` is therefore not used as evidence of serialized marker
positions. `tools/measure_native_bookmark_insertions.py` reproduces the reference
from the external reference captures. Prepending probes are retained as observations;
the current insertion controls expose rows below and columns to the right.

The rebaser computes insertion endpoints once per affected row/cell collection,
then reuses them for overlapping bookmarks. Structural repair scans surviving
segments for their endpoints without sorting, and avoids temporary copies of
unchanged marker metadata. Unit and browser regressions compare
all ranges and point positions, exercise bookmark navigation and cell typing,
and verify export/reopen, undo and redo. The conformance gate separately checks
all four browser exports against the native reference's literal markers, inserted text, table
structure and untouched package parts before schema validation.

## Remaining gaps

- Declared WordprocessingML font families and themes now resolve as described
  above. Embedded font loading, reference font substitution, font-native decorations
  and script metrics for other families, complex-script `szCs`/`iCs`, RTL,
  bidirectional text and full Unicode line breaking remain gaps. Other scripts
  may use browser glyph fallback fonts.
- Single-section page geometry, paragraph keeps/widow control, the tab compatibility flags and the two explicit-break compatibility flags
  above are supported. Other reference compatibility flags, document grids
  and precise reference pagination remain unimplemented. The
  editor keeps a blank insertion surface after a terminal page break; its page
  count is an editing preview, not a claim of native reference print-pagination equivalence.
- Imported unsupported formatting may still be retained without faithful
  preview. Horizontal scaling, character spacing, superscript/subscript and manual positioning now
  have the explicit subsets above. The subset gate does not yet
  cover every pre-existing property that may affect text appearance.
- Font size limits and supported underline forms are deliberate application
  limits, not limits imposed by the full OOXML standard.
- Native reference comparisons apply only to the explicitly recorded fixtures and probes.
  No claim of general visual equivalence or complete ECMA-376 conformance is made.

Next iterations should continue adding one bounded feature, testing its specified
semantics independently, and reducing these gaps rather than treating schema
validation alone as completion.

### SVG pictures with automatic dimensions
The MS-ODRAWXML SVG representation can contain a viewBox without explicit pixel dimensions. SVG 2 section 8.12 supplies an intrinsic aspect ratio in this case; CSS Images section 4.3.2 supplies concrete object sizing. The preview fits ratio-only vectors into a 300 by 150 default box, derives one missing dimension from the ratio, and supplies those concrete dimensions only to its isolated decoding copy. Original SVG bytes and both DOCX image representations remain intact. Unsupported active SVG content remains read-only. The independent svg-viewbox-pictures fixture covers ordinary pictures, cropping, groups and shape fills, with browser edit/export/reopen checks.
References: https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG2/coords.html#IntrinsicSizing and https://www.w3.org/TR/css-images-3/#default-sizing .


### Ellipse presets and shape text frames
DrawingML prstGeom (ECMA-376 Part 1 section 20.1.9.18) now supports rect and ellipse without adjustment guides. Ellipse paths use native curves and the standard preset definition's inscribed 45-degree text rectangle. Shape solid fills and outlines resolve untransformed schemeClr references through the document theme and color mapping. Explicit fill/outline properties override shape style references; unresolved theme effects and unimplemented color transforms remain unsupported. Shape fontRef defaults are applied below explicit paragraph and run formatting. Original shape markup remains atomic and unchanged through body editing and export.
Native reference observation: bodyPr (Part 1 section 21.1.2.1.1) describes compatLnSpc and vertOverflow. In independently authored wps:wsp / w:txbxContent probes, the native reference produces identical text positions for compatLnSpc=0 and 1. It clips overflowing text to the text frame even with vertOverflow=overflow, and top-aligns overflow for top, center and bottom anchors. The renderer follows these observed reference rules for Wordprocessing shapes; this is not a claim about DrawingML a:p text. Text frames include half of the outline width. Independent ellipse/rectangle and nonuniform-transform probes, source document hashes and native reference PDFs are in tests/fixtures/shape-text-native. Relevant generators are canvas_ellipse_fixture.py and canvas_shape_spacing_fixture.py. Browser checks cover curves, clipped text, editing/export/reopen and existing group text scaling.



## Nested tables

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.80 (`trHeight`) constrains exact row height. Independent
`nested-clipping-*` probes establish that visible content must satisfy every
containing exact-height cell clip. Preserve source text beneath those clips;
intersect clips for text, selection, nested cell fills and borders, and move
existing clips together with vertically aligned content or repeated headers.
Six clipping source packages and their edited browser exports pass schema checks.
Native reference PDF renders and browser measurements currently agree
within one point for painted vertical bounds; this is not complete pixel equivalence.

**Reference/spec divergence:** §17.4.49 (`tblHeader`) says a leading marked row repeats
on each page displaying that table, without a nested-table exception. Independent
`nested-clipping-header-inner.docx` places a marked row in a two-page nested table.
The explicit compatibility-mode-15 variant confirms the same behavior. The native reference preserves that nested `tblHeader` in its serialized XML but prints it only
on the first page. `nested-clipping-header-outer.docx` confirms that the containing
table's marked row still repeats. `nested-clipping-header-container.docx` confirms
that an outer header repeats its complete nested content, including exact-height
clipping. Rendering follows the native reference while retaining every imported header flag in
the model and DOCX. The comparison records source hashes, reference version/build,
retained flags, page counts and the pages containing each identifying label.
