The clipping/header source probes and reference measurements are now under
`tests/fixtures/nested-tables`, with generators in `tools/nested-table-probes`.
Raw reference captures and measurement tools remain in the sibling work directory.
Complete provenance packaging, remaining nested fixtures, nested
UI behavior, broader regression/performance gates and corpus verification remain
required before promotion. The nested controls now explain non-repeating header
flags and allow their explicit removal; broader layout and performance gates remain.


Nested insertion now accepts a collapsed caret in a cell. The canvas supplies the
resolved spanned-cell width minus effective horizontal writing insets in twips;
the model reserves the new table’s exterior border halves and creates
a child table owned by that cell and splits the surrounding paragraph in one
undo transaction. The trailing paragraph remains in the parent cell. This uses
the table/cell block-content model of ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.4.37 and 17.4.65.
Ten independent-fixture unit cases cover paragraph start/middle/end, two nesting
levels, invalid geometry, round-trip and exact package restoration on undo.
Browser exports independently verify the authored grids against parent-cell
writing widths. This insertion coverage does not complete nested-table authoring
or its remaining UI, broad regression and performance requirements.

**Additional reference/spec divergence:** section 17.4.63 says table percentage widths
use page text extents. Independent `nested-clipping-width-half` and `width-full`
probes show the native reference uses the containing cell's writing width for a nested table.
The same behavior occurs with explicit compatibility mode 15. Source packages,
source hashes, the native reference build/mode, and captured reference PDF/FlatOPC are recorded under
`tests/fixtures/nested-tables`; source generators are in `tools/nested-table-probes`.
The existing recursive layout follows the native reference's parent-relative percentage rule.
The nested control now says "Fit to cell"; Table properties explains percentage
widths and retained header flags. Nested repeat-header authoring is disabled with
an explanatory option; existing flags can be explicitly removed and undone.

**Horizontal border geometry:** twenty independently authored reference probes cover
compatibility modes 12/15, fixed/AutoFit layout, dxa/percentage widths, left/center/
right alignment, thick and asymmetric borders, and zero/wide cell margins.
Nested tables and mode-15 top-level tables align their first row's exterior ink edges within
the writing area and reserve the border halves in the percentage-width basis.
Centering accounts for unequal exterior border widths. Legacy top-level tables
align their grid boundary instead; their percentage basis includes the exterior
cells' effective writing insets. Cell writing insets are at least half their
resolved border widths. This legacy percentage behavior further qualifies the
unconditional page-text-extents wording of section 17.4.63.

The layout and intrinsic-width measurement follow these reference observations.
Original source preferences remain unchanged. Native canvas comparisons pass
all twenty probes with the original strict one-point bound; geometric stroke
comparisons pass with a 0.65-point bound against half-point PDF raster samples.
The previously failing mode-15 UI comparison now passes without changing its
tolerance. The existing AutoFit fixture was separately captured in native reference mode 14:
its first row totals 370.8 points, establishing the corrected legacy expectation.
Raw captures, hashes and source generators accompany the reference fixtures.
These probes do not establish complete reference equivalence for every table:
sparse grids and deeper AutoFit combinations still require broader coverage.

Eight further original `first-row-table-inset` controls establish the first-row
choice for unequal row-side borders: absent/3 pt/6 pt edges, AutoFit and fixed
layout, and left/center/right alignment. Wider later-row borders extend beyond
that alignment rather than shifting the complete table. The width/layout
calculation now uses the first logical row's exterior halves for this modern
alignment policy; legacy percentage-width adjustments remain unchanged.
All 32 independent reference cell origins and twenty border positions are checked
within 0.15 pt in the browser (PDF origins vary by up to 0.13 pt),
including after undo and reopening. The source table properties are preserved.
This is a measured refinement of the native reference's border geometry, not a newly identified
contradiction with the table-border/justification clauses (§§17.4.28, 17.4.38,
17.4.66). Sparse first-row grids remain outside these new controls.


**Nested AutoFit border contributions:** three further independent probes put a
fixed or preferred-dxa child inside an automatic-width parent, including a
three-level hierarchy. The native reference expands each parent to include its children's outer
border halves. Previously the two-level parent was four points too narrow and
the deeper source failed layout. Intrinsic table widths now include those
exterior halves recursively, while retaining the source width preferences.
Geometric and native-canvas comparisons pass against the captured reference bounds;
edited browser exports retain table sizing properties and untouched package
parts. Sources, raw captures, hashes and the reproducible generator are under
`tests/fixtures/nested-tables` and `tools/nested-table-probes`.

## Native font line metrics

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.33 (`spacing`) defines automatic line spacing in
240ths of a line. Native font measurement now retains fractional ascent and
descent rather than using the browser's integer-rounded bounding box at the
requested small font size. A 2048px sample and the same face's CSS normal line
box provide the normalized metrics, including external leading above the
baseline. The bundled Noto font continues to use its existing exact metrics.
Font metric samples are discarded after loading document fonts. These are
layout measurements only; stored font names, sizes and package parts remain
unchanged.

The independently authored `public/fixtures/native-line-metrics.docx` tests
Arial, Times New Roman, Calibri and Courier New at 11, 20 and 38 points with
single automatic line spacing. Native reference PDF/FlatOPC captures and baseline
coordinates are retained under `tests/fixtures/native-line-metrics`, together
with source provenance. All 39 browser baselines differ by less than 0.17pt
from the captured reference PDF. The browser comparison permits 0.25pt for PDF
coordinate rounding and requires the original fonts to be installed; substitutes
cannot validate that reference. Browser coverage also checks editing, complete
undo, export and reopening. This is an implementation of automatic spacing,
not a claimed reference/spec divergence. These probes do not establish all native
fonts, scripts or style combinations.

## Large numbering-label line metrics

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.9.27 (`rPr` in a numbering level) and 17.3.1.33
(`spacing`) supply label formatting and paragraph line spacing. The native reference's automatic
line layout raises the first baseline for a label whose ascent exceeds the body
text ascent, but advances below that baseline using the body text descent.
Including the label descent incorrectly pushes subsequent lines downward.

The independently authored `marker-line-metrics.docx` compares 20pt Symbol,
Arial and Courier New bullets and 20pt Arial decimal labels with 12pt Arial
body text. Native reference PDF and FlatOPC captures are retained under
`tests/fixtures/marker-line-metrics`. All eight body baselines match within
0.11pt; the browser test allows 0.25pt for PDF coordinate rounding and also
checks editing, undo, export and reopening. Existing numbering alignment,
suffix, navigation and round-trip checks remain covered. The specification
does not detail this particular label-descent calculation; this records the native reference's
observed layout behavior rather than asserting an explicit normative conflict.

## SVG XML whitespace declarations

The SVG subset accepts the XML namespace `space` attribute with its two legal
values, `default` and `preserve`, on supported SVG elements. These whitespace
processing declarations do not introduce external references or executable
content. The original SVG bytes remain unchanged. Unknown namespaced
attributes, `xml:base` and invalid whitespace values remain rejected.
`svg-space-pictures.docx`, generated independently alongside the original SVG
fixture, exercises ordinary pictures, group pictures and shape fills. Unit and
browser checks cover rendering, retained source representations, editing and
complete undo; exported packages pass the DOCX schema checks.

## Character spacing on anchored pictures

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.35 (`spacing`) adjusts character pitch; §20.4.2.3
(`anchor`) places floating drawings separately from inline text. Inherited and
direct character spacing on a positioned drawing run is retained through
import, edits and export, without changing the floating image frame. The
inline-picture restriction remains in place. Formatting a selection containing
anchors may change text spacing without rejecting the entire selection.

`anchor-spacing.docx` is independently authored from the page/margin anchor
probe, with inherited +2pt spacing and alternating -1pt direct overrides.
The native reference renders the same eight image frames as the zero-spacing probe;
raw PDF/FlatOPC and sampled image bounds are in `tests/fixtures/anchor-spacing`.
Unit checks cover direct edits, inherited declarations, geometry, round trips
and exact undo. Browser checks cover native image bounds, selection, deletion,
undo and reopening. This confirms ordinary anchor behavior, not a normative
reference/spec divergence. No document-specific positions are introduced.

## Header/footer preview and page fields (in progress)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.10.1 (`evenAndOddHeaders`), §17.10.2
(`footerReference`), §17.10.5 (`headerReference`) and §17.10.6 (`titlePg`)
govern page-story selection. References resolve through internal relationships
and declared part types; first/even/default stories inherit independently.
An absent enabled first/even story is blank unless inherited from the preceding
section. It does not fall back to the default story.

The read-only preview parses ordinary story paragraphs using the document's
styles and paints them at header/footer distances. The field parser retains
simple and complex field XML (§17.16), including split instruction runs and
cached results. PAGE, NUMPAGES and SECTIONPAGES use layout counts; optional
MERGEFORMAT is accepted. Automatic PAGE/NUMPAGES in page stories refresh even when locked; locked SECTIONPAGES retains its cached text (see the reference controls below). Reflow does
not overwrite source field XML or the source package. Paragraph shading and
borders use story coordinates, separately from body selection and hit testing.

Independent source files and native reference PDF/FlatOPC references live in
`tests/fixtures/page-stories`, generated by `tools/page_story_fixtures.py`.
Their deliberately stale cached PAGE value 99 renders as actual 1/2/3 in the native reference
and the preview. Browser tests check all three selection variants, native Arial
footer coordinates, absence of first-page text when appropriate, and exact
original downloads. Coordinate checks require the reference font; text and
preservation assertions also run without it. Unit tests cover relationship
validation, malformed fields, section counts, reflow, and source preservation.
The schema gate now includes header/footer parts and rejects an independently
constructed invalid footer property order. Field-specific reference variations are
documented in the page-field capitalization section below.

This is unfinished rendering support, not editable header/footer support.
The original preview milestone kept all documents containing these references
read-only; later sections document retained body editing, drawings, numbering
formats and table support. Story links, nested fields, more field switches,
and body clearance for tall stories still need implementation and native reference probes.
Additional field switches and complex header content need direct reference comparison. Unsupported
story layout does not prevent the body preview from opening. Story editing,
selection, accessible text, undo and serialization must be completed before
editable attachment is enabled; the workshop agenda remains under review.

## SVG text spacing

[SVG 1.1 chapter 10](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG11/text.html) defines `text`,
positioned `tspan` contents, font selection, anchoring and spacing. Static SVG
text now uses the isolated browser SVG renderer with local font-family lists,
individual font properties, positions, baseline/alignment properties and
character spacing. Original character data, CSS and media bytes are retained.
Text paths, font resources, CSS font shorthand and active/external content
remain outside the validated subset. Text is limited to 100,000 characters;
possible nonbreaking-space preview spans share the existing 20,000-element
budget. Raster fallbacks and relationships remain untouched on export.

Fourteen original controls in `tests/fixtures/svg-text` compare native reference
ink bounds with the preview within one SVG pixel. They establish
Arial fallback for absent/unavailable families, a 12px default size, installed
family selection, bold/italic, positioned spans, anchoring, preserved spaces,
negative/positive letter spacing and combined word spacing. Font defaults are
consumer choices; the SVG font-family initial value is user-agent dependent.
The preview freezes its own defaults rather than inheriting application UI
fonts. Authored installed families retain priority. No font file is installed
or redistributed by the implementation.

**Native reference compatibility divergence:** SVG's inter-character spacing description
does not exempt ordinary spaces. Native reference PDF text advances omit the letter-spacing
increment after ordinary spaces, while retaining it after nonbreaking spaces.
The controls include both, plus preserved repeated spaces and centered/end
anchors. The preview compensates ordinary word-space advances and restores
nonbreaking-space advances in temporary spans; automatic kerning remains on.
The underlying SVG is never rewritten. Equivalent XML CDATA paints identically.
The controls do not establish every SVG text property, script or font metric.

## Thin SVG strokes in native reference exports

SVG 1.1 §11.4 defines fractional `stroke-width` in user units; zero means no
stroke. See the [W3C stroke-width definition](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG11/painting.html#StrokeWidthProperty).
The `asvg:svgBlip` extension supplies the SVG representation alongside its
retained raster fallback. The workshop agenda exposed a visible divergence:
its SVG rectangle has a 0.5-unit black stroke, but the native reference's PDF export
draws a heavier outline than the browser's standard SVG renderer.

Six independent `svg-strokes*.docx` probes demonstrate the same behavior for
rectangles, paths, lines and circles, with explicit dimensions, viewBox-only
sizing, larger intrinsic dimensions and uniform group/viewport transforms.
The native reference's PDF forms impose a 0.14 internal-unit floor on positive strokes;
geometry converts at 0.12 internal units per intrinsic SVG CSS pixel. The
resulting minimum is 7/6 intrinsic pixels, applied after uniform transforms.
`tests/fixtures/svg-strokes` retains source hashes, raw PDF/FlatOPC captures
and widths extracted directly from the PDF operators. This proves the export
behavior; native reference screen rasterization has not been independently measured.

The preview follows these reference widths. A temporary isolated SVG tree
resolves the authored cascade, inheritance and uniform transforms. Only the
decoded preview changes: SVG bytes, PNG fallbacks, relationships and drawing
XML remain intact. Positive widths above the floor, zero widths and absent
strokes remain unchanged. Browser tests compare normalized widths and painted
ink, then edit, undo and reopen files while checking retained package parts.
Existing SVG picture/group/fill and unsupported-resource tests also pass.

Anisotropic/skew transforms, non-scaling strokes and unresolved percentage/calc
widths retain their previous stroke rendering pending direct reference probes.
The viewport correction below does not claim complete SVG equivalence or
complete the workshop review without rechecking that original.

The original controls in `tests/fixtures/svg-viewport-geometry` now explain
the native reference's size-dependent SVG inset. Nine controls cover small, medium, fractional,
odd, overflowing, shifted-viewBox, physical-unit, ratio-only and percentage
geometry in full, cropped, grouped and shape-fill placements. Four retained
nested metafiles were extracted from the native reference's
[Range.EnhMetaFileBits](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vba/api/word.range.enhmetafilebits)
output using the documented
[EMF+ image](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-emfplus/02c80141-208e-4335-ad51-190b40a1802c)
and [metafile](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-emfplus/503573f8-791a-469c-a2af-d4b570585944)
structures. These native bytes provide the frame and reference-device values;
they are not fitted screenshot offsets.

The captured reference device is 4700×6200 pixels and 199×262 whole millimeters.
[MS-EMF 2.2.9](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-emf/e4a35c41-e8e3-43f9-bc07-a18e99bb866d)
defines its physical frame in 0.01 mm. For each axis, the captured frame rounds
the half-pixel bounds downward to that grid; the native reference's EMF+ draw source includes
one final device pixel after conversion back. The shared SVG preview uses this
recorded native reference device profile. Other printer/device profiles are not
claimed to have identical rounding. The fractional control also proves integer
intrinsic sizing before fitting the unchanged viewBox: 120.5×80.25 becomes a
121×80 viewport, with the authored viewBox retained.

The correction transforms the root viewport after native sizing and retains
the authored viewBox, percentage geometry and stylesheet tree. A viewport clip
prevents overflowing artwork from painting the new margin. Resource IDs avoid
collisions, and source SVG/package bytes remain untouched. Authored root clips
or transforms, and ratio-only coordinates whose native raster size would exceed
the existing image budget, retain their previous decoding/composition path.
This is a rendering compatibility correction, not a change to DOCX drawing
extents, embedded artwork, or the general EMF decoder.

The original `svg-fill-viewport.docx` and `svg-opacity-values.docx` controls
also reproduce the viewport inset with filled geometry and an opacity
quantization difference. SVG 1.1 §14.2 and §14.5 specify alpha compositing
and object/group opacity; the independent reference PDF captures truncate the
tested simple fill opacities to 8-bit alpha, including .1 to 25/255 and .5
to 127/255. See the [SVG compositing specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG11/masking.html#ObjectAndGroupOpacityProperties)
and `tests/fixtures/svg-fill-viewport/README.md` for the control geometry,
tested declaration forms and reference limitations.

Solid, unstroked vector shapes now combine resolved object opacity, fill
opacity and solid-color alpha before truncating to a byte in the temporary
preview tree. The original SVG/package remains untouched. The separate
`svg-opacity-composition.docx` control proves that .9 object opacity times
.9 fill opacity becomes 206/255; independently quantizing each declaration
would incorrectly yield 205/255. Attribute, inline-style, stylesheet and
inherited fill-opacity declarations use the isolated browser CSS cascade.

The same control establishes a different reference path for translucent ancestor
groups and translucent shapes with both fill and stroke: the PDF contains
raster images instead of vector fills. Those paths, gradients and SVG text
retain their existing rendering pending separate reference-backed corrections.
The viewport inset and small color-channel differences from PDF color/alpha
rasterization remain open. This is an opacity correction, not a claim of
complete SVG or native reference screen equivalence.


## Relationship-resolved Document Settings

ECMA-376 Part 1 §11.3.3 identifies the Document Settings part through the
implicit settings relationship from the Main Document part; its filename is
not fixed. Settings content is defined in §17.15. The importer now resolves
that internal relationship before reading compatibility mode, default tab
stops, theme language/color mapping, protection and even/odd story selection.
Missing, external, duplicate or wrong-root settings are rejected for editable
import; best-effort preview remains available. Unrelated conventional files
are not treated as settings.

Default-tab edits update the original related part without changing its path
or relationship. If no settings relationship exists, a new part is created
at a free name without overwriting orphaned package content. Untouched parts
and exact undo remain byte-preserved. The schema gate validates declared
Settings parts regardless of their filename.

The independent settings-location fixture places Settings outside `word/`.
Native reference captures and provenance are in `tests/fixtures/settings-location`.
Unit regressions cover relative/absolute targets, protection, theme settings,
footer selection, malformed references, edit/export/reopen and exact undo.
The browser regression compares tab and table positions with the native reference, changes
tab spacing and body text, and verifies exports and undo. This corrects a
package-resolution bug, not a reference/spec divergence. Broader settings content,
Strict OOXML and alternative Main Document locations are not added here.


## Baselines within automatic line spacing

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.33 (`spacing`) and §17.18.48
(`ST_LineSpacingRule`) define automatic line height in 240ths of the single
line calculation. They do not prescribe an internal baseline distribution.
Independent reference probes show that enlarged automatic multiples retain the
natural ascent, with extra leading below the baseline. Multiples below one
scale the ascent by the same fraction as the line advance. The previous
centering rule moved glyphs down incorrectly for enlarged multiples.

The layout now follows that native reference placement while retaining line advances,
wrapping, page allocation and source positions. Painting, caret and selection
geometry consume the same corrected baseline. Exact and minimum spacing keep
their existing rules; exploratory reference probes show those also need further
baseline review, so this correction does not claim complete line-spacing
fidelity. It introduces no new font measurement or layout passes.

`automatic-line-baselines.docx` is independently authored XML with twelve pages
covering two native fonts/sizes and six automatic multiples. Native reference PDF/FlatOPC,
hashes and extracted coordinates are retained in
`tests/fixtures/automatic-line-baselines`. Browser checks compare 48 baselines
within 0.2pt and exercise spacing changes, export, undo and reopen. Unit checks
cover line advances and caret/hit testing alongside the existing spacing,
pagination and baseline-shift regressions.


## Row writing insets at conflicting horizontal borders

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.38 (`tblBorders`), 17.4.66 (`tcBorders`), 17.4.74
(cell `top`), 17.4.68 (`tcMar`) and 17.4.80 (`trHeight`) distinguish authored
cell borders, margins, row heights and shared-edge border conflict resolution.
Independent reference probes show that the row reserves its own effective top-border
width for text placement even when a different opposing border wins painting.
With coordinates on the shared stroke's centerline, the top inset is the top
margin plus that row's top-border width minus half the winning stroke width.
The top inset is also at least half the winning stroke width, keeping text
outside its ink when padding is narrow. Existing zero-margin mixed/column
border reference probes establish this floor. The bottom inset remains the bottom
margin plus half the winning stroke width.
Inherited table inside borders participate; absent/nil sides reserve zero.

The layout now makes this distinction before allocating rows and merged cells.
The existing reference-proven exact-height border/padding floor is retained, and
collapsed exact rows retain a zero-height clip even with a negative writing
inset. Border conflict winners, source XML and editable content are unchanged.
No additional border-resolution or pagination pass is introduced.

Two manually authored documents cover 18 pages of unequal opposing borders,
nil/absent sides and an omitted header grid column. Raw reference captures, source
hashes and 90 text positions are retained in `tests/fixtures/row-border-insets`.
Browser checks compare those positions and exercise body edits, download,
undo and reopening. Existing row-height, exact-row, continuation and merged-row
regressions cover interactions beyond the new isolated probes. This records
the native reference's measured placement, not a claimed conflict with an explicit standard
formula for the writing inset.

Additional independent `compound-row-insets.docx` probes cover single,
double and triple 2pt borders with automatic, minimum and exact body-row
heights. All 45 short-row reference baselines match within 0.12pt. The separate
eight-versus-nine-page repeated-header regression was subsequently traced to
table-wide style borders and physical bottom-border reservation (see below).
The original browser page-count assertion now passes; short-row results alone
do not establish correct continuation geometry or complete border painting.


## Font-table alternative names

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.8.3.1 (`altName`) provides alternate names to try when the
primary font is unavailable. The related Font Table part is resolved through
its internal relationship, regardless of filename. The importer retains its
single-name alternatives separately from authored run/style font names.
Available primary fonts keep precedence; available declared alternatives are
used before the existing bundled fallback. The original font table and source
font declarations remain unchanged on save.

Font availability is browser-local. Alternative selection belongs to each
rendering context, so independent documents can map the same missing name to
different installed fonts. Body text, paragraph marks, list markers, page
stories and decoded drawing text use the same choice for measurement and
painting. The font toolbar names the actual substitute. No font download,
font redistribution or package-wide run rewriting is introduced.

Two independent reference probes and references in `tests/fixtures/font-alternatives`
cover absent primary fonts, available primary precedence and italic table text.
Browser checks include source preservation, edits, undo, reopen and isolated
contexts. The schema gate now validates declared Font Table parts too.

MS-OI29500 documents session-dependent substitution metadata in
[MS-OI29500 §17.8](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/09b83e15-30de-481d-8ddf-777107d4122e)
and single-value treatment of `altName` in
[MS-OE376 §2.1.264](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oe376/6e8d1c56-bd7c-49fd-bf54-6fba80806032).
This implementation uses a single name per declaration and retains source
metadata rather than reproducing the native reference's session-dependent rewrites. The final
probes use distinct short primary names. Long names, comma-separated lists,
embedded fonts and metric-based substitution when both names are unavailable
remain outside the verified reference-matching subset.

## Reflected pictures inside drawing groups

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.7.6 (`xfrm`), Annex L.4.7.3 and §20.2.2.1
(`blipFill`) apply to pictures inside retained reference drawing groups too.
`flipH` and `flipV` accept XML boolean spellings and reflect the cropped
picture about its frame center before ancestor group scaling. Transparent
crop margins reflect with its content; source crop edges and authored XML
are retained unchanged. Both axes can be combined, including through nested
groups with unequal scales and nonzero child coordinate origins.

The reader delegates picture validation to the existing picture importer;
the scene painter now applies those validated flip flags. Group and shape
reflections and nonzero rotations still reject rather than opening an
incorrect editable rendering. This change does not add transform controls
for retained atomic drawings or change their layout extents.

The manually authored `group-picture-flips.docx` and independently captured
references in `tests/fixtures/group-picture-flips` agree on 96 interior
color samples covering the combinations above. Browser checks cover actual
page pixels, editing, retained package parts, exact undo and reopening. Unit
tests retain malformed-flag/rotation guards, and schema checks include both
the ECMA fallback view and supported reference drawing-extension view. No reference
divergence was observed in these cases.

## Drawing theme matrices and solid-color transforms

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.4.1.14 (`fmtScheme`), §20.1.4.1.13 (`fillStyleLst`),
§20.1.4.1.21 (`lnStyleLst`), §20.1.4.1.7 (`bgFillStyleLst`) and the
`lnRef`/`fillRef` style-matrix references provide inherited drawing appearance.
The reader resolves the related theme part, applies reference colors to
`phClr`, and merges explicit line attributes and fill/dash/join choices over
the selected line style. Direct shape fills take precedence over theme fills.
Index zero suppresses the corresponding inherited style; background fills
use indices above 1000. Source theme and drawing markup remain untouched.

Supported solid DrawingML colors are sRGB and resolved scheme colors with
ordered `shade`, `tint`, `lumMod` and `lumOff` transforms (§20.1.2.3).
Shade/tint mix in linear RGB, while luminance operations preserve HSL hue and
saturation. Values clamp after each operation; channels round to 8-bit only
at the resulting paint-color boundary. This intentionally does not reuse
the separate WordprocessingML `themeTint`/`themeShade` interpretation.
Native precision controls establish linear-RGB quantization to 1/100000 units
at input and output, with floating-point channels retained between ordered
transforms. This resolves all 96 `drawing-luminance-precision` swatches and all
96 independently authored `drawing-color-sequences` swatches exactly. The
second set distinguishes boundary quantization from quantizing between every
operation, which produces a wrong result. Neutral HSL/modifier/literal controls
also rule out a universal half-byte rounding rule: their thresholds move in
both directions according to linear-channel precision. The diagnostic now
passes both sets with source/PDF hash verification. Literal RGB bytes remain
unchanged. This is an observed reference conversion detail within the color model;
no normative contradiction is asserted. Direct `hslClr` import and the separate
WordprocessingML theme-byte precision issue remain outside this correction.
Centered, single, flat-capped solid outlines support round, bevel and miter
joins. Miter bounds reserve their allowed stroke extension to prevent clipping.

The independent `shape-theme.docx` and native reference captures in
`tests/fixtures/shape-theme` verify reference-color substitution, inherited
fill/line appearance, partial line overrides, explicit noFill and transform
order. Following the linear-RGB quantization correction, browser probes compare
all 24 interior colors exactly and verify editing, source retention, undo and
reopening. The unit oracle uses those retained reference PDF samples, including
#194D7F for reversed luminance transforms, and checks the capture manifest.
Vector-edge antialiasing is not claimed to be bit-identical to canvas
rasterization. Source and browser exports pass the ECMA and supported
MS-ODRAWXML schema views. Gradients, active theme effects, other color spaces
and unsupported transforms still reject rather than silently changing pixels.

The independent `shape-display-resolution` fixture verifies 0.5pt vector
outlines (20.1.9.6, `ln`) at device scale 4. Three native 384dpi profiles retain
fully opaque stroke centers. Drawing scenes now select display/zoom resolution
instead of enlarging fixed-2x previews, restoring native contrast without
changing physical pen widths. The 2x path remains for ordinary displays;
line ends, compound/picture outlines, patterns, text and shadow layers scale
consistently. Original drawing geometry, pagination and DOCX bytes are retained.
Each scene reuses one current bitmap and closes it on replacement/disposal.
Existing 8192px/16MP surface and 64MP session limits remain; optional upgrades
fall back to the baseline when the session budget rejects them. Zoom, resource
fallback, disposal, all 54 pattern presets at scale 4, and editing/export/undo/
reopen have regressions. Separate 3D-picture preview resolution is unchanged.
Rotated controls retain native visual evidence; numeric profiles cover the
unrotated edge. This is not a reference/spec divergence. See the fixture README
and retained reference PDF for provenance and sampling limits.

### Table-wide style cell borders and page-cut writing space

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.7.6.9 permits `tcBorders` in table-wide style cell
properties. The native reference ignores these declarations, as documented by
[MS-OI29500 §17.7.6.9](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/9e742550-b438-4b9d-9606-4ae34d83830f).
The importer follows this reference divergence while preserving the original
styles part. Effective sides use table `tblBorders` (§17.4.38) and direct
cell `tcBorders` (§17.4.66). Other supported style cell properties still
inherit normally. Conditional table styles remain a separate unsupported case.

Physical row continuations reserve the full bottom-border ink inside the
page writing area; their table-level fallback is the exterior bottom side,
not `insideH`. Logical shared row boundaries retain their half-width allocation.
The independent `style-cell-borders.docx` and native reference PDF/text origins in
`tests/fixtures/style-cell-borders` cover the divergence and ten-page long-row
flow. Existing short-row, compound-border and continuation references remain
regression checks. Remaining mixed-border fixture offsets are recorded in the
new reference README rather than being hidden by page-count checks.

### Continued row bounds, paragraph after-spacing and shading edges

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.6 (`cantSplit`), 17.4.80 (`trHeight`), 17.4.84
(`vMerge`), 17.4.32 (cell `shd`), 17.3.1.33 (`spacing`) and 17.3.1.9
(`contextualSpacing`) provide the source constraints. Native reference probes
in `tests/fixtures/row-fragment-ends` establish the physical allocation:
an ordinary split row ends below its fitted text, nested content, retained
paragraph after-spacing and cell padding. Adjacent and merged cells share that
edge. A declared minimum remains a lower bound; exact/oversized constrained
allocations retain their existing clipping behavior.

The paragraph paginator reserves fitting after-spacing with the final cell
paragraph line and exposes its effective amount to row geometry. Contextual
suppression between matching paragraphs within a cell is retained. Body-page
after-spacing suppression remains unchanged. Cell backgrounds paint between
the leading horizontal ink edges of the row, including when a neighboring
cell has the widest border.

Browser references verify numbered text flow, border/fill extents and round
trips for long rows, minimum heights, a bottom-aligned neighbor and vertical
merges. The reference README explicitly records unresolved merged-neighbor
baseline offsets, contextual spacing at cell boundaries, and native reference clipping
when paragraph after-spacing is larger than a page. These limited corrections
do not establish complete fidelity for those separate cases.

### Conditional table styles

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.55, 17.7.6 and 17.18.89 describe conditional table
formatting. `table-style-regions.js` supplies XML-independent region selection
and property-group inheritance. The importer applies supported conditional
paragraph/run declarations, cell shading, borders, margins and alignment.
The region geometry and paragraph cascade are refreshed after row/column
insertion and deletion, merge/split, and header edits. Direct cell declarations
remain separate from inherited values. Style parts and retained source
declarations are preserved during unrelated edits. The implementation follows
the MS-OI29500-documented deviations: omitted tblLook is 04A0, omitted band sizes are
zero, column bands override row bands, row edge formatting overrides column
edges, and wholeTable conditional properties are ignored. Source declarations
will remain intact rather than being rewritten to those effective defaults.

The manually authored `conditional-table-styles.docx` and the installed reference's
15-page PDF establish 374 observed cell text colors, shading fills and bold
states. They also establish firstRow across leading header rows, positional
selection despite contradictory cnfStyle, band offsets only for declared edge
regions, and replacement of present regional property groups across basedOn.
The fixture README links the MS-OI29500 normative variation notes and records
the exact coverage. Unit/browser checks verify the effective colors and fills,
structural edits, export/reopen and undo. A separate six-page reference
checks region border geometry and 96 cell text origins. The native reference's column-style
insideH rules paint without contributing their width to the next row's own top
inset; row-oriented conditional rules do contribute. The model preserves that
distinction without materializing it as direct cell formatting.

Conditional trPr properties and conditional table properties beyond borders,
cell margins and shading remain guarded. Diagonal visible borders retain the
existing guard. This is not complete table-style conformance: the original
color fixture exposes an unresolved 10pt/12pt reference font normalization; upper
vertical border colors in successive headers/bands and crossing-stroke color
precedence still differ. The full references retain those mismatches.
Conditional column borders at page cuts and additional omitted-grid/vertical
merge combinations need independent reference comparisons. Existing table editing
and pagination regressions remain part of the verification suite.


## Shape editing locks

ECMA-376 Part 1, DrawingML nonvisual properties (§20.1.2.2), `a:spLocks`,
`CT_ShapeLocking` and `AG_Locking` (also checked against the supplied strict
RELAX NG schema), within MS-ODRAWXML `wps:cNvSpPr`.

The retained shape reader accepts empty locks and the standard `noGrp`, `noRot`,
`noChangeAspect`, `noMove`, `noResize`, `noEditPoints`, `noAdjustHandles`,
`noChangeArrowheads`, `noChangeShapeType`, and `noTextEdit` boolean flags.
Shapes are immutable atomic drawings, so their geometry and internal text cannot
be modified. False `noSelect` is supported; true `noSelect` retains the read-only
guard because selection is still available. Unknown/qualified attributes, invalid
booleans, non-whitespace text, duplicate locks and extension children are guarded.
Original lock XML survives surrounding edits, export/reopen and full undo.

Independent fixture: `public/fixtures/shape-locks.docx`, generated from original
XML by `tools/canvas_shape_locks_fixture.py`. Locked/unlocked reference PDF references
and their comparison are in `tests/fixtures/shape-locks`. Unit and browser tests
cover the supported restrictions and preservation. Custom geometry support is described below; page-story drawings still omit
header divider lines in a corpus birthday card.


## Custom DrawingML geometry guides

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.9.8–12 (`custGeom`, connection sites and guides),
§20.1.9.22 (shape text rectangle), §20.1.10.27 (guide formulas), and
Annex L.4.9.4. Guide declarations are evaluated in order after adjustment values.
All 17 formula operators are implemented, including trigonometric angles in
60,000ths of a degree. Unknown/forward references, duplicate or reserved names,
incorrect arity, nonfinite/excessive results and more than 10,000 guides are
rejected before editable import. Undefined arithmetic such as division by zero
remains guarded rather than guessing the native reference's recovery behavior.

Shape-space built-ins supply dimensions, centers, standard width/height/short-side
fractions and angle constants. Numeric or guide-based move/line coordinates are
resolved into each path's own grid before scaling. Guide-based text rectangles
use shape coordinates and are normalized for the existing text layout. Connection
sites validate their angle and position references but add no painted ink;
retained atomic drawings preserve their XML. This does not implement connector
routing or adjustment-handle editing. Nonempty adjustment-handle lists, unsupported
preset geometry and curved/arc path commands remain guarded.

**Native reference behavior:** the spec describes `at2 x y` using `arctan(y/x)`. The native reference's
independent quadrant probes give 135 degrees for (-1,1) and -135 degrees for
(-1,-1), requiring quadrant-aware `atan2(y,x)`. Resolved path points round to the
nearest integer grid coordinate, with ties away from zero; intermediate guide
values retain fractions. The spec does not spell out this rounding stage.
The probes distinguish a small 180-unit grid from EMU-sized paths and include
-0.5, -1.5, -2.5 and -3.5 path positions. No template-specific values are used.

Empty `a:headEnd`/`a:tailEnd` now use the `CT_LineEndProperties` default type
`none`. Visible arrowheads remain guarded. Independent source fixtures are
`custom-geometry-guides.docx` and `custom-geometry-negative.docx`; their original
XML generator, reference PDFs, extraction script and references are included. Browser
checks compare 40 bar extents, the text rectangle's horizontal origin, editing,
undo, export and reopen. Unit tests cover formulas, order, guards and exact part
preservation. The corpus candle artwork now renders; header fold lines, full
raster equivalence and complete document editing remain unverified.


## Independent table row justification

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.26–28 (`jc` in table-property exceptions, row properties,
and table properties), §17.18.45 (`ST_JcTable`). LTR rows support left/start,
center and right/end independently within the available page or containing-cell
writing area. Direct row alignment overrides `tblPrEx`; direct table alignment
outweighs row alignment inherited from a table style. With no direct table `jc`,
the inherited row alignment remains effective. The independent reference probe
verifies these precedence cases; no template-specific alignment rule is used.

The shared column-width calculation remains intact. Row origins are positioned
individually and horizontal border conflicts use physical intervals when origins
differ, so disjoint row borders do not suppress each other. Nested tables use the
containing cell's writing area. Imported alignment markup and exceptions remain
intact through text/structural edits and undo. New rows retain their source row's
alignment. An explicit table-alignment command applies to every row, including
inherited or direct overrides, and writes row properties in schema order.

Table Properties displays Mixed when row alignments differ. Applying unchanged
properties preserves that state; choosing an alignment applies it to all rows.
Existing homogeneous tables retain their usual controls. Width-only changes do
not reset row alignment. Regressions cover clicking text in shifted rows,
unchanged Apply, insertion, export/reopen and exact full undo.

Independent fixture: `public/fixtures/table-row-alignment.docx`, authored by
`tools/canvas_row_alignment_fixture.py`; native reference PDF and 36 horizontal text origins
are in `tests/fixtures/table-row-alignment`. All sampled horizontal origins match
within 0.3pt. This is not a claim about font rasterization or vertical baselines.
Vertical merges spanning differently aligned rows remain guarded, and Merge
Below is unavailable until those rows have the same alignment. RTL/bidi tables,
conditional row properties and other unsupported table-property exceptions are
not enabled by this change. A corpus card's picture metadata is supported
below. The earlier continued-row spacing suspicion came from a cropped reference
image and was disproved by the full reference PDF coordinates.

### Shadow obscuration metadata in picture and shape properties

MS-ODRAWXML [§2.3.1.12, shadowObscured](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-odrawxml/ee983459-9592-43f9-b312-9e66f3a89fc5)
and [§2.3.3.40, CT_ShadowObscured](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-odrawxml/5f9f9e60-9290-4a68-b61f-13807194e80b)
define the flag inside `a:extLst/a:ext` with URI
`{53640926-AAD7-44D8-BBD7-CCE9431645EC}`. It controls obscuration of an existing
shadow and does not create a shadow. The currently published schema defaults
the optional `val` boolean to false; the importer preserves its original value
or omission rather than materializing the default.

Shadow-free pictures (including grouped pictures) and WPS shapes accept and
retain this extension. The namespace, URI, boolean lexical value, attributes,
child structure and duplicates are checked. Visible unsupported effects and
unknown extensions still prevent editable import. This does not declare the
entire a14 namespace understood for MCE or enable arbitrary shadow rendering.

The original `shadow-obscured.docx` fixture exercises direct and grouped
pictures, shapes and both XML Schema boolean spellings. Installed reference exports
with and without these flags have identical pixels on both pages. Unit/browser
regressions cover source preservation, transforms, surrounding edits, undo and
export/reopen. `check-docx-schema.py` additionally validates every flag against
the hash-pinned published declarations in a temporary cache, including retained
MCE branches. See `tests/fixtures/shadow-obscured` for reference evidence.

### Inline drawings wider than the paragraph

ECMA-376 §20.4.2.8 (`inline`) places drawings in text flow; §20.4.2.7 (`extent`)
supplies their declared size. The native reference's overflow behavior was established with the
independent `oversized-inline.docx` fixture: body paragraphs and fixed table
cells, left/center/right alignment, text before/after and nonzero indents.
Oversized drawings keep their dimensions on a separate line at the left indent.
Body pictures extend beyond the text area; table-cell picture ink is clipped at
the cell edge. Following spaces start the next line.
No explicit contradictory specification rule was identified.

The layout scanner now accepts these unbreakable objects without rejecting the
document. Existing non-image text-width and page-height guards remain intact.
Overflowing drawings retain their original package dimensions; hit targets and
selection follow the visible cell intersection. Page and row clipping also apply. The
six reference picture origins and dimensions match within 0.1pt. The reference does
not certify font-dependent vertical baselines or every pagination combination.

The fixture and native reference PDF are documented in `tests/fixtures/oversized-inline`.
The PDF placement matrix alone does not describe visible ink: the three cell
pictures have 234-point extents but only 180 visible points. The recorder now
checks rendered artwork pixels as well as matrices, correcting the earlier
incorrect claim that the pictures remained visible in the neighboring cell.
Regressions exercise visible-edge selection and rejection of hidden hits, editing, image
rotation, full undo, export/reopen and preservation. Browser/schema checks also
revisit the third birthday card's bookmarks and pictures. That card now opens
editable with its patterned artwork. All ten painted text origins match the full
reference PDF within 0.2pt, including the Title style's existing 3pt raised-text paint
transform. Comparing an unshifted line baseline had incorrectly suggested a
title discrepancy. See the corpus review for the corrected reference comparison.

### Wide markup-compatibility trees

ECMA-376 Part 3 §§7.5–7.7 and §§9.3–9.4 define selection and processing of
alternate content. A wide drawing previously caused `activeDescendants` to pass
its complete descendant array as arguments to `push`, exceeding the JavaScript
argument limit and preventing even a read-only preview.

An iterative traversal now collects active elements in the same document order,
checks compatibility attributes on active nodes/containers/selected branches,
and excludes inactive branches. Unknown active `MustUnderstand` namespaces,
unsupported `ProcessContent`, malformed alternatives and unsupported selected
features retain their existing guards; the importer never silently selects a
different representation after a selected branch fails.

The independent `large-drawing.docx` contains ten 7,001-command nonpainting paths
within an otherwise ordinary grouped drawing. It reproduced the old exception,
opens editable with the fix, and was opened/exported by the installed reference. Native
browser regressions verify preservation of all paths and alternatives through
surrounding edits, export/reopen and complete undo. See
`tests/fixtures/large-drawing`. This is a loading-correctness fix, not a change
to drawing geometry, supported effects, or existing path-command limits.

### DrawingML quadratic and cubic curves

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.9.7 (`cubicBezTo`) and §20.1.9.21 (`quadBezTo`)
supply respectively two control points plus an endpoint, or one control point
plus an endpoint. Custom geometry now accepts both, resolves guide coordinates
on the existing integer path grid and paints them through nested group scaling.
True interior extrema determine bitmap bounds; control points outside the frame
do not themselves enlarge the image, and visible curve ink is not clipped to
the nominal frame. Stroke outsets retain their existing behavior.

**Native reference divergence:** §20.1.9.6 says to ignore lines and curves after `close`.
The independently authored `bezier-close-paths.docx`, opened in the installed reference, instead suppresses the entire path for close-to-line, close-to-quadratic,
close-to-cubic and repeated-close sequences, including a curve with no second close.
A new `moveTo` after close starts a visible new subpath. The importer matches
this behavior for the whole affected path; other paths remain independent.
Source XML, including the suppressed commands, is preserved unchanged.

`bezier-paths.docx` covers both degrees, filled and stroked curves, ink beyond
the frame, reduced-degree curves, guides and anisotropic nested groups. Native reference
PDFs and raster cross-sections are in `tests/fixtures/bezier-paths` and
`tests/fixtures/bezier-close-paths`. The browser compares 96 cross-sections
within 0.75pt through text edit, undo and export/reopen, and verifies exact
package-entry restoration on undo. Samples avoid tangent/horizontal boundary
rows where different antialiasing makes a horizontal extent unstable; this
is not a pixel-identical raster claim. Malformed point counts, namespaces,
coordinates, nested content and unknown guides remain rejected.

Drawing objects remain atomic; this does not introduce individual control-point
editing. Arcs, other unsupported preset geometries and 3D effects remain
separate gaps. Preset lines and dense paths are covered below. Another corpus
card still requires dense guide lists, group fills/shape flips and 3D
picture support before editable import.

### Preset lines inside drawing groups

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.9.18 (`prstGeom`), §20.1.10.56 (`ST_ShapeType`) and
the accompanying `presetShapeDefinitions.xml` define `line` as an open path
from `(l,t)` to `(r,b)`. It is now rendered as a stroke without area fill.
A grouped line may have zero width or zero height; a unit coordinate grid
avoids division by zero while retaining the exact declared transform.
Negative extents, zero-sized non-line shapes/groups and zero child coordinate
spaces retain their guards.

The independent `preset-lines.docx` covers diagonal, horizontal and vertical
lines, nested nonuniform group scaling, ink outside the nominal group frame
and explicit no-outline behavior. The native reference retains a 2pt pen width in
all these cases, including a group stretched by 2 in one axis and 0.5 in the
other. The painter therefore uses physical stroke units for this preset, with
matching bitmap outsets. Other shape presets retain their existing stroke
behavior. No explicit specification contradiction was established here.

The exact fixture's reference PDF, eight ink bounds and 48 cross-sections are in
`tests/fixtures/preset-lines`. Browser checks compare them within 0.75pt before
and after surrounding text edits, undo and DOCX export/reopen. Unit checks
cover zero dimensions, nested scene data, immutable shape geometry, atomic
deletion/undo, preservation and malformed transforms. Complete undo restores
every original package entry byte-for-byte.

This enables the geometry of grouped horizontal/vertical fold lines used in
that corpus card. Its connector properties are covered below; dense guide
lists, group fills, shape flips and 3D picture effects remain outstanding.
Rotated/flipped lines, arrowheads, dashed/capped outlines,
zero-by-zero point lines, and standalone drawings with a zero frame dimension
remain unsupported. Line objects remain atomic; no endpoint editing is added.

### Dense custom paths

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.9.15 (`path`) and Annex A.4.1 `CT_Path2D` permit an
unbounded sequence of path commands. The importer no longer rejects a valid
path solely because it contains more than 10,000 commands. Command validation,
geometry resolution and painting are unchanged; this does not add arc support
or simplify, split or discard any path content.

The existing 20MB compressed / 50MB expanded package limits, 2,000 package-part
limit, scene depth/object limits, per-shape path-count limit and bitmap resource
limits remain in force. No lower aggregate command limit replaces the removed
per-path cutoff: that would reject previously accepted multi-path drawings.

The original `dense-path.docx` fixture has a visible, filled 16,386-command
polygon. It reproduces the former import rejection and was independently opened
and exported in the native reference. Eleven raster cross-sections match within
0.75pt after import, text editing, export/reopen and undo. Browser exports retain
all 16,384 line segments; full undo restores every package entry exactly. The
native browser reader checks the complete command count and quadrant endpoints.
See `tests/fixtures/dense-path` for the reference PDF, reference extraction tool and
source hash. Existing wide-tree, curve, line and group regressions cover the
shared import/paint paths.

The corpus card's two groups contain 67,568 and 63,886 path commands, with an
11,688-command longest path in each. Those paths no longer hit an arbitrary
per-path cutoff. After adding connector properties, an actual-source recheck
still omits both groups: nested-group solid fills and the separate 10,000-guide
limit remain blockers. Some shapes contain 20,796 guides. Shape flips and 3D
pictures remain unsupported. Source preview remains read-only and its download
remains byte-identical to the original.

### WordprocessingShape connector properties

The published MS-ODRAWXML WPS schema makes `cNvSpPr` and `cNvCnPr` mutually
exclusive alternatives. `cNvCnPr` uses DrawingML `CT_NonVisualConnectorProperties`.
The importer now accepts this alternative and validates its ordered, optional
`cxnSpLocks`, `stCxn` and `endCxn` elements. Relevant ECMA-376 Part 1 clauses are
§20.1.2.2.11, §20.1.2.2.13 and §20.1.2.2.36; endpoint IDs and indices use the
unsigned-integer lexical/value domain from Annex A.4.1.

Connector geometry still comes from the authored transform and preset/custom
path. Endpoint references are retained as routing/editing metadata; the engine
does not move internal shapes independently or reroute their connectors. The
independent probe connects a horizontal line to two rectangles and verifies
its authored position against the native reference. This does not claim general automatic
connector routing, endpoint editing or resolution of dangling references.

Transformation/edit locks are enforced by the existing atomic drawing model.
An active selection lock remains guarded, as do unknown attributes/children,
extensions, malformed booleans/unsigned integers, duplicate or misordered
properties, and conflicting shape/connector alternatives. `noTextEdit` is a
shape-only flag and is not accepted on connector locks. Original metadata and
geometry remain unchanged through surrounding edits, export/reopen and undo.

`public/fixtures/connectors.docx` derives only from the original line-probe
XML, adding connector properties, lock forms and two attached endpoints. The
exact source was opened/exported in the native reference; its eight bounds and 48
line cross-sections match within 0.75pt before and after editing and reopening.
The fixture/export schemas and byte-exact undo are checked. See
`tests/fixtures/connectors` for the PDF, source hash and reference provenance.


## Dense custom geometry guide lists

Part 1 Annex A.4.1 `CT_GeomGuideList` permits an unbounded sequence of `gd`
definitions in `avLst` and `gdLst`. The evaluator no longer rejects their
combined count above 10,000. Ordered evaluation, duplicate/forward-reference
checks, formula validation and nonfinite-result rejection remain unchanged;
existing package byte limits still bound imported input.

The original `dense-guides.docx` fixture has one adjustment and 32,768 dependent
guides. Its final guide determines a visible rectangle's width. The native reference
renders the rectangle at 150 by 180pt; browser tests compare eleven ink rows,
resolved vertices, editable import, text edits, export/reopen, retention of all
guide definitions and complete ZIP-entry preservation after undo. Pure evaluator
tests cover long chains across both lists and invalid late definitions. See
`tests/fixtures/dense-guides` for the PDF, source hash and reproduction details.


## Dense custom geometry connection sites

Part 1 Annex A.4.1 `CT_ConnectionSiteList` permits unbounded `cxn` children.
Custom geometry now validates and retains lists above the former 10,000-site
cutoff. Sites do not change a retained shape's ink; their angle/position guide
references and structure are still validated. This does not implement connector
rerouting or connection-site editing. Package limits remain in effect.

The independent `dense-sites.docx` has 16,384 sites and a visible rectangle.
The native reference's captured ink is compared across eleven rows. Browser checks
cover editable import, exact resolved geometry, surrounding text edits,
export/reopen, full connection-list XML retention, complete ZIP-entry undo and
rejection of invalid sites after a large valid list. Source, original generator,
reference PDF, hash and reference extractor are retained with the fixture.


## Group fill inheritance

Part 1 section 20.1.8.35 (`grpFill`) specifies inheritance of group fill
properties. WPG groups now accept solid, noFill and grpFill properties; WPS
shapes with grpFill use the enclosing resolved solid color. Existing scheme
colors and ordered luminance/tint/shade transforms apply. Explicit child fills
win, and absent child fills retain existing theme/default handling. A grpFill
is itself explicit and is not replaced by a theme fill reference. Unknown or
conflicting fills remain guarded. Gradient, pattern and picture group fills
remain unsupported rather than silently approximated.

**Native reference compatibility observation:** the specification describes parent-group
inheritance but does not describe this nested noFill lookup. The native reference
continues through a group with absent, grpFill or explicit noFill to an enclosing
solid group fill. A shape's own noFill still suppresses its ink. The original
12-case `group-fills.docx` independently demonstrates this behavior, including
nested overrides and no enclosing color. Its reference PDF, source hash and 36 RGB
samples are retained. Browser tests verify ink through edit/export/reopen and
undo, complete group XML retention and exact ZIP-entry undo. Scene tests also
check invalid/conflicting fill structures and explicit grpFill versus styles.


## Individual shape reflections

Part 1 section 20.1.7.6 defines `flipH`/`flipV` as reflections about the frame
center. WPS shapes now retain both boolean flags, reflect paths and their ink
bounds, and compose the reflection with ancestor group scales. Source path
coordinates and transform attributes remain untouched for export. Curves with
ink outside the frame are included in reflected preview bounds. Existing
picture reflection remains separate. Group reflections and nonzero rotations
remain guarded.

**Native reference text compatibility behavior:** the original `shape-flips.docx` proves
the native reference leaves text upright under horizontal reflection and rotates it
180 degrees under vertical reflection, including combined H/V. The painter
uses this text transform separately from the path reflection. The six-case
fixture includes asymmetric outside-frame quadratic geometry and anisotropic
nested scaling. Native reference PDF ink cross-sections and text matrix axes are compared
in the browser; tests also cover edit/export/reopen, retained scene data and
exact ZIP-entry undo. This does not assert identical default-font rasterization.


## Empty section-break paragraphs

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.6.18 stores a nonfinal section's properties on its last
paragraph; §17.6.22 defines next-page section transitions. The independent
eleven-case `empty-section-boundary.docx` demonstrates the native reference's special treatment
of its otherwise empty boundary paragraphs: no additional body line, spacing,
border, shading, page-break-before or numbering increment. Text and literal
spaces remain real content and retain ordinary overflow. The renderer follows
this reference behavior while preserving the paragraph, source formatting and
section markup. A virtual insertion line keeps keyboard editing/caret mapping
available within the writing area. Typing restores normal paragraph layout.

The twenty-four-page reference and source hash are retained in
`tests/fixtures/empty-section-boundary`. Unit/browser tests cover pagination,
list continuation, suppressed paint, boundary editing, export/reopen and exact
undo. This rule does not discard ordinary empty paragraphs or change existing
guards on unsupported section-transition types.

### Keep-with-next at an empty section boundary

The special reference behavior also terminates the preceding paragraph's
`keepNext` chain (§17.3.1.15). A zero-height section insertion position must
not add the preceding after-spacing to a keep group: that could move a real
paragraph to an unnecessary page before the next-page section transition.
The paginator stops its existing look-ahead at virtual `emptySectionBoundary` lines, while
retaining the ordinary gap/section-spacing path and virtual caret position.
No paragraph formatting or package content is changed. A boundary containing
text remains a real paragraph and participates in the keep chain.

Ten independently authored controls in `tests/fixtures/section-keep` record
22 native reference pages. They distinguish keep on/off, zero/large after-spacing,
empty/text-bearing boundaries, ordinary/table preceding content, continuous/
next-page sections, an empty preceding paragraph and a longer keep chain.
Three initial controls failed before the fix; page assignments and native
text origins are checked after it. Browser coverage includes typing into an
empty boundary (restoring a three-page kept layout), undo back to two pages,
and editable export/reopen. This extends the documented empty-section reference
behavior rather than inventing a special rule for the source template.

## Retained 3D pictures

Original perspective/orthographic projection and ray intersections for extruded
rectangles and ellipses live in `drawing-3d-geometry.js`. `docx-picture-3d.js`
and `canvas-picture-3d.js` connect these to retained picture import and painting.
Supported cameras are `orthographicFront`, `perspectiveRight` and
`perspectiveLeft`, with zero shape z, no bevel, and the lighting below. Original
DrawingML, relationships and image parts remain untouched through surrounding
edits and export. Internal picture transformations remain guarded. The published Open
Specifications support documents camera magnitude as 6.28 / tan(FOV/2) and FOV
clamping. The inch-to-point scene mapping is checked against five independent
reference rectangular cases, including both camera turns, extrusion and two sizes.
Interior/outside silhouette scans match within 0.75pt. These tests do not claim
arbitrary cameras or complete 3D conformance.

The `picture-3d.docx` reference has thirteen cases, including separate contour-only
and extrusion-only ellipses, rectangular contours and flat ellipses under both
cameras. Native reference PDF, COM properties,
source hash and measurements are retained. Silhouette extraction includes dark
neutral extrusion faces; the initial saturation-only detector missed these.
The painter uses analytic surface intersections and bilinear texture sampling.
Contours are unlit strokes of projected front/back boundaries with round joins
and visible rectangular side connections. The front face is positioned half a
contour width behind the scene origin, matching the independent reference cases.
Resource bounds include contour and extrusion outsets; the original layout
frame and wrapping extents stay independent of the preview bitmap.

`drawing-3d-lighting.js` implements the `threePt`/top-direction, `warmMatte`
combination using the numerical light/material tables in MS-OI29500
sections 2.1.1274(c) and 2.1.1334(b). The published scene-vector transform is
(-y, -x, z); incoming vectors are negated for surface-to-light calculations.
Warm matte uses Phong power 8 and specular RGB 0.3, without Fresnel or ambient
contributions for this rig. The rig stays in the object's scene coordinates;
camera projection changes the surface-to-viewer vector.

The independent reference checks 52 front-face and six side-wall RGB
samples across thirteen cases, within three levels per channel. The native reference's side
samples require evaluating the specular lobe independently of the sign of the
diffuse incidence. This is observed reference behavior where the standard does not
fully specify the illumination algorithm, rather than a template-specific
adjustment. These measurements do not prove pixel-identical rasterization.
Other rigs, directions and materials explicitly reject. Grouped 3D pictures,
nonzero frame rotation/reflection, differing inner extents and unsupported scene
properties remain guarded. Solid ordinary outlines are supported as described below.

Primary numerical reference (August 18, 2026 edition):
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/1fd4a662-8623-49c0-82f0-18fa91b413b8

Four additional reference probes isolate flat perspective/orthographic ellipses and
orthographic ellipse/rectangle contours. The ellipse raster-boundary discrepancy
also occurs with zero extrusion and an orthographic camera. The measured fringe
must be distinguished from geometry when comparing contours;
no fitted ellipse-size change has been applied.
Twenty additional contour samples match the source contour color exactly across
both cameras and geometries, with and without extrusion. The native reference's contours are
unlit in these cases; applying the face's warm-matte shader to them would be
incorrect. Browser checks cover all 78 color samples within four RGB levels and
full silhouette boundaries within 1.25pt in both directions. Row and column
extrema cover shallow edges; Euclidean boundary distance avoids exaggerated
horizontal differences on near-tangent scan rows. No pixel-identical claim is
made. The browser also checks thirteen-page pagination, text edits, exact
ZIP-entry undo and edit/export/reopen; unit tests guard unsupported 3D inputs
and internal object mutations.

### Ordinary outlines on retained 3D pictures

`picture-3d-outlines.docx` adds seventeen independent reference cases for solid
ordinary outlines, themed colors, omitted width, noFill, flat/deep geometry,
contours, wide strokes and explicit round joins. Relevant clauses are ECMA-376
Part 1 §20.1.2.2.24 (`ln`), §20.1.10.39 (`ST_PenAlignment`) and §20.1.8.52
(`round`). The fixture README records the reference divergences: omitted width is
0.75pt rather than zero; zero-depth/zero-contour pictures place the outline
outside the original frame even with explicit centered alignment; extruded
rectangles retain sharp outer corners even with an explicit round join.

The painter shades the ordinary outline with the face material and uses its
color as the default extrusion color. The separate contour remains unlit and
follows the outside of the outlined solid. Original ellipse closest-point and
parallel-curve geometry maintains constant stroke width. The source photograph
keeps its original texture frame. Dashed/compound outlines, inset alignment,
unsupported caps and arrowheads remain guarded. This does not change ordinary
two-dimensional picture outline support.

The independent reference PDF, COM properties, source hash, color samples and full
silhouette measurements are retained alongside the fixture. Browser tests use
four-level RGB and 1.25pt bidirectional silhouette tolerances, plus edit, exact
ZIP-entry undo and reopen checks. Opening the edited seventeen-page browser
export in the native reference preserves all seventeen picture crops pixel-for-pixel against
the reference at 144 DPI. This establishes picture preservation on that fixture,
not complete document fidelity or arbitrary 3D support.


## Header drawing preview and preset outline dashes

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.10.2/17.10.5 (story references), §17.6.11 (header/footer
margins), §§20.4.2.3/20.4.2.6/20.4.2.10–11 (anchors, effect bounds and position),
§20.1.8.48 (`prstDash`) and §20.1.10.49 (`ST_PresetLineDashVal`) govern this
iteration. The preset binary patterns are implemented in pen-width units and
verified against native reference PDF dash operators for all eleven values.

Read-only page stories now import supported inline pictures and retained
DrawingML shapes/groups. Each story gets its own relationship reader and drawing
asset namespace, including nested group pictures/fills, so a reused relationship
ID cannot resolve against the body. Inherited markup-compatibility declarations
remain available while parsing normalized field runs. Source story parts remain
untouched. Tables, hyperlinks and charts in stories remain unsupported.

Anchored story drawings repeat on the selected pages. Page/margin positioning
uses physical section geometry; paragraph positioning uses the translated story
paragraph. They stay outside body selection, caret offsets and hit testing.
Story images behind text paint before body images behind text; foreground
objects retain the corresponding paint layer.

[MS-ODRAWXML percentage sizing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-odrawxml/1a38a99a-16ae-420d-8c79-23dc2e922717)
is supported for no-wrap anchors relative to the page or its margins, independently
on each axis. Zero placeholders retain the saved extent; malformed percentages
and unsupported positive-size bases reject. Positive relative sizes include effect
extents, while aligned anchors position their whole effect box. Fixed-size and
relative-size reference controls independently establish the distinction. Numeric
position offsets use the effect-box rule documented below when either dimension
is relative. Percentage-sized raster drawings
are retained objects, preventing property edits from silently overriding only
the cached extent while leaving the percentage active.

For a final image-only single-spaced footer line, the invisible paragraph mark's
descender no longer adds bottom clearance. Native reference controls with visible descenders
and following empty paragraphs retain their original clearance. Other spacing
modes are unchanged. These are measured reference layout refinements; no contradiction
with a normative rule was identified. All fixtures are original, generated by
`tools/header_drawing_fixture.py`; references and precise measurements are in
`tests/fixtures/header-drawings`.

Remaining work: editable page stories, story table layout, unsupported wrapping
anchors, automatic body clearance around tall stories, additional relative-size
bases, and rerasterizing retained shape text/strokes at new percentage dimensions
when the physical page size changes. The current scene preview is decoded at the
saved frame size and scaled to the resolved frame; arbitrary scale changes are
not claimed to reproduce the native reference's physical text/stroke metrics. The existing
editable-body fixture covers surrounding text edits and exact undo, not that
remaining rescaling work.


## Out-of-note reference marks

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.11.6 (`endnoteRef`) and 17.11.13 (`footnoteRef`) allow marks
outside their respective notes to be ignored. The native reference instead renders
ordinal one, using the effective footnote numbering format for both element
kinds, even with different endnote formatting and non-one `numStart` values.
This reference compatibility choice is proven by the independently authored controls
in `tests/fixtures/inactive-note-marks`; it is not a document-specific rule.

Main-body and table-cell marks retain their original element identity, run
formatting, and atomic selection/replacement behavior. Supported formats are
decimal, decimalZero, lower/upper Roman and lower/upper letter. Formatting and
neighbor edits preserve the mark; replacement removes it and inserts ordinary
text. Malformed CT_Empty elements, unsupported formats, marks in drawings/page
stories, and actual note references remain guarded. Untouched packages and parts
are retained, and undo restores their original content.

The large-superscript control remains visually partial: the native reference allocates less
descent for these marks than for identical ordinary superscript text, while the
current layout uses its ordinary script metrics. Font-dependent script ink
sizing also remains unresolved. The source booklet now loads editably but is
not marked complete on the basis of this import/serialization improvement.
Validation: 60 unit tests, five browser workflows, production build/license gate
and 85 XML checks across 23 source/export packages pass. Booklet 15 opens as ten
editable pages, matching the native reference's count, and passes export/reopen and exact undo;
page-count agreement does not establish full rendering fidelity.

## MACROBUTTON display labels

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.16.1 (field syntax), 17.16.5.34 (`MACROBUTTON`),
17.16.18 (`fldChar`) and 17.16.19 (`fldSimple`) govern this support.
Complete simple or complex MACROBUTTON fields within one inline container render
their instruction label, including fields without a cached result. Split
instruction runs preserve the label fragments' run formatting. Command names
are stripped; no macro execution or interactive button action is attached.

Native reference compatibility: the installed reference renders literal quotes and trailing
whitespace in the instruction tail, rather than stripping the optional argument
delimiters from the general field grammar. It uses this label even when the saved
result is stale or the field is locked. The independently authored nine-case
`macro-button-labels.docx` and reference in `tests/fixtures/macro-buttons` reproduce
these observations. This behavior is specific to the field type, never to a
corpus filename or text value.

Projection does not mutate package XML. Complete text prompts in a body paragraph
or an explicit hyperlink are editable; other unsupported document features still
trigger read-only fallback and original-file download. Unknown, malformed,
incomplete or nested prompts retain the existing fallback. Fields spanning
containers/paragraphs, graphical labels, prompts inside inline content controls
and general field evaluation remain open.
Native selection evidence now covers replacement, formatting and arrow-key
boundaries in `tests/fixtures/macro-buttons/native-edits.json`, tied to the
independent `editing.docx` by SHA-256. The native reference replaces the entire selected prompt
on typing, including a locked field, but preserves and formats its instruction
on italic application. Moving right crosses the prompt as one unit. These
behaviors are implemented with instruction-backed atomic prompt ranges. Clicking
or selecting inside a prompt selects its complete visible label; arrow movement
crosses it, and replacement/deletion removes its field. Boundary typing inserts
outside it. Find replacement expands a hit to its owning prompt and replaces
multiple hits in the same prompt once. Formatting retains the field. Whole-prompt
bookmarks and hyperlinks are emitted outside the instruction. Undo restores the
original package, including unchanged parts and caches.
The instruction-label codec now reads complete simple/complex text prompts and
writes formatting edits while preserving the command, cached result, delimiter
properties and lock/dirty flags. Unchanged envelopes are retained. A formatted
simple field becomes an equivalent complex field so split label formatting can
be represented independently of cached content (§§17.16.18–19). Text replacement
is explicitly excluded from this formatting codec: the model must remove the
field, as shown by the native selection evidence. Nested fields and simple-field
metadata that cannot be preserved by conversion are rejected. This codec is
tested independently and used by the body serializer. The importer retains
original paragraph XML separately from the display projection, so changing
another paragraph never serializes a synthetic display wrapper.
Body integration validation: 162 unit checks, six browser workflows, 36 XML
checks across eighteen packages, production build and license gate pass. The
independent editable control matches all eight reference text lines within 0.10pt;
its full-page comparison and edit/export/undo/reopen checks pass. Booklet 15
advances to a separate unsupported main-story `footnoteRef` and remains partial.
The independent fixture and browser download pass the ECMA schema checker;
52 relevant unit tests and 7 browser tests passed (one optional corpus smoke
test skipped). These checks do not establish full field or booklet fidelity.


## Saved content inside unsupported controls

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.5.2.33–36 defines `sdtContent` at cell, block, row and
inline levels. In read-only body import, the saved content is now parsed through
