the normal style, table and drawing readers independently of unsupported wrapper
editing semantics. This preserves supported title/run formatting, images and
tables inside persistent, locked and nested controls. Wrapper-local namespace
bindings remain available after projection, including prefixes used by MC values.
Malformed duplicate content containers are not arbitrarily selected.

Projection changes only the disposable read-only DOM. Strict editing checks and
the original OPC bytes remain unchanged; no exporter is attached to the preview.
The independent locked/unwrapped controls and native references are recorded in
`tests/fixtures/control-preview`. The native reference's two pages are pixel-identical at 96 DPI;
browser tests also compare the two variants after image decoding. This is evidence
for wrapper-independent saved-content rendering, not full reference layout equivalence.

This does not update custom XML bindings, regenerate empty/glossary placeholders,
implement interactive control adornments, or enable persistent/locked control
editing. Page-story control projection is covered below. Unsupported inner content
and later layout failures can still require a simpler preview.


## Legacy numbering label placement

ECMA-376 Part 4 §14.6.2 (`legacy`) augments numbering levels and full level
overrides. Import reads valid flags, signed indent and unsigned gap measurements,
retaining original package XML. New ordinary lists remain modern. Generated and
restarted definitions preserve relevant legacy declarations.

**Native reference divergence:** The native reference treats an omitted flag as off (the standard
says on), interprets the indent as a label-area width relative to the ordinary
first-line position (rather than a symbol offset from the text margin), and hides
the label for a negative indent. For active nonnegative values, text follows the
larger of the label-area width and measured label advance plus the declared gap.
An absent indent uses the ordinary hanging distance. Legacy placement replaces
the saved suffix behavior. Left/right/center alignment follows the independently
measured rules in `tests/fixtures/legacy-numbering/README.md`.

The original 24-case fixture and hashed reference cover these differences;
native-browser tests compare every label/text x coordinate with the PDF within
0.2 pt. Seventy unit tests and three browser tests pass, covering text edits,
restart, reopen, undo, unrelated parts, flags and malformed measurements. Actual
continuations retain ordinary paragraph indentation. Unsupported numbering
formats, graphic bullets, complex-script labels and out-of-range geometry keep
their existing checks; this does not claim every legacy list feature.

## Indentation on actual paragraph lines

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.12 (`ind`) distinguishes the first-line hanging offset
from the indent on subsequent lines. Layout now validates the geometry of each
line when it is produced, rather than rejecting a paragraph because a hypothetical
continuation would have no writing space. This permits empty and short paragraphs
in narrow cells whose left/hanging pair gives the first line a valid text area.
It also permits first-line-only body paragraphs with an unused off-page indent.
The original indent values and XML are preserved.

The independent `unused-continuation-indent.docx` fixture and native reference in
`tests/fixtures/unused-indent` demonstrate five first-line-only cases. Empty
paragraph height, insertion geometry, ordinary edits, reopen and exact undo are
covered. The later exhausted-cell implementation below extends this behavior to
actual cell lines without writing width. Body validation remains unchanged.
No specification divergence was identified.

Validation: 76 relevant unit tests, two browser tests, source/export schema
checks, license check and production build. The reference comparison establishes
line existence and indent placement, not complete row-height/font-metric equivalence.

### Exhausted paragraph widths inside cells

When paragraph indents consume a table cell's writing width, retain the indented
origin with zero available width instead of rejecting the document. The line
builder accepts its first item, then starts the next item on a new line; ordinary
spaces do not hang onto these exhausted lines. Keep the existing physical cell
clipping and source indentation values. Positive widths below one pixel remain
positive, while body paragraph geometry validation is unchanged.

The original fourteen-row `exhausted-cell-indents.docx` fixture compares empty,
left/right/both, first-line/hanging, negative/valid, center/right and tiny-font
controls against the native reference. All 58 nonempty native lines agree within
0.2 point. Regression coverage includes each cell's line count, clipped ink,
insertion into an exhausted empty cell, package preservation, exact undo and
editable export/reopen. See `tests/fixtures/exhausted-cell-indents/README.md`.
This follows the native reference in a layout case not prescribed by §17.3.1.12; no explicit
normative contradiction was found. It does not relax unsupported body geometry.

Validation: 85 unit checks across eight files, eight browser checks, 168 XML
checks across 24 fixture/export packages, license policy and production build.
The corrected fixture's XML ordering was revalidated with fresh reference output;
native positions were unchanged, and its unit/browser checks were rerun.


## Installed face names that differ from CSS family names

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.26 (`rFonts`) names the document's fonts. A successful
browser `local()` lookup does not establish that the same string is selectable
as a CSS family: full-face and PostScript names can resolve only through an
explicit FontFace registration. Availability checks now register the loaded
local face under the document name only when the CSS family is otherwise
unselectable. Existing native families retain their full style selection.

Concurrent requests share the same load; missing fonts keep the existing explicit
fallback behavior. No font is fetched by name or bundled, and DOCX declarations
remain unchanged. `tests/fixtures/local-font-face` records the independent fixture,
reference and measured Franklin Gothic Demi mismatch. Browser regressions
compare registered-face advances to a separately loaded reference; mandatory
unit cases cover the same selection distinction without depending on host fonts.
This does not solve general line metrics, synthesized styles or missing fonts.
## Rotated preset lines inside drawing groups

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.7.5–20.1.7.6 and §20.1.10.3 define group/shape
transforms and signed angles in 1/60,000 degree units. Annex L §§L.4.7.4–L.4.7.5
describes scaling along a child's local axes before rotation, rather than an
ordinary concatenation of affine transforms. Nested preset `line` shapes now
retain their rotation until painting, including flat extents, negative and
multiple-turn angles, and horizontal/vertical reflections. Group coordinate
offsets/scales compose before locating the child's center. Pen width and dash
lengths remain physical; direction is preserved, including dash phase. Exact
frame dimensions are retained; only bitmap allocation rounds to pixels.

**Native reference compatibility divergence:** the annex's axis-product description does
not specify exchanging the parent's scale axes at quarter-turn orientations.
The native reference does exchange them for child angles in [45°,135°) and
[225°,315°), then rotates the resized child about its transformed center.
For example, a 72×36pt line at 45° under 1.5×/0.5× scaling has a directed
endpoint difference of approximately (−12.728,63.640)pt, rather than the
annex-description result (63.640,89.095)pt. The independently authored
`rotated-group-lines.docx` and retained reference PDF demonstrate 22 cases, including
the four interval boundaries, nested scaling and flips. Geometry tests compare
actual canvas stroke endpoints with PDF endpoints within 0.015pt, alongside
editing/reopening, exact undo and schema checks. The fixture does not establish
general support for all rotated drawings: rotated groups, other preset
or custom shapes, and text on rotated lines remain guarded.
Nested picture support is established by the separate controls below.
## Standalone lines with a zero frame extent

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.4.2.7 (`extent`), 20.1.7.6 (`xfrm`) and the
`ST_PositiveCoordinate` schema type permit a zero coordinate. Standalone
DrawingML preset `line` shapes now retain exactly one collapsed axis in both
the inner shape and outer frame. They use the nonzero axis to resolve raster
scale, without adding artificial width/height to text flow. Rotation and
physical pen widths use the existing line geometry path. Selection follows
the directed visible stroke with a 3px minimum pointer tolerance; selection
bounds include the stroke and respect enclosing cell/line clipping.

The original eight-page `tests/fixtures/flat-lines` controls cover horizontal
and vertical frames, ±45° rotation, doubled frame scale, and inline placement.
Native reference ink bounds are measured independently at 0.25pt resolution; browser
checks compare within 1pt including canvas raster rounding. Editing retains
the complete drawing XML, and package/undo/reopen checks protect source data.
No document-specific branch or newly asserted reference/spec divergence is involved.

Ordinary pictures and groups continue to require positive dimensions. Point
lines (both dimensions zero), text on standalone flat shapes, mismatched
collapsed axes, and percentage-sized flat frames remain guarded. The retained
objects cannot be resized or have their internal geometry edited. The controls
do not establish all wrap/relative-size combinations.

## DrawingML line caps

Part 1 §§20.1.2.2.24, 20.1.10.31 and 20.1.8.48 define outline caps and
preset dashes. The scene reader accepts `flat`, `rnd` and `sq` for supported
DrawingML paths. Both ordinary and rotated-line painting apply the cap to each
dash and to the path ends. Round caps extend by half the physical pen width;
square cap bounds also include diagonal corners outside the nominal frame.
Compound strokes remain unsupported. Original drawing XML is retained through
body edits and exports.

**Native reference divergence:** §20.1.2.2.24 states that an omitted cap defaults to square.
The native reference uses flat caps in the independent `drawing-line-caps.docx`
probes. The renderer follows the native reference, retaining the source's absent attribute.
For round/square caps, the native reference's PDF shortens every preset dash by one pen width
and lengthens every gap by one pen width. This leaves zero-length centerline
dashes for dots, which the round/square caps paint. The period is unchanged.
The 22-case fixture covers absent/explicit caps, solid/dot/system-dot/dash-dot
strokes, rotation, reflection, nested scales and out-of-frame ink. Its retained
reference PDF provides 2,524 interior pixel checks; edit/reopen/undo and schema
checks additionally cover package preservation. The existing flat-cap dash
and header drawing regressions remain applicable.
## Small point line heights

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.1.33, 17.18.48 and 17.18.81 define minimum/exact
line heights in twentieths of a point, without a six-point lower bound. Import,
direct paragraph editing, style editing and their dialogs now accept 0–600pt
in whole-twip steps. Minimum heights below the text/picture height retain the
natural height. Positive exact values remain bottom-aligned and clipped as
specified. The former six-point guard caused entire otherwise supported tables
to fall back to plain paragraphs when a cell inherited `atLeast` 1pt.

**Native reference compatibility exception:** The native reference treats `line="0"` with
`lineRule="exact"` as natural line height with visible text, rather than a
literal zero-height clipped line. The renderer follows that behavior while
retaining the stored zero/rule. Automatic zero multiples retain zero advance;
they are not changed to natural height. The independent twelve-cell
`small-line-spacing.docx` tests minimum/exact 0, 0.05, 1, 5.95, 6 and 24pt.
The retained reference PDF supplies baseline advances checked within 0.15pt with
Arial installed. That tolerance includes PDF coordinate rounding, not a claim
of whole-page table-spacing equivalence. Unit tests additionally cover inline
pictures, inherited styles, edit/reopen and exact undo; browser tests cover
small-point dialog values, table retention and export. Negative line values,
absolute-unit spellings and heights above the existing resource limits remain
outside this subset. This supersedes earlier six-point bounds in this record.

## Picture opacity and saved image corrections

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.8.6, 20.1.8.13, 20.1.10.46 and 22.9.2.11
specify BLIP alpha modulation and positive percentage values. The reader
accepts repeated `a:alphaModFix` modifiers, including the default 100%,
transitional integer thousandths of a percent and decimal percent spelling.
Opacity belongs to each picture instance, leaving shared source pixels intact.
Inline/positioned pictures, grouped pictures and shape picture fills multiply
source alpha while retaining crop/transform geometry. Retained 3D pictures
apply alpha to the texture before lighting; explicit outline colors remain
independent. The original effect XML survives edits, export and undo. This
adds rendering support, not a new opacity editing control. Other BLIP effects
remain outside the supported editable subset.

**Native reference divergence:** the standard describes multiplication, with no 100%
upper bound on the amount. The native reference clamps each amount at 100% before
multiplication. Original `picture-alpha.docx` probes include partially
transparent source pixels, 150%/200%/500% amounts, repeated 50% amounts, and
200% then 50% in both orders. Both mixed cases produce 50%, distinguishing
per-modifier clamping from clamping the final product. The renderer follows
the native reference. The retained reference PDF and hash-bound color samples cover all 15 cases;
canvas comparisons allow three RGB levels for compositing quantization.

[MS-ODRAWXML §3.3 Pictures](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-odrawxml/f10da8b6-40f3-4527-9c3d-9f5c2e9cff45)
identifies the main BLIP as the processed display image and `a14:imgProps` as
saved correction metadata referring to the original image. The reader retains
that extension unchanged and uses the main BLIP, without decoding the original
layer or applying its effects again. A contrasting original-image layer in the
fixture independently verifies this behavior. The extension must contain one
`imgProps` and one `imgLayer`; its saved editing subtree remains opaque.
Standard-view XSD checks cover the fixture and exports, but do not establish
full validation of that vendor extension's editing subtree.

## Saved content controls in headers and footers

The read-only story importer now applies the same saved `sdtContent`
projection as the body before parsing PAGE fields and paragraph formatting.
ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.5.2.34 and 17.5.2.36 describe block and inline saved
content; §§17.10.1–2 and 17.10.5–6 define footer/header parts and references.
Persistent, locked, nested and building-block controls therefore no longer
hide otherwise supported story paragraphs. Projection affects only the
throwaway DOM: wrapper properties, bindings, cached results and all package
bytes remain unchanged. Malformed duplicate content containers and unsupported
inner story blocks retain the existing fallback; story editing remains disabled.

The original `story-controls-plain.docx` / `story-controls-wrapped.docx` pair
covers nested block wrappers, inline PAGE fields, first/even/default headers
and footers, and stale cached values. The native reference renders all three pages
pixel-identically between variants and replaces cached 99 with page values
1/2/3. Browser tests compare all three page bitmaps, check the six displayed
story values and verify identical uncompressed package entries. Body editing
now retains these wrappers; the regression also checks edited exports, unchanged
story parts, exact undo and reopen. Unit tests preserve malformed
wrapper guards and unaffected sibling stories. Both fixtures and their original
downloads pass the standard-view XSD checks. No reference/spec divergence was
observed for this projection. Section page-number restarts remain a separate
unsupported behavior; these probes use continuous numbering.

## Section page numbering and duplex restart parity

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.6.12 (`pgNumType`) supplies the initial page value and
number format; an omitted start continues from the preceding section's last
value. §§17.16.5.42, 17.16.5.44 and 17.16.5.55 define NUMPAGES, PAGE and SECTIONPAGES;
§17.18.59 defines number formats. The story reader retains each section's
optional start and format separately from page dimensions. PAGE uses that
section's logical number. NUMPAGES remains a physical document count, while
SECTIONPAGES counts pages belonging to the section. Locked fields retain their
cached result.

The supported rendering formats are decimal, decimalZero, upper/lower Roman
and upper/lower alphabetic. Omitted format is decimal, independently of the
preceding section. The native reference's alphabetic sequence repeats letters after Z; zero in
Roman/alphabetic format paints a space, and Roman values above 3999 are allowed.
Starts are supported from zero through 2147483647. Very long alphabetic/Roman
expansions remain resource-limited. Unsupported formats and chapter-prefixed
PAGE fields retain their saved result in best-effort rendering and report a
layout limitation without hiding the story's other text or count fields.
Negative starts and malformed declarations remain outside this subset.

**Native reference compatibility/divergence:** [MS-OE376 §2.1.298](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oe376/66274c6b-6552-47b6-a1b1-3cfcd9c064f4)
records that the native reference chooses odd/even stories using section page-number values,
rather than physical page ordinality. The renderer follows that rule, including
page zero and initially even sections. Independently, the original reference probes
show that, with even/odd headers enabled, a next-page section whose explicit
restart changes parity inserts a completely blank page. This extends the literal
next-page behavior in §17.6.22. Parity is compared with the next logical value
of the preceding section, not the physical document index. These filler pages
have no story, count toward NUMPAGES and the existing 200-page resource limit,
and do not count toward SECTIONPAGES. Preflight and the editor use the same
pagination inputs, so exceeding the limit falls back before editor attachment.

Four independent 13-section fixtures and retained reference PDFs cover 99 physical
pages, including duplex/simplex, initially even and zero/title-page variants.
Unit and browser checks compare all page values and blank-page positions,
verify stale results are not used for supported fields, and preserve original
package bytes. Mirror-margin-only duplex behavior, non-next-page section
pagination, chapter prefixes, other number formats and field format switches
remain separate gaps. This supersedes the earlier section-restart limitation
in the saved story-controls entry; it does not enable header/footer editing.

### Inherited numbering and paragraph indents (native reference compatibility)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.7.1–17.7.2 describe basedOn inheritance and numbering
before paragraph styles; §17.3.1.12 defines indents and §17.3.1.19 defines
numbering references. The native reference resolves inherited list indents more
specifically: the numbering level overrides ancestors of the nearest paragraph
style declaring numId. That style's own indents and its descendants override
the level. Repeating numId on a descendant moves this boundary. Direct numbering
overrides the full style chain, and direct paragraph indents remain last.
This differs from flattening all inherited paragraph-style indents after
numbering. The engine follows the observed reference behavior without style-name or
document-specific exceptions. It does not change tab or contextual-spacing
precedence; those properties retain their existing independent behavior.

`tools/list_style_indent_fixture.py` creates an independent 24-case, three-page
DOCX. `tests/fixtures/list-style-indents/native.pdf` and its hashed coordinate
reference prove ancestor/declaring/derived/direct precedence, first-line and
hanging conflicts, explicit zeros, repeated numbering references and Normal
ancestry. Unit and browser tests compare marker, first-text and continuation
positions with the native reference within 0.1 PDF point, and cover style edits, direct indents,
list removal, text edits, save/reopen, untouched parts and byte-exact undo.

A follow-up reset-fixture check in the native reference confirms resolved left/hanging indents
of 18/−18 points after removing direct paragraph properties, superseding the
old regression expectation of an inherited 10.8-point left indent. That check
also exposes a separate remaining gap: with an inherited numId whose level
pStyle does not match the paragraph's style chain, the native reference can retain list indents
while displaying no marker. The engine currently falls back to level zero;
the reset counter test verifies model persistence, not native reference marker fidelity.

### Before-spacing at section and explicit page boundaries

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.33 specifies paragraph spacing and ordinary maximum-gap
resolution; §17.3.1.23 defines pageBreakBefore, §17.3.3.1 run-level breaks, and
§17.6.22 next-page sections. The native reference applies additional boundary rules
not expressed by simply restarting ordinary paragraph spacing on a fresh page:

- At a next-page section start, retain only `max(0, before − preceding after)`.
  The preceding after-spacing participates even if the section-ending paragraph
  is empty and its line is suppressed. The first section has no preceding gap.
- An actual pageBreakBefore transition uses that subtraction in the default
  legacy mode and explicit mode 14. Mode 15 suppresses the before-gap entirely.
- A paragraph following a terminal run-level page break with a virtual paragraph
  mark starts without before-spacing. A paragraph mark moved by
  splitPgBreakAndParaMark remains a real line under the existing behavior.

These are observed reference compatibility rules. Existing treatment of before-spacing
inside a paragraph containing a leading break is separate; this change does not
claim complete fidelity for all break/compatibility combinations. Border insets
remain intact, spacing declarations remain unchanged, and cached measured blocks
do not retain spacing from a previous pagination call.

The original `section_before_spacing_fixture.py` generates four 18-page variants
covering omitted settings, modes 14/15, and suppressSpBfAfterPgBrk in mode 15.
The retained reference PDFs, package hashes and 72-page baseline reference are in
`tests/fixtures/section-before-spacing`. Unit/browser checks compare first/body
baselines within 0.1 point and cover preceding paragraph edits, reopening,
untouched package parts, byte-exact undo, existing section boundaries, pagination,
contextual spacing and section page numbers.

### Deferred before-spacing after leading run-level page breaks

ECMA-376 Part 4 §14.8.3.42 postpones before-spacing until content follows a
leading page break, unless suppressSpBfAfterPgBrk is enabled; Part 1 §17.3.3.1
defines the break and §17.3.1.33 defines paragraph spacing. The native reference also
subtracts the preceding paragraph's after-spacing from that deferred gap,
clamping the remainder to zero. That preceding value survives consecutive
leading breaks. This is a reference compatibility refinement to applying the raw
before value described by Part 4. Text or a space before the break makes it a
mid-paragraph break, which does not receive deferred before-spacing.

Unlike pageBreakBefore, a leading run-level break retains the remainder in
compatibility mode 15 as well as modes 11, 12 and 14. The explicit suppression
flag still removes it; explicit false in mode 15 retains it. The independent
`leading_break_spacing_fixture.py` creates six variants, with all 78 native reference PDF
pages, hashes and baseline references retained in `tests/fixtures/leading-break-spacing`.
Unit/browser checks compare both target and following-body baselines, preserve
blank pages, and cover edits, save/reopen, untouched parts and exact undo.

## Thin/thick large-gap compound borders

Paragraph and table borders additionally support `thinThickLargeGap` from
ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.18.2, through the existing per-side inheritance, editing,
serialization, spacing, clipping and pagination paths. Shared table edges use
the native reference's weight number 17 and existing tie/color rules, documented by
[MS-OI29500 §2.1.169](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/7c791c5d-44c3-4fe8-abdd-8f136761bb93).

The standard's ambiguous multi-line description differs from the native reference's two-stroke
rendering, as explicitly corrected in
[MS-OI29500 §2.1.528](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/923382bf-235a-4f4a-b9df-d5a0f8b2ead8).
Independent original controls and native reference PDFs are retained in
`tests/fixtures/compound-borders`. Sizes 0, 2, 8, 11, 12, 13, 17, 24, 48 and 96
show fixed 1.44pt/0.72pt ink strokes, with the declared size controlling the gap.
The gap rounds down to a 600dpi unit, with a one-unit minimum even at zero.
Unlike double/triple table borders, this total width is not multiplied again.
Without `frame`, thick ink precedes thin ink along both coordinate axes.
Paired `frame="1"` controls establish paragraph reversal on bottom/right sides;
the winning table edge retains its originating side. The table-body/cap
distinction is detailed in the corner follow-up below.

The existing border dialogs expose the new style. No-edit and complete undo
preserve every OPC part; paragraph/cell edits and reopening preserve supported
declarations. Additional small/medium-gap styles are described below; other
compound styles remain unsupported pending evidence.
This is not complete border fidelity: paragraph frame positioning has small
residual differences from the native reference. Matching ink widths and supporting editable
import do not establish pixel equivalence.

### Continuous table-border corners

Two-edge table corners now join continuous ink bands before painting. Equal
style/size borders connect corresponding outer/inner rings. Unlike styles or
sizes use the native reference's horizontal-over-vertical butt join. Different colors retain
the same geometry, with horizontal color owning the corner overlap. Single,
thick, double, triple and supported compound patterns share this geometry.
The pre-pagination row-width pass is unchanged; guide-only borders do not
allocate corner records. Junction records are indexed by table, page and
logical endpoint, so they do not connect different tables or page fragments.

Independent controls in `tests/fixtures/border-corners` retain native reference
PDF rectangles/colors, source hashes and generators. Browser checks compare
36 table cases, including unequal widths, two/three-stroke mixtures, four side
colors and isolated frame flags. The native reference reverses a framed vertical table edge's
straight body, including the left edge; the left cap stays unreversed, while
the adjoining horizontal flag controls the right cap. The initially missed
left-body/right-cap distinction is corrected from these isolated controls.
This reference-specific painting behavior is not quantitatively specified by
ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.38, 17.4.66 and 17.18.2.

Only two-edge continuous corners are changed by that feature. Single-border
cross junctions are covered below; T/compound junctions and dashed corners
remain open. The controls also expose pre-existing paragraph
double/triple width and frame-position discrepancies that remain pending.

### Cell border `none`, spacing and overlapping conditional regions

Original controls in `tests/fixtures/cell-border-none` cover 48 native reference
pages. Part 1 §§17.4.66, 17.4.38, 17.3.4 and 17.18.2 define cell/table border
declarations and common attributes. The native reference distinguishes a default `none` from
one carrying a nonzero width, explicit color, spacing, frame or shadow. A
default cell declaration clears the inherited cell side and exposes the table
border. Nondefault `none` suppresses its own ink. Its spacing still contributes
to cell layout; `nil` ignores that spacing. Source width and other attributes
are retained rather than rewritten to imitate the observed effect.

Conditional cell declarations use the same distinction. Part 1 §17.7.6.6
describes sequential application of first-row and last-row formats. The native reference
instead excludes the last-row region when that row already receives first-row
formatting in the crossed controls. Separate bold/italic and shading properties
prove this is exclusion rather than a reversal of the application order.
First-column/first-row controls still combine distinct run properties.

Invisible border extents are separate from painted stroke widths. Shared row
boundaries reserve one extent; mixed cell padding is combined with each cell's
own invisible extent before choosing the row inset. Horizontal writing insets
use half the extent. Legacy automatic left indentation is established from
direct/table borders before conditional cell borders determine the final inset.
Original XML survives no-edit export, unrelated editing and exact undo.

This does not establish complete reference behavior for all combinations. Dedicated
native proof for no-ink spacing at page cuts, repeated headers and opposite
visible edges remains outstanding. A separate right-aligned legacy indentation
probe still differs by approximately half a point. These remain review gaps.

### Single-border table cross junctions

At a four-way intersection, the native reference assigns the overlap to the wider single
border; equal widths belong to the horizontal border regardless of color.
The six original `table-crossing-borders` controls include reversed red/blue
colors and horizontal white against vertical black to distinguish this rule
from shared-edge brightness precedence. The retained reference PDF and hash-bound
reference measure twelve crossings independently of browser layout.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.38 defines table borders and §17.4.66 defines cell borders
and conflict resolution for adjacent coincident edges (printed pp459–461).
Those shared-edge choices remain unchanged. Orthogonal intersection painting
follows the observed reference rule, without a discovered conflicting normative
cross-junction algorithm. §17.18.2 defines the single border style.

The losing stroke excludes the winning stroke's clipped area. These cuts affect
painting only and use stroke-relative coordinates for header/footer translation.
Row heights, border boxes, selection geometry and stored properties stay intact.
Compound/dashed crossings are not newly covered. The later cell-border `none`
controls additionally prove that a continuous horizontal single border caps a
wider terminating vertical single border at both outer T junctions. The blue
2 pt perimeter/red 6 pt divider cases retain independent native ink bounds;
paint-order reversal is also checked. Regression
checks include order independence, story translation, reference pixels, editing,
unrelated-part preservation, exact undo and reopening.


## Page-field capitalization and automatic story refresh

Part 1 §§17.3.2.5 (`caps`), 17.3.2.33 (`smallCaps`), 17.16.5.42 (`NUMPAGES`),
17.16.5.44 (`PAGE`), 17.16.5.55 (`SECTIONPAGES`), 17.16.18 (`fldChar`) and
17.16.19 (`fldSimple`) provide the general semantics. Original controls
in `tests/fixtures/page-field-caps` establish two reference variations:
generated PAGE numerals in page stories retain their number-format case and full run size,
and automatic PAGE/NUMPAGES refresh in headers despite their lock flags.
Locked SECTIONPAGES keeps its cached text, including ordinary capitalization.

Layout applies these distinctions on copied story runs. It does not rewrite
source text, run properties, caches, lock flags or OPC parts. Normal-context
locked field evaluation remains unchanged. All three two-page controls cover
simple/complex PAGE, lower/upper Roman and lower alphabetic formats, direct and
paragraph-style capitalization, and cached section counts. Original downloads
remain exact; header/footer editing is still read-only.

The controls exposed a separate small-caps sizing limitation at 16pt (the native reference
approximately 13pt versus the former 14pt). The correction below addresses it.
Field assertions alone do not establish complete font geometry fidelity.


## Small-cap sizing correction

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.33 describes a fixed two-point reduction. Independent
reference controls instead establish 80% sizing, rounded to half points,
with a 1pt floor. `tests/fixtures/small-caps-sizes` retains the original XML
fixture, six-page reference PDF and measured glyph sizes for 162 cases across three
fonts, half-point boundaries, large text and Latin/Greek/Cyrillic pairs.

The renderer uses this generic rule without changing stored sizes, source
characters, grapheme offsets or package XML. Uppercase letters, digits and
punctuation retain full size; kerning thresholds still compare the original
size before script/width transforms. The previously noted 16pt-to-14pt mismatch
is corrected to the native reference's 13pt. This supersedes the earlier fixed-reduction size
limitation, without claiming complete native font-shaping fidelity.

The independent `small-caps-spaces` controls extend this behavior to ordinary
U+0020 spaces: the native reference gives them the reduced size regardless of neighboring case
or punctuation. NBSP and the tested en/em/thin spaces retain their authored
sizes; tabs retain tab-stop geometry. Automatic line spacing uses the authored
font metrics even if all visible letters are reduced small capitals. This
extends the native compatibility record for §17.3.2.33 and automatic spacing
(§17.3.1.33); the source case, sizes and capitalization XML remain unchanged.

The 37 controls on four native pages cover three fonts/sizes, split runs,
formatting changes, centered text, wrapping and a manual line break. All 286
non-whitespace glyph positions agree within 0.213pt horizontally and 0.152pt
vertically. The test compares neighboring glyph positions instead of treating
PDFium's synthetic space font sizes as native paint evidence. Existing 162-case
size controls remain the half-point/Unicode sizing evidence. Body/table shaping,
carets and painting use the same capitalization parts; no document-specific
offset or font replacement was added.

### Empty shape effects and single-column spacing

Wordprocessing shapes accept empty DrawingML `effectLst` and `sp3d` declarations
(Part 1 §§20.1.8.26 and 20.1.5.12). These contribute no effect or 3D geometry;
nonempty declarations remain unsupported rather than silently losing appearance.
`bodyPr/@spcCol` is validated as a positive coordinate including zero and ignored
for the supported single-column text body, as §21.1.2.1.1 requires. Multiple
columns remain unsupported. Retained XML is unchanged.

The eight original `shape-defaults.docx` controls and their reference PDF establish
equivalent rectangle appearance with/without text. Browser coverage checks native reference
pixel samples, text editing, retained drawing markup, reopening and exact undo.

### DrawingML scRGB and transparency

Shape/group solid fills and outlines accept linear `scrgbClr` as well as sRGB
and scheme colors (§20.1.2.3.30). Conversion retains floating-point channels
through existing color transforms before final paint rounding. Ordered `alpha`,
`alphaMod` and `alphaOff` (§§20.1.2.3.1–3) retain opacity separately from RGB,
clamp after each alpha transform, and composite against the actual canvas
background. Theme placeholders carry transparency into inherited fills/lines.
Optional font-reference colors (§20.1.4.1.17) may be absent; opaque-only text/3D
color consumers still reject translucent colors rather than silently drop alpha.

Twelve independently authored layered controls and the native reference's exported PDF are in
`tests/fixtures/shape-alpha`. Browser checks compare measured reference colors with
one-byte compositing tolerance and retain XML through edit/reopen/exact undo.
These controls agree with the specification. Low-valued drawing layer ordering
exposed a separate reference discrepancy, recorded for further investigation.

### Automatic spacing after inline objects

For object-containing lines, automatic spacing adds leading based on text
metrics while retaining the object's natural height (§§17.3.1.33, 20.4.2.8).
Compressed spacing moves the baseline by the corresponding text contribution;
it does not scale the picture height. Isolated-object minimums still follow
the existing compatibility-mode rule; visible text retains its descender.
Exact and minimum spacing retain their existing behavior. Source spacing values
and drawing XML are not changed.

The 48 original `inline-object-advance` controls compare the following paragraph
as well as object bounds against the native reference, covering zero through double spacing,
small/tall objects, and adjacent text. This closes a gap in the earlier baseline
checks, which did not measure advancement past the object. It fixes the two
extra-page CI failures for large inline drawing controls. The independent
nested-table position failures were subsequently traced to pixel sampling;
see the corpus review's regression follow-up.

### Custom picture geometry

Picture `spPr` accepts the existing validated `custGeom` subset (Part 1
§§20.1.9.8, 20.1.9.15–16; picture properties §20.2.2.6). Standalone and grouped
pictures retain their original source geometry and use line/quadratic/cubic
paths as texture coverage. Unfilled paths contribute no coverage. Guides,
dimensions and unsupported commands pass the same validation as shape geometry;
this does not add support for arcs or adjustment handles.

The twelve original controls in `tests/fixtures/picture-geometry` establish
the native reference's texture mapping under `stretch` (§20.1.8.56): the combined filled path
bounds, including actual curve extrema, define the destination rectangle.
Subpaths within a path use nonzero winding; separate paths paint independently.
Opacity applies per path, accumulating in overlapping translucent areas.
Source crops and reflections compose before ancestor group transforms.
These are measured reference behaviors for details not fully quantified by the
referenced clauses; no normative contradiction has been established.

Browser coverage compares native reference pixels through editing/reopening/exact undo,
including holes, disjoint paths, crop, flip, empty coverage, offset bounds and
transparency. Package parts and original picture markup are retained. Custom
pictures with 3D or standalone rotation and other unsupported
geometry remain explicit import limitations. Music Festival's first-page artwork
now renders; its second-page group still requires nested picture rotation.

### Nested picture rotation

Nested pictures retain validated signed rotations in the drawing scene and
paint about their transformed frame centers (§§20.1.7.5–6, 20.1.10.3;
Annex L §§L.4.7.4–5). Sixteen independently authored reference controls in
`tests/fixtures/group-picture-rotation` confirm the same scale-axis exchange
divergence documented above for rotated lines. Parent scales compose before
rotation; the [45°,135°) and [225°,315°) intervals exchange those scales.
Negative angles normalize without rewriting the retained source XML.

Scene bounds include rotated frame corners, including ink outside group frames.
Custom geometry, texture crops and flips compose in the picture's local frame.
The synthetic inline input used to resolve its texture omits the already
validated scene rotation, avoiding an inapplicable inline effect-extent check.
Original source rotations, extents and package parts remain unchanged.

This restores Music Festival's second-page artwork and editable import. The
schedule table position remains a separate unresolved discrepancy. Rotated
groups, nonrotating fills, rotated custom standalone pictures, 3D pictures and
rotated ordinary shapes/text retain their existing restrictions.

### Explicit AutoFit table widths beyond the writing area

Preferred `tblW` dimensions (§17.4.63) are retained when they exceed the page
writing width or parent cell. The AutoFit caller's available-width limit now
allows an explicitly declared absolute/percentage preferred width, including
indentation and center/right alignment. Automatic widths retain their existing
limit and content constraints; fixed-width allocation is unchanged. The
physical-page overflow guard remains in effect.

Part 1 §§17.4.53 and 17.18.87 start AutoFit from the preferred fixed allocation;
the page-width guidance describes content-driven preference overrides, rather
than an unconditional cap on an already wider declaration. Twelve original
controls in both legacy and mode 15 establish the native reference's behavior, including nested
overflow and conflicting preferences. Their PDF cell rectangles, actual canvas
fill coverage, edit/export/reopen and exact undo are checked independently.
No new normative divergence is claimed.

This corrects Music Festival's schedule from 13,680twips to its declared
14,130twips and restores its column positions without a source-specific rule.

### Content-aware reduction of AutoFit cell preferences

Under §§17.4.63, 17.4.71 and 17.18.87, AutoFit retains the first explicit cell
preference as the column's preferred maximum until distributing the final table
width around content minima. Capping that preference at the already-reduced
fixed allocation loses information and can widen one column at another's
expense. The saved grid, table width and cell preferences remain immutable;
fixed-layout sizing is unchanged.

Sixteen original reference cases in `tests/fixtures/autofit-cell-preferences` vary
content minima, omitted/explicit AutoFit, fixed layout, vertical merges and
compatibility modes 12/15. Absolute column origins and widths agree within
0.2 point, with independent painted-fill, editing, retention, undo and reopen
checks. This matches observed reference behavior within the standard's algorithm
guidance, not a newly identified normative divergence.

### Exact line spacing in drawing text boxes

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.1.33 (spacing), 17.18.48 (line-spacing rule),
17.3.1.38 (text-box contents), and MS-ODRAWXML WPS text bodies apply. Retained
shape text now accepts exact paragraph spacing, including inherited values.
The native reference places the baseline at 80% of the exact line height and allows glyphs to
overlap neighboring line bands, clipping only at the text frame. This is a
documented divergence from §17.18.48's clipping requirement; body paragraphs
retain their existing clipping and font-dependent baseline behavior. Zero
exact spacing retains natural metrics. Group transforms still preserve
physical point sizes and insets.

Eight independently authored `shape-exact-spacing.docx` controls and the
installed reference PDF prove short/tall exact spacing, automatic/minimum spacing,
and top/center/bottom anchoring. Browser tests measure actual ink bands,
preserve drawing XML through edit/reopen, and check exact undo. This removes
one unsupported feature in The Charred Effect; text-box fields and other
unsupported decorations remain separate gaps.

### AutoFit noWrap cell sizing

Part 1 §§17.4.29 (noWrap), 17.4.71 (preferred cell width), 17.18.87 (AutoFit
algorithm), and 17.7.6 (table styles): import direct and inherited noWrap,
including conditional regions and explicit false. AutoFit absolute-width cells
protect their preference; automatic/percentage cells use whole explicit lines
as their minimum. Final wrapping and hard grapheme/padding floors remain active.
Fixed-layout cells ignore noWrap, including when contributing nested intrinsic
widths. Original cell markup is preserved; newly serialized cells emit noWrap
in schema order.

Independent reference controls establish an additional 17-twip allowance on protected
absolute minima, not specified by §17.4.29. Follow this reference-specific behavior
across widths and fonts; no template-specific values are used. When minima
exceed the writing width, compress whole preferred widths proportionally before
enforcing hard floors, matching the native reference's page-limit controls. Twenty-eight original
cases compare fixed/AutoFit, dxa/auto/pct, false/true, multiple widths/font sizes,
short neighbors and forced page-width compression. Native reference PDF cell bounds,
browser painting, edit/reopen, exact undo and malformed/style/unit checks cover
the feature. See `tests/fixtures/table-nowrap/README.md` for evidence and limits.

### Conditional table-row headers

Part 1 §§17.7.6.10 (conditional trPr), 17.4.49 (tblHeader), and 17.7.6
(table styles): import conditional row header flags through the table style
chain, including explicit false and direct overrides. Resolve flags once from
base/direct row regions before refreshing cell/text regions, avoiding circular
band/header evaluation. User changes and inserted body rows retain explicit
overrides across export/reopen; unchanged package parts remain intact.

Independent reference controls establish a distinction between firstRow formatting
and page repetition. With firstRow enabled, formatting includes the first row
and consecutive following marked rows even if the first row is unmarked.
Repetition still requires a contiguous marked run beginning at the first row.
This reference-specific formatting behavior is not defined by the repetition rule
alone. Ten original cases and a 15-page reference PDF cover row/column/band rules,
inheritance, look flags and pagination. See
`tests/fixtures/conditional-row-header/README.md` for reproduction and checks.

Only tblHeader is accepted inside conditional trPr; other regional row
properties remain guarded. MS-OI29500 §2.1.256 also documents reference restrictions
on this container. Conditional tcPr row-wide behavior for noWrap, tcMar and
vAlign needs separate controls; the current cell-region implementation is not
a claim of complete reference behavior for those properties.

### Simultaneous caps and smallCaps

Part 1 §§17.3.2.5, 17.3.2.33 and 17.7.3 apply. The prose prohibits both
elements on one run, but the installed reference accepts all four boolean combinations.
Support this divergence while retaining both source flags: resolve simultaneous
declarations independently, then give effective caps precedence over smallCaps.
Character-style toggles are evaluated before choosing the visible form;
paragraph/table/direct declarations set the flags. Based-on resolution keeps
the nearest declaration of each flag and treats a same-level pair together.
The writer supports both declarations when rebuilding properties, and the
style dialog displays the imported pair without changing it on unrelated edits.

Forty-eight original controls and a four-page reference PDF establish glyph case
and size across direct, paragraph, character and conditional table formatting.
See `tests/fixtures/combined-caps/README.md` for scope and reproducible evidence.

### Paragraph spacing in line units

Part 1 §17.3.1.33 and MS-OI29500 §2.1.60: import beforeLines/afterLines,
including inheritance and explicit zero. The native reference's tested paragraph-gap line unit
is 12pt, independent of font, paragraph-mark and document-default size or
inter-line spacing. Nonzero line units override related point spacing even
from an earlier hierarchy level; zero leaves point spacing active. This is a
documented reference interpretation of the standard's line-unit/precedence prose.
Effective gaps retain the existing 0–600pt bounds and pagination/collapse rules.

Point edits explicitly disable inherited line-unit and automatic flags;
removing style spacing removes the corresponding point, line and automatic
declarations. Unchanged XML and unrelated OPC parts are preserved. Forty-two
original reference controls compare painted gaps and verify edit/export/reopen/undo.
See `tests/fixtures/paragraph-line-units/README.md`. Enabled automatic spacing
remains guarded; its separate six-page diagnostic is evidence for future work,
not a claim of support. Active document-grid interaction remains unverified.

## Page fields in WordprocessingShape text boxes

Part 1 §§17.16.5.42 (NUMPAGES), 17.16.5.44 (PAGE), 17.16.5.55
(SECTIONPAGES), 17.16.18 (fldChar), 17.16.19 (fldSimple), and §17.16.4.3.3
(field result formatting) govern the supported field subset. Drawing text uses the same
field parser as header/footer paragraphs. Nested fields, other instructions and
unsupported switches remain guarded. Shape source XML and cached results are
retained for export; generated values exist only in the drawing preview.

Drawing rasterization receives the physical page's document count, section count
and formatted page number, including section restarts. It resolves each field
before laying out the text box and refreshes after repagination. Groups recurse
through child text boxes. Ordinary shape text can also paint caps/small caps
using the same layout fragments and painter as body text; other unsupported run
decorations retain their guards.

Three independently authored three-page reference controls establish body/header
behavior, simple/complex fields, locked cached values, lowercase Roman/decimal
section restarts and capitalization. With MERGEFORMAT, body fields retain result
formatting. Without it, unlocked body fields use instruction-run properties;
simple fields use paragraph defaults. A distinct 14pt instruction/20pt cached
result proves this independently. In body text boxes PAGE observes caps and
small caps. In repeated headers the native reference instead preserves number-format case and
full run size, refreshing locked PAGE/NUMPAGES but not locked SECTIONPAGES.
This qualifies the earlier page-story-specific reference variation; it is not a
universal exception for PAGE in every story.

The supplied fifth-edition Part 1 §17.16.5.55 describes SECTIONPAGES as the
current page within a section. The native reference instead returns the section's total count:
both pages of the first section display 2, and the last section displays 1.
The independent controls record that divergence; rendering follows the native reference.

References and provenance are in tests/fixtures/shape-page-fields and its header
and plain variants. Tests compare painted strings and font sizes to native reference PDF
output, verify edited page/section counts, round-trip body edits and restore exact
OPC parts after undo. Header/footer editing and text-box content editing remain
unsupported. Multi-run results still use the existing atomic field representation;
these controls do not establish mixed-format result fidelity.

Performance note for later measurement: repeated header drawings currently keep
one raster per asset and replace it when their page context changes. Large
repeated drawings may benefit from a bounded cache of resolved field values.
No general optimization work is included in this rendering fix.

## Paragraph-relative drawing origins and paragraph spacing

Part 1 §§20.4.2.11 (`positionV`) and 20.4.3.5 (`ST_RelFromV`) define
paragraph-relative positioning. §§17.3.1.33 (`spacing`) and 17.3.1.9
(`contextualSpacing`) govern the paragraph gap. The positioning clause identifies
the containing paragraph but does not spell out which spacing edge is the base.
Twelve independent reference controls establish the base before the current
paragraph's contribution to collapsed before-spacing and top-border clearance.
Preceding effective after-spacing remains; contextual and suppressed gaps must
not be subtracted a second time.

Pagination records that applied displacement on the first placed line. Floating
frame placement subtracts it only for paragraph-relative vertical positioning.
Keeping a displacement rather than a page coordinate preserves the existing
translation of lines in table fragments and repeated stories. Paragraph text,
source offsets, page/margin-relative drawings and retained anchor XML do not
change. Positive and negative drawing offsets use the corrected origin.

Original fixture/reference provenance is in tests/fixtures/paragraph-anchor-spacing.
Native reference image matrices are recorded independently from the app; browser checks
measure painted pixels and exercise corrected hit testing, deletion/undo,
body edits, export/reopen and exact-package undo. Unwrapped anchors are proven;
joined borders and complex text-wrapping combinations need further controls.

## WordprocessingShape text-box paragraph edge spacing

Part 1 §21.1.2.1.1 (`bodyPr/@spcFirstLastPara`) specifies suppression of the
first paragraph's before-spacing and last paragraph's after-spacing when false
or omitted. Its examples use DrawingML `a:p`, `spcBef` and `spcAft`. Applied to
WordprocessingShape `wps:txbx/w:txbxContent`, that rule differs from the installed reference: ordinary reference paragraph before/after spacing (§17.3.1.33) remains active
for omitted, false and true flags. The 21 original controls in
`tests/fixtures/shape-edge-spacing` establish this compatibility distinction.

The shape text layout now retains those effective paragraph values for all
three flag states. Center/bottom alignment uses the resulting complete content
height, including final after-spacing, while internal gaps still collapse through
the reference paragraph engine. No source flag, paragraph property, cached field,
shape frame, or OPC part is rewritten. DrawingML-only `a:p` text bodies are not
implemented by this change. Existing overflow, insets, group scaling and
unsupported autofit/vertical text restrictions remain.

The independent reference PDF supplies exact-line baselines and measured ink bands
for top/center/bottom anchoring, before-only/after-only spacing, one/two paragraphs
and zero-spacing controls. The previous grouped-drawing unit expectation was
based on DrawingML edge suppression without a reference text-box reference; it now
checks the behavior established by these controls and source immutability.

## Cell-margin reset precedence

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.68 (tcMar), 17.4.41–42 (tblCellMar),
17.4.60 (tblPrEx), 17.4.87 (table measurements), and 17.7.6 (table styles)
define cell exceptions and table defaults. The MS-OI29500 notes for
[§17.4.35](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/799ae85c-14ec-4a04-a583-768fbb6a05aa)
and [§17.4.77](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/8446a422-0fe8-401b-b11f-a2d4933ee83c)
document the native reference's divergence from the standard's zero interpretation of nil.

The independent 22-page `cell-margin-reset.docx`/reference PDF controls clarify
that ignoring nil does not retain an earlier cell-style exception. A declared
nil, auto or percentage cell side cancels that exception and restores the
applicable table default. Missing declarations retain prior cell exceptions;
explicit dxa zero remains zero. Resolve table-style/direct table defaults,
conditional table defaults and row defaults separately from global/conditional
cell exceptions. An explicit cell-style number wins over a direct table or row
default; direct cell properties are applied last. Derived-style nil survives
until the table defaults are known. No source XML is rewritten for rendering.

`tests/canvas-cell-margin-reset.test.js` checks the independent reference text origins,
resolved margins, untouched package parts, margin edits, inherited reset removal,
row insertion, reopen and exact undo. The browser regression checks actual ink
x edges and body-edit export/reopen. Its README records a separate roughly 1pt
Courier New vertical ink discrepancy; these checks do not claim complete font
or full-document fidelity. Existing margin UI, conditional-border and editing
regressions remain required. New metadata stores resolved table/row defaults on
cells so editing another side cannot accidentally discard a retained nil reset.

## Encoded Symbol numbering glyphs

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.9.11 (lvlText), §17.9.24 (numbering rPr), and
§17.3.2.26 (rFonts) provide the literal label and its font properties. See the
[LevelText reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.leveltext)
and [numbering run properties](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.numberingsymbolrunproperties).
A font vendor's text-engine explanation in the
[Unicode archive](https://www.unicode.org/mail-arch/unicode-ml/Archives-Old/UML022/0292.html)
describes Symbol's private-use encoding and the U+F0B7 bullet.

Retain the encoded glyph alongside the readable label fallback for the existing
supported Symbol bullet. Measurement and painting use U+F0B7 when the selected
available font is Symbol; an unavailable/different resolved font uses U+2022.
Keep the encoded label during numbering regeneration and preserve untouched
numbering XML through body edits. Replacing the label does not reintroduce the
old symbol. Other private-use labels are now supported as literal font-selected
text (see Font-encoded numbering labels below). This correction adds no fonts,
network font loading or third-party dependency.

The original two-page `symbol-bullet.docx` and native reference PDF contain 24 controls for
private-use versus Unicode labels, Symbol versus Arial, 10/20pt sizes and four
bold/italic combinations. Unit tests cover glyph/fallback agreement in measure
and paint, replacement/regeneration and exact package undo. Browser tests check
the eight encoded glyphs against native reference ink relative to their baselines, then
edit/export/reopen. The control README records separate exact-line-spacing,
synthetic style and Unicode-with-Symbol differences; no absolute full-control
fidelity is claimed. Corpus source 22 has automatic line spacing and changes
only in its two bullet glyph regions, with all other pixels unchanged.


## Oversized graphemes in fixed cells

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.2.35 (`spacing`), 17.3.2.43 (`w`), 17.3.1.13 (`jc`),
17.4.52 (`tblLayout`) and 17.18.87 (`ST_TblLayoutType`) define the declarations
and fixed table layout. The independent `oversized-glyph.docx` establishes
the native reference's detailed overflow behavior rather than asserting that the standard
requires rejection of a character wider than the line.

The native reference accepts all 11 controls, wraps each oversized grapheme onto
its own line without changing column widths, uses the left writing origin even
for center/right alignment when no positive alignment space remains, and clips
ink at the physical cell edge. The retained PDF explicitly contains those
clipping rectangles. Controls cover normal, condensed, expanded and scaled
text, combinations, and the editor's upper spacing/scale limits. This corrects
the previous application-only rejection policy, which could discard an entire
styled preview merely because a substituted font widened a drop cap.

Full glyph advances remain available to shaping and DOCX output; visible caret,
hit and selection positions follow the clipped cell area. Oversized inline
pictures retain their independently established behavior. Reversed advances,
vertical/page limits and unsupported document structures retain their existing
safety checks. No dependency or font asset was added. Absolute baseline and
font-substitution fidelity remain separate open requirements.


### Shape edge-spacing checks with substituted fonts

The shape-edge-spacing browser regression captures actual offscreen text paint
baselines and checks all 21 independent reference controls within .15pt. It checks
native glyph bounds at those reference baselines, constrained by the fixture's frame
insets, within 1pt, and retains the original reference ink comparison when the local
Arial face is installed. Both declared-font and deliberately missing-font
variants exercise edit, reopen and exact undo. This corrects a test oracle that
required Arial's ink bounds even when that face was unavailable; it makes no
change to document layout and does not claim substitute-font fidelity to the native reference.


## DrawingML duotone picture effects

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.8.23 defines `duotone` as interpolation between two
DrawingML colors; its schema requires exactly two color choices. The prose
does not specify the grayscale coefficients or rounding. Independent manually
authored controls establish the native reference's quantized Rec.709 sRGB luma (integer weights
2126/7152/722, division by 10000 rounded down), followed by interpolation of
sRGB endpoint channels rounded to the nearest byte. Ordered duotones compose.
The native reference retains source alpha, ignores endpoint-color alpha, and composes existing
`alphaModFix` transparency before or after this RGB-only effect identically.
These compatibility details are retained explicitly rather than inferred from
the interpolation sentence alone.

The shared color reader supports all 190 preset names and aliases from
§20.1.10.48 and saturation modulation from §20.1.2.3.27. Signed and greater-than-
100% modulation scale chroma around HSL lightness and clamp the resulting RGB
channels; reference controls include 0%, 50%, 135%, 200% and -50%, after a 45% shade.
Duotone accepts existing sRGB, scRGB and resolved theme colors and their
supported transforms. Other color models/transforms remain guarded.

Rendering creates a separate session bitmap for each source-media/effect-chain
combination, including nested pictures and shape fills. Raw media, relationships
and original drawing shells remain unchanged on export. New materialized
pictures serialize their resolved duotone endpoint colors. Normal images keep
their existing decoding path. The first effect's 256 possible gray levels form
a color-remapping palette; chained effects do not multiply full-image passes.
No color adjustment is tied to a source document or theme name.

`tools/picture_duotone_fixture.py` authors the original PNG, XML, theme and OPC
parts directly using the standard library. The retained reference PDF and independent
recorder cover 17 cases with 16 grayscale, color and transparency swatches each.
The browser checks painted colors within three channel values, accounting for
the native reference's premultiplied-alpha byte rounding, and verifies edit/export/reopen and
exact undo. Opaque color transforms also match the reference swatches exactly in
unit checks. The corpus brochure remains partial because of a separate
positioned-picture restriction. No dependencies or third-party assets were added.

### Floating custom-picture crop and reflection

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.8.55–56 (`srcRect`/`stretch`), §20.1.7.6
(`xfrm`), §20.1.9.8 (`custGeom`), and §§20.4.2.3/20.4.2.15
(`anchor`/`wrapNone`) permit source cropping and reflection inside a floating
picture's geometry. The previous blanket positioned-image restriction incorrectly
rejected these retained picture scenes. Custom-geometry pictures now retain those
transforms in their existing scene renderer; ordinary transformed positioned
images and unsupported rotated/3D custom pictures retain their guards.

Eight independently authored reference controls verify positive/negative crop offsets,
both reflections independently and together, duotone with 50% opacity, and a
triangular clip. Interior/exterior color comparisons repeat after editing, undo,
and reopening; source/PDF hashes bind the reference. Original drawing markup and
untouched OPC parts survive export, with exact package restoration after undo.
No reference/spec divergence was found for these controls.

### Rotated ordinary shapes and physical outline width

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.7.5–6 (`xfrm`), §20.1.10.3 (`ST_Angle`),
§20.1.9.8 (`custGeom`) and §20.1.2.2.24 (`ln`) describe retained shape geometry,
rotation, reflection and outlines. Non-text shapes now retain signed rotations
normalized modulo one full turn, with integer/range validation. The independent
16-case reference control confirms the scale-axis exchange previously documented for
pictures and lines also applies to custom shapes and ellipses: the native reference exchanges
ancestor scale axes in [45,135) and [225,315) before rotating about the scaled
center. This compatibility behavior is preserved instead of a simple local
rotation followed by anisotropic ancestor scaling.

The same control exposes an older shape-outline bug: the native reference keeps the pen width
physical while transforming the path. All shape paths now stroke in page units,
consistent with the already supported preset-line renderer. Allocation includes
physical cap/join extents. Rotated curve bounds transform the control points
before computing extrema; ellipse bounds use the transformed radii. Original
vector XML, relationship/media parts and undo semantics remain unchanged.
Rotated shape text and rotated groups still require separate support.

Empty WordprocessingShape text boxes do not prevent ordinary shape rotation.
The importer fully validates `wps:txbx`/`wps:bodyPr`, then distinguishes retained
empty paragraphs from actual text or fields. Empty paragraph data and autofit
settings remain in the scene; source XML remains untouched. Actual text/fields
on rotated shapes still require separate support. Independent controls in
`tests/fixtures/rotated-empty-text` pair absent and empty text boxes at four
angles, including upright=true on an empty box; the native reference paints identical geometry
within each pair. This establishes no additional reference/spec divergence.

### DrawingML grayscale picture effect

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.8.34 (`grayscl`) converts colors to luminance without
changing alpha. The eight-case independent reference control confirms its sRGB
Rec.709 quantization matches black-to-white duotone exactly. The importer now
adds that mapping at its original position in the existing ordered effect
pipeline, preserving transparency, alpha modifiers and noncommuting duotone
order. Matching effect chains share decoded assets and original media bytes.
Original drawing shells retain `a:grayscl`; new shells use its equivalent
black-to-white duotone representation. Unsupported attributes/children/text and
effects after the extension list remain guarded.

### Ellipse picture geometry and character spacing

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.9.18 (`prstGeom`) and §20.1.10.56 (`ST_ShapeType`)
define the ellipse preset. Picture import now retains that ellipse clip using
the existing curve renderer, including source crops, flips, alpha and ordered
color effects. Nested pictures retain clipping in their parent scene. Adjusted
ellipses and unsupported standalone rotations remain guarded; the existing 3D
path is unchanged. Nine independent reference controls cover eight floating cases
and one inline grayscale case, with pixel comparisons through editing and reopen.

Character spacing (§17.3.2.35) on an inline drawing (§20.4.2.8) remains in its
run formatting/XML but adds nothing to its advance. Five independent reference
controls use 0, ±10 and ±50pt spacing: every 144pt-wide picture begins at 36pt
and the following unspaced text begins at 180.05pt. Import, direct/style edits
and insertion now accept that formatting; the existing picture layout already
has the correct advance. Adjacent text continues to use its own spacing.
The specification does not explicitly resolve drawing-placeholder spacing;
these controls establish native reference behavior without an explicit spec contradiction.

### Solid document background and automatic ink

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.2.1 (`background`) supplies a document-wide fill behind all
page content. Solid RGB and theme colors (including mapping, tint and shade)
now enter the page model and painter. Absent/automatic backgrounds use white.
Unchanged background XML and theme declarations survive unrelated edits; explicit
model background changes serialize a solid RGB declaration or remove it for auto.
Drawing/image/gradient background children remain unsupported for editable import.

Transparent cells and unshaded paragraphs inherit the page fill when resolving
automatic text. Explicit cell, paragraph and run shading retain their precedence.
The independent two-document reference controls confirm automatic text ignores the
highlight overlay (§17.3.2.15), while run shading (§17.3.2.32) changes its contrast.
This follows the native reference's consumer-defined automatic color behavior (§17.3.2.6), not a
claimed explicit specification contradiction. Explicit foreground colors remain
unchanged even when they have poor contrast. The existing contrast threshold is
retained; these controls establish dark/light cases, not every intermediate RGB.

### Retaining empty header/footer parts during body edits

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.10.1–2 and §§17.10.5–6 define footer/header parts and their
section references. A reference alone no longer forces read-only mode when every
referenced story contains only paragraphs and paragraph properties. Relationships,
content types, variants and formatting still validate; original story parts and
references are retained through body editing and export. The later retained-story
extension below permits supported runs; bookmarks, controls and tables still
require additional story support.

An empty paragraph is not necessarily invisible: the independent reference companion
control adds shared paragraph shading and paints bands in all six header/footer
variants. Editable story layout therefore resolves current shared styles once per
story per layout, without mutating imported paragraphs. Changed styles are also
validated against retained stories during export. Browser layout validation occurs
before installing an editable document. Direct story-text editing is still absent.


### Repeated DrawingML geometry guides

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.9.11–12 specifies ordered guide calculation and named
references; its name attribute does not require uniqueness. Repeated names in
adjustment/guide lists now replace the current binding, without recalculating
previously evaluated dependents. Explicit built-in-name replacement is supported.
The native reference independently renders the nine authored controls in
`tests/fixtures/geometry-guide-rebinding`: duplicates, adjustment/guide collisions,
prior-value snapshots, built-in replacement and ordinary self-reference.

Native reference compatibility extension: a currently evaluating ordinary guide resolves
its own name to zero, including on redeclaration. This differs from interpreting
ordered calculation as reuse of the previous declaration; the specification does
not explicitly define this self-reference case. Unknown/forward references,
invalid formulas and nonfinite results remain rejected. Self-referential built-in
names remain guarded: the exploratory `w` control produced off-page geometry in
the native reference and does not establish a safe general rule. This unresolved case is not
claimed as supported. Painting does not evaluate source formulas; source XML is
retained through edits and exact undo.


### Inactive shape text orientation

ECMA-376 Part 1 §21.1.2.1.1 defines `bodyPr/@upright` as a boolean, default false,
that affects text transforms. Explicit false is accepted. True is accepted when
there is no text box or only empty text paragraphs, with no text or field runs to
orient. The existing checks still reject decorated paragraphs/runs, active upright
text and unsupported rotated text. No shape geometry or text layout is changed.

The eight original `shape-upright-inactive` controls cover both boolean spellings,
missing text boxes, an empty centered paragraph and explicit false with text.
The installed reference renders the entire page identically to the baseline control at
144 DPI. Retained shape XML, body edits, reopening and exact undo are checked.


### Saved invisible fills

MS-ODRAWXML §2.3.1.5 `hiddenFill` retains `a:CT_FillProperties` when a shape's
fill is invisible; visible shape fills ignore it. The importer now accepts its
standard extension URI on shapes and pictures, checks the namespace, container
attributes and single fill choice, and preserves the dormant subtree. It does
not paint it, decode its images or require its fill type to be actively supported.
Unknown or duplicate extensions and malformed fill containers remain guarded.
The independent conformance checker validates the complete subtree using the
existing hash-pinned MS-ODRAWXML declaration and ECMA fill schema.

Eight original reference controls pair visible and invisible shapes with saved red
fills and preserve saved gradient, pattern, picture and group fills. Unit/browser
checks cover unchanged appearance, retained XML, body edits, reopening, exact
undo and coexistence with shadow flags and saved outlines in grouped drawings.
No reference/spec divergence was found. No dependency was added.

Specification: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-odrawxml/51d55b23-c9a5-483a-b9eb-a0dd11d46ab5


### Tables crossing the paper edge

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.50, 17.4.52, 17.4.87 and ST_TblLayoutType govern signed
indentation and preferred sizing. Table geometry may extend beyond the physical
page; it is no longer rejected merely for doing so. Cells retain their logical
widths, wrapping, source text and export properties. Canvas page bounds clip ink;
body-paragraph writing-area guards and invalid cell-width checks remain intact.
Lists in overflowing table cells use their containing writing area.

Native reference compatibility difference: independent controls in compatibility modes 12
and 15 show negative nested indentation clamped at the containing writing edge;
positive nested indentation remains effective. §17.4.50 does not specify this
nested clamp. Stored indentation remains unchanged on export. The same controls
show that an exact-height containing cell clips horizontally overflowing nested
content. Optional horizontal cell-clip bounds now compose and propagate through
alignment, header repeats, fills, text, images, borders and interaction.

Original evidence is in `tests/fixtures/table-page-edge`. Nine cases per mode
cover fixed/AutoFit widths, both edges, alignment, wholly off-page content and
nested tables. Pixel comparisons certify fill coverage and clipping, not all
text appearance: the medium-blue control reveals an existing automatic-ink
contrast discrepancy (reference black, canvas white) that remains open.

### Page/margin floating drawings anchored in cells

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.4.2.3, 20.4.2.10–13 describe anchors and positioning.
Unwrapped, fixed-size drawings whose two coordinate bases are page or margin
now resolve against their physical table cell. Horizontal offsets/alignment use
its full width; vertical offsets use its top plus top cell margin. The native reference ignores
the anchor's vertical alignment in these cases. They neither grow the row nor acquire the
row's text clip, including exact-height rows. Source anchor coordinates and
flags remain untouched through export. Body positioning is unchanged.

Reference/spec divergence: §20.4.2.3 describes cell resizing for layoutInCell=true and
specified positioning with table adjustment for false. Independent mode-12 and
mode-15 reference controls show no row growth for these wrapNone drawings. Mode 15
also treats false as true, whereas mode 12 honors page/margin coordinates for
false. Layout now applies these compatibility behaviors without rewriting the
flag. Behind-document drawings remain below table fills.

`tests/fixtures/table-global-anchors` contains 44 independently authored reference pages covering flags, alignment, signed offsets, cell margins, a later
anchor paragraph, overflow and exact rows. Other mixed axes, cell-relative percentage
sizes and other wrapping modes remain outside this new subset. Existing
column/paragraph-relative floating-cell behavior remains separately tested.

Numeric column-relative horizontal/page-relative vertical `wrapNone` anchors
also use this physical-cell reference. Independent controls in
`tests/fixtures/mixed-cell-anchors` cover modern/legacy modes, layoutInCell
true/false and behind/in-front stacking. All eight reference frames establish the
same compatibility behavior: mode 12 with layoutInCell=false uses the page's
column and page top; the other cases use the physical cell. Alignment-based
column/page combinations remain unsupported in cells. Source coordinates and
flags are retained through edits, export and undo.

Cell `w:vAlign` (§17.4.85) is separate from anchor `wp:align`: center/bottom
alignment includes these drawings' bottom bounds in the content extent and
translates both text and drawings by the resulting free-space shift. Independent
`tests/fixtures/mixed-cell-alignment` controls cross top/center/bottom cells,
page/column horizontal coordinates, and pictures/zero-height lines. A 12pt left
cell margin displaces column-relative anchors but not page-relative anchors.
Alignment
does not resize their exact rows. Nested content retains its own cell shift;
outer-cell movement is already reflected by its physical cell box. Legacy
layoutInCell=false page-bound positioning remains separate.

### Tiled shape picture fills

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.8.14, 20.1.8.55 and 20.1.8.58 define picture fill,
source cropping and tile scale/alignment/offset/flip. Retained shape fills now
support tiled PNG/JPEG textures. The same validated relationship, crop, color
and opacity readers serve stretched and tiled fills. Native Canvas patterns
repeat the visible texture within each shape path, preserving the original
vector/package XML and avoiding tile-count-dependent drawing loops.

Nineteen independent reference controls establish tile periods, phase, polygon
clipping and crop behavior. Native reference compatibility differences: these shape fills
ignore the declared tile flip; physical tile size uses image density rather
than explicit blipFill DPI, and source outsets repeat the visible image region.
The source attributes remain untouched. Nonpositive scale has no fill ink.

PNG pHYs and JPEG JFIF/Exif resolution readers inspect bounded metadata without
pixel decoding. The core reference PNG controls cover density and local-DPI flags;
four extended density controls have unit coverage but their additional reference
capture remains pending (see `tests/fixtures/picture-tiles/README.md`). Tiled
vector images, ordinary pic:pic tile fills and nonrotating tiled fills on rotated
shapes are not added by this change. No runtime dependency was introduced.

### Unused positional tab stops inside shape text

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.1.37–38 define positional tab stops used by paragraph tab
characters. Shape paragraphs without tab characters now retain validated left,
center, right and decimal tab declarations without rejecting the entire drawing.
The underlying paragraph reader still rejects unsupported/malformed stops,
including bar tabs. Active custom tabs remain outside the shape text subset.

Eight original controls show identical reference glyph boxes and 40 raster samples
with and without the unused stops; no reference/spec divergence was observed. Source
