XML remains intact through adjacent body edits and exact undo. Validation:
61 targeted unit checks, four browser edit/export/reopen checks, 27 fixture/export
XML checks and the production build/license gate pass.

### Preserve table previews around unsupported cell anchors

The supported cell-position combinations for ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.4.2.3 anchors
are now checked during import, while the read-only reader can still replace
only the unsupported drawing. Previously a mixed coordinate basis could reach
layout, fail there, and force the entire document into a plain-text preview.
This does not add mixed-coordinate positioning support or change supported
page/margin and column/paragraph placement. Original package parts remain intact.

A variant of the original 22-page table-anchor control changes one vertical
basis to paragraph. The browser retains 22 table pages and neighboring artwork,
omits the unsupported drawing, disables editing and downloads the original
package exactly. Ten targeted unit tests, five browser checks, 20 XML checks
and the production build/license gate pass.

### Closed compound shape outlines and omitted outline width

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.2.2.24 defines `a:ln`, §20.1.10.15 names
`ST_CompoundLine` values, and §20.1.8.48 defines preset dashes. Closed shape
contours now support double, thick/thin, thin/thick and triple outlines with
transparent gaps and preset dashes. Independent reference controls establish band/gap
ratios of 1:1:1, 3:1:1, 1:1:3 and 1:1:2:1:1 respectively. Curve subdivision in
physical coordinates and a seam at the last flattened vertex match the recorded
native reference rectangle and ellipse dashes; these numeric rules are inferred from native reference
output, not specified by the compound enum. Existing raster density is unchanged.
Open compound paths and explicit zero-width compound hairlines remain guarded.

**Reference/spec divergence:** the `ln` clause describes omitted `w` as zero; the native reference
renders an omitted width as 0.75 pt (9525 EMU), for single and compound lines.
The original `shape-outline-default-width.docx` and its reference PDF prove this:
single strokes set PDF line width to 0.75 and compound edges extend 0.375 pt
on either side of the path. The importer uses this default only for absent
width, preserving explicit and inherited widths and original package XML.

Original fixtures cover rectangular and curved geometry at two sizes, solid and
system dashes, source preservation through editing, export/reopen and exact undo.
Reference provenance and remaining limits are recorded under
`tests/fixtures/shape-compound-outlines` and `shape-outline-default-width`.

Validation for this change: 77 targeted unit checks (including theme inheritance),
11 browser checks, 78 source/export XML schema passes, and the production
build/license gate pass. The browser checks include 14,324 exact compound-line
RGB samples plus 5,928 stable omitted-width control samples. These results do
not establish support for all DrawingML geometries or pending corpus features.

### Relative-sized page/margin drawings inside cells

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.4.2.3 supplies the anchor placement rules; the
[MS-ODRAWXML §5.11 schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-odrawxml/1a38a99a-16ae-420d-8c79-23dc2e922717)
defines `wp14:sizeRelH` / `sizeRelV`. Existing no-wrap page/margin placement in
cells now accepts the supported page/margin relative sizes. Size percentages
use physical section geometry, independently of the cell-coordinate placement.
Zero placeholders retain the saved dimension. Existing mode-12/mode-15 behavior,
cell padding, stacking and overflow rules remain intact.

Native reference controls also show that standalone pictures fit proportionally inside the
requested relative box; groups scale their two axes independently. Alignment
uses the requested box before the picture fit. The importer retains that picture
semantics separately from grouped drawings, including outside cells. This is an
observed reference rendering refinement, not a newly identified normative conflict.
Source drawing markup stays untouched through surrounding edits and exact undo.

Original controls cover 44 table-picture pages across compatibility modes,
four grouped-picture pages and four ordinary body-picture pages. Existing fixed
anchor and header controls remain regression checks. Additional positive-size
bases and wrapping modes remain outside the supported subset; arbitrary changes
to a group's physical dimensions still have the previously documented scene
text/stroke scaling limitations.

Validation: 41 targeted unit checks, 13 browser checks, 97 source/export XML
schema checks and the production build/license gate pass. The restaurant source
was also reopened and visually compared on both pages; its original package
remains byte-identical on download and its remaining image issue is still tracked.

### EMF vector picture playback

DrawingML `a:blip` image relationships (ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.8.13) now accept
EMF parts with `image/emf` or the native reference's `image/x-emf` content type, after signature,
record framing and supported-operation validation. The original vector reader
implements the MS-EMF path, solid brush/pen, mapping, world-transform and clipping
subset documented in `tests/fixtures/emf-paths/README.md`. It preserves the source
media and drawing XML through surrounding text editing, export/reopen and undo.
Unsupported operations remain a read-only fallback; arbitrary metafiles are not
silently treated as complete drawings. Raster/SVG image paths remain separate.
No runtime dependency or third-party implementation was added.

Relevant specifications: MS-EMF [header](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-emf/e4a35c41-e8e3-43f9-bc07-a18e99bb866d),
[path brackets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-emf/b930b989-30ec-4954-a889-1dc60ce0b689),
[extended pens](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-emf/5b67b3ee-ea00-4f80-9b73-2959804381be),
and [path clipping](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-emf/4a26bcf8-6607-4a09-8ec3-a8768eadc8e8).

**Reference/spec divergence:** [§2.3.11.21](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-emf/2637d0d0-92dd-48e8-be5e-6400b4d1fc5e)
declares an integer miter limit, but [Appendix A note 90](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-emf/f5148c7c-30c5-4d95-bf1b-b449c1f8f53d)
documents Windows FLOAT playback. Independently authored DOCX controls encode
both integer 10 and float 10; their reference PDFs demonstrate different join tips.
The implementation follows the native reference. A third control proves that physical frame
placement is independent of the tighter ink bounds.

Validation: 73 distinct targeted unit checks, 18 browser checks, 125 source/export
XML schema passes, and the production build/license gate pass. One optional
private birthday-card browser check was skipped because its path was unset.
The existing multi-import malformed-raster test exceeded its default five-second
limit; its assertions passed on rerun with a 30-second per-run timeout. No
repository timeout configuration was changed. The actual restaurant brochure
passed body editing, export/reopen, unrelated-part preservation and exact undo.

## Imported text with no declared font size

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.38 (`sz`) inherits the previous hierarchy level and allows
a consumer-selected size when none is declared at any level. DOCX import now
uses the native reference's 10 pt fallback instead of the editor's 12 pt authored-document
setting. Explicit document defaults, table/paragraph/character styles and direct
sizes retain their existing precedence. No default size is injected into the
source package; new documents still serialize their explicit 12 pt default.

The manually authored `default-run-size.docx` control compares an unspecified
Arial run with explicit 10 and 12 pt runs. The native reference's PDF exports 9.96, 9.96 and 12 pt
respectively. The control, PDF and hashes are recorded in
`tests/fixtures/default-run-size/README.md`. This consumer choice is permitted by
the specification rather than a reference/spec divergence. Unit and browser coverage
checks inherited/explicit sizes, new-document settings and edit/reopen/exact undo.

## System colors in DrawingML shapes

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.2.3.33 (`sysClr`) and 20.1.10.58
(`ST_SystemColorVal`) bind drawing colors to named system elements. `lastClr`
is an optional record of the generating application's last computed RGB value;
it does not override that binding. Shape fills, outlines and drawing style
references now accept all 30 system names. Existing ordered tint/shade,
luminance/saturation and alpha transforms apply after resolving the base color.
Unknown tokens, malformed saved colors/attributes and unsupported transforms
remain guarded. Original color markup survives no-edit and unrelated editing.

Rendering uses the standard Windows system palette verified against the installed reference
and `GetSysColor` on the reference host. It is independent of application
CSS and dark mode. Browser legacy CSS system colors do not faithfully expose
all native colors (for example window frames and active borders). Custom OS
palettes are not yet represented; this is a documented rendering limitation.
The existing cached theme-color reader, chart color reader and 3-D material
restrictions are unchanged by this addition.

The original `system-colors.docx` fixture exercises all 30 names, four
contradictory saved colors, tint and transparency. The native reference's independent PDF is
checked at 324 interior RGB samples, with edit/export/reopen/exact-undo coverage.
Source, PDF hashes and recording method are in
`tests/fixtures/system-colors/README.md`. The saved-color behavior agrees with
the standard; no reference/spec divergence is claimed.


### Automatic paragraph spacing and cell border clipping

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.33 (`spacing`) and Part 4 §14.8.3.15
(`doNotUseHTMLParagraphAutoSpacing`). Automatic before/after flags inherit
through the existing paragraph property cascade, accept the OOXML on/off
spellings, and override point/line-unit gaps. Rendering uses the native reference's 14pt HTML
spacing, suppresses automatic before-spacing at the start of a story and at
cell starts, suppresses automatic after-spacing at cell ends, and suppresses
adjacent automatic gaps within the same abstract numbering definition.
Different list definitions retain the gap. Empty paragraphs retain their gaps.
Explicit point edits turn off only the affected automatic flag; no-edit and
undo exports retain all original package entries exactly.

**Reference/spec divergence:** the fixed-HTML compatibility flag is specified to
substitute 5pt before and 10pt after. Original reference controls instead show that
the native reference ignores automatic flags, uses inherited/explicit gaps, and adds adjacent
gaps, including on ordinary paragraphs. The renderer follows this observed
behavior. The retained setting is validated and preserved through export.
Seven original fixtures and 22 native reference pages document the distinction in
`tests/fixtures/automatic-spacing/README.md`; their generator, PDF hashes,
baselines, layout tests, browser paint checks and edit/undo tests are retained.

Paragraph borders (`pBdr`, Part 1 §17.3.1.24) can extend outside a cell because
of their text distance or paragraph indents. The native reference clips their ink at the cell
boundary. The renderer now clips each border to its physical cell fragment,
intersected with existing exact-row/nested-cell clips, instead of rejecting
that layout. Body-page guards remain in effect. The independent three-row
control and native reference are in `tests/fixtures/paragraph-border-overflow`.
This change proves cell clipping, not exact border offset/raster equivalence.

### Unwrapped drawings anchored to table-cell paragraphs

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.4.2.3 (`anchor`), 20.4.2.10–11
(`positionH`/`positionV`) and 20.4.2.15 (`wrapNone`). Column/paragraph-relative
unwrapped drawings no longer inflate paragraph or row height, force keep-lines,
or clip to automatic/exact cell boundaries. Their ink remains on the anchor's
page. Center/bottom cell alignment includes the drawing's bottom extent in its
content envelope without adding that extent to text flow. Unsupported mixed
coordinate systems and wrapping modes retain their existing guards.

**Proven reference/spec divergence:** the anchor's layoutInCell description says
the cell is resized as needed for true, and describes a table-line rather than
cell reference for false. Independent reference controls instead retain cell height
even when a wrapNone drawing lies entirely outside the cell. For column offsets
with false, compatibility mode 12 uses the document-column origin, while mode 15
uses the cell origin. Rendering follows these measured reference behaviors.

Six original OPC/XML controls and 28 native reference pages cover automatic,
minimum and exact heights, paragraph counts, negative/overflowing offsets,
foreground/background order, vertical alignment, a second-paragraph anchor,
and an indented second-cell origin. Sources, PDF hashes and geometry are recorded
in `tests/fixtures/cell-anchor-flow/README.md`. Unit and browser checks cover
geometry, ink outside cells, hit testing, selection, resize/edit/export/reopen
and exact undo. This does not claim support for additional wrapping modes.

### Joined paragraph border clearance

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.1.5 (`between`), 17.3.1.7 (`bottom`),
17.3.1.24 (`pBdr`) and 17.3.1.42 (`top`). Ordinary adjacent paragraphs with
identical border sets use only their between-border clearance. Pagination no
longer adds top-border clearance again when beginning a new keep-next group.
Explicit page and section boundary spacing adjustments retain their existing
top clearance. Differing border sets still reserve both touching edges.

The original `joined-border-spacing-12.docx` and `-15.docx` controls cover body
and cell paragraphs, with and without keep-next, a between border, and a changed
bottom distance. Sixteen reference pages and hashes are recorded in
`tests/fixtures/joined-border-spacing/README.md`. The native reference agrees with the standard;
this correction introduces no compatibility exception. Regression coverage
includes painted baselines, border edits, package preservation, reopen/undo and
explicit page-break clearance.

### Continuous paragraph shading at fractional raster boundaries

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.31 (`shd`) and the adjoining paragraph border clauses
§§17.3.1.5, .7, .24 and .42. Consecutive same-color paragraph shading rectangles
paint as one path, preventing independently blended shared edges from exposing
the page color. A gap is included only when matching opaque single-border ink
covers it completely, including polygon corners and cell clipping. Different
colors, patterned borders and uncovered gaps do not receive that fill.
Logical shading bounds, layout, serialization and later border paint order are
unchanged for the remaining ink. The already-filled interior is subtracted from
later border bands to avoid a second fractional alpha blend. This fixes raster
coverage; it introduces no reference/spec divergence.

The original eight-page `paragraph-shading-seams.docx` native reference control and pixel
samples are retained in `tests/fixtures/paragraph-shading-seams`. Browser checks
cover three display scales, contrasting dividers, edit/export/reopen and exact
undo. Unit checks include clipped/incomplete coverage and changing widths.

### Horizontal paragraph decoration extent

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.1.31 (`shd`), 17.3.1.24 (`pBdr`) and 17.3.4
(`CT_Border`). The native reference extends paragraph shading and the border reference frame
by approximately 1.5pt on each horizontal side of the indented text rectangle.
This measured convention is not prescribed by the standard's border-distance
attribute. The extension is independent of the declared distance, border width,
paragraph font and document default font. The renderer now includes it only in
paint bounds; text wrapping, source offsets, indents and serialized XML retain
their original values. Existing page/cell clipping contains the additional ink.

Five original controls and 27 native reference PDF pages are retained in
`tests/fixtures/paragraph-paint-width`. The side controls also record separate
remaining gaps: shading beside a lone left border, and retained spacing for
explicit none/zero-width borders. Those are not claimed resolved by this width
correction. Reference tests state which fill cases are compared and continue
to check the active border coordinates.

### Persistent inline rich-text controls

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.5.2.31/36 (run-level control/content), 17.5.2.26
(rich text), 17.5.2.39 (placeholder state), 17.5.2.43 (`temporary`) and
17.17.4 (boolean properties). Omitted or false `temporary` retains an unlocked
inline rich-text wrapper when its contents change. Supported controls retain
their ID, alias/tag, properties, run formatting and package parts through text
edits, formatting, hyperlinks, internal bookmarks, export/reopen and undo.
Temporary controls retain their existing text-edit removal behavior.

Typing replaces displayed placeholder content using the input properties and
clears `showingPlcHdr`. Deleting all content restores the declared single-paragraph
text placeholder from the related glossary part, including its run formatting;
without a definition, an imported placeholder cache is retained when available,
otherwise the reference's five-space default is used. The glossary package
part itself is not rewritten. Search replacement retains persistent ownership
and adjusts bookmarks for restored placeholder length.

Glossary run content also supports manual line breaks (`w:br`, including
explicit `textWrapping`/`clear=none`, and `w:cr`) and page breaks. These use
the same run-level break characters as ordinary document content; they do
not split the inline control's paragraph. Column and text-clearing breaks
remain unsupported, and malformed break attributes/children are rejected.
ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.3.1 defines `br`; the
[carriage-return definition](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.carriagereturn)
specifies the same line-ending behavior as a default break. The original
`placeholder-breaks.docx` control and native reference restoration capture verify
both forms, retained bold/color formatting and the unchanged paragraph/control
count. Export normalizes restored manual breaks to `w:br` while preserving
the original glossary part; undo restores all original package parts.

Ordinary inline drawings retain persistent ownership. Picture insertion uses the
actual replaced prompt's position, including when the original caret was inside
the prompt. Replacements spanning an entire unlocked control and surrounding
text remove that selected wrapper. Explicit false placeholder flags are retained
on unrelated edits and changed only when the placeholder state changes.

Inline paragraph splits are rejected before changing the model, consistent with
the native reference's limited editing-zone error in the original probe. Nested inline controls,
locked/data-bound controls, widgets, persistent block wrappers, non-text or
multi-paragraph glossary definitions, and empty imported wrappers remain outside
this supported subset. Explicit persistent boundary affinity is currently inward;
the retained COM probes establish this for ranges derived from the control, not
every mouse-caret boundary interaction. Ambiguous grapheme boundary edits are
rejected rather than silently stripping a persistent wrapper.

Original OPC fixtures, nine successful reference edit snapshots, the rejected split,
a baseline PDF and a glossary-restoration snapshot are retained under
`tests/fixtures/persistent-inline-controls`. This is implementation of the
specified lifetime, not a claimed reference/spec divergence.

## Page-border preview isolation

Page borders (Part 1 section 17.6.10) are distinct from pgMar (17.6.11), pgSz
(17.6.13) and cols (17.6.4). Unsupported border parsing must not replace valid
section geometry with application defaults. Best-effort import now recovers
pageBorders independently in both final and paragraph-ended sections, retaining
size, margins, orientation, columns and other supported page settings. Strict
import still throws; the recovered package stays read-only and cannot export
edits. Original downloads preserve unsupported border markup and all other parts.

The independent border-preview fixture exercises two page sizes, orientations,
asymmetric margins and columns against the native reference. Unit tests compare the
border-free control and retain guards for unsupported art and shadow styles.
Browser checks verify native text geometry and original download/reopen. This
does not implement art borders or promise complete geometry recovery for every
other unsupported page-setting combination. No standard divergence is asserted.

## Linked numbering styles

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.9.21 (numStyleLink) and 17.9.27 (styleLink)
define abstract numbering indirection through a numbering style. The importer
resolves the matching styleLink definition, following the numbering style's
basedOn chain when needed. Native controls establish that the style's numId
does not supply the definition or instance overrides. A valid linked definition
replaces local levels. The caller's abstract ID and instance overrides remain
unchanged, preserving independent alias sequences and explicit restarts.

The importer projects resolved levels into memory and leaves all source XML
untouched. Editing and restarting retain source definitions and cloned instance
metadata. Resolution detects style/abstract cycles and ambiguous or missing
styles/backlinks. An existing local level remains usable when the valid style
has no backlink, matching the native control. Empty unresolved aliases remain
guarded: the native reference's marker/indent suppression for those aliases is demonstrated but
not yet implemented. This is a stated gap, not a claim of full numbering support.

Independent controls: tests/fixtures/linked-numbering (16 cases with/without
backlinks, native reference PDFs and hash-bound marker/image references). Unit tests
cover exact labels, inheritance, override precedence, edits, splitting, restart,
undo, reopening and invalid links. Browser checks compare native glyph geometry
through edit/undo/reopen. No specification divergence is asserted.

## DrawingML cloud and cloud-callout presets

ECMA-376 Part 1 section 20.1.9 (DrawingML geometry), including arcTo and prstGeom,
and the accompanying presetShapeDefinitions.xml define cloud and cloudCallout.
The importer implements their body contours, interior outline segments, text
rectangle and two callout adjustments. Ellipse ray angles are converted to
parametric angles before generating cubic segments of at most 45 degrees.
Callout bubbles use the shorter physical side for their radii and retain circular
geometry on wide/tall shapes; they may extend outside the shape rectangle.
Source preset XML and adjustment formulas remain untouched during export.

Eight independently authored reference controls cover default, diagonal and cardinal
callout positions on wide/tall shapes. Native PDF operators establish that all
fills precede all strokes, keeping overlapping bubble outlines visible. The
immutable cloud scene explicitly records this order. No specification divergence
is asserted. Browser tests compare retained reference pixels through editing, undo and
reopening, with explicit rasterizer tolerance. Round-trip tests bind source/PDF
hashes and verify package preservation. Existing custom geometry, flips, group
rotation, triangle and frame controls remain regression coverage.

This adds cloud presets, not arbitrary custom arcTo support. Degenerate callout
positions with zero distance to the body boundary are guarded rather than
producing nonfinite coordinates. Native cloud text and such degenerate positions
remain calibration gaps. Fixture: tests/fixtures/cloud-callouts.

## DrawingML frame preset

ECMA-376 Part 1's `ST_ShapeType` (§20.1.10.56) and the accompanying published
`presetShapeDefinitions.xml` define `frame` with default `adj1=12500`, pinned to
0–50000. Thickness is the shorter dimension multiplied by that adjustment over
100000. The outer and inner rectangles have opposite winding, preserving a
transparent opening; the opening also defines the text rectangle. Import now
resolves this geometry into the existing retained drawing scene. Source XML is
preserved through body edits, export and undo.

The independent `frame-shapes.docx` and native reference cover omitted, ordinary,
zero, maximum and out-of-range adjustments in non-square frames. Unit tests
also cover portrait dimensions and invalid formulas. No reference/spec divergence
was found. This adds one published preset, not arbitrary preset support.

## Compatible table-shading scope

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.32 says omitted cell shading uses table-level or table
exception shading. The native reference instead uses the table's cell style, as documented in
[MS-OI29500 §2.1.144(b)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/4f0cccae-70c2-492a-bc94-3ccc39172119).
The original five-page `table-shading-scope.docx` proves this divergence in
the installed reference: direct table, table-style and conditional-region `tblPr/shd`
leave cells unfilled. Ordinary/conditional `tcPr/shd` still inherits, and a
direct cell declaration still overrides it. Native reference PDFs and independently sampled
colors are retained under `tests/fixtures/table-shading-scope`.

Import and conditional-style recomputation now follow the native reference. Table-level paint
and its XML remain retained; this change does not add cell-spacing support.
Removing a direct cell fill restores the cell style or automatic no-fill,
including after row insertion, export and reopen. Untouched package parts and
full undo remain byte-exact. No document-specific rule is used.

## Terminal page-break paragraph fit

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.3.1 (`br`) and Part 4 §14.8.3.38
(`splitPgBreakAndParaMark`) distinguish the authored page break from the
paragraph mark. Without that compatibility setting, a terminal break retains
the mark on its line. The native reference requires that line, including paragraph borders, to
fit the current writing area; otherwise it moves before applying the break.
A leading break followed by text retains its existing full-page behavior.

Six independently authored controls prove the distinction after ordinary
paragraphs and exact-height tables, with fitting/overflowing space and borders.
Native reference PDFs and measured page assignments are retained in
`tests/fixtures/terminal-break-fit`. The earlier unconditional empty-break
clamp was incorrect for terminal breaks. Layout now identifies breaks carrying
their paragraph mark, and pagination applies ordinary line-fit constraints to
them. Virtual insertion carets after terminal breaks remain zero-height.

The eight original `terminal-break-metrics` native reference controls additionally establish
that a terminal page break sharing its paragraph mark uses the mark's metrics,
not the break run's font size. Visible text and whitespace still contribute
their own metrics; a tall mark still requires room on the old page. Inherited
and explicit oversized break runs behave alike. Manual line breaks, interior
page breaks and the split-mark compatibility setting retain their distinct
behavior. The cited clauses specify placement but not this font-metric rule;
this is an observed reference refinement, not a demonstrated textual contradiction.
Stored run/mark formatting and source XML remain unchanged.

## Authored ASCII hyphen wrapping

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.3.31 (`t`) retains literal authored text; §17.3.3.29
(`softHyphen`) separately defines optional hyphens. Literal ASCII `-` now
provides a wrapping opportunity after the character, shared by paragraph
layout and AutoFit intrinsic minimum widths. No source text or package part
is rewritten to achieve the wrap. Run boundaries do not change the rule.

Ten manually authored controls and the installed reference's PDF are retained under
`tests/fixtures/hyphen-wrap`. They establish ordinary compound, leading and
numeric ASCII breaks and distinguish literal U+2010/U+2011 and minus signs.
This follows measured reference behavior; it does not claim complete UAX #14
conformance. The Unicode default rules have context-sensitive hyphen behavior
(see https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr14/tr14-54.html), whereas these reference
controls permit leading and numeric ASCII breaks and keep U+2010 compounds
together. No conflicting normative OOXML wrapping requirement was established.
Automatic linguistic hyphenation, soft-hyphen support and general multilingual
line-breaking rules remain separate gaps. Forced grapheme wrapping of oversized
unbreakable content retains its existing behavior.

## Body editing with retained nonempty headers and footers

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.10.1–2 and §§17.10.5–6 define independent header/footer
parts and section references. Supported paragraph runs, DrawingML drawings and
page fields in these parts no longer force the entire document read-only.
The same strict paragraph, run, drawing and field readers validate them before
body editing is enabled. Existing section variants, story-local image
relationships, live page fields and shared-style resolution remain in use.

Story XML, relationships and artwork are retained byte-for-byte through body
edits; shared styles can intentionally change story appearance without rewriting
the story part. Body repagination repeats the retained drawings on the new pages.
Original manually authored header-drawing, page-field and empty-story fixtures
and their independent references now cover editable import, export/reopen,
repagination and full undo. Package entries, rather than ZIP compression bytes,
are compared for editable exports.

CI follow-up: run 35452026523 exposed four obsolete section-page-number tests
that still required read-only export after this support was enabled. The unit
and browser tests now require editable import and package-entry preservation;
the browser controls also exercise body editing, exact undo and reopen. Their
reference page-number/parity checks and excessive-page fallback remain intact.
Seventeen unit tests, five browser tests and 70 exported XML schema checks pass
locally. No runtime behavior is changed by this test correction.

Direct header/footer text editing is still unavailable. Story tables, hyperlinks,
bookmarks and unsupported saved content remain guarded; strict import also retains its
unsupported-formatting checks. Oversized-header/body clearance and wrapping
anchors remain separate layout gaps. This removes an unnecessary body-editing
restriction, not those remaining feature limitations.

## Roundoff at the minimum paragraph writing width

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.16 (`gridCol`), 17.4.71 (`tcW`), 17.4.42 (`tblCellMar`)
and 17.3.1.12 (`ind`) supply twip-based geometry. Their conversion to binary
floating-point CSS pixels can make an exact one-pixel writing region subtract
to `0.9999999999999432`. Paragraph validation now uses a `1e-6` pixel tolerance
at its existing minimum. It does not change stored values, layout edges or
permit materially narrower regions; 0.99999 pixels still fails.

`tools/narrow_cell_roundoff_fixture.py` authors an original fixed-grid table
with a 361-twip spacer and two 173-twip margins. The retained reference PDF and
independently sampled green band under `tests/fixtures/narrow-cell-roundoff`
confirm a one-page table. Unit and browser tests cover layout, caret geometry,
invalid widths, body editing, source-part preservation, exact undo and reopen.
This corrects numerical validation, not a reference/specification divergence.

## Numeric square side wrapping

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.4.2.17 (`wrapSquare`) requires wrapping around a virtual
rectangle, including effect extents and declared text distances. Original
controls in `tests/fixtures/square-wrap-flow` establish left/right/central
obstacles, same-baseline text on both sides, and exclusion extending into later
paragraphs. The renderer retains numeric column/paragraph offsets and text
distances, measures separate text intervals on each baseline, and carries the
exclusion into following paragraphs. Page placement and wrapping are reconciled
until stable, so paragraph spacing, page breaks and keep rules move the anchor
and its exclusion together. Documents without these anchors use one layout pass.

The paired footer controls flag a reference compatibility divergence: with no mode
setting, the installed reference overlaps footer text and the square; changing only to
mode 15 makes text avoid the square and its side distance. Exact/automatic line
spacing, two text sizes and two image heights confirm the distinction. The
normative square-wrap clause has no such footer exception. PDFs and extracted
glyph origins/picture bounds are retained. This is measured legacy behavior,
not permission to ignore square wrapping in modern documents.

The measured legacy/modern distinction is applied to footers. Body selections
use separate rectangles for the two text intervals; source offsets remain
continuous across the intervening picture. Caret affinity distinguishes the
end of the left interval from the beginning of the right interval. Original
anchor XML and unrelated package parts survive body edits and exact undo.

The supported subset remains unrotated drawings without nonzero effect extents,
numeric column/paragraph positions, and paragraph text outside table cells.
Other coordinate bases, contour wrapping and wrapped drawings inside tables
remain unsupported. A failure to settle page placement reports a layout error
instead of painting text against stale exclusions.

The retained Arial controls expose a separate existing exact-line baseline
difference of approximately 1.1pt versus the native reference. Line breaks, horizontal interval
origins, baseline advances and picture bounds are checked independently; these
controls do not establish perfect absolute text baselines. Optimization note:
side-wrapped documents can require repeated measurement as pagination settles;
no caching or unrelated performance work is included in this rendering change.

Local validation: 123 unit tests, 27 browser tests, 258 fixture/export XML schema
checks, and the production build/license check pass. Browser coverage includes
existing full-column, unwrapped, page/margin, cell and header drawings, plus
clicking both caret positions at a split-line boundary. Full CI remains separate.

## Retained content controls in headers and footers

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.5.2.29/31 define block/run structured document tags, and
§§17.5.2.34/36 identify `sdtContent` as the saved display content. Section
17.5.2.13 identifies `docPartObj` gallery metadata as an editing choice, rather
than a requirement to replace that saved content with a locally installed part.
The renderer now validates control envelopes and projects saved content on the
disposable DOM of a retained header/footer part. Paragraph, run, drawing and
page-field validation still applies after projection. This entry point refuses
body document roots; editable body controls keep their existing model/parser.

Header/footer XML is never reconstructed from the projected paragraphs. Locks,
IDs, nested wrappers, gallery properties, tag formatting, relationship IDs and
other metadata remain in the original package part through body edits and undo.
Complex PAGE and NUMPAGES fields inside inline controls still refresh from live
pagination. Tag-only run properties do not become properties of printed text.
Direct story editing and refresh from external XML bindings or glossary
placeholders are not implemented; saved contents are rendered and retained.

The original `retained-story-controls.docx` and two-page reference PDF establish
nested locked block controls, inline page fields with stale cached values,
tag formatting and a story-local square-wrapped image. No reference divergence was
found. Both reference pages were visually inspected; the schema-corrected fixture
was re-exported and produced pixel-identical pages. Validation: 88 unit tests,
16 browser tests (one optional corpus case skipped), 126 fixture/export XML
schema checks, and production build/license checks pass. The corrected fixture
also passed its six unit cases and browser case on rerun.

## Retained page-story tables

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.10.2/17.10.5 govern footer/header references; §17.4.38
(`tbl`) and §17.4.65 (`tc`) define their table and nested block content. The
strict importer now reads supported tables in retained headers and footers
through the ordinary table/block readers, using a separate registry per story.
The body model and its selection/hit testing never receive those story cells.
Story images resolve through their own relationship parts. Story paragraphs,
tables and all original parts remain unchanged during body editing/export.

The story layout passes that registry to generic table layout and translates
cells, line clips, borders and border clips together to header/footer positions.
The painter includes story shading/borders and excludes inline story pictures
from body selection highlights. Cell-anchored drawings use translated physical
cell boxes. A final standalone image-only footer's descender adjustment is not
applied to table rows. The separate nested-terminal-paragraph control fixes the
empty trailing paragraph allocation in generic cell layout.

The original two-page `page-story-tables` fixture covers shaded cells, a merged
header row, a nested footer table, an inline picture and PAGE refresh. All
printed lines and their origins/baselines match the native reference within 0.2pt. Body edits,
repagination, unrelated-part preservation, exact undo and reopening are tested.
Direct header/footer editing remains outside this subset. Story bookmarks and
links still require independent identity/relationship support; numeric field
format switches and body clearance for oversized stories remain open.

## Body and header/footer drawing layers

The native reference scopes drawing order to the header/footer layer and the body layer.
The complete header/footer layer paints first, including its foreground
drawings; body backgrounds, text and drawings then paint above it. This does
not suppress story content or change `titlePg`, drawing flags or package parts.
Within each existing layer, behind/front text and retained drawing order still
determine the result. Header-versus-footer overlap rules are not newly defined.

This is a reference-specific exception to the global wording of ECMA-376 Part 1
§20.4.2.3: `behindDoc` (printed p3103) describes overlap with document text,
and `relativeHeight` (printed p3108) orders drawings globally by front/behind
and then numeric order. The original five-page `story-drawing-layers` fixture
demonstrates body-behind drawings covering header/footer text and higher-order
header-front drawings, while ordinary body text remains above header drawings.
Body foreground drawings still cover body text. An uncovered fifth page proves
that header/footer content remains present. The retained reference PDF and hash-bound
pixel-region reference establish the exception without private template content.

The browser checks covered and visible text regions, overlapping picture colors,
body editing, undo, export preservation and reopening. The change only orders
painting; pagination, anchor geometry, source metadata and hit testing are
unchanged. Body selections/caret remain in their existing interaction layer.

## Terminal empty paragraphs after nested tables

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.65 permits paragraphs and nested tables in cells;
§17.3.1.33 supplies ordinary paragraph spacing. The native reference suppresses the line and
before/after spacing of a truly empty final cell paragraph immediately after
a nested table. The manually authored `nested-terminal-paragraph` fixture
proves the exception with 18pt/36pt exact heights, two 8pt paragraph gaps,
visible text, spaces and two consecutive empty paragraphs. The latter three
cases retain normal allocation. This reference behavior is implemented in generic
cell layout, with no story- or document-specific adjustment. Stored paragraph
formatting and an insertion caret remain; typing restores height and undo
restores exact source parts. The specification does not explicitly describe
this suppression exception; the retained reference control establishes it.

## Paragraph-mark metrics on nonempty lines

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.29 assigns `pPr/rPr` to the paragraph-mark glyph,
separately from the runs; §17.3.1.33 defines line spacing. The original
`paragraph-mark-metrics` control establishes that the native reference does not let an
oversized terminal mark enlarge a line containing text. Empty, spaces-only,
tab-only and empty post-break lines retain that mark's metrics. Direct
manual-break run metrics are separate, as are existing image-only minimum
height rules and `hideMark` suppression. The source and mark formatting are
preserved for editing; this changes only measured line allocation. The native reference's
13.8pt text lines remain 13.8pt with 24pt marks, while empty 24pt marks occupy
27.6pt. The retained one-page reference covers body and table paragraphs.
The clauses do not explicitly prescribe this allocation distinction, so this
is recorded as native reference layout behavior, not an explicit normative divergence.

## Reviewed missing-font assets

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.26 (`rFonts`) identifies the requested font; resolving
that font does not change the source declaration. The browser now loads the
reviewed, unmodified Bebas Neue regular face from a same-origin asset when the
requested family is unavailable locally. Installed selectable families take
precedence. Unknown names never produce network lookups; a failed asset uses
the existing unavailable-font fallback. Requests are deduplicated. No font is
loaded until requested, and the asset URL respects the deployment base path.

The font's OFL-1.1 license, pinned binary/source provenance and SHA-256 are
retained and checked by the license gate. Native metrics apply to this face;
Noto-specific constants do not. The original reviewed-font control and native reference PDF
verify glyph origins, automatic baselines, line breaks and retained edits.
Its README records independent exact-line baseline and Arial shaping gaps;
this change does not claim those gaps are fixed or establish a reference divergence.

The registry also includes Oswald (normal, weights 200–700) and Open Sans
(normal/italic, weights 300–800 and widths 75–100%). All faces of a requested
family finish loading before registration; a failed face leaves the ordinary
fallback in place. Binary hashes, OFL-1.1 notices and corresponding source
revisions are recorded in `public/fonts/PROVENANCE.md` and the license gate.
There is no arbitrary remote font lookup, local-font enumeration or DOCX font
renaming. The original `reviewed-family` fixture exercises regular, bold,
italic and bold italic with native references and retained editable exports.
It verifies ten line breaks, baselines within 0.2pt and Oswald origins within
0.2pt. Open Sans glyph origins still drift up to 2.515pt and remain a separate
strict expected-failure oracle. This restores family availability without
claiming complete font-version/shaping fidelity or a reference/spec divergence.

## Empty column breaks at the writing-area boundary

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.3.1 and 17.18.4 define column-break advancement.
An empty authored column break remains in the outgoing column even when its
line box no longer fits. Automatic overflow must not advance once before the
authored break advances again. This also terminates a preceding keep-with-next
chain. Terminal column breaks retain the real paragraph-mark line in the
destination column; terminal page-break mark compatibility is unchanged.

Leading column breaks defer paragraph-before spacing until following content,
including repeated breaks, collapsed preceding after-spacing and
`suppressSpBfAfterPgBrk`. Part 4 §14.8.3.42 describes that compatibility rule
for page breaks; the native reference's application to column breaks is an observed extension,
not an established contradiction of a normative column-break spacing rule.
Eleven original reference controls under `tests/fixtures/column-break-boundaries`
retain source/PDF hashes and native text positions. They cover full/near-full
columns, single/repeated/terminal breaks, large break fonts, keep chains and
deferred spacing, with hit testing, OPC preservation, editing and export/reopen.

## Minimum body-line baselines: reference divergence

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.33, printed page 250 (PDF page 260), requires centering
text when an exact/minimum line has spare height. The installed reference
instead bottom-aligns text in expanded minimum (`atLeast`) lines, as it already
does for image-only minimum lines. The engine follows that measured behavior
without changing line heights, stored spacing, automatic or exact rules.

Twenty-four original controls under `tests/fixtures/minimum-line-baselines`
retain source/PDF hashes and native text positions. Three fonts, two text
sizes, three minimum heights and three paragraph-mark sizes distinguish
bottom alignment from centering, natural expansion and automatic line spacing.
The original centered baseline differed by more than 6 pt in the tallest
controls. The native comparison retains a 0.15 pt tolerance and requires the
reference font; it is not a pixel-identity certification.

Combined validation for these column-boundary and minimum-baseline fixes:
113 distinct targeted unit cases pass, with one 5-second style-editing timeout
in the combined run passing on an isolated default-timeout rerun. All 87
browser cases pass, including continuous sections, page-break spacing/metrics,
exact baselines and line-spacing UI/style edits. Thirty-five source packages
and 211 browser exports pass 536 XML checks. The Construction brochure remains
editable on two pages, pixel-identical to its retained browser renders; its
edit/undo/reopen workflow and a further 39 export XML checks pass. Production
build and license checks pass. Template 109 remains read-only on four pages
versus the native reference's three; these fixes do not complete that source's review.

## Exact body-line baselines: reference divergence

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.33, printed page 250 (PDF page 260), describes
metric-based centering when exact/minimum lines are tall and bottom alignment
when they are short. The original `exact-font-baseline.docx` matrix establishes
a reference divergence for positive exact heights: Arial, Times New Roman, Courier
New and Bebas Neue at 12/24 pt all use a baseline at 80% of the 12/24/36 pt
line height. All 24 measurements agree within 0.05 pt of PDF output rounding.
The four reference pages were visually reviewed. Source/PDF hashes and independent
measurements are retained under `tests/fixtures/exact-font-baseline`.

Body layout now follows that measured exact baseline, as the existing shape
and image-only paths already did. Declared line heights, line advances and
source spacing attributes are unchanged. Automatic, minimum and zero-exact
spacing keep their existing behavior. Carets and decorations follow the new
baseline. The original control also exposes a separate short-line ink clipping
difference: the native reference's PDF prints ink outside the line box while body text is still
clipped here. That limitation remains open; this fix does not claim complete
exact-line visual fidelity or support for suppressTopSpacing/vertical text.

Validation: 157 unit tests, 13 browser tests (plus a successful rerun of the
raw-canvas capture), 86 source/export XML checks and build/license checks pass
locally. All four browser control pages were visually reviewed; the known
short-line clipping difference remains visible. The actual SaaS template's
five pages are pixel-identical to its preceding render, and retained editing,
undo and reopen pass. This does not establish full-corpus conformance.

## Exact-line text ink versus picture/background clipping

The original `exact-line-ink.docx` and installed reference PDF distinguish glyph ink
from other content in short exact-height lines. ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.33
(printed page 250) describes clipping short lines from the top. The native reference diverges:
24pt text and underlines remain visible outside a 12pt line box, including
raised/lowered runs and overlapping adjacent lines. Highlighting and inline
pictures are still clipped to the nominal line. Nine independent PDF ink
measurements and source/PDF hashes are retained with the original control.

Layout records text clipping separately from the existing line bounds. The
painter releases the exact-line clip for glyphs/decorations and retains it for
run backgrounds and each inline picture. Cell/page clips, horizontal text
clips and hidden empty section boundaries remain active. Line advances,
caret/selection geometry, image hit testing and serialized OOXML are unchanged.
This resolves the short-line glyph truncation recorded in the four-font
exact-baseline control; it does not claim unsupported compatibility settings.

Validation: 67 unit tests, 19 browser cases and 44 source/export XML checks pass,
as do the production build and license gate. The original reference/browser pages
were visually reviewed. Existing nested-table, exact-row and empty-section
checks retain their guards. The spacing-dialog regression now checks complete
glyph ink in both exact and minimum modes, replacing the obsolete truncation
expectation; its corrected rerun passes.

## Numeric pictures on page fields

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.16.4.2 (printed pp1183–1184) defines the `\#` numeric
format switch. PAGE, NUMPAGES and SECTIONPAGES now retain and evaluate numeric
pictures, with quote-aware switch arguments and MERGEFORMAT in either order.
The original simple/complex field XML, lock state and cached results remain
unchanged. Existing locked-field refresh rules apply. A numeric PAGE picture
takes precedence over section numeral formatting; chapter-prefixed numbering
remains explicitly unsupported.

The nonnegative integer page-field domain supports required `0`, space-padded
`#`, `x`, radix and grouping separators, signs, literal characters and quoted
text, and positive/negative/zero sections. The negative section is retained
but cannot be selected by a page count. `%` is literal, not scaling. Output
radix/grouping characters use the browser locale. Backtick SEQ references
require sequence evaluation and remain rejected. Malformed quotes, duplicate
switches, excessive sections and invalid radix/grouping patterns also reject
editable import instead of silently losing field semantics.

The original five-page `numeric-page-fields` native reference control restarts at zero,
one, twelve and 1234, then twelve with Roman section numbering. It records
native reference details beyond the clause's explicit rules: zero's first optional
fractional position prints zero, trailing fractional x is unpadded, and x
truncates high integer digits only when it is the first integer placeholder.
The latter differs from a literal reading of “drops digits to the left of
the x placeholder”: the native reference formats 1234 as 1234 with `0x0`, but as 234 with
`x##`. The control and retained reference PDF prove the implemented behavior.
No actual template text or document-specific condition is used.

Validation: 75 unit tests, 13 browser cases, 192 source/export XML checks,
production build and license gate pass. Every original control page was
visually reviewed against the native reference. The browser test checks all text, line origins
and baselines, plus closing-bracket positions to verify optional padding that
PDF text extraction collapses. Native editing, unchanged source parts, undo
and reopening pass for both the control and the exposing invoice.

## Fixed-table expansion to preferred width

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.18.87 (printed pp1496–1497), §17.4.63 `tblW`, §17.4.71
`tcW`, and §§17.4.14–15/85–86 describe table preference and omitted columns.
After resolving fixed-table cell requests across all rows, expand an undersized
occupied grid proportionally to a larger explicit absolute/percentage table
preference. Keep columns omitted in every row outside this allocation; their
independent gap widths are unchanged during either expansion or reduction.
Columns occupied in any row participate normally. Auto/nil table preferences
and AutoFit's separate content-based allocation retain their existing paths.

The clause's suggested fixed algorithm describes reduction but omits expansion.
The original fifteen-table `fixed-table-preference` control and native reference PDF prove
the implemented completion of that guidance, including later conflicting rows,
spans, arbitrary source grids, and leading/trailing gaps. This is recorded native reference
behavior, not a claimed contradiction of normative text. Geometry changes do
not rewrite the retained table/grid/cell declarations.

Validation: 71 table unit checks, 29 browser cases, 112 source/export XML checks,
production build and license gate pass. One optional private-card browser case
is skipped. All fifteen original tables were visually reviewed against the native reference;
the browser oracle verifies 44 cell rectangles and painted coverage through
editing and reopening. The exposing invoice now matches the native reference's five grid
boundaries within 0.111pt and completes its individual review. A pre-existing
six-import aggregate timeout was reproduced on unchanged main and corrected
by giving each unchanged assertion its own test case.

### Signed header/footer body clearance

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.6.11 (`pgMar`) requires nonnegative top/bottom margins to
reserve the greater of the declared margin and the selected header/footer text
extent. Negative margins keep the body edge fixed and permit story overlap.
The original layout now measures stories with the same field expansion, styles,
font metrics, tables and footer image trim used by the story painter. Selection
uses each section's first/default/even references and logical page number.
NUMPAGES/SECTIONPAGES-dependent heights are repaginated to stable counts within
the existing page limit; unsupported/nonconvergent layouts remain guarded.

Physical bounds carry through paragraph widow handling, nested and merged cell
flow, row clipping, and repeated table headers. They do not rewrite stored page
margins or drawing anchors. Layout results retain plain geometry, allowing exact
undo comparisons and cloning. The existing best-effort story fallback and
unsupported-feature editing restrictions remain in force.

Nested-cell intrinsic measurement must not select physical page stories before
logical page numbers exist. `cellPageAt` therefore removes physical callbacks
when the enclosing measurement has replaced the physical page height, including
stale callbacks on deeper cells. Actual pagination retains the callback and
accumulated physical offsets. This fixes the plain-text fallback caused by a
layout exception in nested body tables with headers/footers; it does not alter
OOXML content or provide new content-control editing support.

The independent three-page `nested-table-stories` control (nested cells,
§17.4.65) uses first/even/default headers of different heights. All six inline
picture positions agree with the installed reference within 0.004pt. Browser regression
checks positions within 0.2pt, unchanged ZIP parts, editing, exact undo and
reopening. Unit coverage checks multiple nested intrinsic contexts, stale child
callbacks, and physical-page offsets.

Validation for that measurement fix: 42 targeted unit tests, 15 selected browser
cases, the control's source schema and 30 browser export package checks, plus
production/license build pass. An existing repeated-header test clicked beyond
the first glyph midpoint and failed identically on unchanged main; its click now
targets the leading edge, retaining its exact caret/edit/export assertions.

The eight original controls under `tests/fixtures/header-clearance` have native reference
PDFs, reproducible DOCX sources and hashed border-position references.
Their browser regression passes at 0.2-point tolerance and verifies package
retention, editing, undo and reopening. Synthetic unit tests additionally cover
varying first/even/default bounds, signed footer margins, page-count wrapping,
widows, caret mapping and repeated/oversized/merged tables. These tests establish
the supported cases; they do not claim complete reference layout equivalence.

Validation: 246 targeted unit checks, 33 browser cases, 468 source/export XML
checks, production build and the 199-package license gate pass. The exposing
eight-page report retains editability and exact undo/package retention; its
separate font and chart geometry differences remain under review.

### Floating-table positioning and wrapping

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.57 (`tblpPr`) removes floating tables from normal text
flow and anchors paragraph-relative positions to the next regular non-table,
non-frame paragraph. `tests/fixtures/floating-tables` supplies twenty original
controls and an independently measured native reference PDF in
compatibility mode 15. The source passes eight XML schema checks.

The controls establish two reference/spec differences. Although the clause defines
omitted `horzAnchor` and `vertAnchor` as page, the native reference uses margin on each omitted
axis. Paired controls with 144pt offsets give (144,144) for explicit page,
(216,216) for explicit margin and omitted anchors, (216,144) for omitted
horizontal only, and (144,216) for omitted vertical only. Also, although the
clause says `tblpYSpec` is ignored for text anchors, adding `center` changes a
12pt paragraph offset from y=114pt to approximately y=102pt. Additional controls
vary table width (72/144/288pt), anchor font size (12/18pt), and wrap clearance
(0/2/18pt). Native PDF vectors and glyph origins support a twelve-twip extra
horizontal alignment frame in mode 15, a minus-seven-twip text-anchor offset
when relative alignment is present, and horizontal wrap clearance of at least
24 twips, otherwise the authored distance plus 15 twips. These are measured
reference compatibility rules, not additional requirements attributed to OOXML.

The engine imports positioned tables, measures their cells with the existing
table layout, and places them independently of body flow. Exclusion rectangles
wrap the anchor and subsequent text; preceding paragraphs retain their flow.
A word moves intact to a later available interval instead of breaking across
a narrow sliver. The existing table alignment and indent controls update the
floating frame while preserving vertical positioning and other source XML.
No-edit export, surrounding/cell edits and undo retain original package parts.

The current implementation requires a following anchor paragraph and a float
that occupies one physical page. Multi-page floating tables remain guarded;
explicit `tblOverlap` remains unsupported. Nested placement is described below.
Further native controls
are needed for overlap resolution, story/section interactions, parity-based
alignments, and border-dependent frame/clearance rules. These gaps keep the
corpus goal open. Source and PDF hashes bind the numerical references; none
of the native expectations is derived from the engine's layout.

#### Floating tables inside cells

The eighteen original `nested-floating-tables` controls establish another
context-dependent difference from §17.4.57: explicit `page` offsets inside a
cell use the containing cell's edges, rather than the physical page edges
specified in the clause. The native 36pt-offset control starts its table at
(318.670,123.020) relative to a cell beginning at (282.670,87.020), rather than
at page position (36,36). Margin/text horizontal anchors use the cell's writing
edges; paragraph-relative vertical offsets follow the next ordinary paragraph.
Signed positions are clamped to the cell's starting edges, and large horizontal
offsets are clamped at its far edge. Left/center/right alignment uses the writing
area and a twelve-twip wider frame. In the automatic, top-aligned parent controls,
vertical alignment keywords place the child at the parent's writing top.

The shared cell paginator keeps these floats outside normal block flow and
includes their bottom text clearance in the parent row's natural extent.
Exclusions affect only paragraphs in the owning cell, including preceding text
when a negative offset reaches it. Native controls distinguish nested horizontal
clearances (authored distance plus 12 twips left / 15 twips right) from the
top-level minimum-clearance rule. Original positioning XML is retained through
editing, export, and undo. Exact-row clipping uses the existing common clipping
path for text, table shading/borders, selection and hit testing.

The current subset requires each containing cell and floating child to fit one
physical page; split parent cells and floats crossing a page boundary remain
guarded. Compatibility modes beyond the native mode-14 controls, vertical parent
alignment, overlap policy and complex story interactions need further native
coverage. Browser checks compare all eighteen native controls' absolute Y,
dimensions, wrapping origins and caret hits. Nested X is compared relative to
the inline control because the source also exposes an existing legacy outer
table offset; this does not certify absolute visual equivalence of that parent.

`nested-floating-borders` adds twenty independently authored reference controls for
border-dependent horizontal frame construction (§17.4.57). The first row's left
half-border adds to the starting overhang; the largest right half-border over
all rows expands the frame only beyond the existing 15-twip right clearance.
Thus a right border in a later row still changes center/right alignment, whereas
a later-row left border does not move the frame. Controls distinguish 1/1.5/2/3/6pt
right borders, first/later rows, both sides, and left/center/right/numeric positions.
The clause describes alignment against the entire frame but does not specify
this asymmetric border construction. Geometry derives from resolved cell borders;
source border/position properties remain unchanged. Browser comparison checks
relative text origins and painted shading against the native PDF, while unit
coverage checks border edits, export/reopen, exact undo and redo.

The existing native square-picture controls also exposed a baseline mismatch
on unchanged main: joined exact-spacing intervals used font-centered metrics
while ordinary lines used the native reference's 80%-of-line-height baseline. Both paths now
use the latter rule, including mixed fonts. This corrects the observed 1.04pt
advance discrepancy without changing the native reference or its tolerance.

## Exposed outer bottom table-border caps

ECMA-376 Part 1 section 17.4.66 (`tblBorders`) defines table border sides and
conflict behavior. Twelve original native reference controls in
`tests/fixtures/isolated-table-border` establish an additional consumer paint
rule: the exposed leading end of a solid outer bottom edge extends one CSS
pixel. Omitted/AutoFit/fixed layouts, empty/text cells, cell margins, multiple
border weights, header tables and adjacent cells reproduce it. Top and
internal edges do not extend; visible left corners retain normal joins.
This ink detail is not claimed as an explicit OOXML requirement.

Only painted band endpoints change. Layout boxes, grid widths, row-height
prepasses, text and hit geometry retain their existing values. Source markup
is preserved. Independent native PDF vectors, negative controls and package
edit/undo/reopen checks cover this behavior. Other border styles and consumer
versions are not established by these controls.

## General numeric formats on page fields

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.16.4.3 and 17.16.4.3.1 define the `\\*` general
formatting switch. PAGE, NUMPAGES and SECTIONPAGES now accept Arabic,
ArabicDash, ROMAN, roman, ALPHABETIC and alphabetic, preserving the original
instruction and cached-result XML. Case-sensitive Roman/alphabetic forms
select the corresponding upper/lower output. General formats override section
numbering; ArabicDash adds the specified spaced hyphens. The existing locked
field behavior is retained.

Five original reference pages (`tests/fixtures/general-page-fields`) verify zero,
letter repetition above 26, an upper-Roman section, simple/complex fields,
MERGEFORMAT order and count fields. Native controls establish that numeric
pictures take precedence regardless of order and that the last repeated
general numeric format wins. These precedence details are measured consumer
behavior. Unsupported language-specific numeric formats and other general
formatting switches remain guarded rather than silently discarded.

## Contextual before-spacing across cell boundaries

ECMA-376 Part 1 section 17.3.1.9 suppresses a paragraph's before-spacing when
its preceding paragraph has the same style. Sixteen original reference controls in
`tests/fixtures/cell-leading-space` establish that the preceding source
paragraph can be in another cell or immediately before the table. The engine
now carries that style context into the first paragraph of each cell before
measuring row height and aligning its content. Only measured formatting is
changed; saved paragraph formatting and source XML remain intact.

The existing `allowSpaceOfSameStyleInTable` compatibility override disables
this suppression. Different styles, explicit contextual-spacing resets and
ordinary before-spacing keep their existing behavior. Native controls compare
top/center/bottom alignment, automatic/exact row heights, asymmetric padding,
a shared style, repeated-header marking and 11/12pt text. This is a measured
application of the specification's preceding-paragraph rule, not an arbitrary
vertical offset. Contextual after-spacing across separate cell boundaries is
not established by these controls.

## Web-hidden text in paginated view

ECMA-376 Part 1 section 17.3.2.44 (`webHidden`) applies to Web Layout view,
not paginated document display. The canvas now accepts valid direct/inherited
web-hidden declarations and renders their text normally. Source run properties
and style definitions remain retained through edits and exports. The app does
not currently provide a Web Layout mode or a command for changing this flag.

Seven original reference controls in `tests/fixtures/web-hidden` cover direct
true/false, paragraph/character inheritance and explicit resets. Native text
and geometry, formatting within a marked run, unrelated-part preservation,
exact undo and reopening are tested. Malformed declarations are guarded;
`vanish` remains unsupported. This follows the specification without a
reference-specific exception.

## Retained sections with different paper sizes

ECMA-376 Part 1 section 17.6.13 defines `pgSz`; sections 17.6.17 and 17.6.18
define final and paragraph-level section properties. Editable import now allows
different valid paper sizes across supported next-page sections. Four original
reference controls in `tests/fixtures/mixed-page-sizes` establish dimensions,
wrapping, percentage-table widths and right-aligned footer positions.

Each canvas uses its physical page's dimensions for sizing, painting and
clipping. Keyboard navigation and cross-page hit testing use cumulative page
heights. Table commands resolve the selected section's writing width, and
image insertion uses the selected physical page. The document-wide background
is carried across all section geometries. Source section markup remains intact
through content edits, undo and reopening.

Multi-section page-setup changes and edits across section breaks remain guarded
as before. Continuous/column transitions beyond the existing first-section
case remain unsupported. This support does not claim arbitrary section-layout
conformance; no consumer-specific exception was needed for these controls.

## Cached nested field results and TOC character formatting

ECMA-376 Part 1 17.16.18 defines complex field boundaries, optional result
separators, nesting and the treatment of unclosed fields at a story boundary.
Read-only import now projects cached body-field results while retaining their
run properties, character styles, hyperlinks and bookmarks. The field scan
spans paragraphs and inline containers, excludes inactive compatibility branches
and deleted text, and does not consume drawing text from another story. Nested
results inside an outer instruction remain hidden. Simple-field wrappers are
unwrapped only in the private display DOM; source package parts remain intact.
MACROBUTTON instruction labels retain their separate inert preview behavior.

**Reference/specification divergence:** 17.3.2.29 applies all referenced character
style properties at the character-style level. The native reference instead
suppresses non-font properties of the built-in Hyperlink style within a cached
TOC result (17.16.5.68). Font family slots survive, and direct formatting still
overrides the result. The original `toc-hyperlink-style` control defines that
style with the noncanonical ID `LinkStyle`, proving that its style name, rather
than a hard-coded style ID, identifies it. Native output suppresses its 16pt
size, italic, blue color and underline inside the TOC, retains Times New Roman,
and honors direct red/double-underlined formatting. A custom character style
still applies fully; the same built-in style outside the TOC also applies fully.
The preview matches this observed behavior instead of applying an offset or a
corpus-specific rule.

`toc-pageref-formatting` retains character-style labels and directly formatted,
locked PAGEREF results. The locks distinguish cached display from the native reference's export
refresh of unlocked PAGEREF fields (17.16.5.45). Native PDFs and glyph references
are recorded for these controls. This work does not enable editable TOC/PAGEREF
import or regenerate field results. Those features remain outstanding; previews
stay read-only and download the original bytes.

## Solid w14 text outlines

MS-DOCX §§2.6.1.26 (`textOutline`) and 2.6.3.36
(`CT_TextOutlineEffect`), with ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.10.35 (`ST_LineWidth`),
define the retained text-outline properties. Reference:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-docx/5b065f17-63c7-4d54-83e3-6f3c161f3afa

The run model resolves centered, single, solid outlines through paragraph and
character styles and direct formatting. Supported colors are sRGB and document
scheme references without transforms; the ordinary text fill remains independent.
Width uses EMU, with zero as the omitted-width default. Round, bevel and miter
joins and flat, round and square caps are retained. Explicit noFill suppresses
an inherited outline. Gradient/transformed colors, compound/inset/dashed lines,
and extended text fills remain guarded rather than silently discarded.

The painter fills glyphs and strokes their contours with the resolved outline,
including the existing capitalization and text-transform paths. The ordinary
shaping and line metrics are retained. Source theme markup survives unrelated
edits; explicit outline edits serialize resolved sRGB properties. No outline
control is added to the toolbar in this change.

The original `text-outline-control.docx`, its generator, reference PDF
and glyph reference cover direct/inherited outlines, ordinary foreground-color
overrides and text in neighboring table cells. They demonstrate a missing
feature, not a divergence from the specification. Unit/browser checks cover
rendering, malformed/unsupported declarations, edits, export, reopening and
byte-exact undo. Remaining corpus soft-hyphen editing support is separate.

Adjacent runs with different outlines share shaping and caret geometry. Outline
properties are carried on the existing foreground paint ranges so each stroke
is clipped to its own run, including transitions to plain text. A mixed `AVAV`
regression verifies unchanged kerning/stop geometry and a browser stroke check
verifies the middle run's clipped ink. This also covers differently colored
outlines inside one shaped fragment.

## Optional hyphens

ECMA-376 Part 1 `softHyphen` (CT_Empty) specifies an optional break which has
zero width unless selected for wrapping, when it displays as hyphen-minus.
See the element's specification excerpt:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.softhyphen

The editor retains U+00AD as a source/document position, imports and exports
`w:softHyphen`, omits unused markers from shaped text, and paints a hyphen for
a selected fitting opportunity without changing source offsets. The ordinary
caret stops remain available around hidden markers. Wrapping and table
intrinsic sizing share the same opportunities: a break minimum includes the
hyphen, while the unwrapped maximum omits it. Terminal markers do not add a
hyphen to the intrinsic width. Hidden markers retain the treatment of trailing
spaces. This implements authored discretionary hyphens, not language-based
automatic hyphenation.

The original soft-hyphens control and native reference cover unbroken,
wrapped, multiple, isolated and trailing markers. Unit checks also cover
source offsets, forced breaks, table widths, editing/export and exact undo;
browser checks compare native reference lines and positions and verify UI preservation.
No reference/spec divergence was observed in these controls.

## No-wrap drawing overlap restrictions

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.4.2.3 (`wp:anchor`, `allowOverlap`) requires repositioning a
drawing that is not allowed to intersect another DrawingML object. The reader
accepts and preserves both boolean values for `wrapNone`; false on text-wrapped
anchors remains guarded until wrapping and collision displacement can be solved
together. Authored coordinates and source markup remain unchanged on export.

After pagination and coordinate resolution, no-wrap floating frames are displaced
in source order when either member of an intersecting pair prohibits overlap.
The native reference's native behavior moves the later frame to the earlier frame's right edge,
or its bottom edge when the new right edge would exceed the physical page.
Collision resolution precedes stacking, applies across behind/in-front layers,
and is recomputed after edits. Ordinary all-overlap documents keep the existing
layout path. Displacement involving a text-wrapped frame is explicitly guarded.

**Reference/spec divergence:** The native reference places the moved edge one twip inside
the obstacle rather than making the rectangles strictly disjoint. The original
22-page `no-wrap-overlap.docx` and captured PDF transformation matrices establish
this behavior, including the exact physical page boundary transition.

Cross-story and inline-object collision interactions, effect extents, rotated
objects, and overflow past the page bottom need further native characterization.
The controls reveal a separate existing foreground stacking difference when
both objects allow overlap; this change addresses collision geometry, not that
paint-order issue. See `tests/fixtures/no-wrap-overlap/README.md`.

## Temporary cell-level structured document tags

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.5.2.32–33 define `w:sdt`/`w:sdtContent` around a single
complete table cell; §17.5.2.43 removes a temporary wrapper when its content is
edited. The parser now reads temporary rich-text cell wrappers with the same
validated property subset as temporary block controls. Saved cell content,
properties and widths participate in ordinary table layout, without flattening.

Cell controls use the existing content-range and undo machinery. Formatting and
unrelated edits retain the wrapper; text edits remove the nearest temporary
wrapper. Placeholder replacement keeps the owning table cell. Export writes
retained wrappers around `w:tc`, never inside it, and preserves their properties.
Untouched vertical-continuation wrappers retain their serialized cell container.
Persistent, locked, data-bound and row-level controls remain guarded.

The original `cell-controls.docx` fixture and native reference cover multiple
paragraphs, adjacent ordinary cells, spanning cells and empty/nonempty placeholders.
The native reference's six controls survive formatting and become five after inserting text into
one cell. This agrees with the specification; no divergence was observed.

## Numbering continuation across instances

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.9.16, 17.9.18 and 17.9.26 identify numbering instances,
references and start overrides; §17.9.23 maps paragraph styles to levels and
§17.9.11 controls subordinate restarts. The engine retains each authored instance
reference and its formatting, but projects counters by abstract numbering ID.
A new instance's first numbered paragraph applies a start override at its current
level. Unvisited ancestor overrides do not reset existing ancestor values, and
returning to an encountered instance does not apply its initial override again.

**Native reference interoperability distinction:** independent counters keyed by `numId` do
not reproduce the native reference. Eighteen original controls prove sharing across directly
numbered and style-inherited paragraphs, with and without a `pStyle` level link.
Different abstract definitions remain independent. Parent-triggered subordinate
resets use the parent instance's starting values, even if the next child refers
to another instance. In case 16, the child instance has a start override of 5 but
the native reference prints 2.1 after a base-instance parent; case 17 reverses the instance roles
and prints 2.5. This observed cross-instance rule is more specific than treating
starting values as properties solely of the child paragraph's reference.

`inherited-list-restarts.docx` and its native reference PDF/marker reference cover
starts, returns, inherited styles, ordinary paragraph/table interruptions and
multilevel resets. Source numbering XML is unchanged by layout. Unused unsupported
levels remain retained and are validated when used, as before.


### Rotated drawing groups

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.7.5 (`xfrm`, group shape), §20.1.10.3 (`ST_Angle`)
and Annex L.4.7.3 describe group coordinate transforms and rotation. Group
angles now retain signed 32-bit source values and normalize only in scene data.
Group child origins/extents compose at every nesting level. Bounds transform
curve controls before computing extrema and retain out-of-frame artwork.

The 16 independent native reference controls in `group-rotation` confirm the same
scale-before-rotation and quarter-turn scale-axis exchange already established
for nested pictures, lines and shapes. Ancestor orientation must be retained
when rotating descendants; reading only a canvas matrix's diagonal loses it.
This compatibility behavior is generic and does not inspect document identity.

Native stable color/bounds comparisons cover nested rotated groups, pictures,
reflections of child shapes, curves and ellipses, with edit/undo/reopen checks.
Group reflections and text inside rotated groups remain guarded pending their
