separate native controls. Source drawing XML and unrelated package parts remain
unchanged by surrounding text edits. The renderer does not rasterize source XML
on export.

The supplied 2016 Part 1 PDF's §20.1.7.5 prose says group rotation uses
1/64,000 degree, but refers to `ST_Angle`; the native reference uses 1/60,000 degree as for
other DrawingML rotations. The original 5,400,000-unit group control renders
at exactly 90 degrees in the native reference, not 84.375 degrees. The implementation follows
this measured behavior. The retained native PDF makes this discrepancy explicit.

## Edge rulers

The canvas view has horizontal and vertical rulers, enabled by default, with
View → Ruler and inches/centimeters controls. Tick spacing scales with zoom;
the horizontal strip tracks horizontal scrolling and the vertical strip tracks
the first visible page. This is original UI code, using the existing document
mutation, layout validation, painting and package-preserving serialization APIs.

- ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.6.11 `pgMar`, §17.6.13 `pgSz`: draggable left/right and
  top/bottom margins. Preserve gutter, header/footer distances and the sign of
  fixed negative vertical margins. Geometry includes gutter in the ruler origin.
  Multiple-section margins remain display-only, matching the page-settings API.
- §17.3.1.12 `ind`: first-line triangle changes the first-line offset; lower
  triangle changes the body indent while keeping the first line stationary;
  the rectangular left-indent handle moves both together. Right indent is
  measured inward from the right text boundary. Selection edits reuse paragraph
  formatting commands. Mixed values have no corresponding marker; changing a
  shared left indent preserves each paragraph's distinct first-line offset.
- §§17.3.1.37–38 `tab`/`tabs`, §17.18.84 `ST_TabJc`: cycle left, center, right,
  decimal using the tab selector, click to add, drag to move, drag away to remove.
  Moving a stop preserves its leader; inherited-stop removals serialize clears.
  Mixed tab sets are edited through the existing precise dialog. Numbering-only
  stops are retained but have no editable marker. Bar tabs are not implemented.

Pointer drags preview a marker/guide and commit one undo step on release.
Escape, pointer cancellation and scrolling cancel a drag. Arrow keys move a
focused marker (1/16 inch or 1 mm); Alt gives one-twip precision. Delete removes
focused tabs. Invalid layout rolls back using the editor's existing transaction.
Read-only documents show disabled controls and retain the original download;
text mode hides the rulers. Double-click a paragraph marker for exact settings.
Table-cell indents, table column/row resizing and vertical text rulers remain
outside this UI subset; the existing table/paragraph dialogs remain available.
This does not claim full UI or layout equivalence with the native reference.

`tools/canvas_ruler_fixture.py` independently generates `public/fixtures/ruler.docx`
using Python's standard library and original OOXML, with hanging/first-line
indents, three tab types, a dot leader, asymmetric margins, a gutter, two pages
and an unrelated package part. No third-party binary assets are included.
`tests/canvas-rulers.test.js` and `tests/browser/rulers.spec.js` cover edits,
undo/redo, cancellation, units, zoom/scroll alignment and export/reopening.
Validate the fixture and browser exports with `npm run check:conformance -- <paths>`.

## Text color and highlight palettes (2026-09-20)

This UI iteration retains the existing color (§17.3.2.6, §17.18.38) and
highlight (§17.3.2.15, §17.18.40) subsets above. Toolbar and Format-menu
palettes apply swatches immediately to the retained selection or future typing.
Automatic and No highlight remain explicit `auto` and `none` declarations.
Text colors offer inline custom RGB entry and up to eight recent custom colors
for the current app session; highlighting offers only the 16 standard named
values, using the engine's exact ECMA RGB mapping. Mixed selections have no
checked swatch. Escape and outside dismissal do not mutate the document;
custom color adjustments remain a draft until explicitly applied.

`tests/color-palette.test.js` covers exact highlight values, checked states,
keyboard navigation, dismissal, stale actions and custom validation. Browser
regressions in `text-colors.spec.js`, `text-highlights.spec.js` and
`color-palettes.spec.js` exercise selection retention, focus, undo/redo,
menu navigation, responsive placement and save/reopen. The existing independently
generated `text-colors.docx` and `text-highlights.docx` fixtures and browser
exports remain the round-trip evidence; this change adds no engine behavior
or serialization claims. Existing color/theme/layout conformance gaps remain.

### Whitespace in font names

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.26 `rFonts` and §17.18.89 `ST_String` retain the authored
family strings. Display lookup now trims surrounding whitespace as the native reference does,
without rewriting font slots, styles, theme declarations or untouched package
parts. The original `font-name-spaces` controls establish exact glyph equality
for ordinary leading/trailing spaces and trailing U+00A0, across Arial, Times
New Roman, Courier New, and Arial bold italic. Browser baselines remain within
0.2pt of the native reference; the fixture README separately records canonical shaping drift.

Availability caching, native CSS selection, reviewed fallback families,
alternate font names, bundled Noto Sans and encoded symbol rendering all use
the resolved display family. Internal spaces are retained. No fonts are newly
installed or redistributed by this change. Source preservation and export/undo
remain independent of display-name resolution.

### Cached doughnut charts

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§21.2.2.50 (`doughnutChart`), 21.2.2.49 (`dLbls`),
21.2.2.52 (`dPt`), 21.2.2.68 (`firstSliceAng`), 21.2.2.82 (`holeSize`)
and 21.2.2.104 (`manualLayout`) govern the retained chart scene. Supported
charts have complete finite caches, explicit per-point fills/outlines, a
10–90 percent hole, and integer clockwise first-slice angles from 0–360.
Earlier series form inner rings. Native reference controls establish absolute
magnitudes for negative values, no ink for all-zero series, and circular plots
centered within explicit inner rectangles or automatic 11pt frame clearance.

Manual plot rectangles require edge x/y coordinates and factor width/height.
Single-series generated titles support explicit Latin text formatting and
manual edge placement, with native 3pt side and 1.5pt vertical text insets.
Series data-label flags override chart flags individually; explicit deletion
suppresses inherited labels. Visible labels, legends, exploded points, inherited
point appearance, automatic titles and unsupported layouts remain guarded.
Existing chart-style override checks apply. Source chart/workbook parts remain
immutable; formulas and embedded workbooks are not executed.

The original 16-case `doughnut-charts` fixture and retained reference PDF establish
14,313 exact stable pixel samples and title origins within 0.2pt. Browser tests
repeat comparisons after editing/export/reopen and verify exact undo and
unrelated-part preservation. These chart-local checks do not establish table
or paragraph placement fidelity. Validation: 89 focused unit tests, 22 browser
regressions (one optional local-sample test skipped), and production/license
build pass. The fixture and all 61 browser exports pass official schema checks.

### Direct numbering cancellation and inherited indents

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.9.18 (`numId`) describes zero as removing numbering
properties at that hierarchy level. The native reference also resets inherited
left and first-line/hanging paragraph indentation when a paragraph directly
declares `numId=0`, including a style with no numbering. It retains inherited
right indentation and separately declared direct indent components. The
additional reset is not explicit in the clause; original body/table and direct
override controls are retained under `tests/fixtures/numbering-cancel-*`.

Style resolution now applies that reset before direct paragraph properties and
editor overrides. Authored style/paragraph declarations remain unchanged in
the package. No chart offset or table-specific adjustment is involved.

### Legacy table indentation reference

The earlier legacy grid-alignment description is qualified by independent
reference controls for ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.28 (`jc`), 17.4.50 (`tblInd`),
17.4.42 (`tblCellMar`) and 17.7.6 (table styles). In compatibility modes 12/14,
left-aligned tables with a resolved indent declaration position their leading
cell writing edge at that indent. Without a declaration, the grid is the
reference. Explicit zero differs from omission. A table-style declaration and
its based-on chain participate; an empty custom style does not imply zero.
Ignored `auto`/`pct` indent declarations do not change the reference edge.
The built-in default table style supplies implicit zero even when its stored
indent is omitted. These native observations qualify the specification's
default-zero wording without rewriting authored XML.

Legacy centered tables retain grid centering. Right alignment uses the leading
cell inset; independent left/right margin changes prove that it does not use
the trailing inset. These positioning offsets are separate from table width
calculation. Modern and nested exterior-border alignment remain unchanged.
The original `legacy-table-*` and `table-style-origin-properties` controls
retain 101 native reference image origins spanning modes, styles, indents, widths, margins,
borders and justification. Their README records provenance and remaining scope.

Validation for the table-reference and paragraph-cancellation changes: 74
focused unit tests, 42 browser regressions, all 13 original source fixtures and
39 browser exports (259 XML checks), and production/license build pass. The
source generators reproduce all 13 fixture ZIP part sets exactly. Table width
and source-part preservation remain independent of these placement corrections.

### Retained inactive header/footer variants

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.10.1 (`evenAndOddHeaders`) and 17.10.6 (`titlePg`)
require disabled variants to be ignored. Import now resolves the set of story
parts that can appear in any section under those settings before parsing their
contents. Inherited first-page references remain eligible when a later section
enables them; a shared part remains eligible if any enabled reference uses it.
Default stories remain eligible even if the current pagination does not yet
show them. Body edits can add pages without bypassing their validation.

Inactive stories retain their original parts and references. Relationship,
content-type and root validation still applies. No new VML or AUTHOR-field
editing support is claimed. The independent `inactive-stories` controls and
native reference PDFs prove enabled/disabled selection; tests cover body edit/export,
exact undo, reopen, inheritance and shared references.

Validation: 26 unit tests, 6 browser regressions, three source fixtures and ten browser exports pass schema checks; production/license build passes. The original proposal passes edit/undo/reopen with both page rasters unchanged.

### Numbering cancellation within a style hierarchy

The `numId=0` indentation reset also applies at a paragraph style's position in
its `basedOn` chain (ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.9.18). Native reference controls confirm the
same extra geometry reset for numbered and unnumbered ancestors. Resolution
now clears inherited left/first-line/hanging values before merging the
cancelling style's own declarations. Descendant styles, direct formatting and
editor overrides retain their normal precedence; right indentation survives.
The original `numbering-cancel-style` control records 24 native image origins
across 12 cases, including separate first and continuation lines. Source
style definitions and unrelated package parts are retained through editing.

Validation: 38 focused unit tests, 8 browser regressions, the new source fixture and 10 browser exports pass; production/license build passes. Original-template and matched-font-copy edit/undo/reopen checks pass.

### Reviewed exact font-face aliases

WordprocessingML font declarations (§17.3.2.26, rFonts) can identify a particular
face through a legacy family name. CSS may report such a name selectable while
substituting an installed sibling. The reviewed exact-face catalog therefore
requires a successful local face load before accepting native availability.
Otherwise it loads the reviewed same-origin face pair atomically. Ordinary
family detection and installed exact faces retain their previous behavior.
Failed reviewed loads do not falsely report the requested face as present.

Source sans pro light is the first such catalog entry, using unmodified Adobe
Light/Light Italic binaries under OFL-1.1. Full notices, hashes and corresponding
editable source references are retained. DOCX declarations are not rewritten.
The independent reference control matches plain-light advance within 0.05pt. Native
synthetic-bold advances and italic-version differences remain documented in
`tests/fixtures/source-sans-light/README.md`; this change does not claim those
separate issues fixed. Font loading is not an OOXML geometry workaround.

Validation: 44 focused unit tests and the 9-case browser suite pass (the pre-existing Open Sans shaping diagnostic remains an expected failure). The original source control and all 15 browser-exported packages pass schema checks; production/license build passes. Native-control edited export retains all unrelated package parts, including style/font declarations.

### Synthesized bold ink

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.1 (`b`) requires bold presentation without specifying
how to synthesize a missing face. Independently authored three-family controls
show the native reference using regular glyphs plus a centered em/35 stroke for synthesized
bold, while Arial uses its real bold face. The canvas text painter now applies
that stroke only after confirming synthesis through regular/bold ink comparisons
against a temporary single-face alias. This is native reference behavior in an unspecified
case, not a claimed contradiction of a normative synthesis rule.

Real bold, already-bold faces, unknown detection results and explicit text
outlines retain their existing paint. Temporary probe faces are always removed.
Preparation is cached for document fonts and explicitly selected fonts; ordinary
font-availability listings do not require raster probes. Body and shape text use
the common painter. Chart text remains on its existing path. Stored formatting,
glyph measurements and text advances are unchanged; synthetic advance differences
and low-resolution rasterization differences remain open.

The original `synthetic-bold-ink.docx` control covers regular and bold at 8/12/24
points. High-resolution reference ink references, real/alias-face checks, ordinary
paint and advance preservation, temporary-face cleanup, edits, export/reopen
and exact undo are covered by `tests/browser/synthetic-bold.spec.js`. See
`tests/fixtures/synthetic-bold-ink/README.md` for reference identities and limits.

Validation: 27 focused unit checks and 31 text-width checks pass. One existing
text-width edit/round-trip test reaches its five-second deadline on both this
change and an unchanged checkout of main; no deadline was increased. Fourteen
browser checks, 50 XML checks across 13 source/export packages, the license gate
and production build pass. The older synthetic-bold diagnostic is retained;
its ambiguous Franklin Gothic cases remain open.

## TIFF image parts

ECMA-376 Part 1 §15.2.14 explicitly lists `image/tiff` among image-part content
types. §20.1.8.13 (`blip`) supplies the image relationship; DrawingML extents,
crop and transforms retain their existing meaning. TIFF signatures now enter the
same immutable asset pipeline as PNG/JPEG. Existing TIFF parts, content types,
relationships and metadata survive edits unchanged. New TIFF insertion writes
the original bytes with a `.tiff` part name and `image/tiff` content type.

The existing MIT-licensed UTIF 3.1.0 decoder is reused through a shared worker.
The codec loads only for TIFF decoding. Preflight bounds the directory, tags,
strip/tile ranges and pixel dimensions; the worker retains its 15-second deadline
and termination path. DOCX retains its 10MB, 8,192-pixel-side, 16-megapixel per
image and aggregate asset limits. HWP decoding and orientation behavior are
unchanged. No dependency or license policy change was made.

The independent `tiff-pictures` control has 17 pictures and an installed reference
PDF. The native reference uses encoded pixel order for TIFF orientation tags 1–8, and displays
only the first image of a multipage TIFF. DOCX follows that observed compatibility
behavior without rewriting the tags. OOXML does not specify a TIFF orientation
algorithm. Raw RGB, LZW, DEFLATE, PackBits, grayscale, Group 4 bilevel, palette,
unassociated alpha and first-page content have native pixel comparisons.

Remaining gaps: native CMYK/ICC color management is not matched. The CMYK control
retains a separate expected-failure diagnostic rather than relaxed color checks.
BigTIFF, unsupported pixel/compression layouts, and DrawingML tiled TIFF fills
remain unsupported. This change does not claim full TIFF codec or color fidelity.

Validation: 69 targeted unit tests (including the existing HWP image suite),
7 passing browser cases plus the explicit expected CMYK failure, the independent
source control and 8 exported DOCX schema checks, and production/license build.
The original invoice logo now renders with exact no-edit package preservation.
Fine raster downsampling still differs from the native reference and remains a separate fidelity
issue; color blocks do not establish thin-stroke resampling equivalence.

### Plain-text content controls (template 68; validation in progress)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.5.2.44 requires formatting applied to part of a plain-text
control to affect its entire contents. Import now accepts uniformly formatted
text controls, including temporary wrappers around one paragraph or cell and
persistent inline wrappers. Direct formatting, character styles and clearing
formatting use the whole control while preserving the visible selection.
Persistent plain-text controls reject picture and hyperlink insertion before
mutation. Unsupported nested controls, mixed formatting in real plain-text
content, and persistent block wrappers still require read-only import.

Native reference compatibility for cached placeholders (§§17.5.2.34, 17.5.2.39, 17.5.2.44):
while `showingPlcHdr` is active, a plain-text control can display multiple cached
paragraphs and mixed text formatting. The installed reference accepts these
as plain-text controls even with `multiLine=0`; it rejects the corresponding
multi-paragraph content when `showingPlcHdr` is absent. This is an observed
exception to the plain-control paragraph/run restrictions, not permission for
arbitrary multi-paragraph plain-text values. Import accepts the supported text
cache without flattening it. Formatting expands to the whole cache; typing
replaces all its paragraphs and follows the existing temporary-wrapper removal
rules. Persistent block lifecycle, nested controls, tables and non-text cache
runs remain unsupported. Independent source and native selection-based editing
evidence: `tests/fixtures/plain-text-block-placeholders`.

The original `tests/fixtures/plain-text-controls` fixtures and installed references distinguish placeholder appearance from input formatting
(§17.5.2.27). Formatting real content updates both its runs and input properties;
formatting a placeholder changes only its displayed prompt. Text entry replaces
the prompt using the original input properties. Temporary wrappers survive
formatting and unwrap on text changes (§17.5.2.43).

Observed reference divergence: Selection.TypeText and Range.Text accept U+000B even
when multiLine is false or omitted, retaining a w:br in saved XML. The editor
follows this text-entry behavior while retaining the declared attribute.
Range.InsertBreak(6) rejected insertion even for the multiline native control;
this API is not used as the text-entry reference. Existing soft breaks remain
visible. Persistent inline controls still cannot span multiple paragraphs.

Validation so far: 105 focused unit tests pass, and both original fixtures pass
OOXML schema validation. Nineteen browser tests pass (one optional local corpus
test skipped), all 36 browser exports pass schema validation, and the production
build including license checks passes. The original invoice opens editable on
one page, preserves the exact no-edit package, and passes edit, unrelated-part
preservation, exact undo and reopen checks.
The fixture README and reproduction tools
record the native commands and their scope. No corpus completion count changes.

### Linear DrawingML gradient fills

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.8.33, §20.1.8.36, §20.1.8.41 and §20.1.8.59 define
gradient fills, stops, linear directions and tile rectangles. Shapes now render
explicit and theme-derived linear gradients with ordered color stops, including
existing supported color transforms and alpha. Shape source XML remains atomic
and unchanged through unrelated text edits. Conflicting fills, malformed stops,
unsupported shading modes and nonempty tile rectangles fail strict import.

The native reference diverges from §20.1.8.41's scaled-vector formula. Twelve
independently authored controls show normalized `(cos(a)/w, sin(a)/h)` instead
of the stated `(w*cos(a), h*sin(a))`. All axes match the native PDF within 0.006pt.
The implementation follows the native reference; the control README documents extraction and
provenance. Canvas colors at 108 interior samples match the independent reference
axes and PDF color functions within three channel levels through edits and reopen.

At that milestone support excluded path gradients (circular paths are supported
by the later entry below), nonempty tile rectangles, gradients on
group properties/line outlines, and fills fixed against shape rotation. Those
require additional native references and rendering support. The existing shape
transform pipeline applies to supported fills; zero-area shapes avoid nonfinite
scaled coordinates. No new dependency or license is introduced.

Validation: 42 focused unit tests initially passed across gradient, alpha, theme
and flip behavior; the final flat-geometry guard has an additional targeted test.
Four browser tests pass, eight exports pass schema validation, and the production
build includes license checks. Template 69's wave artwork and white names return;
its ten logo pictures still need DrawingML luminance effects, so it remains partial.

### Picture brightness and contrast

DrawingML `a:lum` on image BLIPs now follows ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.8.42:
brightness shifts RGB channels and contrast changes their separation while
preserving alpha. The independent 29-case `picture-luminance` control establishes
the native reference's channel transfer formula, extremes, repeated effects and grayscale
ordering. These effects run on a decoded copy, in source order, with unchanged
source media and drawing XML. Existing duotone-only and grayscale-only decode
paths remain unchanged. Newly inserted effect-bearing images serialize the
ordered chain, including fractional percentage values.

Opaque samples match the native reference exactly in unit tests and within
three channel levels in browser canvas tests. Partially transparent luminance
colors still differ from the native reference's premultiplied rounding; an explicit expected-
failure browser test records that unresolved fidelity gap. This is not a claim
of exact transparency rendering. Malformed attributes and out-of-range
percentages are rejected by strict import.

Validation: 22 focused unit cases pass across luminance, grayscale and duotone
(the final luminance rerun passes all 11 cases); three browser regressions pass
plus one expected-failure transparency diagnostic. Six exported packages pass
schema checks, and the production/license build passes. Template 69 now reaches
unsupported EMF record 82 in its logo images; the logos are still absent and the
source remains read-only with exact no-edit ZIP preservation.

### EMF logical fonts and Unicode text

The original EMF decoder now reads logical fonts (MS-EMF §2.3.7.8) and
EMR_EXTTEXTOUTW (§2.3.5.8), including explicit per-character advances, two-axis
advances, text color, baseline/top/bottom and left/center/right alignment.
Font state follows object selection and SaveDC/RestoreDC. Text and font names
are escaped before constructing the isolated SVG. Original EMF bytes remain
unchanged. Invalid buffers, unsupported glyph-index records, rotated logical
fonts, stock-font drawing, implicit advances, opaque backgrounds and text inside
paths fail before editable import. Unicode storage alone does not establish
complex-script shaping or full font availability across platforms.

Compatible-mode text keeps glyph proportions and upright orientation while
character origins follow the transform; only font height scales. This matches
the documented Win32 GM_COMPATIBLE behavior and the anisotropic native control:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-setgraphicsmode
Full face names retain first preference, with matching Bold/Italic style suffixes
also expressed as a CSS family fallback. No font binary or dependency is added.
Rendering relies on an available system font; bundled web-font embedding into
EMF previews is not established by these controls.

through edit/reopen. Their positive Y advances move subsequent text upward in
native playback; the control caught and corrected the initial sign error.

browser regressions. The final export-schema and production/license checks are
recorded with this change's task-scratch logs. This is a supported subset, not
complete EMF conformance.

### Inline picture content controls

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.5.2.24 (`w:picture`), §17.5.2.38 (`w:temporary`):
unlocked inline picture-only controls import as ordinary drawing runs with
retained wrapper metadata. Picture formatting and geometry edits preserve both
temporary and persistent wrappers. Selected-content text replacement/deletion,
search replacement and hyperlinks fail before mutation. Boundary carets type
outside the wrapper; an enclosing selection can remove the wrapper itself.
Block/cell picture wrappers, locks, bindings, nested controls and non-picture
content remain unsupported for editing. Original media and unrelated parts are
preserved; no new rendering path or document-specific behavior is introduced.

Eight independently authored controls and native reference XML/PDF references in
`tests/fixtures/picture-controls` establish the supported editing behavior.
The reference application's InlineShapes.AddPicture API inserts an additional picture before the
selected contents: persistent wrappers retain both pictures, temporary wrappers
unwrap. This diverges from the clause's single-picture requirement. The engine
implements that observed insertion result and accepts picture-only multiple
contents on reopening; this does not claim native picture-replacement UI equivalence.
Temporary-control content signatures compare picture identities and assets,
separately from formatting, so resizing does not incorrectly unwrap them.

Picture placeholder state is separate from ordinary picture content: the
additional eight native cases with `w:showingPlcHdr` confirm that insertion
replaces the placeholder image, clears the persistent placeholder flag, and
unwraps a temporary control. Resize retains both the wrapper and placeholder
flag; text entry and selected-content deletion remain rejected. Selections
spanning table cells retain the inserted image and remove fully enclosed
wrappers without mistaking each cell's subrange for a content-only deletion.

### Numeric offsets of percentage-sized anchor effect boxes

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.4.2.3 (anchor), §20.4.2.6 (effectExtent), and the
`positionH`/`positionV` elements define the ordinary anchor components.
[MS-ODRAWXML §5.11](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-odrawxml/1a38a99a-16ae-420d-8c79-23dc2e922717)
adds the `sizeRelH`/`sizeRelV` percentage-size extension. Independently authored
reference controls in `tests/fixtures/relative-anchor-effects` establish how those
components interact for numeric offsets.

If either axis has a positive relative size, the native reference adds the leading left and top
effect extents to both numeric coordinates. Width-only sizing therefore changes
the vertical origin too; height-only sizing changes the horizontal origin too.
Only the dimensions that are relative subtract their pair of effect extents.
Fixed-size numeric offsets retain their existing shape-origin meaning. Aligned
coordinates already position the effect box, so they receive no additional
shift. Page/margin anchors inside cells apply the same relative-size shift after
resolving their existing cell position. Source drawing XML remains unchanged.

This observed reference extension behavior is proven by sixteen independently authored
rectangle/ellipse placements across body and cell documents, retained native PDFs,
and extracted frame/raster measurements. It is not a document-specific stroke
inset or a newly established conflict with base OOXML. Other relative bases remain
outside the existing supported subset. Sub-tenth-percent precision and drawing
stroke resampling at changed relative dimensions are separate unresolved topics.

Validation: 58 distinct focused unit tests and 25 browser cases pass. The two
final independent sources, 43 broad-run browser exports, four final control
exports and eight final original/matched-font corpus exports pass schemas.
Production build and license gate pass. Both native control pages and the
original/matched-font cover-letter comparisons were visually reviewed. The
initial cell comparison's title-font discrepancy was removed in the authored
control by specifying its font and exact paragraph spacing, then recapturing
both native PDFs; no production text-layout change was made.


### Section columns: equal-width flow

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.6.3 and 17.6.4 define column entries and section
column sets. The importer and paginator now support equal-width section columns
without separators. Ordinary overflow advances to the next column; explicit
page breaks advance to the next physical page. Physical page counts continue to
select headers/footers and page numbering. Text, tables, decorations, clipping,
carets and hit testing use the translated column coordinates. Column settings
are retained through ordinary editing/export; this stage does not add a column
settings UI. Unequal widths, separator painting and positioned/floating objects
in columns remain guarded and are outstanding work. Explicit column breaks are
supported by the later implementation documented below.

Original controls in `tests/fixtures/column-flow` retain native references
for equal/unequal flow, explicit breaks, separators, final short content and
fixed tables wider than a column, plus authored physical page breaks and table
rows flowing to a second column. The five currently supported controls pass
browser comparisons of physical page counts and native text coordinates within
0.15 pt, hit testing, selection, editing, unchanged-part preservation, full undo
and editable export/reopen. Unsupported controls remain implementation evidence,
not passing support claims. Equal-width attributes ignore stale child widths;
unequal interval parsing remains available for the next layout implementation.

Positioned-drawing eligibility is scoped to the section containing the anchor.
A positioned drawing in an earlier or later single-column section does not
invalidate another section's column flow. `mixed-section-drawings` supplies
an independent three-page reference, with drawings on both sides of a
two-column section, native text positions and drawing bounds. The negative
test retains the restriction when the anchor itself is in the column section.
The drawing scan runs once only if column flow is encountered. This follows
section ownership in §§17.6.3–17.6.4 and anchor semantics in §20.4.2.3; no
reference/spec divergence or general floating-object-in-columns support is claimed.

### Implicit table margins: reference divergence

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.34 and 17.4.10 specify 115-twip default
leading/trailing cell margins when no value exists in the style hierarchy;
§17.4.42 delegates omitted table margins to these defaults. The installed reference
instead reports zero side padding for both empty default and empty
custom table styles. With no resolved table style (absent or empty styles part),
it reports 0.5 pt / 10 twips. Explicit 115-twip style margins remain 5.75 pt.
The same implicit values occur in compatibility modes 14 and 15. A named built-in Normal Table supplies 108 twips and implicit zero indentation; an unnamed style merely marked default does neither. The canonical built-in style name, rather than its arbitrary styleId, identifies that behavior. A borderless
control isolates padding from the half-border writing inset.

`tests/fixtures/table-margin-defaults` contains ten original minimal controls,
native reference PDFs, and COM padding observations. They derive only from the
independently authored column fixture, with no corpus content. The generator
and read-only reference exporter are `tools/table_margin_defaults_fixture.py` and
`tools/table_margin_defaults_native.ps1`. All ten sources pass transitional schemas. Runtime import applies these defaults before style, table, row and
cell overrides; existing explicit margins and newly inserted tables retain
their authored values. This is a documented reference-compatibility divergence,
not literal conformance to the normative 115-twip fallback.

Equal-column integration verification: 280 unit checks across 17 relevant files;
42 distinct targeted browser cases passing across final runs; 18 original
control sources and 106 collected browser/original-document exports pass
transitional schemas; production build and license check pass. Browser controls
also verify preserving the horizontal caret offset across column/page transitions.
Native Arial baseline comparison is conditional on that installed reference font;
font substitution on other hosts is annotated, while geometry and editing checks
continue. This is scoped regression evidence, not a whole-corpus certification.

### Ordinary picture outlines and outside placement

Part 1 §§20.1.2.2.24 (`ln`), 20.2.2.6 (picture `spPr`), 20.1.9.8
(`custGeom`) and 20.1.9.15–16 (paths) govern picture geometry and line styling.
Supported closed picture contours now retain and paint solid RGB/theme outlines
separately from their textures. Geometry stroke/fill flags remain independent,
as do picture opacity, crop, reflection and physical pen width. Existing line
cap, dash, join and compound-line parsing is shared with shapes. Open stroked
picture paths, non-centered explicit alignment, unsupported line fills,
standalone custom-picture rotation/3D and sketch regeneration remain guarded.

**Reference-specific placement:** the twelve manually authored controls in
`tests/fixtures/picture-outlines` show that the native reference offsets a picture's
outline centerline outward by half its physical width, even with omitted line
alignment. The default centered shape pen alone does not reproduce this picture
behavior. Offset the actual contour edges in physical coordinates, expanding
outer contours and contracting holes; do not expand just the frame. The native reference's cubic
outline is flattened before offsetting. Reflections and nested nonuniform group
scales must not scale the pen. Original source attributes and drawing XML are
retained rather than rewritten to encode this compatibility behavior.

The ordinary controls compare 3,749 flat native color samples and twelve ink
bounds through text edits, exact undo and export/reopen. Independent geometry
checks use PDF-measured rectangle and triangle centerlines, holes, disjoint
contours, reflection, repeated points and collinear edges. Source/PDF hashes
bind the native reference. A missing line fill paints no border, as verified by
a separate reference probe; width alone does not introduce ink.

`tests/fixtures/picture-sketch-outlines` records a separate unresolved case.
The native reference regenerates geometry from `ask:lineSketchStyleProps` rather than necessarily
painting the supplied custom paths. MS-ODRAWXML §2.38.4.1 describes the seed's
role in repeatable shape generation. This extension remains rejected by strict
import; preserving cached paths is not claimed as equivalent regeneration.
Corpus template 95 still requires this feature and its unavailable font.

### Saved sketch geometry in read-only previews

MS-ODRAWXML §2.38.3.2 (`CT_LineSketchStyleProperties`) stores shape/type/seed
metadata for regeneration. The standard custom paths remain governed by Part 1
§§20.1.9.8 and 20.1.9.15–16. When strict import rejects a sketch extension,
read-only preview can now retain those materialized paths instead of dropping
the entire drawing group. This is a display approximation; the native reference may regenerate
different geometry, as the independent sketch control demonstrates.

The projection recognizes only the published sketch extension and known type
names, requires materialized `a:custGeom`, and validates seed values as unsigned
32-bit integers. Unknown extensions, malformed metadata and unsupported base
geometry retain their existing fallback behavior. It removes regeneration
metadata only from a temporary line-property clone. All package parts and the
original drawing shell remain unchanged. Cached stroke contours are painted
without an additional ordinary-picture outside offset; texture and stroke path
flags remain independent.

Only the rich preview pass enables this projection, including drawings in page
stories. Strict imports still reject the extension, the package remains
read-only, edited export throws, and the UI downloads the original file bytes.
The independent `picture-sketch-outlines.docx` fixture verifies stored geometry,
read-only interaction and original-file reopening. It does not certify sketch
regeneration. Template 95's portrait and decorative group now appear, while its
font and exact regeneration gaps remain open.

The original controls in `tests/fixtures/opentype-kerning/README.md` expose an
interaction between run kerning (§17.3.2.19), w14 ligatures and the
`enableOpenTypeFeatures` compatibility setting (MS-DOCX §2.3.3). In the installed reference, enabling the setting with standard/contextual ligatures widens
Goudy Old Style numeric and letter samples, consistent with omitting legacy
kern pairs. Arial, Times New Roman and Calibri retain their measured positions.
Without the ligature declaration, the setting did not change these samples.

The current Canvas path does not reproduce that interaction. The four-font,
32-line controls and native PDFs are diagnostic evidence, not a shipped fix.
A generic implementation must account for requested OpenType formatting and
font capabilities; neither a Goudy-specific adjustment nor a digits-only rule
is justified. This is not a proved contradiction of the normative kern clause;
the MS-DOCX extension does not prescribe this exact legacy-table behavior.

## Explicit column breaks

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.3.1 and 17.18.4 define `w:br w:type="column"`
as advancing to the next available column, or to the next page in the last
column or a single-column section. The body text importer, paginator, editor,
and exporter now retain this distinction from authored page and line breaks.
Ctrl+Shift+Enter inserts a column break; plain-text copy substitutes a newline.
The internal marker is serialized as a break element, never an XML control
character. Untouched package parts remain unchanged.

The six independent controls in `tests/fixtures/column-breaks/README.md` cover
inline, leading, terminal, repeated, and single-column cases against the installed reference. Terminal column breaks retain the following paragraph-mark line in the
new column. Existing page-break compatibility behavior remains separate.
Breaks in table cells and shape text remain guarded, as do unsupported column
configurations. Continuous section transitions are covered by the later
implementation below.

## Continuous sections with matching page geometry

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.6.22 places a continuous section after the preceding
paragraph. Its type belongs to the section being started. The first section
still starts at the document origin regardless of its stored type. Equal-width
columns (§§17.6.3–4) balance before a following continuous section, subject to
authored column breaks and keep constraints.

The layout retains separate section regions on shared physical pages. Text,
table cells, caret hit testing and vertical navigation use each region's
column geometry. Balancing operates on measured blocks and preserves keep
groups that fit at full height; candidate regions must contain their actual
line/cell geometry. Ordinary next-page sections retain their existing path.

A shared page uses its first occupying section's header/footer. Later pages
use the continuing section's stories. Section page totals count every occupied
physical page, including shared pages, but exclude empty trailing regions.
Drawing fields use their owning region's section totals; header/footer
drawings use the page's story owner. Source section XML remains unchanged
through edits. Editing section types and deleting across section boundaries
remain guarded.

This implementation requires identical resolved paper geometry and margins
across a continuous transition. Page-number restarts in continuous sections,
unequal/separated columns, and positioned drawings or floating tables in
columns remain unsupported. Missing page-level properties that require
different inheritance from following sections are not implemented by guessing.
The ten original reference controls and their reference details are documented in
tests/fixtures/continuous-sections/README.md.

Template 109 now places its introductory text and first six signatures in
shared-page columns. It remains under review: drawing hyperlinks still block
strict import, pictures are missing from the read-only approximation, and
the gallery's remaining pagination differs from the native reference.

story and drawing-field runs. A one-off 30-second CLI timeout was used: the

the corrected native text positions are identical and the corrected source,
reference hashes, unit/browser reruns and schemas are the final evidence.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.4.2.5 (`wp:docPr`), 20.2.2.3 (`pic:cNvPr`),
21.1.2.3.5 (`a:hlinkClick`) and §A.4.1 define nonvisual hyperlink metadata.
Import checked external HTTP(S), mailto and tel destinations from the drawing's
own part relationships. Preserve the original metadata and shared relationships.
The original four-picture reference control shows that outer `wp:docPr` links are

Hyperlinks collection or PDF annotations. The engine follows that observed
activation behavior without asserting a normative precedence rule.

DrawingML link, without creating a second WordprocessingML text hyperlink.

other images sharing the old relationship retain their destination. Undo and
untouched export preserve original package bytes. Tooltips/history and other

existing noopener/noreferrer opener. Other target frames, actions, sound behavior,

### Picture solid backing fills

Part 1 §§20.2.2.1 and 20.2.2.6 permit a picture texture and a separate shape
fill on the same picture; the transparent-picture example on printed pages
3090–3092 illustrates this layering. §20.1.8.54 defines solid fill, with the
ordered color transforms from §20.1.2.3. The reader now accepts a single solid
backing fill or noFill, rejects conflicting/duplicate/malformed declarations,
and retains the original package markup. Existing color/theme/alpha resolution
is reused. No reference/spec divergence is asserted for this behavior.

For flat pictures, the renderer paints the geometry's backing first, the cropped
texture second, and any outline last. Texture opacity does not change backing
opacity. Grouped pictures use the same layers, including inherited transforms.
For the existing supported 3D subset, texture and backing are composed before
surface lighting. Crop outsets expose the backing. Existing unsupported rotation
combinations, gradients/pattern backing, shadows, bevels and lighting presets
remain guarded; accepting a solid fill does not discard those other features.

The independently generated ten-page `picture-surfaces/backing.docx` control
and installed reference PDF cover absent/white/shaded/translucent backing,
ellipse clipping, crop outsets, texture opacity, front-facing supported 3D,
grouped pictures and picture outlines. Original transparent PNG artwork and
source/PDF hashes are included. The browser comparison samples six interior or
corner locations per page; tolerance is three RGB levels for existing raster
compositing/3D rounding, not a claim of pixel-identical edges.

### Outer-shadow reference investigation (not implemented)

The original seventeen-page `picture-shadows` source/PDF/reference isolates

verifies all labels and four exact RGB-equivalent flag combinations; explicit
true changes visible pixels compared with false. The empty shadowObscured
element matches false, consistent with the current MS-ODRAWXML schema; the older
2012 default-1 excerpt must not guide implementation. Reference documentation
links the current primary specification. No current-standard divergence is
claimed.

The native reference's exported shadow bitmap resolution changes with blur size. The retained
edge profiles and image dimensions distinguish that rasterization from the

### Standalone picture outer shadows

Part 1 §20.1.8.45 and the CT_OuterShadowEffect schema define the imported shadow
parameters. Unscaled/unskewed outer shadows now compose behind standalone flat
pictures and the existing supported 3D pictures. The source drawing, relationship
and image parts remain retained; only session preview bitmaps are generated.
Offsets and blur are physical lengths. Expanded effect bounds do not change the
picture's layout frame. Existing image-resource limits apply before allocating
the expanded bitmap, and the consumed source bitmap is closed after composition.
Documents without shadows keep their existing decode paths.

The normal mask uses composed picture alpha, including backing fill, crop and
outline. Current MS-ODRAWXML §2.3.1.12/CT_ShadowObscured defaults to false. Explicit
true casts the full rectangular/elliptical silhouette, then removes the shadow
inside that shape before painting the picture. Twenty original reference controls
include the critical translucent-image case: clipping the alpha-derived shadow
alone makes the exterior too faint. No current-standard divergence is asserted.

Native reference PDF samples establish colors, offset direction and blur behavior.
The browser oracle compares picture-interior colors and shadow profiles outside
the frame's one-CSS-pixel coverage fringe; profile colors must match within three
RGB levels, allowing one native shadow texel plus half a CSS pixel of position
uncertainty. Interpolation accounts for subpixel sampling at sharp edges. Native
PDF shadow rasters have blur-dependent resolutions, so these checks do not claim
pixel-identical picture-edge antialiasing. Existing foreground/3D geometry checks
remain separate. The renderer uses a Gaussian sigma of one third the supplied
blur radius; it does not reproduce the native reference's PDF resolution selection heuristic.

Combined effects, rotated frames, grouped picture shadows, scaled/skewed shadows
and obscuration with custom or perspective geometry remain guarded. The gallery
portrait's two-point lighting and bevel are still unsupported, as is its pending
pagination issue. Adding shadows does not complete template 109.

### Scaled standalone picture shadows

The scaling restriction above is now lifted for otherwise supported standalone
picture shadows. Part 1 §20.1.8.45 and `CT_OuterShadowEffect` define signed
horizontal/vertical percentages, all nine alignment anchors, and bottom-center
alignment when omitted. The renderer scales the alpha mask about that physical
frame anchor, then offsets and blurs it; negative scales flip and a zero scale
casts no area. Effect bounds expand independently of the layout frame, with
the existing allocation limit checked first. Original DrawingML remains intact.
Nonzero skew, rotated frames and other previously guarded combinations remain
unsupported. No per-document conditions or new paint-time probes are added.

Fourteen original controls in `tests/fixtures/scaled-picture-shadows/` verify
alignment, unequal scales, flips, collapse and blur. The thirteen sharp/small-blur

or longitude, other materials/rigs, and unimplemented implicit directions remain

not specify their interaction. The independent fourteen-page picture-lighting

### Absolute positional tabs (`w:ptab`)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.3.23 and §17.18.71–73 define the positional-tab character,
its left/center/right alignment, margin/indent base, and five leader values.
All three attributes are required by CT_PTab. Import validates them and retains
each tab as one text position with separate metadata. Serialization writes the
original character type after paragraph edits; ordinary typing does not inherit
positional-tab metadata. Untouched package parts retain their original bytes.

The layout ignores custom/default tab stops for positional tabs, aligns the
following field, emits leaders using the existing leader painter, and moves a
tab to the next line when its target has been passed. Empty leading left tabs
do not produce repeated empty lines. Caret offsets retain the tab and any
trailing spaces; those spaces do not contribute to positional-field alignment.

Independent native reference controls establish divergences from the
specification's margin-relative example: right tabs respect the paragraph right
indent in both modes; leading left tabs cannot move backwards into indentation;
indent-center includes half the left indent but ignores the right indent and
first-line indent. The engine follows these observed rules. Evidence and exact
coordinates are retained in `tests/fixtures/positional-tabs`: 60 body controls
and two three-page contextual sources with native PDFs and hash-pinned reference
data. Context controls cover headers, footers, fixed/AutoFit cells, two columns
and repeated fields, including trailing spaces before a subsequent tab.

(four positional-tab workflows and five ordinary leader regressions), plus
source/export XML validation. This evidence does not certify every combination
of oversized aligned fields and floating-object wrapping. Template 109 now opens
editable on three pages; its body insertion, exact undo, export/reopen and OPC
preservation pass. Its three page rasters are unchanged from the preceding
read-only capture. Detailed source fidelity review is still incomplete.

### Whitespace classification for vertical line metrics

The picture-only rule cannot use JavaScript/Unicode `trim()` to identify text.

U+200B, U+3000 and U+FEFF as blank-line characters. NBSP, narrow NBSP, thin,
hair, figure and punctuation spaces and the other tested Unicode spaces retain
text metrics. An inline picture beside those characters retains a text
descender, and an oversized final paragraph mark does not enlarge that line.
A text-only blank line instead takes the paragraph mark's metrics, even if its
whitespace run uses a larger font. Stored characters and caret advances remain
unchanged.

The relevant clauses remain ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.1.29, 17.3.1.33,
17.3.1.39 and 20.4.2.8. This is measured reference consumer behavior; OOXML does not
mandate equivalence with Unicode's whitespace predicate. Original controls in
`tests/fixtures/inline-picture-whitespace` vary 23 character cases and two mark
sizes, with and without pictures. The original Verdana sources additionally

all 184 Before/After baselines match the native reference within 0.15pt. No fallback-font
mapping is hard-coded into production code.

## Shape-autofit sizing implementation

The pending evidence above now has a rendering implementation for WPS
`a:spAutoFit` (ECMA-376 Part 1 §21.1.2.1.4, `bodyPr` §21.1.2.1.1,
`CT_TextShapeAutofit` §A.4.1). Shapes grow or shrink after font measurement;
physical font and inset sizes survive group transforms. Mixed/nested groups
refit their child bounds. Measured frames feed body/story pagination, header
clearance, painting and hit testing. Source paragraphs, drawing XML and edit
history retain their original dimensions. Ordinary documents retain the
existing paragraph path when no fitted drawing map exists.

The 72 original native pages plus 12 new edge pages establish native reference
compatibility. The edge controls cover mixed/nested groups, ellipse,
outline, paragraph spacing and empty text. The native reference fits ellipse text once using
the original non-text height; it does not iterate the new inscribed rectangle
to eliminate clipping. This behavior is not specified as an algorithm by
OOXML. The independent controls in `tests/fixtures/shape-autofit-edges/`
record the observed result, including its partially clipped last line.

Malformed/conflicting autofit modes remain rejected. Active `normAutofit`, autofit
with page-dependent fields and autofit with page-relative dimensions remain
guarded pending their own sizing implementation. Other existing unsupported
shape/text properties retain their guards. Source 114 now reaches decorated
text-box runs and remains read-only/partial; this is not a whole-document fix.

is approximately .65 in both dimensions; its native 20pt test run is 12.96pt
in the PDF, versus 12pt vertically in the current renderer. Combined script
and explicit baseline shifts also change the line baseline by about .57pt.

shape guard. The experimental guard removal was reverted; no production
behavior changes in this evidence step. See `work/shape-transform-probe.json`
and the fixture README. Grouped width-scaled glyphs become PDF artwork, so

## Declared script size for line allocation

The shared layout engine now separates script ink/caret metrics from line
allocation. ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.42 (`vertAlign`) preserves the declared
run size while changing its displayed script; §17.3.2.24 (`position`) shifts
the run explicitly, and §17.3.1.33 (`spacing`) controls paragraph lines.
The precise allocation behavior is established by native reference controls rather
than a numerical algorithm supplied by those clauses.

Thirty independent pages in `tests/fixtures/script-line-boxes/` show that
the native reference allocates the declared font's ascent/descent without script scaling.
An explicit baseline shift moves that box, with surrounding runs and the
paragraph mark providing the remaining minimum ascent/descent. This applies
to script-only lines as well as mixed text. The previous engine reused the
smaller painted glyph box, shortening lines and misplacing following content.

Measurement now supplies separate allocation metrics for scripts. Line
building, paragraph marks, tabs, numbering and text beside inline objects
consume those metrics; painting, decoration geometry and insertion carets
retain their existing script transforms. The shared path also feeds retained
shape autofit. No source run, font-size declaration or XML is rewritten, and
no extra font measurement pass is introduced.

Browser measurements of Before/After and mixed-line Start baselines match

and Times New Roman. Exact no-edit/undo packages, editing and reopening are
checked. Targeted unit coverage totals 174 passing checks, including distinct
caret/selection boxes, blank script marks, whitespace and retained-shape
autofit. Eight import/export-heavy checks exceeded the local 5s default;
two representative checks also fail at unchanged HEAD. All eight pass with a
20s command-line test deadline; repository timeout settings remain unchanged.
Evidence: `work/script-line-boxes-unit*`, `work/script-line-boxes-new-unit.log`
and `work/script-line-boxes-baseline-timeouts.log`.

This fixes allocation, not font-specific script glyph size/offset. The

### Relative sizing before local drawing rotation

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.4.2.3, 20.4.2.6–7, 20.1.7.5–6 and MS-ODRAWXML §5.11
provide the anchor, effect/frame extents, transforms and percentage sizing.
Twenty-three independent reference controls in `tests/fixtures/relative-shape-frames/`
establish an additional ordering rule: page-relative sizing resizes local frames
before their rotation. It does not behave like stretching the final bitmap or
adding another group-coordinate scale. The group's existing quarter-turn
scale-axis exchange still applies to its own coordinate transform.

The importer marks relative scenes as runtime frame-dependent. The decoder
copies/resizes local frame and group-coordinate extents when the resolved page
frame changes, preserving source geometry coordinates, text size and physical
pen width. Stored scene data and drawing XML remain unchanged. Unchanged
frame/field/pattern-phase requests reuse the current raster; replacements
retain the existing per-drawing and 64-megapixel session limits. A rejected
replacement is closed without discarding the previous usable image.

The controls cover eight rotation angles, nonuniform resize, effect extents,
physical pens/text, nesting and pattern fill. Visible bounds improve from
errors as large as 141.75pt to at most 0.75pt at 96dpi. Both text controls,

pass browser checks. Source 114's previously displaced top-band right edge
and bottom-band left edge now match the native pixel positions.

Additional fixed/relative controls with differing outer `wp:extent` and root
group extent establish that the group's extent supplies physical geometry.
The saved outer extent remains the layout and percentage-resize basis, without
adding a second geometry scale. Nonuniform nested group controls distinguish
this behavior from ordinary group-coordinate scaling. These are native reference
compatibility findings; the extension schema does not specify their ordering.

line-gap values. The three verified faces are MS Gothic, MS PGothic and

additional 38/256 em on each side to match the native reference's automatic baseline/advance.

claim about every East Asian font.

The cached native-face measurement applies the profile only when both the
displayed family and base geometry agree. Other families and substituted or
changed faces keep their native metrics. The same corrected natural extents
flow through mixed text, tables, selection/caret geometry and pagination;
font size, glyph outlines and retained DOCX source remain unchanged. No standalone font
binary or third-party renderer is distributed, and no extra DOM measurement
or per-character font access is introduced.

## Row-level table border and look exceptions

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.40, §17.4.55 and §17.4.61–62: the importer now
accepts `tblBorders` and `tblLook` within a row's `tblPrEx`. Missing border
sides inherit the table; cell declarations retain precedence. Explicit row
`none`/`nil` removes that inherited stroke, subject to the existing opposing
cell-border conflict rules. Original exception XML remains in the row shell
through unrelated edits and copied rows. Conditional regions are recomputed
with the physical row's look flags after structural edits.

Independent reference controls establish the physical paint behavior: interior
horizontal boundaries use insideH; a page fragment's outer bottom uses the
last physical row's bottom exception. Vertically merged cells keep per-row
side segments. Their hidden horizontal boundaries retain small exposed caps
where the vertical side changes format. At a T-junction an unchanged vertical
side stays continuous; a changed side receives a horizontal transition cap.
These are generic table rules, not source-document offsets.

The original source, native reference PDF and hash-bound color references
are in `tests/fixtures/table-row-exceptions/`. Sixteen cases span eighteen
pages, including partial declarations, cell precedence, none/nil, adjacent
rows, horizontal/vertical merges, conditional bands and repeated headers.
The browser test checks every disconnected colored band to 1pt before and
after editing/export/reopen. Unit tests cover inheritance, topology edits,
malformed declarations, exact undo and merged fragment bounds.

This extends the existing supported LTR, zero-cell-spacing table border
subset. It does not add all other tblPrEx properties or arbitrary border
patterns, and schema validation does not prove full reference fidelity. Original
corpus source 116 now opens editable instead of a plain-text approximation;
its remaining font-substitution pagination difference is recorded in the
corpus ledger.

Validation: 197 unit tests, 31 browser cases, 311 XML checks across 63
source/export packages, production build and license gate pass. Construction's
two page rasters remain RGB-identical. The source 116 and Arial-only diagnostic
editing/undo/export checks pass; their two-versus-one-page difference remains
an explicit font-availability gap. Evidence: scratch `work/row-exceptions-*`,
`work/template116-final-*`, `work/template116-arial*` and
`work/construction-row-exceptions-*`.

## Extended w14 text fills

MS-DOCX `textFill` / `CT_FillTextEffect` extends ordinary run foreground color
(ISO/IEC 29500-1 §17.3.2.6). The extension reference is reproduced in the Open XML SDK
[FillTextEffect documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.office2010.word.filltexteffect?view=openxml-3.0.1).
Direct and inherited no-fill and untransformed solid sRGB/theme fills are retained
through the model, styles, history and export. No-fill suppresses glyph fill,
automatic underline and strike ink without removing advances, caret stops,
kerning or line allocation. Explicit underline color and glyph outlines remain
visible. Solid text effects override ordinary foreground color without erasing it.
Fill changes are paint spans, not new shaping groups, including WPS shape text.

Native reference divergence: the type definition specifies solid black for an empty
`textFill`. Independent reordered controls show the native reference instead carries
its preceding solid text-effect color across body paragraphs, starting black;
ordinary foreground and no-fill text do not reset it. Separate WPS text boxes
start black. Layout copies resolve empty declarations, leaving source/history
and exported empty elements intact. Numbering-label and paragraph-mark effects
on this carry have not been independently established. Gradients, color transforms
other than the luminance operations documented below, and unsupported extension
children still trigger safe fallback.

Original controls, native PDFs, hashes and reference extraction are under
`tests/fixtures/text-fill/`, generated by `tools/text_fill_fixture.py` and
`tools/text_fill_reference.py`. Unit coverage checks inheritance, editing,
serialization, undo, decoration ink, malformed extensions and unchanged shaping.
Browser coverage compares native per-line color ink and checks export/reopen.
Standard MCE-view schema validation alone does not prove extension semantics.

The native controls additionally expose the existing Arial underline-thickness
gap: at 18pt the native reference's rule is 1.32pt, versus the current .9pt generic metric,
independently of fill selection. The text-fill checks verify the explicit rule's
continuity, color and horizontal span; they do not assert thickness equivalence.
See `decorations.docx` in the same independent fixture folder.

## Native-font ordinary underline metrics

ISO/IEC 29500-1 §17.3.2.40 (`u`) and §17.18.99 (`ST_Underline`) specify the
underline declaration and pattern. The OpenType
[post table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/post)
defines suggested underline top-edge position and thickness. Independent native reference
controls across Arial, Calibri, Times New Roman and Cambria, four faces
and six sizes, match those values within .061pt of PDF coordinate rounding.
The renderer previously applied bundled Noto Sans underline metrics to all
families, making Arial's rules too thin and placing some other faces incorrectly.

Reviewed numeric post metrics now enter the existing per-face cache, guarded by
its measured line ascent/descent and selected weight. They change only ordinary
underline ink; advances, line allocation, caret positions and source XML remain
unchanged. Font substitution uses the displayed family, not the requested name.
No font binaries, new font downloads, permissions, DOM probes or per-character
font-table reads are introduced. Unreviewed/differently measured faces retain
the existing fallback; matching line geometry alone cannot identify arbitrary
font-version changes. Installed-font hashes and numeric provenance are retained
in `tests/fixtures/native-underlines/reference.json`.

Native pattern controls confirm the vertical metric rule for single, words,
dotted, dash, dashLong, dotDash and dotDotDash. Heavy, double and wavy variants
use other size-dependent reference rules; applying the single-rule metric would
worsen those existing approximations. Their previous ink geometry is retained
and regression checked. Full pattern equivalence, including ordinary dash spacing
and phases, remains open. This is not an OOXML/spec divergence: the pattern
enumeration does not prescribe fixed physical pen dimensions. The earlier
text-fill section's Arial single-rule thickness gap is corrected by this change.

Original generators and reference extraction: `tools/native_underline_fixture.py`
and `tools/native_underline_reference.py`. Eighteen native reference pages provide 96
face/size cases and 34 pattern cases. Browser checks compare native rectangle
geometry and actual UI paint, plus editing/export/reopen and exact undo.

The native underline controls also record an existing horizontal-advance gap:
Cambria regular at 10pt differs by 2.754pt over “Underline sample” (.744pt bold);
other tested cases differ by at most .394pt. The underline correction leaves
advances and baselines exactly unchanged against the prior metric path. Native
checks assert rule position/thickness and retain the width evidence as an open
issue, rather than claiming complete native text-width equivalence. Font-dependent
browser comparisons require their named fonts and report an explicit skip if
unavailable; numeric metric/guard tests remain platform-independent.


## DrawingML triangle and right-triangle presets

ECMA-376 Part 1 `ST_ShapeType` (§20.1.10.56), `prstGeom` (§20.1.9.18),
`gd` (§20.1.9.11) and the supplied `presetShapeDefinitions.xml` define these
paths and inner text rectangles. `triangle` uses default `adj=50000`, clamped
to 0–100000, to place its apex horizontally. Its text rectangle spans from
half the apex fraction to that value plus one half, and from half-height to
the bottom. `rtTriangle` runs bottom-left/top-left/bottom-right; its text box
is (1/12,7/12)–(7/12,11/12) of shape dimensions.

Both now resolve into ordinary retained paths at import. Existing shape/group
transforms, fills, outlines and text layout continue to consume that scene.
No new painting branches, runtime probes, document-name checks or changes to
source XML serialization are introduced. Triangle adjustment formulas use the
existing ordered guide evaluator; unknown adjustments and invalid formulas
remain unsupported rather than being discarded. Right triangles have no
published adjustment handles.

Independent original controls and native references cover apex limits,
flips, rotation and text rectangles. The native right-triangle text baseline
has a remaining 0.229pt discrepancy (test limit 0.3pt); no geometry compensation
was added and no cause or reference/spec divergence is claimed for it. Other preset
shapes remain subject to their existing support checks. Source markup survives
body edits, export/reopen and exact undo.


## Vertical merge border ownership and hidden row reserves

ECMA-376 Part 1 (5th edition) §17.4.84 `vMerge`, §17.4.66 `tcBorders` and
§17.4.80 `trHeight` govern this behavior. They define the merged grouping,
cell-edge borders and row height, but do not explicitly prescribe the spacing
contribution of hidden merge-interior borders. Ten original reference controls
establish that those physical boundaries retain border-width reserves even
though their ink is suppressed inside the merge. The last continuation supplies
the visible merged bottom edge, including absence, nil and inherited borders;
a restart's bottom declaration is not moved to that edge.

The row-border prepass now measures one physical row per cell declaration.
Merged painting selects the final continuation's effective bottom border.
Existing border conflict resolution, model ownership, source XML preservation,
page fragmentation and border editing remain in their respective layers. No
new paint-time probes or document-specific conditions are used. Independent
controls include differing restart/final borders, middle-only borders,
opposing interior edges and table-level inheritance; exact row and oversized
merge pagination retain their existing regression coverage.

See `tests/fixtures/merged-border-ownership/`. Native baselines match within
0.081pt on the reference machine. This is verified reference behavior, not a claimed
normative divergence: no contradictory wording was found in the cited clauses.
The older SDK documentation uses different clause numbering; this entry uses
the supplied 2016 PDF (PDF pages 468, 483 and 488, zero-based).

### Automatic table and cell border color

ECMA-376 Part 1 fifth edition §17.3.4 (`CT_Border/@color`, PDF page 367,
zero-based) permits a consumer-selected `auto` color. §§17.4.38 `tblBorders`
and 17.4.66 `tcBorders` govern application and border conflict resolution.
Independent reference controls establish black automatic table/cell borders on
black, blue, gray and mixed cell fills, on both white and dark blue pages.
This is not a demonstrated normative contradiction: the common border
definition permits consumer choice rather than requiring a contrast formula.

Resolve table border automatic ink as black for painting and conflict
brightness comparisons. Keep explicit colors, paragraph/text contrast rules,
geometry, editing and serialized automatic declarations unchanged. No new
font probes, raster analysis or per-document conditions run in the editor.
See `tests/fixtures/automatic-table-borders/` for the original controls,
retained native PDFs, hashed RGB references and editing/export regression.

Separate known gap: fractional raster seams at outer table T-junctions also
occur with explicit black borders. The complete automatic/explicit-black
browser rasters are identical in both controls. Color samples exclude these
junctions; this change does not claim native pixel equivalence there.

## Unordered and repeated gradient stops

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 20.1.8.36 (`gs`) and 20.1.8.37 (`gsLst`) define
positions in the color band, without requiring ascending XML order. Import now
stably sorts parsed stops by position while preserving the original package XML.
Already ordered lists keep their existing linear import path and the 256-stop bound.

The native reference's native axial shading functions establish that repeated positive
positions use the first color, while zero uses the last. Canvas instead produces
a hard transition. Painting now resolves these ties in one bounded pass without
mutating the parsed list. The specification does not explicitly resolve ties;
this is native reference compatibility behavior, not a demonstrated normative contradiction.
Ten independently authored controls and native PDF references are retained in
`tests/fixtures/gradient-stop-order`; they cover all six permutations, stable and
reversed interior ties, and endpoint ties. The browser checks 100 native colors,
editing, export/reopen, original stop order and exact undo. Existing gradient
axis/color coverage also passes. This restores the Mardi Gras flyer's background,
photo and celebrations artwork; its nested group transform remains unsupported.

Validation: 23 targeted unit checks, two browser checks, production build and
199-package license gate pass. The corpus/control/browser packages pass 96 XML
checks across 18 paths. Construction remains editable on two pages with exact
RGB equality to the prior accepted capture, preserved no-edit package parts,
body edit/export/reopen and exact undo; its three exports pass 39 XML checks.
Evidence: scratch `work/gradient-order-*` and `construction-gradient-order-final-*`.
These local checks do not establish remote CI success or complete corpus fidelity.

unreflected groups retain their previous path; no additional bitmap is allocated.

described under Reflected text boxes below.

contradiction was found. The earlier recorded rotation-unit and scale behavior
still applies. Browser checks also cover body editing, retained source parts,

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.3.2.26 (`rFonts`), 17.3.2.1 (`b`) and 17.3.2.16
(`i`) retain the requested font and style declarations. A selectable browser
family does not necessarily select the exact installed face named in DOCX.

than its exact local face, while the native reference uses the exact Medium face.

The existing one-time synthetic-bold ink probe now reports this mismatch as
well, reusing its regular-ink comparison. Correctly matched families retain
native style matching and require no additional raster probes. Mismatched
families, and exact faces whose names are not selectable CSS families, register
the exact face and available local Bold/Italic/Oblique companions. Missing styles
use browser synthesis with the existing reference ink correction. Resolution is
cached per document font name; no font enumeration or remote font request is
introduced. Original font declarations and package parts remain unchanged.

Sixteen original native reference controls in `tests/fixtures/native-face-selection`
cover regular/bold/italic/bold-italic for two ambiguous installed face names and
two ordinary families. All native first-to-last glyph advances agree within
0.25pt; edit/export/reopen and exact undo pass. This is a host font-selection
correction, not a demonstrated reference/spec divergence. Local companion discovery
uses conventional full-face style names; arbitrary localized/custom companion
names are not enumerated.

### Picture color replacement compatibility

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 20.1.8.16 (clrChange), 20.1.8.17 (clrFrom) and
20.1.8.19 (clrTo), printed pages 2859-2860, define replacement colors and the
useA switch; CT_ColorChangeEffect defaults useA to true. The importer accepts
one clrFrom and one clrTo in order, validates useA and color containers, resolves
the shared supported DrawingML color models/transforms, and preserves source XML.
Malformed declarations and effects following extLst remain guarded.

Flagged reference compatibility behavior: the prose describes replacing instances of
the source color without specifying tolerance. For PNG, the native reference matches
each RGBA channel within one byte when useA is true. False useA ignores effect
alpha but matches exact opaque source RGB only; this differs from treating every
input alpha as eligible. JPEG uses sixteen-byte per-channel tolerance with
either flag; ignored effect alphas become opaque before matching. Independent
JPEG/decoded-PNG grids establish colored and diagonal boundaries and alpha
239 versus 238. The decoded payload format, not its part extension, selects
this rule. Fully transparent pixels have decoded black RGB. The native reference applies
all color changes in source order before grayscale, duotone, luminance and the
picture-wide alpha modifier even when surrounding XML order is reversed. This
ordering is a compatibility departure from a literal sequential effect chain.
The independent, manually assembled source control demonstrates these behaviors
without using application rendering code to derive the native reference.

The shared picture pipeline implements these rules for ordinary and nested
picture sources, caches effect variants with their source bytes, and serializes
resolved color-change declarations on newly inserted image assets. Existing
pictures retain their authored drawing XML. Other picture effects keep their
existing path when no color change is present. No dependencies were added.
