in schema-valid rich text, but the native reference renders only the first 255. The
painter reproduces that display limit for the supported BMP Latin subset while
retaining all original source XML. OOXML rich title content does not impose this
255-character source limit. Export, editing around the chart and undo preserve
untouched chart parts. Native coordinate checks do not establish full chart
fidelity; bottom legends and inherited chart-style appearance remain separate gaps.

### Automatic bottom column-chart legends

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§21.2.2.93 (`legend`), 21.2.2.95 (`legendPos`),
21.2.2.132 (`overlay`) and 21.2.2.216 (`txPr`) define the legend structure,
position, overlap and text formatting. The cached-column reader now accepts
bottom legends with explicit supported text styling. Chart-style parts remain
validated: explicit no-fill/no-line overrides must be permitted by the style,
and inherited unresolved text/appearance is not silently replaced.

Automatic bottom layout uses measured font face boxes, proportional square
keys, a font-dependent text/key gap, single-row spacing and equal-width columns
when multiple rows are necessary. A one-column stacked legend reverses series
order, as shown by the original controls; two-column layouts retain normal
row order. Plot spacing includes the legend and a 6pt gap. Existing right-hand
legend behavior is retained. Twenty-one independent reference controls cover font sizes,
font families, widths, multi-row ordering and positive clustered-axis headroom.
Positive clustered axes now leave 5% headroom before rounding the upper bound
to an automatic tick; original controls probe both sides of that boundary.
For positive clustered charts with explicit axis text, tick density uses plot
height and the value-axis face height, capped at ten intervals. Height-only
controls and 18pt value labels cross-check the density transition. Nonoverlaid
titles also reserve the extra top half-box required by large value-axis labels.

These are observed reference automatic-layout choices, not OOXML-mandated geometry
or a claim of a normative specification divergence. Manual/overlaid legends,
entry deletion, decorated text, left/top positions and oversized individual
label wrapping/clipping remain gaps. The standard's original package parts,
including chart styles and caches, are retained through edits and undo.

### Numbering markers with automatic line multiples

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.33 specifies automatic spacing in 240ths of a line.
The existing tall-marker behavior raises the first baseline and keeps the body
text descent. The additional spacing share now also retains body text ascent
and height before applying the marker's larger ascent. This prevents expanded
spacing from multiplying the marker's extra height and gives the corresponding
body-based baseline adjustment for compressed spacing. Exact/minimum spacing,
marker positioning, glyph selection and original XML remain unchanged.

The 24 original `encoded-marker-lines` controls cover two body fonts, encoded
and Unicode Symbol markers, Arial markers, two marker sizes, three line
multiples, explicit line breaks and following paragraphs. All 96 native reference
baselines match within 0.16pt. This resolves the source-158 method-page bullet
drift without a font-name or document-specific condition. The controls retain
known Unicode-Symbol missing-glyph and bold-Symbol raster differences; they do
not certify those unrelated glyph behaviors. No new normative contradiction
with the automatic-spacing clause is asserted.

visual page review verify the glyphs. Browser checks cover native glyphs,

## Completed merged cells across a moved row

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.84 (`vMerge`), 17.4.80 (`trHeight`), 17.4.6 (`cantSplit`)
and 17.18.37 (`ST_HeightRule`) define the merged rows and height constraints.
When a later row moves to a fresh page, a merged owner's already-finished text
has no remaining space demand. The page-dependent height calculation previously
interpreted an end on an earlier page as a positive forward interval, creating
an extra empty table page. It now returns zero for completed intervals. Actual
forward continuation, row minimums, exact clipping and page-story bounds retain
the existing behavior. There is no additional layout pass or font measurement.

Four independently authored controls in tests/fixtures/finished-merge-pagination
cover empty, short and long merged owners, with and without a footer. The native reference
renders each in two pages. The pre-fix empty-footer control produced
three app pages; after correction all page assignments and recorded text X/Y
origins match within 0.3pt, including all 26 continuing merged lines. Eight
native/app page pairs were visually inspected. This is an engine arithmetic
error, not a new reference/spec divergence.

Validation: 75 unit tests and nine browser scenarios pass, covering existing
merged cells, row minimum/exact heights, oversized merged overflow, row fragment
ends and empty table fragments, plus editing, caret hit testing, untouched parts,
exact undo and export/reopen. Source/control/export schema checks pass 207 XML

## Empty paragraph indentation in AutoFit cells

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.18.87 (`ST_TblLayoutType`), 17.3.1.12 (`ind`), 17.4.68
(`tcMar`) and 17.4.71 (`tcW`) govern AutoFit content demand and stored geometry.
Native controls show that a paragraph without content or a visible list marker
does not reserve its indents in intrinsic cell widths. The engine now skips
that empty demand while retaining cell padding, preferred widths, source
formatting and the normal demand from spaces, tabs, breaks and list markers.
The correction changes only intrinsic measurement, with no new layout pass.
The standard allows different AutoFit implementations and does not explicitly
prescribe empty-paragraph demand; no normative reference/spec contradiction is claimed.

hanging, combined indents, and space/tab/break/text content. All page pairs were
visually inspected. Nine cases match native shaded-cell edges within 0.6pt; the
tab case retains a separate preexisting width discrepancy (approximately 58pt
native versus 32pt app) and remains outside the fidelity assertion. Unit tests
explicitly retain demand from an empty bullet item with a visible marker.

Source 162's empty merged spacer contained a 27pt left indent. Removing only
empty-cell indents in a private Arial diagnostic leaves all three reference pages

restores the native column allocation without altering the source. The Arial
diagnostic's 41 matched lines have maximum X/Y errors below 0.11/0.20pt; the

passes 183 XML checks; 47 distinct unit tests and five browser scenarios pass.

## Conditional table cell alignment compatibility

ECMA-376-1 fifth edition §17.4.83 (`vAlign`) specifies vertical alignment within

demonstrate a compatibility-dependent divergence: in mode 15,
unconditional center/bottom cell alignment takes precedence over conditional
alignment. Unconditional top or absent alignment allows the conditional value.
Direct `tcPr/vAlign` continues to override both. Modes 12 and 14 use conditional
precedence. Import now carries the existing document compatibility mode into
conditional table resolution, including nested tables, and structural edits
retain it. No source XML declarations are rewritten to materialize inheritance.

## Repeated merged-cell AutoFit preferences

inferred share. AutoFit likewise prefers an explicit single-column request over
a merged-cell share when determining its content-aware target. The existing
content minima, width limits, overlapping-span solver and source XML remain

## Contextual spacing resets at physical table rows

ECMA-376-1 fifth edition §17.3.1.9 describes same-style contextual spacing;
§17.4.83 and §17.4.84 cover cell vertical alignment and merging. The native reference resets
the preceding-paragraph comparison at the first physical cell of each new row,
while still comparing adjacent cells within a row. The specification does not
spell out that physical-row boundary: this is a reference-specific interpretation,
established with independently authored XML controls rather than inferred from
one corpus document. It applies equally to unnumbered, directly numbered and
style-numbered paragraphs. Existing table-start and within-row behavior remains.

The layout now carries the row boundary into paragraph measurement. Empty
vertical-merge continuations also retain their final paragraph's style ID so
the next cell can compare against the physical preceding paragraph, even though
that continuation has no editable text. New merges use the default paragraph
style for their generated empty continuations; split and promotion operations
clear stale continuation metadata. Retained source XML is unchanged, and there
is no additional text-measurement or page-layout pass.

## Two-endpoint gradient interpolation

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.8.33 (`gradFill`) defines a gradual transition through
specified stops; §20.1.8.41 (`lin`) supplies the linear axis. The specification
text does not prescribe the native reference's color-easing curve. Independent original XML
controls establish that the native reference uses a gamma-corrected Gaussian cumulative
transition for exactly two opaque stops at 0 and 100 percent. Inset endpoints,
three-stop lists and transparent stops retain piecewise-linear interpolation.
This compatibility distinction is now implemented without changing the axis,
source stops, XML order, layout or export representation.

The normalized cumulative Gaussian integrates over [-2,2]; RGB channels mix with
a 2.2 gamma. The original implementation evaluates the integral with a convergent
series and supplies 256 Canvas stops. Shared curve weights and a weak cache of
per-fill paint stops keep this calculation out of repeated drawing paints; no
extra layout, text measurement, decoding or UI operation was introduced.

The independent coincident-positive-stop control also establishes that the native reference
extends the original final color to 100 percent, even when an earlier tied stop
owns the interior position. The painter now retains this implicit endpoint.
The original two source stops and their order remain unchanged in the package.

Native PDF functions provide the color reference. Rasterization of those PDFs
adds lookup quantization (also observable for three-stop gradients), so opaque
color assertions evaluate the actual exported PDF functions. Transparent samples
compare final native composites. A few native PDF samples immediately next to
black quantize to zero, while the smooth curve remains positive: the maximum
observed difference is eight channel levels in the first two of 255 intervals
for dark endpoint controls. This small endpoint precision gap remains recorded;
it is not a claim of universal pixel identity. The pink/orange source endpoints
do not exhibit that near-black case.

Validation: 42 unit tests and four browser scenarios pass. All 792 color samples
from the 24 original controls pass (maximum channel errors 1 for the color page
and 4 for the edge/transparency page); both full page pairs were inspected.
No-edit preservation, body editing, unchanged gradient XML/unrelated parts,
exact undo and export/reopen pass. Nineteen source/control/export packages pass
136 XML checks. Production build and the 199-package license gate pass, with
existing build warnings. Source 168's four-page rendering/editing review is now
complete; the Construction brochure retains RGB-identical pages and its full
workflow. Evidence: scratch `work/gradient-colors-*`, `template168-gradient-*`
and `construction-gradient-colors-*`. Remote CI is not established by local tests.

## Cell-ending contextual paragraph spacing

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.9 (`contextualSpacing`) describes suppression between
adjacent paragraphs with the same style, with §17.3.1.33 defining spacing.

contextual paragraph when its style is named Normal. Independent controls
separate the style name from its arbitrary ID, the document default and the
following body paragraph's style. This is a reference-specific extension of the
adjacent-paragraph rule: the clause does not describe an implicit Normal-style
cell boundary. The engine now implements that observed boundary behavior for
inline and floating cells, while retaining source spacing declarations and the
existing `allowSpaceOfSameStyleInTable` override. Style resolution carries the
resolved name so editing the paragraph style updates the decision.

visually inspected. The teal cells retain the previously identified automatic
text-color discrepancy (reference black, app white), outside this spacing change.

## AutoFit reduction outside growing merged spans

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.18.87 describes growing merged cells for minimum content,
then reducing other columns toward their minima; §§17.4.17, 17.4.63 and 17.4.71
provide span and preferred-width semantics. The former prefix-pinning step
satisfied a growing span mostly by shrinking its next neighbor. The engine now
preserves that span's feasible internal boundaries and redistributes the outside
width according to each column's room above its minimum, then checks overlapping
constraints again. When preferences already meet the constraints, the existing
single fitting pass remains. Saved grids/preferences and fixed layout are unchanged.
This implements the described reduction more closely; no normative reference/spec
divergence is established by this change.

The modern independent pressure/no-pressure controls now match all three cell
origins and widths within 0.2 pt. The reference set also contains unresolved
crossing-span internal allocation and legacy total-width cases; these are not
certified by the passing native comparison. Twenty-five targeted unit tests and
eight browser scenarios pass, covering existing cell preferences, repeated spans,
merged/nested tables, editing and export/reopen. One optional private birthday

## AutoFit automatic growth and legacy page-edge allowance

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.18.87 describes enlarging spanned columns for minimum content
before distributing widths; §§17.4.63 and 17.4.71 distinguish table and cell
preferences. The engine now derives an enlarged span preference before choosing
the automatic table total. Automatic tables retain that total when space permits;
declared totals remain the target, subject to content limits. A larger target
scales the growing span's preferred share as a whole, without assigning new
preferences to its internal columns. Outside reduction starts from original
column preferences instead of preferences already expanded for the target.

The legacy page allowance also accounts for the actual leading alignment inset:
a left table without an indent declaration keeps the grid at the writing edge
and gains only the trailing cell inset. A declared indent aligns its text edge;
center/right alignment retains the exterior inset allowance. This complements
§17.4.49 indentation and existing compatibility behavior; modern outer-edge
alignment stays intact. The guidance permits different algorithms, so no new
normative reference/spec contradiction is asserted. Original width XML is retained.

omitted/zero indent, symmetric/asymmetric margins, left/center/right alignment,
300/400 pt writing areas and legacy/modern compatibility. All 90 cell origins
and widths match within 0.35 pt, including native rounding, and the page-region
pairs were inspected. Wider pages are essential evidence: they distinguish
actual preferred-grid growth from a result accidentally capped at the page edge.
The separate crossing-span internal-allocation gap remains open. Its eight
observed internal boundaries retain their pre-change positions; those positions
are not asserted to match the native reference.

## Floating drawings on otherwise blank lines

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.4.2.3 distinguishes floating anchors from inline objects
that affect the text line's height. Paragraph spacing (§17.3.1.33), paragraph
mark formatting (§17.3.1.29), text (§17.3.3.31) and tabs (§17.3.3.32) do not give
an explicit formula for the height of a whitespace-only line with an anchor.
The installed reference uses the paragraph mark's metrics for ordinary
spaces/tabs even when a floating drawing is anchored on that line. This is a
reference-derived layout detail consistent with floating positioning, not a proven
contradiction of a normative height formula.

The existing blank-line rule now ignores positioned drawing fragments when
deciding whether whitespace takes the mark height. NBSP, thin spaces and
visible text retain their existing font-height contribution. Inline pictures,
numbering markers and tab leaders retain their distinct rules; caret advances,
run formatting, picture positioning and OPC serialization are unchanged.

Independent floating-blank-lines controls contain sixteen reference pages comparing
plain and floating-picture paragraphs, eight text/whitespace cases and 10 pt
marks against 24 pt runs. All 52 text lines match within 0.111 pt vertically;
browser tests assert Before/After baselines within 0.15 pt. The fixture source
and native PDF are hash-pinned. The edit regression changes a floating line's
space to NBSP, verifies increased height and reopened text, preserves unrelated
parts, then verifies exact undo. All control page pairs were visually reviewed.

## DrawingML hexagon preset

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.9.18 (`prstGeom`), 20.1.9.11 (`gd`), 20.1.10.56
(`ST_ShapeType`) and the supplied `presetShapeDefinitions.xml` define hexagon
geometry. The scene reader now resolves `adj=25000` and `vf=115470` defaults
with named overrides. Horizontal depth scales with the shorter side and clamps
at half the width. The vertical factor sets the upper/lower vertices through
the standard sine guide. The two branches of the prescribed text rectangle
are retained. Existing scene transformations and paint handle rotations, flips,
fills, outlines and grouped photos; no layout or paint pass is added.

The native reference has a separate adjustment-list import restriction: it opens an
empty list or an ordered `adj`, `vf` pair but rejects `adj` alone or the reversed
pair. Four original minimal DOCX controls, source hashes and native open results
are committed under hexagon-shapes. All four pass the XML schemas. The importer
follows the named standard defaults rather than reproducing the native reference's rejection;
original markup remains preserved, including forms the native reference cannot open. This
compatibility discrepancy is explicitly recorded, not treated as a reason to
discard valid geometry or silently rewrite source adjustments.

## Modern justified-line contraction

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.1.13 (`jc`) and 17.18.44 (`ST_Jc`) describe inter-word
justification but do not specify the native reference's numerical line-fitting algorithm.
Original mode-14/mode-15 controls establish the following native reference
compatibility behavior. Ordinary proportional-font spaces can contract by
at most 25%, including on final and manual-break lines. NBSP and fixed-pitch
spaces do not contract. `doNotExpandShiftReturn` does not disable contraction.

There is also a choice between expanding the shorter line and contracting the
line with its next word. Let D be the new line's overflow, S its total eligible
natural space width, E the shorter line's spare width, and P its eligible space
width. The native reference accepts contraction when D/S <= 1/4 and 2D/S <= E/P (the second
condition is vacuous without a prior space). Differently sized spaces receive
proportional adjustments. Twenty-two boundary pages distinguish this from a
blanket line-width percentage, including equal-width text with differing last
words. This is observed compatibility behavior, not an OOXML-mandated constant.

The layout fitter applies this rule in compatibility mode 15 and later for
ordinary text lines. It only looks ahead on natural overflow and stops at the
maximum contraction bound. Font geometry is cached within the paragraph;
fixed-pitch detection uses advances rather than family-name special cases.
Negative spacing remains display-only and feeds the same fragment/caret/
decoration geometry as expansion. Separate leading fragments receive signed
native-spacing correction. Finite-precision correction remeasures the line
rather than weakening cell bounds. Nonbreaking whitespace retains its break
semantics. Tab fields and discretionary-hyphen alternatives keep the previous
line fitter; extended contraction in those contexts is still pending.

Eight independently authored packages contain 197 native pages covering the
rule, compatibility modes, fonts, mixed space sizes, consecutive spaces,
equivalent joined runs, NBSP and manual breaks. All line breaks match; negative
fragment widths agree with native Canvas measurement. The three formerly
expected-failing justified-line-fit assertions now pass normally. Corpus #180
matches all 60 native text lines within 0.080 pt horizontally and 0.214 pt
vertically; all four page pairs and edit/export/undo behavior were checked.
Construction remains unchanged on both pages with its full workflow passing.
Evidence: tests/fixtures/justification-contraction and scratch
work/justify-balance-*, template180-contraction2-*, construction-contraction-*.

the final whitespace-boundary correction), 146 XML checks across 18 packages,
production build and the 199-package license gate pass. The build retains its
existing chunk-size warnings. These are local checks, not a remote CI claim.

## Section vertical alignment

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.6.23 (`vAlign`) and 17.18.101 (`ST_VerticalJc`) define
top/center/bottom/both positioning between the section's main-story margins.
The importer validates and preserves these values; the model and serializer
support single-section changes and fresh output. Existing multi-section page
setup restrictions remain. Invalid, missing, duplicated or extended declarations
are rejected rather than silently normalized.

The body is aligned after page wrapping converges. Center and bottom shift the
occupied block including paragraph spacing. Both adds gaps between paragraphs
and treats an inline table as one block; manual lines within one paragraph do
not gain gaps. Cell clips, caret baselines, floating frames and border geometry
follow the resulting positions. Top-aligned documents retain the existing fast
path. Continuous-section and multi-column combinations remain explicitly
unsupported until their distinct page-balancing behavior is established.

The native reference diverges from the ST_VerticalJc instruction to ignore `both`
when a document ends mid-page. The independently authored final-page case
distributes three paragraphs from baseline 86.42 pt through 716.52 pt. The
renderer reproduces that behavior. This is an observed reference compatibility
choice, not a claim that the standard mandates it.

Floating-table controls establish two additional interactions. First,
page-positioned tables exclude preceding text as well as text after their
anchor; the prior forward-only exclusion was incorrect. Text-relative and
nested-table exclusions retain their anchor scopes. Second, center/bottom
alignment also shifts page-positioned tables after their wrapping is resolved.
For both alignment, page-positioned tables stay fixed and text-positioned tables
move with their following anchor paragraph. This ordering avoids centering an
anchor first and spuriously forcing its table onto multiple pages.

Two original packages contain 37 native pages. All text origins match within
0.15 pt vertically. Corpus #181 advances past vertical alignment but still
requires `tblOverlap` support and a typography review; a diagnostic source
without that property is not counted as completion. Evidence:
tests/fixtures/page-vertical-alignment and scratch work/page-vertical-*,
template181-*, construction-page-vertical-* and template180-page-vertical-*.

Schema validation passes 224 XML checks across 29 source/export paths. Production
build and the 199-package license gate pass. Construction's two pages and

## Floating-table collision prevention

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.4.56 (tblOverlap) and 17.18.88 (ST_TblOverlap)
allow overlapping by default and require collision avoidance when either table
sets never. Inline tables ignore the property. The importer validates the enum,
shape and attributes and retains the declaration through table editing/export.
The layout pass positions colliding top-level tables in source order, first to
the right and then below when the available horizontal area is exhausted.
Native reference controls establish the facing clearances and minimum frame gaps.
A new vertical level can revisit a taller obstacle; the bounded search allows
that rescan. Displacement moves cell/text clipping, caret stops, selection
segments, paragraph decoration and cell boxes together without changing the
OOXML coordinates. Documents without collision-prevention settings retain the
existing placement path without scanning preceding tables for collisions.

The independently authored table-overlap fixtures contain 38 native reference pages.
The three anchor types, either/both overlap declarations, four widths, symmetric
clearances and one-sided clearance minimums are covered. Tables match native
text origins within 0.35 pt horizontally and 0.2 pt vertically. This is not an
exact-pixel claim. The initially failing body-word wrapping assertion on the last width control
is resolved by the follow-up below; all text on that page is now checked. Nested collision prevention and
collision-driven migration past the physical page remain explicitly unsupported.
The standard requires prevention but does not prescribe the displacement
algorithm; these controls establish native reference compatibility rather than a proven
normative divergence. See tests/fixtures/table-overlap/README.md.

## Intact words beside wrapping obstacles

Within the floating-table/wrapping scopes of ECMA-376 sections 17.4.57 and
20.4.2.17, native reference controls establish that an empty line clears an obstacle
when none of its side intervals can hold the next unbroken word. This is not
a fixed minimum text width: short words use the same interval that a longer
word skips. Even a word wider than the full paragraph clears the obstacle first
and then uses ordinary character breaking. The renderer now requests the first
vertical interval wide enough for the word, capped at the full paragraph width
so oversized words still terminate. Existing usable later intervals and rows
that already contain text retain their established handling. The extra word
measurement applies only when a wrapping obstacle narrows an otherwise empty
line that would force an emergency character break.

Eight independently authored Arial control pages in table-overlap/words.docx
prove the width/word-length distinction. All text origins match the native reference within
0.18 pt horizontally and 0.06 pt vertically. The former expected-failure
assertion is now a normal passing assertion, and the original collision suite
checks all body text again. This establishes native reference behavior; no contradictory
normative statement has been identified. See narrow_table_words_fixture.py
and the retained native PDF/source hashes. Generator reproduction matches all
uncompressed source package parts exactly.

## EMF Dual playback and record-local text clipping

The EMF reader now recognizes structurally valid EMF+ Dual envelopes and plays
only the complete standard EMF representation. This follows
[MS-EMFPLUS §1.3.1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-emfplus/8b9363ba-cf5b-4d35-bced-0620e3b5b5ef)
and the Dual flag in
[§3.2.2.1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-emfplus/10f336a0-5f7c-4ee2-ab89-5329af0720c7).
It checks record lengths, header placement, duplicate/missing terminal records
and a bounded EMF+ record count. EMF+ Only streams still require unsupported
EMF+ rendering and remain read-only; their alternate artwork is not discarded.
Ordinary EMF streams do not acquire an additional record scan.

EMR_EXTTEXTOUTW accepts ETO_CLIPPED alongside ETO_PDY. The logical rectangle
is transformed through the current world/window/viewport matrix and intersects
existing clipping for this text record only. It is not retained in the device
context or applied to the following text. Empty rectangles produce no ink;
inverted rectangles remain unsupported. See
[MS-EMF §2.2.5](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-emf/dd585d0a-5d7c-4034-963a-1141af836972)
and [§2.1.11](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-emf/e7ffcc53-40d1-4873-8eda-c5c5ee104aa5).
Logical-font dimensions are checked when nonempty text actually uses the font:
creating/selecting an unused font after the final drawing no longer rejects an
otherwise supported picture. Drawn unsupported dimensions still reject safely.

Eight independently generated DOCX/EMF controls and a retained reference
PDF are in tests/fixtures/emf-dual-clip. The full native/browser page pair was
visually inspected. Sixteen raster regions check clipped ink, empty output and
subsequent unclipped lines; bounds stay within 0.8 pt and ink within 6% of the native reference.
There is no observed reference/spec divergence in this subset. Final validation:

frame controls, 177 XML checks across 25 package paths, and production build

signed or zero-padded IDs retain their spelling unless actually reassigned.

transactions establish that a restored name relocates a colliding document
bookmark. Reusing a prompt moves its bookmark to the later restored control.

restores them again. This is observed editing compatibility behavior, not a
claimed contradiction of a normative OOXML editing algorithm. Both direct
editing and full-prompt search replacement support restoration/removal, with

### Paragraph spacing and top-edge clearance at floating tables

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.1.33 (`spacing`) and 17.4.57 (`tblpPr`) define paragraph
spacing and table positioning, including the following regular paragraph as the
logical anchor. Independent reference controls establish two interactions
not explicitly specified as an algorithm in those clauses: after a paragraph's
first line clears a floating table, its own space-before still separates text
from the table; and a body line ending exactly at a floating table's top edge
is displaced, while a one-twip separation permits it to remain above. These are
recorded compatibility rules, not a demonstrated normative contradiction.

The square-wrap exclusion model now distinguishes tables from pictures and
retains that before-spacing after clearance. Following-paragraph spacing remains
collapsed normally; continuation lines and lines that fit beside a table gain
no extra gap. Nested floating tables retain strict top-edge overlap, proven by
the existing eighteen-page native nested-table controls. A browser regression
caught that distinction before the change was committed. Picture boundaries
and the stored paragraph/table declarations are unchanged.

The original floating-table-spacing fixture has fifty pages and 182 native
baselines: blank/text anchors, 0/2/6 pt before-spacing, 0/4/10 pt preceding
after-spacing, 0/3 pt borders, text/page/margin anchors, narrow tables and the
exact/one-twip-separated top-edge boundary. It reproduces the original missing
space-before and up to 87 pt of displacement from a missed top-edge collision.
All recorded baselines match the corrected browser layout within 0.11 pt.
The source generator, native PDF, coordinate recorder and bound hashes are
retained; no corpus artwork or new dependency is included.

Active RTL/cs DOCX import/editing remains guarded: Arabic ligature caret
positions still need native context measurement; pointer affinity, visual arrow
navigation, directional small-caps parts, decoration/clipping edge cases,
explicit Unicode controls and full OOXML embedding/paragraph direction need
further verification. Contextual numeric font selection is also unresolved.
Initial prefix-derived RTL carets must not be represented as full shaping-aware
editing support. No corpus template is promoted by these component results.
Performance note for that future activation: inspect repeated stop filtering
on heavily fragmented bidi lines; no speculative optimization was introduced.

### Context-shaped RTL carets (2026-09-22)

The RTL layout component now requests caret advances from the complete shaped
fragment instead of subtracting reshaped prefix widths. A hidden browser range
uses the Canvas font, direction, kerning and spacing; its advances are normalized
to the measured Canvas width. This allocates lam/alef insertion positions within
the ligature and preserves contextual Arabic joining. The request runs once at
fragment completion, never on each prefix or on ordinary unmarked text. Temporary
DOM nodes are removed in a finally block. Source UTF-16 offsets map separately
to shaped-text indices so removed discretionary soft hyphens do not shift later
carets. Text transforms scale these advances with glyph geometry.

Original bidi-layout controls now include native collapsed reference range positions
from tools/record-bidi-carets.ps1, tied to the same source hash. Twenty-three
interior Hebrew/Arabic positions match within the .5pt allowance for the native reference's
.75pt screen rounding (observed maximum .4275pt); hit tests return their source
offsets and the first lam/alef selection uses half the ligature advance. The
three page rasters remain unchanged. These are interaction geometry checks,
not new OOXML serialization semantics or a reference/spec divergence.

The active DOCX guard remains: run-boundary affinity, visual arrow navigation,
small-caps/multiple-font parts, contextual color/decorations and script font
selection still need independent verification. Full RTL editing is not claimed.

### RTL numeric face selection: reference/spec divergence (2026-09-22)

Part 1 §§17.3.2.26 and 17.3.2.30 describe cs-face selection for rtl text; the
published MS-OI29500 rFonts note also says it is unconditional. The independent
rtl-font-context fixture disproves that description in the native reference: weak
ASCII numbers in an explicit RTL run can use the ordinary ASCII face while
retaining bCs/iCs/szCs. The pure-number controls avoid the standard's unspecified
strong-LTR/rtl combination. Cs-only uses cs; combined cs/rtl follows the RTL
numeric behavior. The fixture README links the published note and details the
native evidence. This is explicitly implemented as native reference compatibility.

The original classifier finds numeric groups using Unicode bidi classes,
including internal separators and adjacent terminators. ASCII groups outside
preceding Latin context use the declared ASCII face; non-ASCII numeric groups
keep the complex-script face. Strong Hebrew/Arabic text and tabs reset context;
color-only run boundaries do not. Slash-separated numbers are separate visual
groups under native RTL handling. This is not a per-digit, font-name or source
document exception. Font declarations, cs size/weight and source text remain
unchanged. Ordinary unmarked layout is unaffected.

Fifty-one original cases on eight pages verify fonts, weight, line positions,
ordering, tabs and split colors using the real CanvasEditor on an internal
read-only model. All page pairs were inspected; maximum measured suffix-origin
difference is .152pt and baseline difference .070pt. Active RTL/cs import/editing
is still guarded. Default/missing CS fonts, missing-glyph italic fallback,
complete explicit-control semantics and visual keyboard/boundary affinity need
further implementation and verification. No completed-template claim follows
from these component results.


### Read-only complex-script import

Read-only DOCX style resolution now retains active `w:rtl` and `w:cs` run and
paragraph-mark declarations instead of replacing their enclosing paragraph or
table with plain preview text. It uses the same inherited/direct formatting
cascade and the rendering rules described above (Part 1 sections 17.3.2.30 and
17.3.2.7). Initial display-model validation explicitly permits those two flags;
strict import and mutation validation still reject active script editing.
Hidden text, malformed sizes and other unsupported properties retain their
existing fallbacks. Read-only page-story validation uses the already resolved
imported styles, consistently with the editor's display path.

The original rtl-font-context DOCX now passes through openCanvasDocument and
CanvasEditor for all 51 native comparisons. Its eight imported rasters are
RGB-identical to the independently constructed internal controls. Additional
import tests cover the four script fixtures and an enclosing table. A browser
workflow verifies blocked typing and preservation of every original ZIP part
on download. These checks establish display integration, not complete bidi
editing, explicit-control, missing-font or fallback conformance.


### Minimum single DrawingML outline pen

The native reference paints explicit single-outline widths from zero through 1778
EMU at .14pt; 1779 EMU and larger retain their specified widths. Original
rectangle/ellipse and picture-path controls establish the boundary from native
PDF graphics-state pen operators. Part 1 section 20.1.2.2.24 and ST_LineWidth
(20.1.10.35) specify the declared width but not this floor, so this is explicit
reference compatibility. The original declaration is preserved separately from
physical paint/bounds and remains the input to text insets/autofit and picture
centerline offsets. A zero-width native picture control proves that its
centerline remains at the declared frame while the .14pt pen extends beyond it.
Source XML,
omitted-width behavior, compound pens and noFill remain unchanged. Zero-width
compound pens remain guarded. No source-specific rule or raster-size increase
is involved. Thin-curve Canvas antialiasing differences remain open.

### Physical side borders in vertical merges

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.4.66 (tcBorders) and 17.4.84 (vMerge) define
per-cell edges and membership in a vertical merge. Native reference
controls establish that side-border ownership stays with each physical row:
a continuation with no border does not inherit the restart cell's side ink.
The opposite cell's explicit/inherited border still participates in normal
conflict resolution. The original six-page merged-side-borders control covers
restart-only ink, a middle gap, continuation-only ink, nil/none with inherited
table ink, and a direct opposing border. Source/PDF hashes and native pixel
samples accompany editing/export/undo/reopen regressions.

The existing row-exception side-segment path now applies to every vertical
merge. Pagination clips those segments to each cell fragment before border
conflict resolution. Horizontal border ownership, text layout and source XML
are unchanged. This records the native reference's physical-side behavior without a
source-specific exception or a change to declared border width.

### Automatic leading with shifted inline text and pictures

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.3.1.33 (spacing), 17.3.2.24 (position), and 20.4.2.8
(inline) define the source declarations. The native reference's mixed-content
spacing rule uses the unshifted text/mark font height for automatic leading,
while the natural line box retains the shifted text and picture extents.
Below one-line spacing, the compressed baseline share is the spacing font
height minus the full line descent, including a lowered inline picture.
That share can be negative; clamping it to zero misplaces compressed content.
This is an explicitly recorded native reference compatibility detail beyond the standard's
general line-spacing description.

The original 28-page shifted-inline-leading control crosses seven positive,
negative and independent text/image shift combinations with 0.8, 1, 1.2 and 2
line multiples. Native text origins and image bounds are recorded independently
with source/PDF hashes. The layout change applies to mixed text/inline-picture
leading; image dimensions, stored run shifts and natural allocation remain
intact. Existing image-only, text-only, exact and minimum rules are retained.

### Corner preset geometry: octagon, plaque and rounded rectangle

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 20.1.9.18, 20.1.9.11 and 20.1.10.56, together with
its supplied presetShapeDefinitions.xml, define these three presets. Their
single adj guide defaults to 29289 for octagon and 16667 for plaque/roundRect,
clamps to 0..50000, and scales with the shorter side. Text insets are half the
corner depth, 0.70711 times depth, and 0.29289 times depth respectively.

The original scene reader implements the eight octagon edges and the concave
plaque/convex roundRect quarter circles. Two cubic segments per quarter circle
bound radial approximation error below 0.000005 of the radius while retaining
the established canvas, clipping and compound-outline paths. Rotation, flips,
fills and picture fills use the existing scene pipeline; source XML is retained.
Independent native controls cover defaults, zero/intermediate/near-maximum,
negative/excessive adjustments, conflicting inner bounds and rotated/flipped geometry,
plus three text rectangles for each preset. No corpus-specific offsets apply.

The conflicting-size controls additionally establish the native reference's standalone preset
frame precedence: a 200x90pt wp:extent with an 80x110pt a:xfrm/a:ext evaluates
the preset at 200x90pt. The root preset now uses its WordprocessingML frame for
geometry evaluation. Group children retain their local transforms, custom
paths retain their existing sizing, and zero-extent lines retain their special
handling. This reference compatibility detail is demonstrated by all three native
controls; it does not alter the preserved source declarations.

### Outer shadows on pictures inside drawing groups

ECMA-376 Part 1 section 20.1.8.45 (outerShdw) and CT_OuterShadowEffect govern
these declarations. Grouped picture effects are validated by the containing
scene before the synthetic texture-only input removes effectLst. Previously,
the nested reader wrapped an ordinary shadow as a retained drawing, triggering
an unrelated grouped-3D rejection and discarding the whole picture group.

A grouped picture now retains the shadow beside its texture, clipping paths,
backing fill and outline. The existing shadow compositor paints that complete
surface once. Bounds use the actual picture geometry and physical pen; shadow
direction follows its rotation/reflection only when rotWithShape is active.
Ancestor transforms affect geometry, while physical blur and offset remain
unscaled. Page-relative resizing uses the current picture frame for shadow
bounds. No source XML is rewritten and unsupported effects remain guarded.

Fourteen independent native controls cover nested scaling, picture/group
rotation, reflection, elliptical clipping, outlines, backing fill, texture
alpha, crop outsets, blur and hard directional shadows. Scaled, skewed and
obscured grouped-picture shadows and grouped 3D pictures remain unsupported.
These controls do not certify exact texture reconstruction at sharp edges;
interior colors and independent painted bounds have separate checks.

### w14 text shadows

MS-DOCX sections [2.6.1.23, shadow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-docx/310ab143-02d4-4f02-a369-dc469848cf6d)
and [2.6.3.30, CT_Shadow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-docx/5bd6d3ec-51d3-4b92-bfae-0c49b6c24984)
define this run-property extension. The model retains distance, direction,
blur, scale, skew, alignment and resolved RGB/alpha; the retained OPC properties
preserve theme declarations and color transforms. Missing scale attributes are
zero, as specified. Native controls confirm that default. Explicit editing
serializes qualified attributes and declares MCE compatibility. Zero-distance,
zero-scale transparent shadows provide a neutral explicit override of inherited
effects. Legacy w:shadow is a separate feature and is not added here.

Native reference compatibility behavior beyond the attribute descriptions is established
by 156 original native pages in tests/fixtures/text-shadow-line-metrics:
distance and blur are scaled by (floor(font size in points)/72)^0.7. Shadows
expand automatic line ascent/descent; a shadow only on the paragraph mark does
not expand these text-bearing controls. Fully transparent run shadows still
expand layout. For vertical skew, the native reference's allocation box has a width twice the
font ascent, independent of the string's width. This is not a literal unscaled
EMU offset; retain the authored values rather than rewriting them to rendered
distances. This compatibility behavior is an empirical addition to the spec's
attribute semantics, not a document-specific correction.

The line builder keeps shaping/carets across shadow paint boundaries. Hard
rigid shadows paint native glyphs at the displaced baseline. Other transforms
and blur use an isolated glyph mask; source run windows are clipped before
the effect so shadows can extend beyond a formatting boundary. Outline and
fill share the mask, and shadows paint before the original glyphs. Ordinary
text retains the existing measurement and painting paths.

The native layout oracle covers Corbel, Rockwell and Arial, integer/fractional
sizes through 144 pt, direction, distance, blur, scale/reflection, skew,
alignment, transparency, defaults and paragraph-mark/run distinctions. A
separate paint oracle checks 128 gray interior samples from hard directional
shadows, excluding two display pixels around edges. Exact raster identity is
not claimed. Detailed native paint conformance for blurred and transformed
glyph masks, and interactions with script scaling, decorative underlines and
nonautomatic spacing remain follow-up work; layout evidence alone does not
certify those paint cases.

## Ordinary trailing spaces in aligned tab fields

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.1.37–38 (`tab`, `tabs`) and §17.3.3.32
(inline `tab`) define tab-stop placement and alignment. The local fifth-edition
Part 1 custom-stop definition was reviewed at PDF page 263. The native reference's treatment
of trailing ordinary spaces is recorded as a compatibility detail: center and
right tab fields align their content excluding such tails, even before another
tab, before a manual break, and across formatting runs. NBSP retains its width.
This corrects the earlier declared policy of using complete ordinary field widths.

The line builder now uses its existing content width for center/right alignment,
as positional tabs already did. Stored text, fragment widths, caret advances,
selection and export retain the spaces; replacing one with visible text makes
it participate in alignment again. Left tabs and decimal-number/suffix rules
are unchanged. No additional measurements, dependencies or caches are added.

Independent controls in `tests/fixtures/aligned-tab-tails` provide fourteen
reference origins spanning both alignments and seven tails. Native-font browser
checks and portable caret/edit/undo tests cover this behavior. Corpus #232
exposed it as a roughly 2.4 pt displacement of prices ending with a space.

### Tables and symbols inside retained drawing text

ECMA-376 Part 1 WordprocessingDrawing `CT_TxbxContent` references
`w:EG_BlockLevelElts`, which includes tables as well as paragraphs. The local
strict schema was checked directly. WPS `wps:txbx/w:txbxContent` uses the
WordprocessingML story model (MS-ODRAWXML WPS schema). Part 1 section 17.4
governs the table model; section 17.3.3.30 governs explicit-font symbols.

The scene reader now uses the existing block/table/style readers for tables
inside a text box. Its paragraphs and tables remain local to the retained
scene; body table indices, editable positions and serialization do not acquire
those cells. Layout reuses the body table engine, with the source compatibility
mode, and composes the shape's physical text frame, group scaling, vertical
anchoring and overflow clip. Cell fills and resolved borders are painted inside
that frame. High-quality bitmap reduction is requested only for these new table
drawings so quarter-point rules retain area coverage at fractional placement.
The existing path for drawings without tables is unchanged.

Within retained drawing text, `w:sym` supplies a validated four-digit character
code and explicit font, overriding the surrounding run's font for that symbol
only. The original drawing XML, including controls and symbols, remains atomic
through unrelated body edits. Editable main-story `w:sym` is covered by the
body-symbol implementation below. Independent direct/PUA
Wingdings and Arial controls confirm the observed font mappings. The native reference displays
Arial F041 as a missing glyph, despite section 17.3.3.30's legacy F000-offset
example; do not blindly subtract F000 for every font. The independent control
preserves that native behavior. Unrotated/unreflected `upright=1` text is also
accepted: there is no rotation to cancel. Rotated and reflected group text now
have independent native controls described below. Upright vertically reflected
individual shapes remain guarded.

Existing unsupported text-box content remains guarded (including floating
tables, lists, links, floating drawings, decorated paragraphs/runs and active
tabs). An unsupported nested block is never silently flattened inside an
otherwise editable drawing. Standard cells, merges, shading, borders and
nested tables reuse the validated table reader.

### Main-story font-specific symbols

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.3.30 (`sym`) supplies a font and a four-digit character
code independently of `rFonts`. Main-story symbols now retain that pair as
immutable glyph metadata at one document position. Rendering and AutoFit use
the explicit symbol font while the ordinary run properties remain available
for formatting and adjacent typing. Export writes `w:sym`; original downloads,
unrelated package parts and exact undo retain their established guarantees.
Malformed declarations, control codes below 0020 and surrogate code units stay
guarded. Header/footer symbols and otherwise unsupported content controls are
not enabled by this change.

The fourteen original `body-symbols` controls and native reference edit recording
establish that caps/small caps do not case-convert or shrink the encoded glyph.
Changing the surrounding font, bold formatting or clearing direct formatting
retains the symbol pair. Replacement/deletion removes the symbol; insertion
uses the underlying run font. Plain-text clipboard output carries the encoded
character without font metadata, consistent with the existing plain-text-only
clipboard. Symbol atoms are not plain-text search terms.

Native glyph advances and line baselines are checked separately from an open
Arial label-spacing difference in C11 (0.944pt at the final R origin). This
does not establish full surrounding-text shaping fidelity. The new controls
also confirm the existing reference/font-mapping divergence for Arial F041 rather
than applying a universal F000 subtraction. No font files were redistributed.

Independent controls and native references: `tests/fixtures/shape-tables`,
`tools/shape_table_fixture.py`, and `tools/shape_table_reference.py`. The former nested-table origin gap is resolved by the paired story controls
described below; all native origins are asserted. This supported subset is not
a complete text-box-table conformance claim.

### Placeable WMF filled vectors

The original WMF reader implements MS-WMF placeable/header records, Polygon
(2.3.3.15), solid/null brushes and pen selection (2.3.4), anisotropic window
mapping, polygon fill rules and saved DC state (2.3.5), and lowest-free object
indices (3.1.4.1). DrawingML blips retain their image relationships and original
bytes (ECMA-376 Part 1, 20.1.8.13); `image/wmf` and `image/x-wmf` are accepted.
The browser decodes generated numeric SVG in an isolated image context and
applies the existing crop, reflection and picture-effects pipeline.

Independent eight-panel native controls are in `tests/fixtures/wmf-vectors`.
They prove implicit anisotropic embedding context (MS-WMF 3.1.3), negative window
extents/nonzero origins, even-odd/nonzero filling and the native reference's tolerance of one
additional trailing WORD in a CreatePenIndirect record. MS-WMF 2.3.4.5 declares
a ten-byte pen payload; both standard and padded encodings remain preserved.
See the fixture README for native evidence and reproduction commands.

This initial subset draws null-pen polygons. Visible pen strokes, non-placeable
metafiles, other mapping modes, bitmap/text/region/escape records and other
unimplemented operations reject before editable import. Unsupported records
are not skipped. Size, checksum, record bounds, object indices, EOF, dimensions,
geometry and generated output are checked. This WMF iteration did not remove
the separate floating-rotation guard; that placement is added below. The separate nested text-box table placement discrepancy is addressed below.

### Unwrapped floating-picture rotation

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.7.6 (`xfrm`), §20.1.10.3 (`ST_Angle`) and
Annex L.4.7.3 define the center-based transform and crop/flip/rotation order.
`wp:anchor` (§20.4.2.3), `effectExtent` (§20.4.2.6) and `extent`
(§20.4.2.7) keep the physical picture frame separate from extra layout space.
Standalone `wrapNone` pictures now rotate clockwise about the resolved frame
center, after cropping and reflection. Page/cell clips stay outside the picture
transform. Selection painting rotates with the picture; hit testing applies
the inverse transform, and selection bounds include the entire rotated frame.
Unrotated geometry retains its existing comparisons and avoids trigonometry.

Independent reference controls in `tests/fixtures/floating-picture-rotation` confirm
that floating pictures still paint beyond zero/asymmetric effect extents. The
previous inline reservation guard incorrectly rejected them. Inline validation
is unchanged; no new reference/spec divergence is asserted. Signed and multi-turn
source values survive untouched export, while geometry edits use the existing
normalized angle and extent serialization. Original media/relationships remain
untouched, and body editing, geometry edits and exact undo are tested.

The native fixture covers eighteen page-offset pictures with rotations, flips,
crops and opacity. Its README records the PDF rasterizer cross-check and the
limits of the native comparison. Text-wrapped rotation, nonrotating fills and
other existing unsupported geometry combinations remain guarded. The new
controls do not certify every rotated collision or relative-size/alignment
combination. Corpus #240 now imports as editable with its scissors visible;
the independent text-box nested-table origin discrepancy is addressed below.

### Nested table origins in WPS cells

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.68 (`tcMar`), §17.4.41–42 (`tblCellMar`),
§17.4.50 (`tblInd`), §17.4.28 (`jc`), and §17.4.87 (table measurements)
govern cell margins and table geometry. The native reference's WPS story applies an additional
placement behavior not expressly stated by those ordinary margin clauses:
in-flow nested tables use the parent cell's leading inner border edge as their
origin, while retaining the padded available width for percentage sizing and
alignment. Their own cell margins are unchanged. Main-story placement remains
unchanged. This is recorded as a reference compatibility exception to uniformly
padded placement, not a claim that ordinary text margins violate the standard.

Sixteen manually constructed paired body/WPS controls in
`tests/fixtures/nested-shape-tables` cover margins, borders, indent, percentage
width, and center/right alignment. All 96 native marker origins are checked;
the earlier shape-tables control also includes its formerly excluded labels.
Layout changes only derived geometry. Drawing XML and unrelated package parts
remain preserved through body editing and exact undo. Floating nested tables
inside WPS remain guarded; unsupported bidirectional modes are not newly enabled.

### W14 text-fill transparency

MS-DOCX CT_FillTextEffect, CT_SchemeColor/CT_SRgbColor and
CT_PositiveFixedPercentage govern solid text-fill color transforms. Although
[CT_SchemeColor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-docx/133bd2fe-ad4c-4422-a120-9c3a1a3a4e30)
describes alpha as opacity, independent reference controls demonstrate
transparency semantics for W14 text fills. Zero is opaque and 100000 is clear;
the native reference rounds transparency to a byte before inversion. Repeated alpha uses the
last value. Luminance transforms retain their existing ordered color arithmetic.
DrawingML alpha interpretation is unchanged.

Twelve paired body/WPS pages in tests/fixtures/text-fill-alpha establish endpoint,
near-endpoint, fractional, repeated-transform and theme/luminance behavior on
different backgrounds. Import resolves RRGGBBAA strings for the existing Canvas
fill path; original transform XML remains untouched. Explicit fill edits emit
six-digit srgbClr and a bounded integer alpha reproducing that byte. Plain
foreground edits, no-edit export and undo preserve the existing package. Source
srgbClr still requires exactly six digits; invalid alpha remains guarded.
Gradients and other unsupported transforms remain guarded. See the fixture
README for reference extraction and native comparison limits.


## Small/medium-gap compound borders

Paragraph and table borders support `thinThickSmallGap`, `thickThinSmallGap`,
`thinThickMediumGap` and `thickThinMediumGap` (ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.18.2), through the existing
CT_Border import, style resolution, editing and export paths. Shared edges use
the MS-OI29500-documented conflict weights 11, 12, 14 and 15 respectively (MS-OI29500
§2.1.169). No document identifiers or template-specific fallbacks are used.

Original OPC/XML controls in `tests/fixtures/compound-border-variants` retain
42 native reference pages: seven sizes, both frame values, paired paragraph/table borders
and all four edges. The first two styles have fixed 0.72 pt gap/thin bands;
the medium-gap variant uses independently quantized half-width bands. Native
widths are floored to 0.12 pt units, with a one-unit minimum. See the fixture
README and recorded PDF paths for observations and source/PDF hashes.

These styles use two ink bands. This implements the MS-OI29500-documented correction
to the thinThickSmallGap description in §17.18.2 (MS-OI29500 §2.1.528).
Frame reverses bottom/right paragraph bands and the table's straight vertical
body bands, preserving the existing corner cap behavior. New compound
paragraph corners connect corresponding bands with rectangular joins.
The browser comparison checks ink away from raster boundaries at all four
corners for all 84 paragraph/table cases. This does not certify arbitrary
mixed-pattern paragraph joins or every frame-positioning case; those remain
outside the independent controls' coverage.

The reverse medium-gap style has fourteen additional independent native pages
under `tests/fixtures/thin-thick-medium`, generated/recorded with the same tools'
`--medium-reverse` option. Its band order is full width, half-width gap,
half-width ink, with the same independent quantization and frame/corner rules.
Paragraph/cell border editing, exact undo, package preservation and browser
export/reopen are covered. Part 1's printed page 1342 contains duplicated prose
for this enum; the two-band diagram agrees with the native reference. This implementation follows
that diagram and native evidence rather than inferring a third band from the
duplicated phrase. No new rendering divergence is claimed for this variant.

Complementary thin/thick order now joins outer/inner bands at equal-size
corners within each small/medium gap family. Different enum names do not by
themselves make those two edges unrelated patterns. The 64 original pages in
`tests/fixtures/mixed-compound-borders` cover all sixteen side-order combinations
for both frame values and both families, with independently colored sides.
The reference recorder verifies rectangular PDF paths and retains their color
and paint order. All 128 paragraph/table cases match the native reference's corner ink and
overlap colors; the same samples failed in 112 contexts before the correction.
Existing width/frame/mixed-count cases also pass. The 0.15pt raster-edge
exclusion is unchanged. These joins are native details over §§17.4.38,
17.4.66 and 17.18.2, not a newly claimed normative divergence. Cross-family,
unequal-size and T/cross junction behavior is unchanged.

## Persistent cell controls

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.5.2.32–33 define a structured document tag around one
table cell and its cached content. §§17.5.2.25, 17.5.2.39 and 17.5.2.43 govern
placeholder references, placeholder state and temporary lifetime. Persistent
unlocked text/rich-text cell controls now use the existing block-control editing
lifecycle: text replacement, paragraph splitting, formatting, prompt restoration
and glossary paragraph prompts retain the wrapper. The cell writer synchronizes
showingPlcHdr with model state without rewriting unrelated package parts.

Native reference probes establish an editing conversion, not a demonstrated
spec divergence: horizontal and vertical merges move each persistent cell
wrapper inside the merged cell as a block wrapper (§§17.5.2.29, 17.5.2.34),
retaining ownership only of its original paragraphs. The model converts wrapper
kind and scope before moving contents. New rows/columns and split grid cells do
not inherit the source cell's control. Promoting a merged row rehomes persistent
ownership even after text editing. Deleting its containing cell/row/table removes
the wrapper with its content. Undo restores original structure and package parts.

Remaining scope: persistent controls containing nested tables/block controls,
separate persistent wrappers on vertical continuation cells,
locks, bindings and unsupported control types remain read-only. Inserting a
table inside a persistent block/cell control is rejected before mutation.
This does not change the corpus completion requirement for those features.
Evidence: original OPC/XML `tests/fixtures/persistent-cell-controls`, native
before/after XML and behavior JSON, unit regressions and browser edit/export tests.

## Body field serialization preparation

The page-field codec now replaces same-paragraph cached results while retaining
the OOXML simple/complex field envelope. It preserves the instruction, formatting
switches, lock/dirty flags and delimiter properties; an uncached complex field
gets a separator when result content is supplied. This is a serialization helper,
not a claim of editable body-field support. Field formatting continues to follow
ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.16.4 and the previously recorded native page-field behavior.

Native reference range-edit probes retain PAGE instructions even after result deletion
or paragraph splitting. Body integration therefore still needs field ranges that
can be empty or cross paragraphs, safe boundary editing, explicit refresh and
caret/pagination coverage. Retained source must not be flattened into plain text
or removed merely because a result becomes empty. Evidence: body-page-fields
native JSON, unit tests and browser serialization/schema checks.

## Editable cached body page fields

Body PAGE, NUMPAGES and SECTIONPAGES results now retain zero-width field
boundaries independently of their text runs. ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.16.18 (fldChar),
17.16.19 (fldSimple), and §17.16.4 govern the retained
syntax and instructions. Empty results and fields spanning paragraphs survive
insertion, replacement, formatting, search replacement, undo and export/reopen.
The source instruction and delimiter properties remain intact. Same-paragraph
simple fields keep their wrapper; a split converts them to complex syntax.
Bookmarks in visible results retain their order relative to field delimiters.

The native reference's independent range edits establish that deleting all result text
leaves the field and splitting a result retains a cross-paragraph field. Native
edited XML is also imported directly in tests. Opening and repagination retain
cached results, consistent with the separately recorded native reference observations.
No unconditional refresh was added to body layout.

Remaining work: explicit refresh/F9 and its formatting behavior, fields nested in instructions,
fields within inline content controls, instruction bookmarks, and ranges crossing
cells/sections. Unsupported imports remain guarded; partial boundary replacement
and table insertion inside a field reject before mutation. These limits remain
part of the overall completion objective. Evidence: body-field-editing unit and
browser tests, original body-page-fields fixture and native edit JSON.

### Nested cached body-field results

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.16 describes retained field results and explicitly leaves
update timing outside the standard's scope. §§17.16.18 (`fldChar`) and 17.16.19
(`fldSimple`) govern the retained envelopes. The body reader, zero-width range
model and exporter now support nested results for the existing PAGE/NUMPAGES/
SECTIONPAGES instruction subset. Results can span paragraphs or share empty
boundaries. Opening order identifies each parent; refill extends the containing
results, and serialization retains nested simple wrappers or converts them to
complex envelopes when a paragraph split requires it. Crossing/duplicate ranges,
instruction nesting and cell/section crossings remain guarded.

The independent `nested-page-fields` control exercises all simple/complex
combinations, bookmarks, empty boundaries and three levels. Seven recorded native reference
range edits independently establish result behavior; tests also import
the native edited XML. Browser workflows cover typing, splitting, export/reopen,
unrelated parts and exact undo. The locked visual control matches all ten native
lines within 0.055pt; unlocked reference PDF export refreshes page numbers instead.
This difference in update timing is recorded, not treated as a spec divergence
or evidence that automatic body-field refresh is implemented.

MACROBUTTON display/editing semantics still need integration before booklet 15
becomes editable. Cached TOC/PAGEREF instruction support is described below;
the shared page-story evaluator remains limited to its existing numeric fields.

### Cached TOC/PAGEREF and HYPERLINK body fields

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.16.5.68, 17.16.5.45 and 17.16.5.25 define TOC, PAGEREF and
HYPERLINK. Their body envelopes and cached results now survive editing, splitting,
deletion/refill, bookmark renaming, export/reopen and exact undo. Five independent
reference range edits in `toc-pageref/native-edits.json` establish cached behavior and
are also imported directly. Heading edits retain authored cached entries;
explicit TOC/PAGEREF regeneration is still outstanding. Update timing is outside
the standard's scope, as stated in the introduction to §17.16.

Field-boundary markers retain explicit hyperlink ownership, including empty
results. The TOC Hyperlink-style exception is also retained in editable results
and recomputed after edits so it does not suppress a newly chosen character
style or leak outside a removed TOC. All three original four-page TOC controls
retain their native text placement and paint checks within the existing 0.3pt
tolerance.

The native reference turns a paragraph-spanning TOC hyperlink into a HYPERLINK field. These
fields support the existing internal/absolute-URL navigation policy, retained
ScreenTips/frames, nested PAGEREF and empty results. Result editing preserves the
field. An explicit partial link edit converts the affected envelope to equivalent
paragraph-local hyperlink markup, preserving other targets. Bookmark renaming
updates PAGEREF/HYPERLINK arguments and TOC bookmark scopes without collapsing
instruction runs or losing surrounding switches and properties.

Native reference extension flagged: its generated `HYPERLINK \l "Topic1" \h` contains a
flag absent from §17.16.5.25's switch list. The independently authored
`hyperlink-fields` control includes both forms. The reference application's hyperlink API confirms
their identical bookmark target, and the two-page native PDF and all eleven
text lines match the editor within 0.054pt. The flag is retained without invented
semantics. Relative/file links, combined external/bookmark destinations and
image-map switches remain guarded, as do unsupported field instructions and
instruction nesting. No new evaluator or macro execution is introduced.

Validation: 218 unit checks, sixteen browser workflows, production build/license
gate, and 83 XML checks over 34 source/export packages. Native fixtures, hashes,
recorders and tests cover instruction retention, native edited XML, styling,
navigation, hyperlink removal/retargeting and repeated bookmark renames.

## 3D picture outline joins and neutral sketch metadata

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.8.43 and CT_LineJoinMiterProperties define miter joins;
limits accept the integer thousandths-of-percent and percentage spellings.
Retained rectangular 3D pictures now distinguish sharp miter corners from clipped
corners below the right-angle miter threshold. Bevel joins use clipped corners.
Closed picture paths accept flat, square and round caps without adding endpoints.
Existing absent/round outline rendering is preserved.

Native reference compatibility detail: independent flat/deep controls show that its clipped
outline mesh extrudes the straight segments but leaves the diagonal side faces
open. Back-face culling is necessary to avoid filling those corner openings.
The new mesh follows that native observation instead of treating the frame as a
closed octagonal prism. This is recorded rendering behavior; no claim is made
that the OOXML join description fully specifies the native reference's 3D meshing algorithm.
Beveled 3D surfaces combined with clipped outline joins remain guarded until
that surface/outline interaction is implemented and independently verified.

Both ordinary and 3D picture/shape outlines can retain a neutral saved sketch
extension (MS-ODRAWXML lineSketchStyleProps) with empty saved custom geometry and
an empty/explicit-none type. Import validates the complete neutral structure;
nonempty paths, active sketch types, malformed seeds and unknown extensions keep
the existing guards. Original extension XML remains in the drawing shell through
editing/export. No source filename or document identity affects these decisions.
Evidence: picture-3d-joins authored controls, native PDF/reference data, importer
and geometry unit tests, and browser native-color/silhouette/edit/export checks.

The same corpus review exposed a numerical edge case in bilinear alpha: a sum a
few ulps above 255 produced a tiny negative composited channel, which the strict
3D shader rejected. Source-over weights and output colors are now clamped to the
valid pixel range before shading. A generated 3-by-5 texture with a gray backing
reproduces the old failure independently of the corpus. Unsupported picture
character formatting is also kept local in read-only style resolution, so the
rest of a structured preview can survive. Strict editing guards remain intact.


### Script formatting on inline and anchored pictures

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.42 (`vertAlign`) describes script text alignment;
§§20.4.2.3 (`anchor`) and 20.4.2.8 (`inline`) define drawing placement.
The native reference preserves a drawing run's baseline/subscript/superscript value
without scaling or shifting the picture. Nine independently authored controls
cover all three values with page-relative anchors, paragraph-relative anchors,
and inline pictures. Within each placement mode, the native reference's colored picture bounds
and cropped picture bytes are identical. This clarifies drawing behavior; it
is not evidence of a conflicting text-alignment rule in the standard.

The importer, direct and inherited formatting edits, and image insertion now
retain these values without rejecting the document. Drawing metrics bypass
text script transforms, as before; explicit `w:position` still shifts inline
pictures, and unsupported text-width scaling still rejects safely. Neighboring
text retains its script behavior. The earlier script checkpoint's picture
restriction above is superseded. No-edit and undo preserve the original package;
edited exports retain formatting and reopen editable. Native evidence is in
`tests/fixtures/anchored-picture-script`, with original generator and reference
extractor in `tools/anchored_picture_script_*.py`.


### Image-data creation identities

The drawing creation-ID support above also applies to `a:blip/a:extLst`
(ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.8.13; MS-ODRAWXML §§2.25.1.2 and 2.25.3.2).
The image reader uses the existing identity validator for the registered
`{FF2B5EF4-FFF2-40B4-BE49-F238E27FC236}` extension. Optional IDs, GUID token rules,
namespace/attribute/content checks and duplicate-extension rejection remain
consistent with nonvisual-property identities. Unknown image extensions still
reject. Inline and grouped pictures retain metadata through ordinary text edits,
image resizing, deletion and undo/redo without modifying the source shell.

Original controls add identities to our authored artwork fixture, including
an omitted ID and both extension orders alongside local-DPI metadata. The native reference's
complete page raster is identical with and without these additions; the browser
also produces identical rasters. This is supported extension metadata, not a
reference/specification divergence. Source, reference PDFs and hash-bound native evidence
are in `tests/fixtures/blip-creation-ids`; generator and recorder are
`tools/blip_creation_id_fixture.py` and `tools/blip_creation_id_reference.py`.
No dependency or renderer change was needed.


### Vertically merged shading and shared row padding

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.32 (`shd`), 17.4.84 (`vMerge`), 17.4.68 (`tcMar`)
and 17.4.42 (`tblCellMar`) define the participating cell properties. The native reference's
row geometry reserves shared row padding (including its documented bottom-
padding addition to exact row height). The native reference additionally
retains the restart cell's own padding for the merged painted fill. This
native placement detail is not a new OOXML property or a source-specific rule.

For each merged page fragment, subtract the difference between its last
physical row's shared bottom padding and the restart cell's bottom padding
from the fill's bottom edge. This can leave an unpainted gap or extend the fill
into the following area. On continuation pages, inset the top by any positive
difference between the first physical row's shared top padding and restart
padding. The initial fragment retains its top padding fill. Existing border
insets and containing-cell clipping still apply. The layout carries these paint
insets separately: text positions, row bounds, borders, selection and pagination
do not move. Main-canvas and drawing-contained tables use the same fill bounds.

Twenty-one original controls distinguish merges from separate cells, absent/
nil/none/visible borders, exact/minimum/fractional heights, continuation shading,
neighbor padding of 29/120 twips, top versus bottom padding, and restart versus
continuation declarations. Two additional controls span six pages and distinguish
fragment-local padding from a correction applied only on the final page.
Their source, native PDF captures and hash-bound shaded spans live in
`tests/fixtures/merged-shading-gap`. The browser checks blue coverage so dashed
editing guides and fractional antialiasing do not count as unpainted gaps.
Independent controls, padding-edit/undo/export checks and existing shading,
merged-border and shape-table workflows verify this behavior. The standard's
cell-shading definition does not specify these shared-padding raster boundaries;
the native controls document the reference behavior being implemented.

### Book-fold logical page geometry: initial native evidence

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.15.1.11–13 define `bookFoldPrinting`,
`bookFoldPrintingSheets` and `bookFoldRevPrinting`. They describe arranging
logical pages into printed signatures. This does not justify halving the saved
`pgSz` again when displaying reading pages. MS-OI29500 documents a margin
divergence for both [forward book fold](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/a3f96a73-1cad-4a64-a7e3-cf18ad747708)
and [reverse book fold](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-oi29500/4a4ba769-8bc1-42b3-b662-08b23bd8e953):
the native reference uses right margins at the printed-sheet bisector where the standard
describes left margins. Reverse printing also has a documented sheet-order
difference. Our PDF controls observe reading pages, not physical printer output;
they do not establish printer imposition or sheet ordering.

The ten independently authored packages in `tests/fixtures/book-fold` have
four logical pages each, asymmetric margins (left 72 pt, right 54 pt), explicit
page breaks and left/right aligned text. Native PDF dimensions always match
stored `pgSz`, including the control whose width exceeds its height. Forward
landscape controls swap margins on odd logical pages; reverse swaps on even
pages and takes precedence over forward. Four-page signature metadata does
not change those reading-page results. Portrait orientation and `gutterAtTop`
produce different behavior with no observed margin alternation. The 18 pt
side-gutter control has the same writing extents on every page in this specific
asymmetric-margin configuration; additional gutter values are needed before
generalizing its rule. Text bounds and source/PDF hashes are recorded in
`reference.json` and checked by `book-fold-native.test.js`.

This initial investigation preceded the implementation described below.

### Book-fold reading layout, saved anchors and margin editing

The importer now accepts validated forward/reverse booklet flags and retains
them as immutable print metadata. Reverse takes precedence. Stored `pgSz`
dimensions describe reading pages and are never halved. With landscape
orientation and no top gutter, add the gutter to the saved right margin; swap
this margin pair for odd logical page numbers in forward booklets and even
numbers in reverse booklets. Page-number starts affect parity. Portrait and
top-gutter sections keep ordinary geometry. The original settings part,
including signature size metadata, survives body/page-size/margin edits.

Three additional gutter controls distinguish zero/9/18/36 pt gutters and reverse
printing, bringing the basic controls to 52 native pages. Five combined controls
add 20 pages with tables, header/footer stories, logical numbering starting at
two, repeated even/default stories, page/margin/column drawing anchors, square
wrapping and page/margin floating tables. Text origins and colored drawing
bounds are bound to source/PDF hashes. These controls distinguish several reference
coordinate systems: body paragraphs and ordinary/margin-anchored floating tables
follow alternating margins, while margin-anchored drawings and stories use the
original margins with the gutter on the left. Column drawings follow their
anchor's body column; page anchors remain fixed. This is observed reference behavior,
not a claim that every coordinate detail is specified by the booklet clauses.

Page layout translates measured content after pagination using each page's
