logical number, updates the page/region geometry, resolves anchors afterward,
and translates wrapping exclusions back into measurement coordinates. It
does not alter text widths or introduce another layout pass for booklets.
Ruler edits map a visible side back to the corresponding saved margin, with
the correct gutter subtraction; page setup explains the logical dimensions.
Editing, exact undo, page setup, ruler edits, source preservation and editable
export/reopen are covered by unit/browser tests. Physical printer imposition
and signature ordering remain delegated to consumers of the preserved DOCX
print settings; the canvas displays reading pages. `mirrorMargins` remains
separately guarded, as before.

### Script size and face-dependent native typography (open)

The reduced/repositioned text required by ECMA-376 Part 1, section 17.3.2.42
(`vertAlign`) does not specify a numerical scaling algorithm. OpenType's
[OS/2 script fields](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/os2)
are recommendations. Our current fixed script transform does not reproduce all
reference fonts and sizes; this is a rendering gap, not a proven OOXML divergence.

`tests/fixtures/script-size/control.docx` independently defines 108 mixed-run
cases: Garamond, Arial and Times New Roman, each regular/bold/italic, at six
declared sizes with both superscript and subscript. The native reference
PDF has nine pages. The recorder checks actual PDF font identities and text
matrices, and binds measured sizes, baseline offsets and following-run origins
to source/PDF hashes. Font binaries are not copied; only installed font hashes,
units-per-em and numerical OS/2 fields are recorded.

Despite all nine faces specifying a vertical script size of 1331/2048 em,
the native reference's PDF reports Garamond 12 pt scripts at 6.96 pt and Arial/Times scripts at
8.04 pt. Garamond regular at 10 pt produces 6.48 pt scripts, while italic at
the same declared size produces 6 pt. Superscript positioning also varies by
face. These results rule out a universal ratio and use of the vertical-size
field alone. The earlier controlled-font evidence remains relevant: changing
individual recommendations can change the native reference's fallback behavior as well.

All nine reference/browser page pairs were inspected. Known script size, advance
and baseline differences remain. No-edit preservation, insertion/export,
unrelated-part preservation, exact undo and editable reopen pass. The source
and three browser exports pass 12 XML checks; three native-evidence tests pass.
These tests protect the observations and do not claim renderer fidelity.

### Nonrotating stretched shape picture fills

ECMA-376 Part 1 section 20.1.8.14 (`blipFill`) defines `rotWithShape`;
section 20.1.8.30 (`fillRect`) supplies the destination fill rectangle.
For an explicit false flag on a stretched shape fill, the painter now retains
the transformed path as its clip but maps the image into the upright bounds
of the filled geometry. The texture does not inherit shape/group rotations
or reflections. Cubic, quadratic and elliptical extrema are evaluated after
transformation; unfilled paths and outline width do not expand the texture.
Source cropping, destination insets/outsets and opacity use the existing
picture-fill mapping. The OOXML package representation is unchanged.

Native reference controls independently establish this mapping, including the
unreflected fill inside a reflected shape. The standard describes rotation
behavior but does not specify this detailed bounding-box algorithm; no
contradiction with its stated rotation rule has been established.
Two original fixtures in `tests/fixtures/nonrotating-picture-fill` contain
28 cases on 20 native pages: standalone and nested shapes, child/ancestor
rotation, unequal group scaling, reflections, asymmetric destination insets,
polygon and curved clipping, and outlines. The recorder binds native color
samples to source XML and PDF hashes. Browser tests compare interior colors
and retained editing/export/reopen; unit tests cover imported metadata,
reference identity, package preservation and exact undo.

This change concerns stretched **shape fills**. Existing unsupported guards
for nonrotating tiled fills and grouped picture objects remain in force.
The separate rotated-inline positioning discrepancy observed in scratch
controls remains open; it is not addressed by the texture transform.

### Line-relative floating pictures

Part 1 §§20.4.2.11 (`positionV`), 20.4.2.12 (`posOffset`) and 20.4.3.5
(`ST_RelFromV`) place a line-relative drawing against the line containing its
anchor character. Numeric unwrapped body/story anchors now select that actual
laid-out line rather than the paragraph's first line. Independent reference controls
show the origin at the line box top. Positive/negative offsets, manual line
breaks, automatic wrapping, exact line spacing and paragraph before-spacing
are covered alongside a paragraph-relative control.

Floating anchor characters do not create word-break opportunities. A word can
span text runs on both sides of an unwrapped anchor, so wrapping, contraction
and obstacle word fitting retain that word as a unit. Inline images keep their
existing break opportunity. Source anchor XML remains unchanged on unrelated
edits; export/reopen, picture selection, deletion/undo and exact undo are checked.

The original eight-page fixture is `tests/fixtures/line-relative-anchors`.
All eight measured picture positions match the native reference. Numeric line placement
agrees with the cited standard; no reference/spec divergence is claimed here.
Line alignment, wrapped line-relative drawings, cell-relative combinations and
explicit page/column breaks remain unsupported. Story and automatic-pagination
coverage require further native controls; these remain broader engine work.
# Large source and destination picture rectangles (September 23)

DrawingML `CT_RelativeRect`, Part 1 §§20.1.8.55 (`srcRect`), 20.1.8.56
(`stretch`) and 20.1.10.40 (`ST_Percentage`), together with Part 4's
`ST_PercentageDecimal` (`xsd:int`), permit offsets beyond the former application
limit of 1000%. The importer and crop properties now accept signed 32-bit
thousandths of a percent, retaining positive viewport checks. Percentage strings
outside that range or finer than 0.001% remain unsupported. Existing clipping
limits painting to the physical frame; this does not enlarge decoded bitmaps.
The native reference agrees with these standard values; no divergence is claimed.

Eight original controls in `tests/fixtures/large-picture-rectangles` cover all
destination sides, mixed offsets, source outsets, percentage strings and combined
source/destination mappings. All eight page pairs were visually inspected and
30,061 native interior pixel samples pass. Twenty-three unit tests across three
crop suites and five distinct browser scenarios pass, including authoring a
large crop, reopening it, editing alt text, resetting, package preservation,
editing, exact undo and export/reopen. Fixture and browser exports pass schema
checks; production build and the 199-package license check pass. This fixes one
import guard in corpus #261; its separate EMF failure remains under investigation.

### EMF record counts bounded by input length

MS-EMF Header (2.2.9) defines the unsigned Records count without a 10,000-record
cap: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-emf/e4a35c41-e8e3-43f9-bc07-a18e99bb866d .
The original reader now validates the declaration against the input byte length
(each record has at least eight bytes) and the actual traversal count. Its
existing 8 MiB input, geometry, output, frame and nesting limits remain. The
original emf-record-count fixture adds 12,000 state records per image and keeps
the existing path geometry unchanged. The native reference and browser comparisons
establish identical geometry; this is standard behavior, not a reference divergence.

Verification: 46 EMF unit tests and three distinct browser scenarios pass,
including exact raster equality between the original and high-record controls.
The initial new browser run hit duplicate dialog handlers in test setup; the
corrected isolated rerun passes. Original/corpus preservation, editing, undo,
and reopening pass, as do fixture/export schema checks and production build
with its 199-package license gate. No dependency or optimization was added.

### Merged cells ending in exact-height rows

Part 1 §§17.4.80 `trHeight`, 17.18.37 `ST_HeightRule`, 17.4.84 `vMerge` and
17.4.85 `vAlign` define the constituent properties but do not prescribe a full
mixed-row demand-allocation algorithm. The native reference clips a merged
owner when its final physical row is exact; it does not grow an earlier flexible
row to accommodate that owner's overflow. A final flexible row still grows.
This is an explicitly recorded native reference compatibility interpretation. Existing
legacy handling of an earlier oversized exact row is retained.

Original controls in tests/fixtures/merged-ending-rows cover eight two/three-row
sequences, tall text and nested tables, in compatibility modes 14 and 15. Native
PDF extraction reports even clipped text, so browser checks compare visible
ink in 144 marker regions, including regions that must stay blank. All sixteen
mode-15 page pairs were also visually inspected. The older E-A-E unit expectation
encoded the wrong allocation; the original fixture was exported through the native reference
again before correcting that expectation. Hidden content remains in the model,
export and undo, with caret bounds constrained to its visible cell.

Verification for the merged-ending change: 76 distinct unit tests across six
suites and nine browser scenarios pass, including the earlier oversized-row
and editing regressions. The new 16-page package checks and two unchanged
package-heavy tests exceeded the initial 5s unit timeout; reruns with unchanged
assertions and a 60s limit pass. Both corrected control fixtures pass again.
The initial python-docx controls omitted the required zoom percent; the generator
now supplies it, both native PDFs/references were regenerated, and the affected
browser and schema checks were rerun successfully. Final fixture, browser and
corpus exports pass schema checks. Production build and the 199-package license
check pass. No dependency, optimization or UI change was introduced.

## Unresolved w15 content-control data bindings

MS-DOCX §2.5.1.6 defines `w15:dataBinding` using the standard `CT_DataBinding`
type. Its attributes use the WordprocessingML namespace. ISO/IEC 29500-1
§17.5.2.6 permits application fallback when a binding does not resolve. Independent
native reference controls show that a missing or zero store ID can still resolve to
another custom XML store; the identifier alone does not prove inactivity.

The editable importer accepts an unresolved `w15:dataBinding` only after its
absolute child-element XPath selects no node in any related package custom XML
store. The resolver compares namespace URIs, supports positive positional
predicates per parent, and retains the original binding and custom data. The
saved control contents remain editable through the existing persistent rich/plain
control model. No external stores are fetched. Missing or invalid store parts,
active mappings, unknown prefixes and XPath outside this grammar retain read-only
fallback. Active synchronization, richer XPath and standard `w:dataBinding`
editing remain unfinished work; this is not complete XML-mapping support.

Original fixtures in `tests/fixtures/unresolved-bindings` establish that missing
child nodes and out-of-range positional predicates retain cached text in the native reference. The native reference also renders the browser-edited export with its edited text.
Unit and browser regressions cover mapping fallback guards, namespace aliases,
per-parent indexing, package preservation, control edits, export/reopen and exact
undo. Schema validation checks the actual `w15:dataBinding` declaration against
the hash-pinned MS-DOCX schema and ECMA `CT_DataBinding`, separately from the
standard MCE view that omits the ignorable extension.

References: [MS-DOCX dataBinding](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-docx/2805f4e9-9333-4e7a-bb56-f1ce0e9e8e25),
[published W15 schema](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-docx/d416013d-c112-44fa-8bef-7819b8898117).

## DrawingML paired rounded-corner rectangles

`round2SameRect` follows ECMA-376 Part 1's supplied preset shape definition
(§§20.1.9.18, 20.1.9.11, 20.1.10.56). `adj1` controls the two top corners and
`adj2` the two bottom corners; defaults are 16667 and zero. Both values clamp to
0..50000 and scale against the shorter side. Text side insets use the larger
corner radius, while top/bottom insets use their own radius, multiplied by .29289.
Original path construction reuses the existing painting, image-fill clipping,
transform and outline pipeline; original preset XML remains preserved on export.

Eight independent controls cover unequal radii, defaults, zero, clamps,
conflicting inner/frame dimensions, rotation and flips. All 4,485 native reference
ink samples agree; three text origins agree within .093pt horizontally
and .136pt vertically. No divergence from the standard was observed.
58 targeted units and four browser cases pass, including existing roundRect
regressions, edit/export/reopen, original shape XML retention and exact undo.
Fixture, browser exports and original corpus exports pass schema checks;
production build and the 199-package license gate pass.

The triggering Twine + Burlap pamphlet now opens editable and restores its
arched photograph. Its original fonts Rod and Speak Pro are unavailable to the
browser, which uses Noto Sans; its original two-page result remains partial.
An Arial-only diagnostic copy renders on one page in both the native reference and the browser.
That copy does not replace the original or count as original-font fidelity.

### Percentage anchor positions

MS-ODRAWXML 2.19.1.1/2 defines `wp14:pctPosHOffset`/`pctPosVOffset` as
percentage alternatives within `wp:positionH`/`positionV`, using DrawingML
`ST_Percentage` (ISO/IEC 29500-1 20.1.10.40). The importer retains integer
thousandths-of-percent and literal percentage forms on supported wrapNone
coordinate references, including an MCE-selected wp14 branch. Original source
XML is preserved during body edits and export. Unsupported wrapping/reference
combinations remain guarded.

The independently authored `tests/fixtures/percentage-anchors` body/cell controls
establish that the native reference uses the available writing height for paragraph/line percentages,
cell width or content width for cell X percentages, and content top for cell Y
percentages. Paragraph/line offsets begin at the anchor paragraph/line origin,
and header/footer clearance changes the writing span. A second independent
header control changes paragraph spacing to distinguish this from physical
page-margin coordinates. Percentage axes independently add their leading effect extent;
mixed numeric axes retain ordinary offset semantics. These details are empirical
reference compatibility refinements; no contradiction with explicit normative text
is asserted. Header controls now match native coordinates. The multicolumn
coordinate rule is measured, but full positioned-object column flow remains
explicitly unsupported. Legacy-mode coverage is still pending.

The schema checker downloads the published wp14 schema into its temporary cache,
pins its hash and adds just its percentage-position alternatives to the standard
CT_PosH/V choices. Documents using direct percentage children require this
extension view; no standard-only fallback is claimed. Other optional wp14
metadata retains its existing ignorable processing. Malformed percentage values
are covered by validator self-checks. Publication source:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-odrawxml/1a38a99a-16ae-420d-8c79-23dc2e922717

Validation: 39 distinct focused unit tests pass (38 together, then the final
12 percentage tests including the added unsupported-MCE guard). Nine final
percentage/header browser cases pass; prior line-relative and effect-offset
regressions also pass. The 28 body/cell frames agree within one pixel, and the
exact-height header control agrees at all three origins. All 15 final browser
exports, independent sources and original postcard exports pass schema checks.
The final postcard edit/export/reopen/undo workflow, production build and
199-package license gate pass. Its fold lines are restored; its gift artwork
remains a separate unresolved visual issue, so source #265 stays partial.

### Five-point star preset

`star5` follows the supplied ECMA-376 Part 1 presetShapeDefinitions.xml geometry
and §§20.1.9.18, 20.1.9.11 and 20.1.10.56. Default adj/hf/vf guides are
19098/105146/110557; adj is clamped to 0..50000. Scaled inner and outer radii
produce the ten-vertex contour, with its top vertex fixed at zero and its text
rectangle bounded by the inner guide coordinates. The original implementation
uses the existing shape painting, transformation and text pipeline and preserves
source geometry markup through body edits and export.

Eight independently authored reference controls cover defaults, adjustments, clamps,
horizontal/vertical factors, unequal frame/inner dimensions, rotation and flips.
All 4,493 native ink samples match; three text origins agree within .083 pt in X
and .148 pt vertically. 129 unit tests and four browser cases pass, including
existing geometry/group/corner regressions, edited export/reopening and exact undo.
Sources, original postcard exports and four browser exports pass schema checks;
production build and the 199-package license gate pass.

The native reference rejects the schema-valid independently authored
`tests/fixtures/corner-star5/native-reject-partial-adjustment.docx`, where one star
specifies adj without hf/vf. It also rejected a diagnostic with reordered
hf/vf/adj declarations. The full ordered adj/hf/vf controls open successfully.
These are observed reference import restrictions, not requirements imposed on the
renderer: named guides retain standard defaults, and source XML is not rewritten
to reproduce the native reference's rejection. The controls and fixture README record this distinction.

### Dormant normal autofit on shapes without text boxes

ECMA-376 DrawingML's `normAutofit` / CT_TextNormalAutofit describes text scaling
and line-spacing reduction. When `wps:txbx` is absent there is nothing to scale;
the importer now retains that declaration after validating its attributes and
the mutually exclusive EG_TextAutofit choice. Integer ranges and percentage
lexical forms follow ST_TextFontScalePercentOrPercentString and
ST_TextSpacingPercentOrPercentString in the transitional schema. Unknown
attributes, children, conflicting modes and malformed values remain rejected.
Normal autofit on a real text box remains guarded pending its fitting algorithm.

Eight original native controls cover absent attributes, numeric and percent forms.
Their reference ink samples and the existing shape-defaults browser regression pass,
including edited export/reopen, untouched shape markup and exact package undo.
The source controls, four browser exports and original birthday-card exports pass
schema validation; production build and the 199-package license gate pass.
No reference/spec divergence was observed for this inactive case. The triggering
landscape birthday card now opens editable and renders its complete gift artwork.

## Local SVG reuse and instance rendering

References: SVG 1.1 section 5.6; [SVG 2 section 5.6](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG2/struct.html#UseElement),
including layout, style inheritance and circular references; the SVG picture
relationship/OPC requirements remain those listed above.

Local `use` can reference supported basic shapes, paths, groups, text and other
local instances. Positioned instances retain x/y (including percentages and
physical/font-relative lengths), transformations, explicit/inherited paints,
static CSS, local gradients/clips and nested reuse. Width/height do not resize
non-viewport targets. Nested SVG/symbol viewports, external references and the
other previously unsupported SVG constructs remain guarded. Missing targets,
cycles, invalid positions and unsupported target types cannot open editable.
The 20,000-element/64-level and 100,000-character limits apply to the expanded
instance graph, including nonbreaking-space preview spans, before decoding.

The original SVG and raster fallback remain byte-identical in DOCX. Only the
preview materializes drawable instances, renames cloned IDs and redirects their
local resources. This allows the native reference's existing stroke/text/opacity corrections to
operate on each instance's actual cascade and transformation. Clipping uses stay
native: a generated group is not a valid replacement for a direct clipping child.
Documents without reuse keep the previous SVG rendering path.

Independent controls prove two reference differences from SVG 2, implemented
generically rather than by corpus name or artwork:

- The native reference prefers xlink:href when href and xlink:href both exist (SVG 2 specifies
  href precedence). The two target geometries/colors in the last style control
  unambiguously distinguish the selected reference.
- The native reference retains source-matched CSS declarations, including selectors involving
  source ancestors outside the reused subtree. SVG 2 section 5.6.3 instead
  matches selectors in the instance shadow scope. The first style control is
  blue in the native reference rather than inheriting green from the instance. We retain the
  source's specified declarations, with specificity/order/inline precedence;
  unspecified inherited properties still resolve from the instance parent.

The native reference's previously measured 0.14 metafile-unit pen floor also applies separately
to reused paths at normal and half scale. A 0.3 inherited fill opacity exports
as 76/255, matching the existing reference alpha behavior. Original controls cover
full/cropped/grouped pictures and shape fills. Tests verify native colors and
stroke coverage, local resource IDs, nested/percentage transforms, source
immutability, surrounding edits, export/reopen and exact undo. Native references,
source/PDF hashes and independent generators are in `tests/fixtures/svg-use` and
`tools/canvas_svg_use_fixture.py` / `tools/record_svg_use_reference.py`.

## Zero-axis DrawingML groups

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.7.1–6 define child/display extents, offsets and transforms;
§20.1.10.41 and the supplied transitional `ST_PositiveCoordinate` schema permit
zero (`minInclusive=0`). `CT_GroupTransform2D` uses that type for both `ext` and
`chExt`. The earlier strictly-positive importer restriction was too narrow.
One-zero-axis group frames are retained without inventing body-flow space;
negative extents, fully zero source group frames, mismatched flat outer/group
frames and text inside collapsed groups remain guarded. These remaining guards
describe the supported subset, not schema-invalid OOXML.

Native reference compatibility details are established by independent native controls,
rather than inferred from division by `chExt`: a zero displayed group axis
collapses child positions/dimensions before child rotation. Zero child-coordinate
extents use unit scale; nonzero ones use the displayed/child ratio, including
zero. Consequently the two cases differ after local rotations exchange axes.
Finite orientation and reflection handedness survive singular transforms, and
stroke widths remain physical. Canvas translation/reflection is explicitly
composed when its incremental operations would drop surviving-axis offsets.
The standard's group-transform prose does not fully specify this degenerate
arithmetic; these rules are documented reference behavior, not a blanket claim of
specification contradiction. The previously recorded §20.1.7.5 rotation-unit
prose discrepancy still uses native/ST_Angle 1/60000-degree units.

For MS-ODRAWXML §5.11 `wp14:sizeRelH`/`sizeRelV`, native percentages can expand
the outer group frame while its saved zero artwork axis remains collapsed.
Ordinary child frames are resized before rotation on the nonzero axis. Selection
uses a thin pointer-tolerant frame while collapsed, and the full atomic group
rectangle when the outer frame gains area. Standalone flat lines retain their
existing distinct percentage-expansion behavior. Source XML, coordinates and
OPC parts are not rewritten to encode runtime rendering adjustments.

Four fixtures contain 42 native reference line controls: zero-axis-groups,
zero-axis-group-rotations, zero-axis-group-geometry and zero-axis-group-relative.
Their generators, PDFs, source/reference hashes and actual native endpoint/pen
records are retained. Browser checks compare transformed endpoints, physical
pens and visible/degenerate ink, verify real pointer selection, and exercise
editable import, package preservation, insertion, exact undo pixels and editable
export/reopen. Unit coverage includes malformed frames, preserved scenes,
thin/expanded selection bounds and relative frame dimensions.

Four additional native controls in `zero-axis-group-effects` retain 10 pt
physical shadow offsets and outlined patterned rectangles below singular
scales. Shadow orientation uses the surviving axis plus retained handedness;
its missing axis must not produce a non-finite offset. Zero-area frames paint
their physical outlines without trying to invert a transform for a fill that
has no area. Native PDF color bounds and editable round trips cover both cases.

## Picture downsampling

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.8.13 (`blip`), 20.1.8.14 (`blipFill`),
20.1.8.55 (`srcRect`), 20.1.8.56 (`stretch`) and 20.2 (pictures) retain
unchanged source rectangles, frame geometry and OPC media bytes. The display
sampler uses high-quality filtering when picture pixels are reduced, including
inline crops, grouped pictures and stretched shape picture fills. Enlargement
and intentionally unsmoothed shape-pattern painting keep their existing paths.
Sampling quality is a renderer choice, not a claimed OOXML/reference divergence.

Substantial axis-aligned reductions of immutable ImageBitmaps reuse final device
pixels, keyed by source crop, destination dimensions, linear transform and
fractional device placement. Reuse must not perform a second image reduction or
fractional interpolation. The caller's clipping and opacity apply on composition.
An LRU limits these temporary samples to 4 megapixels (16 MiB RGBA); eviction
closes the sample bitmap, and entries do not retain source bitmaps. Multiple
sizes/crops of one image can coexist within that limit. Closed sources, mutable
canvases and non-source-over composition cannot use stale samples. Rotated/sheared pictures use the direct high-quality path because separately
rasterizing their edges can change coverage where a caller's clip intersects
them. Images whose sample bounds exceed the cache budget also use that path.
No display sample replaces the source image in an exported document.

`tools/raster_sampling_fixture.py` constructs original high-frequency artwork
in four independent picture contexts. Installed references and hashes live
under `tests/fixtures/raster-sampling`; browser checks cover the native stripe
regions, edit/export/undo/reopen, cache reuse and bounds, mutable/closed sources,
and direct-sampling equivalence under fractional, rotated and reflected placement.

## Automatic line spacing at page boundaries

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.33 specifies automatic spacing in 240ths of a line and
exact/minimum spacing in twips. Independent native reference controls establish that
expanded automatic leading advances consecutive lines but does not contribute
to the last line's required bottom-edge extent. Page fitting uses the smaller
of the natural extent and automatic advance. Exact/minimum rules retain their
full allocation; compressed automatic spacing retains its smaller allocation.
This is native page-fit behavior where the spacing clause does not explicitly
specify the pagination algorithm, rather than a claimed literal contradiction.

The same extent applies to keep-lines, keep-next and widow look-ahead and the
fresh-page height guard. Actual placement continues to advance by the full line
height. Square wrapping retains the actual page's exclusions when only trailing
leading crosses its margin. Drawing clearance remains reserved. Stored spacing
and original package parts are not rewritten.

`bottom-line-boundary` contains 58 independently authored controls with native
cutoffs for empty and visible 3 pt Arial Bold paragraphs following tables.
`bottom-line-fresh` adds five 72 pt controls, including 2x/5x advances larger than
the entire writing area. Native PDFs, hashes, generation/recording scripts and
editable round-trip checks accompany both fixtures. This does not claim matching
pagination when an unavailable source font is replaced by different metrics.

## Translucent solid SVG groups

SVG 1.1 §14.5 applies group opacity after compositing its children. The native reference's SVG
metafiles rasterize translucent groups at the intrinsic viewport resolution,
using nearest-integer geometry bounds padded by one pixel on each side.
Independent `svg-group-raster` and `svg-group-transforms` native reference captures retain
the original intermediate RGBA PNGs, bounds, transforms and source hashes.

The display preview samples solid, unstroked path/basic-shape fills on an 8×4
grid, consistent with the documented GDI+ antialiasing filter. Partial coverage
samples are resolved against the path rather than trusting Canvas's intermediate
rounded-edge quantization. Child layers are composed before each group's alpha;
nested groups retain separate compositing. Opaque artwork remains vector.
Positive axis-aligned transforms and intrinsic viewBox scaling are covered.

These generated display images stay inside the isolated SVG preview. No generated
bitmap replaces source SVG or companion raster bytes in exported DOCX. Image
dimensions and total coverage work are bounded. Groups involving gradients,
strokes, clipping, text, rotation/reflection, or excessive raster work retain
their previous vector rendering pending native controls; their full reference fidelity
remains unfinished. A failed outer translucent group is retained as a whole.

The native PNGs distinguish group rendering from the native reference's PDF conversion: the PDF
can retain alpha while additionally multiplying RGB by it. That export color
discrepancy is not applied to the preview. Native comparisons allow small edge
and byte-rounding differences; exact GDI+ pixel equivalence is not claimed.

## Zero-extent custom DrawingML shapes

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.7.6 (`xfrm`), 20.1.9.8 (`custGeom`),
20.1.9.11 (guide formulas), 20.1.9.15 (`path`) and 20.1.10.42
(`ST_PositiveCoordinate`) define the transform, geometry and path coordinate
systems. The path viewport is distinct from the physical shape extent; see
[the normative path description reproduced in the Open XML SDK](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.drawing.path).

Custom shapes accept nonnegative frame dimensions and evaluate guides with the
actual zero dimensions. A missing path dimension inherits the shape-coordinate
system: when that extent is zero, absolute coordinates retain identity scaling
instead of producing 0/0. An explicit positive path dimension still scales its
axis to the frame, including collapse to zero. Painting, curve bounds, transformed
bounds and compound contours use the same scale rule. Flat custom paths may paint
outside their frame; they are not unconditionally skipped or enlarged.

Native compatibility: the native reference suppresses paths in a both-zero custom frame even
when omitted viewport dimensions and absolute coordinates would otherwise yield
visible geometry. This suppression is not stated by the path element's general
coordinate rules; it is established by twelve grouped and twelve standalone
independent controls in `flat-custom-shapes` and `flat-custom-standalone`.
Retained standalone empty drawings keep zero layout dimensions, inert paint and
original XML. Their explicit empty metadata does not admit ordinary malformed
zero-sized pictures or both-zero preset lines. Negative extents, explicit zero
path viewports, nonfinite formulas and flat text boxes remain rejected.

Browser tests compare native ink bounds and all invisible cases, then verify
editing, package preservation, exact undo and edited reopening. Source and exports
are schema-checked. These controls cover solid custom-path fills and outlines;
they do not establish every flat gradient, texture or text-layout behavior.

## Latin ligature defaults — unresolved rendering diagnostic

The original tests/fixtures/latin-ligature-defaults controls establish that the native reference
leaves Calibri ligatures off when the run declaration is omitted or
none. Explicit standard/standardContextual affects the measured samples only
with enableOpenTypeFeatures enabled (MS-DOCX section 2.3.3). Browser Canvas uses
standard ligatures by default even with fontKerning set to none. The Calibri ti
pair narrows by 15 design units; this can change a line break at a narrow boundary.
This is a missing feature-selection behavior, not a font-size adjustment or a
proved reference/spec divergence. The fixtures and recorded native reference positions are
pre-implementation evidence. Generic property inheritance, feature-aware font
selection for paint/measurement, caret behavior and regressions remain pending.

## DOCX optional-ligature defaults

MS-DOCX sections 2.3.3 and 2.6.4.3 distinguish the document's OpenType switch
from each run's ligature declaration. Run declarations now resolve through the
ordinary defaults/table/paragraph/character/direct-format cascade. Omitted
ligatures resolve to none; a disabled or absent enableOpenTypeFeatures switch
forces display off without deleting the original declaration. Duplicate and
invalid declarations/settings are rejected. Splitting, text editing, explicit
format edits, style inheritance/removal, export/reopen and undo preserve them.
The shared shaping key includes the effective mode so different modes cannot
share an incremental shaping group.

For effective none, Canvas textRendering=optimizeSpeed disables its default
optional ligatures. The explicit fontKerning assignment remains independent;
this is a rendering correction, not a performance optimization. Measurement and
painting share this state, including shaped caret measurement. Runs without a
WordprocessingML ligature property retain the previous Canvas behavior. No new
font resources, per-font offsets, asynchronous loads or extra shaping calls are
introduced. Independent installed-reference controls match omitted/none and the
Calibri standard/standardContextual examples with both compatibility settings.
Arabic shaping/carets, kerning and fractional-size boundaries pass regressions.

Limits remain explicit: non-none modes retain the prior browser default
ligatures. Separate contextual-only, discretionary and historical feature
selection, and distinguishing liga from clig for fonts where they differ, are
not implemented by textRendering. The enum is retained, not a claim that every
mode renders faithfully. The earlier Goudy legacy/OpenType kerning diagnostic
also remains open. No ligature UI is added. Complete feature selection remains
in scope; this change corrects the omitted/none behavior that caused source 301.

The source reference is the MS-DOCX ST_Ligatures definition:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-docx/c6219b84-98ae-4060-be2d-320650c2fdfd
See tests/ligatures.test.js, tests/browser/ligatures.spec.js and the independently
authored latin-ligature-defaults fixtures and recorded native reference origins.

## CI follow-up: shape rotation and SVG workflow checks

The older shape-flips negative test still rejected a valid 90-degree transform,
although generic rotated shape/text support and independent reference controls now
cover it. It now verifies quarter-turn preservation across editing/reopening
and exact undo, while fractional and out-of-range rotation values remain guarded.
The source's first textual flipH="true" occurs on its fourth shape (the earlier
horizontal-only shape uses flipH="1"); the positive expectation follows that XML.

The SVG resource round-trip case reproduced its five-second timeout locally.
It combines import, repeated complete ZIP comparisons, editing, export/reopen
and undo. Its case-specific observation budget is now 30 seconds. All equality
assertions remain; production SVG parsing/rendering and runtime budgets are
unchanged. The focused default-timeout run passes all 32 tests across flips,
group-shape rotation and SVG resources. This resolves these two test failures
locally; it does not claim remote CI success. Evidence: scratch
work/ci-shape-svg-{before,after,final}.log and the retained CI failure log.

### Cell-local border and margin contributions (2026-09-24)

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.4.38 (tblBorders), 17.4.66 (tcBorders),
17.4.68 (tcMar), and 17.4.80 (trHeight) govern the relevant declarations.
The independent merged-adjacent-borders fixture measures the native reference's row layout;
this is not evidence of a conflict with an explicit normative inset formula.
Row writing-top reserves now combine each cell's margin and effective top
border before taking the maximum. Bottom reserves combine each cell's margin
with its resolved local bottom segment, including a stronger opposing border.
The existing border-resolution pass supplies segment ownership; global
half-stroke floors and invisible none-border spacing remain intact.

Sixteen independently authored pages vary merged cells, adjacent borders,
outer borders, padding, and automatic/minimum row heights. The original bug
combined padding from one column with a border in another, moving two controls'
headings about 1.6 pt and following text about 3 pt. An own-border-only candidate
failed existing opposing-border controls and was rejected. The shipped approach
passes those controls as well as the new reference positions. Fixture border child
ordering was corrected after schema validation and the native reference regenerated.
Validation: 91 focused unit tests, 27 browser regressions, and production build.
The corrected fixture is also rerun independently and its exports schema checked.
No dependency, font asset, or optimization change is introduced.

### Native-font outline advances

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.3.2.26 (rFonts), 17.3.2.38 (sz), 17.3.2.19
(kern), and 17.3.2.35 (spacing) define the relevant run declarations. Native
fonts can contain small bitmap strikes whose browser advances differ from
the native reference's outline-based placement. This is a rendering implementation correction,
not a demonstrated contradiction of a normative OOXML layout formula.

Native face/size combinations with pixel-rounded sample advances are measured
and painted at a common outline em and transformed back to their authored size.
A cached probe checks five Latin glyph advances without spacing or kerning and
confirms that their outline sum differs. This is coverage for detected strikes,
not a claim to detect every script-specific bitmap font. Other native faces
retain normal-size painting, with the existing fractional measurement-em
correction also applied to painting. Kerning eligibility is resolved at the original
point size; absolute character/justification spacing and text-outline thickness
are scaled with the em and restored by the paint transform. Line-box metrics,
source offsets, font declarations and exported sizes remain unchanged. The
bundled outline-only Noto faces retain their existing paint path and fractional
measurement correction. Font alternatives are resolved consistently for both
measurement and painting. Detection adds five, or at most six, measurements once
per native face/size between font loads; subsequent fragment measurements retain
one shaping call. No font files or dependencies are introduced. A broad initial
outline-paint candidate reduced Calibri Light 8 pt synthetic-bold ink below its
existing native tolerance and was rejected; the selective path preserves it.

The independently authored outline-text-advances control covers three families,
four point sizes, and regular/bold faces on 24 pages. Native END-marker origins,
all line wraps and baselines, painted marker positions, caret hit tests and
edit/export/undo/reopen are compared. Four Cambria cases previously differed
by up to 7.38 pt; outline measurements reduce their errors below 0.14 pt. The
other controls retain effectively unchanged advances. Native PDF rounding is
bounded by a 0.3 pt comparison tolerance (largest unchanged error 0.248 pt).
Existing paint tests inspect transformed visible outline widths; a raw canvas
lineWidth is no longer itself a page-space width for scaled native glyphs.

Validation: 193 unit checks passed during development; the 64 affected checks
passed again after the final detection/paint refinement. All 43 final browser
checks pass (26 native-font/rendering, 17 editing controls), as do the production
build, license gate, and XML schemas for source/control exports. The unchanged
May Riley source now matches the native reference's one-page layout and completes its full
edit/export/reopen/exact-undo workflow. See corpus review #310 for evidence.

## Contextual after-spacing across neighboring table cells

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.3.1.9 (`contextualSpacing`) and 17.3.1.33 (`spacing`)
describe suppression against a following paragraph with the same style, without
explicitly defining cell-boundary adjacency. Independent 48-page reference
controls establish that a cell's final paragraph compares with the first source
paragraph of the next cell in the same physical row. The final cell instead uses
the previously recorded implicit Normal-style row boundary; the next row's actual
style does not replace that boundary. This refines the earlier cell-ending rule:
Normal is not the comparison style at every cell edge.

Layout now carries the next cell's style into final-paragraph measurement and
suppresses after-spacing only when the style identity matches. It preserves the
stored spacing/contextual flags, honors `allowSpaceOfSameStyleInTable`, and
recomputes when a neighboring cell's paragraph style changes. No document name,
text or template-specific exception is used. Original XML controls, native PDF,
reference hashes and all text origins are in `tests/fixtures/cell-next-context`.

Validation: 363 unit checks across 36 files, 18 browser scenarios, XML schema
checks for the control and exported documents, and production build/license gate
pass. Corpus source #313 now matches all three reviewed reference pages and retains
its full edit/export/undo/reopen workflow.


## VML page picture backgrounds

Part 1 §17.2.1 (`background`) and Part 4 §§19.1.2.2 (`v:background`),
19.1.2.5 (`v:fill`) govern document-wide backgrounds. Embedded PNG/JPEG images
with frame/tile fills now resolve through the same relationship, content-type,
pixel-decoding and asset-budget gates as inline pictures. Rendering paints the
image pattern above the base page color and below page stories, body content and
decorations. Every section receives the same document-wide picture background.
It does not affect layout, selection or editable offsets. Source VML, metadata,
relationships and image bytes survive unrelated edits and exact undo.

Reference/spec divergence: Part 4 §19.1.3.4 defines frame as stretching the image to
its shape. The native reference instead repeats a frame page background at 600 source
pixels/inch in the native PDF reference, ignoring encoded image DPI. Explicit
tile backgrounds use intrinsic DPI and round their physical dimensions up to a
600-DPI pixel. Both start at the page origin. The independent five-document,
ten-page page-picture-background control proves these rules and retains native
PDF pattern dimensions and rendered color samples. This is native compatibility,
not a claim about every reference printer/export configuration.

The supported subset retains recolor, color2, title, screen-size and white
black-and-white-mode metadata; the native recolor control does not transform the
saved RGB pixels again. Unsupported fill modes, opacity/transform attributes,
external relationships and non-PNG/JPEG textures remain guarded. Changing page
color removes the picture background; explicit removal and undo are supported.
Creating a new picture background is not exposed. Native calibration of alpha
compositing and additional VML options remains pending. This does not implement
the general VML shape model, gradients or handmade art borders.

## Section page borders

ECMA-376 Part 1 section 17.6.10 (`pgBorders`), its four side elements and shared
CT_Border attributes govern page decoration. Import, page geometry and export now
retain page/text origin, all/first/not-first section-page visibility, front/back
ordering, per-side widths/spaces/colors and header/footer exclusion settings.
Borders do not consume body layout space. Text-relative frames include active
header/footer distances unless the corresponding exclusion setting is enabled.
Unrelated edits retain the original XML and exact undo restores the package.

Original controls in `tests/fixtures/page-borders` contain 49 native reference pages
covering positioning, section-local visibility, overlap/default ordering,
header/footer exclusions, independent sides and unequal widths. Native ordinary
line widths quantize to 600 dpi, with a one-unit hairline for omitted/zero widths;
large authored sizes are retained. CT_Border permits out-of-range reassignment,
so this records native reference behavior without claiming a mandatory-spec contradiction.

Single-line native corner coverage is verified, including removal of pale seams
between independently antialiased triangles. Other recognized line patterns reuse
existing paragraph-border painting but still need broader native page-corner
coverage. Art borders, visible shadows and unsupported attributes remain guarded;
best-effort opening is read-only. Continuous-section page ownership, parity filler
pages and alignBordersAndEdges combinations need additional native controls.
There is no claim of complete page-border OOXML support.


## First-cell paragraph keep and row splitting

ECMA-376 Part 1 section 17.3.1.15 defines `keepNext` between paragraphs and chains.
The native reference additionally interprets the first paragraph of the first cell as
preventing a row split when that paragraph has keepNext. This includes an empty
paragraph; flags on later paragraphs or other cells do not produce that row keep.
It does not chain a short row to its following row. An oversized kept row moves
to a fresh page and may then split. Thirteen independently authored controls (27
native pages), including horizontal spans and explicit off cases, are retained in
`tests/fixtures/first-cell-keep` with native PDFs and source/PDF hashes.

Table pagination now recognizes the resolved first-paragraph flag at the leading
grid column alongside existing cantSplit and delayed-cell-start behavior. The
source paragraph property remains unchanged and editable; removing it reflows the
row, export/reopen retains the edit and undo restores the original package.
The special row interpretation is native behavior beyond the clause's explicit
paragraph wording, not a template-name exception. Broader combinations with
vertical merges, omitted leading cells, nesting and compatibility modes still
need additional native controls; no exhaustive conformance claim is made.

Validation: 73 unit checks across eight files and 29 browser scenarios pass.
Original controls, corpus exports and browser regression exports pass XML schemas;
production build/license gate pass. Corpus #320 now matches all five reference pages
and passes no-edit preservation, insertion, export/reopen and exact undo.

## Multi-page floating tables: numeric body positions (2026-09-24)

ECMA-376 Part 1 section 17.4.57 defines tblpPr positioning and the logical anchor
at the next regular paragraph. Sections 17.4.6 (cantSplit), 17.4.59 (tblHeader)
and 17.3.1.15 (keepNext) supply the associated row/header/paragraph properties.
The native reference's pagination extends the simple following-paragraph anchor description:
the first fragment uses the source-position cursor while the following paragraph
can land on the final table page. This native behavior is implemented generically,
without source names or document-content special cases.

One top-level floating table with numeric page/margin/text positions can span
body pages. Repeated headers and split rows use the ordinary table paginator;
following text resumes beside or below the final fragment. Native compatibility
controls distinguish first-page capacity, modern initial page advances, legacy
translated fragments, border-dependent paper-edge clamping, horizontal origins
and wrap clearance. Floating work is attached to real paragraph segments so it
does not break keepNext chains or paragraph-gap context. Cell/source positions
remain authoritative for caret access, editing and retained-package export.

Thirty-three original controls and 71 native reference pages cover these behaviors,
with source/PDF hashes and native positions. Their browser comparisons pass at
0.15 pt horizontally and 0.2 pt vertically; continuation-page editing, no-edit
preservation, unrelated-part preservation, exact undo and edited reopening pass.
The source controls and browser/corpus exports pass XML schemas. Production build
and the 199-package license check pass.

Multi-page aligned positions, documents with multiple top-level floating tables,
booklet pages and header/footer anchors retain a layout guard and safe read-only
fallback. Broader collision, alignment, section/story and interaction combinations
remain in scope; this is not exhaustive floating-table conformance. Single-page
floating-table behavior remains covered by the existing independent suites.

### Signed paragraph indents beyond the paper

ECMA-376 Part 1, 5th edition, §17.3.1.12 (`ind`) defines negative indentation
relative to the text margins; §17.18.81 supplies signed twip measurements. The
local specification's printed pp. 219-225 describe this independently of physical
page clipping. Native reference controls confirm that a positive-width writing area
can extend beyond either paper edge, including a wholly off-paper aligned line.
This is supported behavior consistent with signed margins, not a discovered
reference/spec contradiction. The previous renderer's physical-edge rejection was
an implementation restriction.

The renderer retains declared paragraph edges for line breaking and alignment.
Canvas page surfaces clip ink. Carets clamp to the physical horizontal page edge,
selection rectangles intersect the paper, and pointer/vertical navigation skips
wholly invisible lines. Source offsets and text remain intact for keyboard and
accessible editing. Existing exhausted-body-width validation remains; exhausted
cell rules are unchanged. Broader unsupported paragraph features keep their
existing guards.

Evidence: six-page original `tests/fixtures/body-overflow-indents/control.docx`,
native PDF and hashed `reference.json`, generated by
`tools/body_overflow_indent_fixture.py` and `tools/record_body_overflow_indents.py`.
Browser comparisons check line contents, wrapping, alignment and baselines at
0.15/0.2-point tolerances, plus click/edit/export/undo/reopen and signed-indent
preservation. Unit checks cover both fully off-paper directions, partial
selections and vertical navigation. Prior tests expecting rejection solely for
an off-paper body indent now assert the native behavior; exhausted-width rejection
is retained. Validation: 155 unit checks, five browser scenarios, nine exports
through schemas, production build and the 199-package license gate pass.

### Table-cell text-direction allocation evidence (integration pending)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.72 defines table-cell text direction and inheritance;
§17.18.93 defines its values. The independent cell-text-direction controls now
also isolate automatic row allocation in btLr/tbRl cells. The native reference uses the
final paragraph mark's line formatting and after-spacing for the physical row's
minimum, not the accumulated rotated text extent. Before-spacing, preceding
paragraphs and run size do not affect that allocation in the measured cases.
Overflowing rotated text stays clipped. Exact-spacing controls agree with an
empty horizontal terminal paragraph; automatic spacing has additional native
leading specific to rotation (0.36pt/0.60pt in the measured cases). Those values
are observations, not hard-coded corrections. Broader metric/spacing boundaries
and the responsible reference/spec interpretation remain under investigation.

The hashed automatic, height and height-horizontal fixtures and native-evidence
tests record this behavior separately from implementation tests. The production
import guard remains until allocation, painting, clipping, caret/selection,
nested-cell/page behavior and round-trip editing are integrated and verified.
No full text-direction support or spec divergence beyond the measured behavior
is claimed by these controls.

### Rotated terminal-mark height calculation

The pending table text-direction implementation now has a separately tested
minimum-height calculation. Additional paired native reference controls at three
fonts and seven sizes (6 through 200pt), together with minimum-spacing controls,
resolve the earlier automatic-leading discrepancy: natural terminal-mark height
plus 1/32 em matches native row allocation. Automatic multiples scale that sum;
minimum spacing takes its maximum with the declared point height. Exact nonzero
spacing uses the declaration without extra leading. Before-spacing is ignored
for this allocation; resolved after-spacing remains. This is measured reference
behavior, not a normative formula supplied by §17.4.72 or a claimed standards
violation. The function leaves ordinary horizontal font metrics untouched.

cell-text-direction-height.spec.js compares the calculation against 49 native
rotated rows within 0.15pt, including the earlier independent content/paragraph
controls. The fixture authoring code, source, reference PDF and hashed border/text
reference are retained. Production integration and editing remain pending;
passing these isolated measurements does not establish rotated-cell support.

### Rotated-cell layout integration checkpoint (not enabled for import)

Table allocation now uses the measured terminal mark for btLr/tbRl model cells
and defers source-text layout until their physical rectangles are final. The
final layout retains local coordinates with a quarter-turn matrix, physical
bounds and unchanged source offsets. Ordinary table layouts take the existing
path. Import still rejects these directions until painting, source interaction
and editing/export are integrated. Split physical cells, nested tables within
rotated cells and hidden terminal marks remain explicitly guarded and in scope.

Twenty-one independent native pages pass the integrated source/wrapping/visible
origin tests. The twenty-page height matrix remains an explicit expected failure
for three tbRl automatic-spacing X origins (0.192–0.209pt versus a 0.15pt bound).
Rotated text measurement now includes the 1/32-em extra leading; equal ascent/
descent distribution matches other measured origins but is not yet certified
for the failing cases. No shared horizontal font metrics or fidelity tolerances
were changed. This checkpoint is not full rendering or editing conformance.

### Rotated-cell paint and pointer geometry (guarded checkpoint)

The current model-level implementation uses the existing text/run-decoration
painter under a cell-local quarter-turn transform, applying physical page/cell
clips first. Pointer hit testing inversely maps to the source reading axis.
Caret/selection rectangles map back to physical coordinates and retain clipping;
rotated carets expose width as well as height. Existing horizontal behavior is
covered by layout/bidi/table/alignment unit and browser regressions.

Independent control and automatic-row fixtures now have twelve visually checked
native/Canvas page pairs. Browser tests require ink in each rotated cell, verify
source hit positions and caret/selection bounds, click the rendered text, type,
and restore source plus exact PNGs through undo. These models restore directions
in tests after the guarded importer reads a diagnostic copy. They do not certify
original-direction DOCX import/export. Keyboard navigation, image/link behavior,
paragraph decorations, split/nested/hidden-mark cases and the three previously
recorded tbRl baseline deviations remain unfinished and in scope.

### Rotated-cell character keys (guarded checkpoint)

For the quarter-turn cell directions in ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.72,
physical Up/Down now follow the local character axis: Up advances `btLr`,
Down advances `tbRl`. Native reference key input on the independent control confirms
both forward Shift-selections; `native-keyboard-observations.json` records the
source hash and observations. `native-navigation.json` separately records Selection
API commands, whose MoveUp/MoveDown behavior is not equivalent to keyboard input.
This is an interaction observation, not an OOXML keyboard requirement or a
claimed specification divergence. Browser checks exercise both directions,
selection extension/collapse and unchanged source text. Cross-line and boundary
navigation, modified keys and bidi cases still require native evidence and work.

### Rotated-cell cross-line keys (guarded checkpoint)

Native physical-key observations on page four of the independent control show
Right advancing a local line for `btLr`, and Left for `tbRl`. The editor now
chooses the next visible local line in the same physical cell and maps the
preserved local reading-axis position to its source stop. The remembered axis
is reset when moving between ordinary text and rotated cell contexts. Browser
checks compare the native first-line selection verbatim and move forward/back
through all four wrapped lines in both rotations.

Boundary handling is not complete: the native reference can select the terminal cell marker
after the last line, while this checkpoint clamps to the first/last source edge
when no visible adjacent line exists. Modified keys, differently aligned
paragraphs, bidi and repeated/split-cell navigation need further evidence.
The importer guard remains; this does not certify full rotated-cell editing.

### Read-only DOCX rotation preview

Best-effort import now retains `lrTb`, `btLr` and `tbRl` on table cells
(ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.4.72), including base/conditional table-style inheritance
and direct overrides. Strict editable import still rejects these declarations.
The read-only package retains every original part and rejects edited export.

Supported structures use the same local layout and painter as the native
controls. A typed unsupported-rotation layout error triggers one read-only
horizontal approximation using copied table models; the source model remains
unchanged. Hidden marks, tables inside rotated cells and cells split across
physical pages still need full rotated support. Other errors are not swallowed.
Style precedence is covered by independently constructed import checks; native
style-direction comparisons, along with all prior editing/fidelity gaps, remain
in scope. The original #338 now previews fifteen pages, matching the native reference's page
count, with all fifteen page pairs visually inspected and page six at full size.

### Rotated-cell inline pictures: native discrepancy identified

Five independently authored controls combine `lrTb`, `btLr` and `tbRl` with
linked text and repository-authored blue/orange inline pictures. The native reference retains
the authored picture orientation and physical dimensions in every cell, including
reversed aspect ratio, center/bottom alignment and surrounding inline text.
The current engine instead rotates picture geometry and paint with the glyphs.
This is an engine/reference discrepancy. §17.4.72 describes text flow; these controls
do not establish a contradiction in the standard's picture requirements.

Native PDF image objects and hyperlink annotations are retained separately in
`pictures-reference.json`, with DOCX/PDF hashes. Picture sizes remain 36×18pt
(or 18×36pt in the tall case). For both rotated directions, center/bottom cell
alignment changes physical X while physical Y stays fixed. The `A ` inline
prefix advances physical Y by 9.45pt in both directions. Thus merely undoing the
bitmap's rotation is insufficient: layout occupancy, placement, selection and
hit testing must share the picture's distinct physical frame.

Three native-evidence tests pass. Five browser comparisons explicitly record
the existing rotated-picture failures, after verifying horizontal picture size
and Y. They also expose a separate 6pt horizontal-origin mismatch, retained in
the comparisons without subtracting it from native coordinates. These are not
five successful fidelity tests. The renderer/hit-test
fix remains open; no production behavior changes in this evidence checkpoint.

### Upright inline pictures in quarter-turn cells

The rotated-cell layout now reserves inline picture height along the reading
axis and width across it, while retaining the original DrawingML dimensions,
rotation and effects metadata. Pictures use a separate physical frame: both
`btLr` and `tbRl` advance their picture Y from the cell's physical top. Painting
cancels only the cell text transform, preserving the outer canvas transform and
cell clip. Image hit testing, picture hyperlinks and picture selection use the
same frame. Selection across disjoint wrapping intervals retains the cell
transform instead of losing it when flattening the intervals.

The five independently authored native controls now agree in physical picture
size, Y, and cross-axis alignment changes. Actual canvas samples verify upright
blue-left/orange-right panels in every cell; picture links and selections follow
the visible pictures. The separate 6pt table-origin discrepancy remains in all
three directions and is explicitly asserted before the five expected fidelity
failures. No native coordinates are rewritten. These controls establish the
basic inline case; own picture rotations/effect extents, exact-line clipping,
multiple wrapped pictures and rotated-cell editing still require expanded
native comparisons. Strict rotated-cell import remains read-only. ECMA-376
Part 1 §17.4.72 governs cell text direction; this fixes an engine/reference mismatch,
not a newly established reference/spec divergence.

### Companion table geometry styles (`stylesWithEffects`)

The six-point origin mismatch in the rotated-picture controls came from the
companion styles part, not cell rotation, compatibility mode or first-table
placement. The original fixtures retained a Normal Table definition there
while their primary styles part contained no table styles. Removing only the
companion's table definitions makes the native reference move to the app's old origin.
The fixture's native coordinates were retained unchanged for the fix.

Independent controls establish selective resolution: the primary requested or
default table style wins when present; otherwise the native reference can use the companion's
matching/default table geometry style. Each inheritance chain stays in its
selected part. An empty primary definition does not acquire companion properties.
Paragraph/character styles and table text formatting continue to use the primary
collection. The importer follows this distinction, reads the companion via its
internal relationship rather than a prescribed filename, and preserves both
original parts through edits/export. It parses the companion only if a table
requires fallback, and reuses the parsed root for subsequent tables.

Sources: ECMA-376 Part 1 §11.3.12 (Style Definitions), §17.7 (styles), and
[MS-DOCX §2.1.1](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-docx/6d73a0c5-2d94-461e-81c8-843ad0e911a6).
The extension describes a copied style part without spelling out the selective
precedence above. This is native extension behavior, not a demonstrated normative
contradiction. Two original one-page controls retain native text/font evidence
and 36 picture frames. Both full page pairs and all five rotated-picture content
pairs were inspected. The five former picture expected failures now pass absolute
native coordinates within .15pt, along with paint, selection and link checks.
Other rotated-cell gaps remain open. A scratch probe also found built-in Normal
Table normalization of a nonzero companion indent; that requires further work
and is not covered by the custom-style inheritance claim.

The schema checker now validates companion style parts by their content type,
in addition to the primary style parts. Native controls, no-edit downloads and
edited exports therefore include those parts in schema validation.

## Straight connector preset geometry

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.9.18 (`prstGeom`) and the supplied DrawingML preset
definitions define `straightConnector1` as an unfilled path from (l,t) to (r,b).
It now uses the same retained unit path and physical pen handling as `line`,
including one-zero-axis transforms allowed by ST_PositiveCoordinate. DrawingML
transforms (§20.1.7) retain reflections, rotations and group coordinate systems.
No source preset is rewritten, and connector endpoint/lock metadata remains
subject to the existing atomic-object rules. No reference/spec divergence was found.

Eight independent standalone controls cover horizontal, vertical, rotated,
reflected, frame-scaled and inline placement. Twelve group controls cover
child/display zero axes, offsets, scaling, nesting and rotation. Native reference PDFs,
hashed ink bounds/endpoints and original generators are retained under
`tests/fixtures/straight-flat-lines` and `straight-connector-groups`.
Browser checks compare native ink and physical strokes, selection, retained
packages, surrounding edits, exact undo and editable reopening.

The separately recorded `straight-oval-lines` controls establish oval
end markers (§20.1.8 headEnd/tailEnd); their implementation is described below.
Point-sized lines, malformed extents, unrecognized presets and unsupported
adjustments also remain guarded. These describe implementation gaps rather
than a claim that every guarded construct is schema-invalid.

## Oval DrawingML line ends

CT_LineEndProperties and ST_LineEndType/Width/Length in ECMA-376 DrawingML
define headEnd/tailEnd and their qualitative size enums. Oval ends now render
on open retained shape paths, including straight connectors, cubic/quadratic
paths and grouped drawings. Closed contours omit them. The reader validates
type, width, length, content and attributes; other visible end types remain
guarded. Source geometry and marker declarations remain immutable XML.

Independent reference controls establish physical size factors 2/3/5 for
sm/med/lg. For positive authored pen p in points the marker base is
max(p, 2, 0.48/p); explicit zero uses 0.24pt. This includes counterintuitive
enlargement below 0.24pt. The source pen, not a display-clamped pen, determines
that arithmetic. Group scales do not stretch marker sizes. Curves use the
endpoint chord reaching half a marker length, found in transformed physical
coordinates; repeated curve controls and closed subpaths are handled separately.
The specification does not quantify this sizing or curved-marker orientation,
so these are documented reference compatibility details rather than a claimed
normative contradiction.

Stroke and markers share an ink surface before the line paint is composited,
avoiding dark overlaps with alpha. Marker bounds participate in raster bounds,
flat-line hit testing/selection and collapsed-group selection. No surrounding
document-flow space is invented for a zero-height/width drawing. The original
resource limits remain active; surfaces are allocated only for marked strokes.

The 36 independently authored oval-markers controls plus eight straight-oval
controls retain native PDFs, exact source/PDF hashes and recorded ellipse/ink
evidence. They cover small/medium/large dimensions, zero/thin/thick pens,
head/tail, two curves, closure, scaling/rotation/collapse, reflection, inline
placement, alpha and dash paint. Tests exercise native geometry, visible ink,
selection, edits/export/reopen, unrelated-part preservation and exact undo.
Unsupported marker types and unverified exotic effect/compound combinations
remain outside the conformance claim.

## Off-page flowchart connector preset

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.9.18 (`prstGeom`), §20.1.10.56 (`ST_ShapeType`) and its
accompanying presetShapeDefinitions.xml define `flowChartOffpageConnector` as a
closed five-sided shape with shoulders at four-fifths height. The renderer uses
that fixed path and the specified text rectangle above its tip. Existing shape
fill, outline, transform, text and package-preservation paths apply. Adjustment
guides are not defined for this preset and remain guarded.

Eight independently authored native controls cover wide/narrow extents, flips
and a quarter-turn. Native/browser colored ink is checked through editing, undo
and export/reopen; existing cloud and primitive geometry regressions also pass.
The native controls agree with the standard; no divergence is claimed. This
addition does not enable other flowchart presets, halfFrame or ribbon2.
See tests/fixtures/offpage-connectors and tools/offpage_connector_fixture.py.

## Half-frame preset geometry

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.9.18 (`prstGeom`), §20.1.10.56 (`ST_ShapeType`) and its
accompanying preset definitions specify `halfFrame`. The renderer supports both
adjustment guides, their default thicknesses, the asymmetric pin limits and
six-vertex outline. The inner corner cannot cross the diagonal joining the two
outer tips. The text rectangle covers the full shape. Existing fills, strokes,
flips, rotation and retained OOXML serialization apply. Invalid adjustment
formulas, unknown adjustment properties and zero-dimensional geometry remain
guarded. This does not enable arbitrary shape editing or other frame presets.

Eight independently authored native controls cover wide/narrow extents,
default/negative/zero/oversized adjustments and transforms. The native/browser
ink comparison passes through insertion, undo and export/reopen. The native reference
agrees with the supplied standard; no divergence is claimed. See
`tests/fixtures/half-frames` and `tools/half_frame_fixture.py`.

## Ribbon2 geometry and folded-face shading

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.9.18 (`prstGeom`), §20.1.10.56 (`ST_ShapeType`) and its
accompanying preset definitions describe `ribbon2`. The renderer evaluates its
two pinned adjustments, elliptical folds, tails, separate outline and central
text rectangle. At zero fold height the arcs collapse to line segments. Shape
transforms and original DrawingML remain preserved through unrelated edits.

The fold path uses `darkenLess`. §20.1.10.37 (`ST_PathFillMode`) describes that
mode qualitatively; it does not prescribe a numeric transform. Native reference
controls establish approximately 205/255 encoded-RGB scaling with retained
alpha. This is native compatibility behavior, not a demonstrated contradiction
of the standard, and is distinct from the linear-light `shade` color modifier.
The fill-only canvas filter also applies to supported gradients, patterns and
pictures; it is restored before outlines or other drawing content are painted.
Ordinary paths do not acquire a filter or extra canvas save/restore operation.

Twenty-four independent native shapes cover adjustment limits, wide/narrow
geometry, flips/rotation, eight solid colors, translucent solids, linear
gradients, two-color patterns and stretched original bitmap fills. Browser
checks compare native ink and exact interior colors through insertion, undo
and export/reopen. The mixed-fill PDF is sampled directly at 96 DPI to preserve
native dense-pattern sampling; supersampling then downscaling introduces a
separate moire artifact. The retained PDF is never altered for comparison.

Other ribbon presets, other path shading modes and general custom-path
`darkenLess` import remain unimplemented. Zero dimensions and malformed guides
remain guarded. See `tests/fixtures/ribbons` and `src/engine/ribbon-geometry.js`.

## Document-default color in WordprocessingML shapes

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.7.5.1 (`docDefaults`), §17.3.2.6 (`color`) and §20.1.4.1.17
(`fontRef`) apply to this interaction. An explicit document-default color must
survive the shape font-reference fallback when no later color is declared.
Paragraph, character and direct declarations still override it; explicit `auto`
still resolves against the shape font-reference color after the cascade.
Font family/size defaults and non-shape paragraph behavior are unchanged.

An independently authored 36-case native variant adds `112233` at document
scope to the existing white/red/no-fontRef matrix. The native reference uses that color
for all omitted-color cases, retains fontRef for later automatic declarations,
and retains explicit blue. The original 36-case matrix remains a regression
control. Both are checked through native glyph comparison, body edits, unrelated
part preservation, exact undo and export/reopen. No new standard divergence is
claimed. See `tests/fixtures/shape-default-color` and its generator/recorder.

### DrawingML donut preset geometry

ECMA-376 Part 1, 20.1.9.18 (`prstGeom`), 20.1.10.56 (`ST_ShapeType`),
and the accompanying donut preset definition specify two oppositely wound
elliptical contours. The engine now evaluates the optional `adj` guide (default
25000, pinned to 0–50000) and scales thickness by the shorter extent. It retains
the transparent hole, both outlines and degenerate inner contours at the
limits. The text rectangle uses the outer ellipse's 45-degree points and is
independent of thickness. Existing group transforms, fill and outline painting
apply unchanged; no source XML is rewritten merely for rendering.

Eight original native reference controls cover defaults, clamp limits, negative and
excessive adjustments, narrow ellipses, flips and rotation. Whole-page native
pixel comparison passes through insertion, export, exact undo and reopening.
The independently exported PDF and reference hashes are retained in
`tests/fixtures/donuts`, with original generator and recorder scripts in tools.
These controls show no reference/spec divergence. Zero-dimensional donut geometry
is rejected; support for other unsupported presets is not implied.

### Inline page and column breaks in table cells

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.3.1 (`br`, including the `type` attribute and reference
to §17.18.4 `ST_BrType`) describes restarting subsequent text according to the
break type. Independent reference controls show a compatibility divergence
inside table cells: inline page and column breaks produce no visible advance,
line break or pagination. Text on both sides joins on the same line. A separate
paragraph containing only such a break still occupies an empty paragraph line.

The renderer follows that behavior in cell line layout and intrinsic width
measurement, preserving source characters, caret offsets and XML. These controls
do not contribute glyph metrics, decoration or word-break opportunities. Ordinary
text-wrapping breaks retain their existing line behavior; body page/column breaks
retain their existing pagination. Insertion, adjacent editing, exact undo,
unrelated-part preservation and editable export/reopen are covered by tests.
Native fixtures, PDF/PNG hashes and measured text origins are retained under
`tests/fixtures/cell-breaks` with original generator and recorder scripts.

Paragraph property §17.3.1.23 (`pageBreakBefore`) is not an inline break. The
native controls move the table when it is set on the first cell paragraph but
do not move the second paragraph in the tested table. That feature remains
guarded pending its own pagination implementation. The current native matrix
does not establish exhaustive merged/nested-table or cross-page interactions.

### Inline pictures inside retained shape text

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.3.9 (`drawing`) and §20.4 place inline DrawingML objects
in run content and allow them to affect line height. Retained
`wps:txbx/w:txbxContent` now accepts inline pictures through the existing image
reader and paragraph layout. The shape painter draws their decoded assets using
the reserved inline frame, crop, opacity and local transformations. Group scale
is removed before text/picture painting, preserving physical inline units;
shape rotation and text-frame/cell clips remain active. Original drawing XML,
relationships and image bytes remain unchanged through unrelated body edits.

Eight independent native reference pages cover scaling, nesting, shape rotation,
center anchoring, clipping and cropped/flipped picture content. The native
comparison and edit/export/undo/reopen controls live in
`tests/fixtures/textbox-pictures`. No new reference/spec divergence is observed.
Floating pictures and separately editing text box contents remain outside this
supported path. Reflected-group text is covered below. The native matrix does not certify all
nested field-dependent drawings or rotated inline-picture clipping combinations.

### Reflected text boxes and inline drawing paint order

ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.7.5 (`xfrm`, grouped objects) defines reflection about the
group bounds center. The native reference transforms text frames but does not mirror
glyphs: horizontal reflection keeps readable text, vertical reflection produces
a half turn. The painter cancels the mirrored local x axis for retained text,
composing nested group transforms with the existing child vertical-flip behavior.
Inline pictures share the text orientation and preserve their physical units.

This is a reference compatibility specialization: applying raw group reflection to
text ink would mirror glyphs, contradicting the independent native controls.
The group-transform clause alone does not explicitly specify this exception.
Twelve original pages in `tests/fixtures/reflected-textboxes` cover horizontal,
vertical, double and nested reflection, rotated children, nonuniform group scales,
and a vertically flipped child. The original eight text-box picture controls
remain covered. Collapsed groups containing text and upright vertically reflected
individual shapes retain their separate guards. Text-box contents remain atomic.

The same controls establish that inline drawing ink extending outside its layout
frame overlays both preceding and following paragraph text. Inline drawings now
paint after glyphs/decorations within each page story, preserving existing cell
and line clips, transforms and image selection highlights. §17.3.3.9 and §20.4
define inline drawing content and layout; observed paint order is separate from
layout extents, which are unchanged. Native comparison checks dark glyph presence
and picture colors. Edit/export/undo/reopen checks preserve unrelated parts and
retained drawing XML. These controls do not certify every interaction between
multiple overlapping inline drawings or upright text.
