A rejected paragraph property no longer discards sibling spacing, indentation, alignment or valid numbering references. A rejected numbering reference is isolated from the remaining paragraph defaults. Complete duplicate-property groups remain rejected together, and the surviving combination is revalidated. Strict import and original package/download preservation remain unchanged; structural style errors, unresolved interactions and later effective-format validation can still require broader fallback.

Independent [paragraph-style controls](../tests/fixtures/style-paragraph-recovery/README.md) cover unsupported diagonal-cross shading in those three contexts and in combination, with supported mixed content. All five fixtures pass transitional schemas. Unit controls additionally verify retained inherited numbering, rejected numbering-reference revisions and duplicate groups; browser comparisons check full canvas pixels/body geometry and original-byte downloads. ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.7, 17.7.5, 17.7.6, 17.3.1.31 and 17.3.1.19 define the underlying styles, shading and numbering-reference semantics. The omitted features remain unsupported; this is preview recovery, not native reference rendering equivalence or a change to the standard's formatting rules.

### Direct paragraph/run property recovery (2026-09-29)

The grouped read-only property recovery used by styles now also applies to direct paragraph properties/numbering references, paragraph-mark formatting, run formatting and content-control input formatting. A rejected direct property no longer immediately flattens the paragraph or replaces an entire mixed-content run with text-only fallback. Supported sibling formatting, text and inline pictures can survive together in body content, cells and headers/footers. The shared helper preserves the source node, probes complete duplicate-property groups and validates the surviving combination. Strict import and original-package downloads remain unchanged. Unsupported inline structure, later effective-format validation, field-state errors and unisolated property interactions still have broader fallback boundaries.

Independent [direct-property controls](../tests/fixtures/direct-property-recovery/README.md) place text/picture/text runs in the body, a cell and a header, then introduce unsupported shading in run, paragraph and paragraph-mark properties individually and together. All five packages pass transitional schemas. Unit checks verify supported formatting and actual image runs after model restyling; browser comparisons check full canvas pixels/body geometry against the matched supported control and exact original download bytes. ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.3.1, 17.3.2 and 17.3.3 define the relevant paragraph properties, run properties and run content. The omitted shading remains unsupported; this recovery policy is not a claim of native reference rendering equivalence.

### Same-run drawing recovery (2026-09-29)

Read-only import now contains typed unsupported drawing failures within the drawing child of a run. Supported text and pictures before and after it keep their formatting and paragraph context instead of being rolled back to a text-only run approximation. This includes selected MCE branches containing one drawing; branch selection itself is unchanged, and a failing selected feature does not trigger a different choice/fallback. Strict import and original package downloads remain unchanged. Non-drawing alternate content, unrelated errors and later layout/effective-format failures retain existing fallback paths. The omitted drawing does not yet reserve a visible placeholder or implement its unsupported semantics.

Independent [same-run drawing controls](../tests/fixtures/run-drawing-recovery/README.md) put an unsupported DrawingML alpha-bi-level effect between two supported pictures and surrounding text in body, cell and header runs, directly and through AlternateContent. All three packages pass transitional schemas in the standard MCE view. Unit checks verify retained content, formatting and source parts; browser comparisons check full canvas pixels/body geometry against a control omitting only the affected drawings and exact original downloads. Relevant sources are ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.3.3 and 20, and Part 3 markup compatibility. This is local preview recovery, not alpha-bi-level support or native reference rendering equivalence.

### Sized inline drawing placeholders (2026-09-29)

After a typed unsupported drawing failure, read-only import now retains an unambiguous unrotated inline frame with valid supported dimensions and effect extents. A neutral vector placeholder makes the missing drawing visible while preserving the space occupied by its declared frame. The placeholder uses session-only asset metadata and allocates no source bitmap. Original package bytes and downloads remain untouched. Floating/anchored placement, rotated transforms, conflicting extents, invalid dimensions and dimensions beyond existing limits remain outside this subset and retain the previous omission behavior. Bitmap decode failures on otherwise imported images still use their existing path.

The independent [same-run controls](../tests/fixtures/run-drawing-recovery/README.md) now include a supported reserved-image counterpart. Browser checks compare body and header line geometry to that control, verify visible pixel differences, and check exact original downloads; screenshots are reviewed for the placeholder and unaffected content. Unit checks cover frame/effect extents, source-node preservation, asset identity and invalid/ambiguous geometry. The new control passes transitional schemas. ECMA-376 Part 1 section 20.4 (WordprocessingML drawing anchoring) defines the inline frame; the neutral missing-drawing symbol is an explicit preview approximation, not native reference rendering equivalence or support for the omitted drawing feature.

## Hyperlink destination recovery (2026-09-29)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.16.22 separates the hyperlink wrapper's destination attributes from its contained run content; §17.3.2 defines that run content and formatting. In best-effort previews, an unsupported destination or invalid relationship now records an issue and renders supported child runs without assigning the rejected link. Text, direct/style formatting and inline pictures survive in body paragraphs, table cells and headers/footers. Strict import still rejects the same destination, the package remains read-only, and original source bytes remain available.

Original controls from `tools/hyperlink_recovery_fixture.py` cover a nonempty `docLocation`, a missing relationship, and a disallowed destination scheme, with matching supported mixed content in all three story contexts. The missing-relationship control is intentionally invalid at the OPC relationship level; XML schema validity alone does not establish package validity. These tests establish preview containment, not support for resolving those destinations. Errors in child structures, nested wrappers, field scope or layout can still require broader recovery.

Validation: focused hyperlink/drawing unit regressions, browser comparisons of pixels and body/header geometry against the same unlinked content, original-download/read-only checks, and all four generated controls' XML schema checks. This is not a claim of native reference layout equivalence or full corpus completion.

## Numbering definition recovery (2026-09-29)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.9 (numbering definitions and levels), 17.3.1.19 (`numPr`) and 17.7 (style hierarchy) distinguish a numbering reference from the paragraph's supported content and formatting. A missing or rejected effective numbering definition now suppresses only that paragraph's list participation in a read-only preview. Existing text, pictures, paragraph/character styles, direct formatting, tables and page stories survive. Other supported lists retain their definitions and counter progression.

`levelFor` identifies definition failures explicitly. Import records the limitation before permitting display-only paragraph resolution; subsequent display-only model construction retains the same approximation. Strict resolution and editing still reject the definition, unsafe package export stays disabled, and the source package is unchanged. This does not implement unsupported number formats or reconstruct unknown level geometry: available paragraph/style formatting is retained, while the rejected level's marker and level-only properties remain unavailable. Counter relationships involving a rejected level, structural numbering-part failures, and unrelated later layout failures still require further work.

Original controls generated by `tools/numbering_definition_recovery_fixture.py` cover direct/inherited unsupported formats, missing instances, missing levels and unsupported overrides in body, table-cell and header content. Missing definitions are intentional semantic defects despite valid XML. Unit checks cover supported sibling counters, retained rich content, strict editing rejection and unrelated style-error propagation; browser checks compare pixels and body/header geometry against the same content without the failed list reference and verify original-file download. All six fixture packages pass the applicable transitional XML schema checks. These controls establish recovery behavior, not native reference layout equivalence.

## Section alignment recovery (2026-09-29)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.6.23 (`vAlign`), 17.18.101 (`ST_VerticalJc`), 17.6.4 (`cols`) and 17.6.22 (section starts) define the relevant declarations. Full non-top vertical alignment with columns or continuous sections remains unsupported. Strict layout still rejects that combination. Read-only layout now displays only the affected section at the top instead of escalating to a document-wide plain-text preview. Supported alignment on separate unaffected pages remains active.

The approximation changes cloned display geometry only. Original page/section properties, columns, tables, pictures, styles, numbering and page stories remain available, and original-file download remains exact. Layout reports the affected section and applied top-alignment approximation; validation replaces the generic alignment failure with that localized explanation, including when import was already read-only for another feature. Unrelated layout errors still propagate normally.

Independent controls from `tools/section_alignment_recovery_fixture.py` cover center/bottom/justified alignment with columns, adjacent continuous sections, a separate supported centered section and a simultaneous unsupported shading declaration. They compare against explicit-top controls, with strict-layout rejection, unchanged source/model, supported no-op export, unknown-measurement-error propagation, browser pixel/body/header geometry checks and read-only original-download checks. All seven controls pass transitional XML schema validation. This proves the recovery policy, not native reference equivalence for the unsupported alignment combinations.

## Header/footer cached field recovery (2026-09-29)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.16, including §§17.16.18 (`fldChar`) and 17.16.19 (`fldSimple`), distinguishes field instructions from retained results. Read-only header/footer import now projects complete unsupported fields to their cached result content without flattening the surrounding paragraph. Logos, inherited/direct formatting and supported PAGE/NUMPAGES/SECTIONPAGES fields remain available. Unknown fields such as DATE are not evaluated or refreshed by this recovery path.

Projection is selective: supported fields inside retained results remain live, while fields inside discarded instruction code stay hidden. Incomplete fields and orphan delimiters are not repaired into valid fields. The existing MACROBUTTON instruction-label handling remains separate. Unsupported field structures that survive projection can still require broader recovery. The default body projection is unchanged; unexpected selector errors propagate before mutation. Only private parsed XML changes; original package bytes and read-only export protection remain intact.

Original controls from `tools/story_field_recovery_fixture.py` cover simple/complex date fields, live nested fields, header/footer logos, inherited/direct formatting and a simultaneous unsupported body property. Browser checks compare both pages against an explicit cached-text control and prove PAGE changes from 1 to 2 and NUMPAGES remains 2 in both stories despite deliberately stale cached values of 9. Unit checks cover source preservation, supported no-op export, incomplete/orphan structures, nested instruction content and error propagation. All five control packages pass transitional XML schema validation. This is cached-result recovery, not full field evaluation or native reference rendering equivalence.

## Continuous-section numbering recovery (2026-09-29)

- **Specification:** ECMA-376 Part 1 (2016), §17.6.12 `pgNumType` and §17.6.22 `type`; page fields §17.16. A specified restart is meaningful authored data. Continuing instead is an explicitly disclosed read-only approximation, not implementation of the restart semantics or a claimed reference/spec divergence.
- **Failure:** a rich control differing only by a continuous-section numbering restart previously fell through to a document-wide text preview, losing its table, two pictures, styles and header. The healthy control remained editable. Baseline and candidate native-browser probes reproduce the boundary independently of corpus documents.
- **Recovery:** strict layout still rejects the unsupported combination. Best-effort layout ignores only that restart before parity/blank-page handling and records the affected section and authored start for the banner. Header/footer PAGE fields and drawing page contexts use the same continued sequence. Authored section/page-story settings and package bytes stay unchanged. Paper-size transitions and ordinary next-page restarts retain existing support.
- **Controls:** `tools/continuous_numbering_recovery_fixture.py` independently builds seven packages: healthy, zero/even/odd restarts, an additional unsupported shading property, changed physical paper, and a next-page restart. Controls include rich content, duplex headers, overflow of the continuous section, and a later supported restart at 7. Recovery must match the healthy control's visible geometry and pixels, including header numbers 1, 2 and 7. This checks the declared approximation, not reference-equivalent restart behavior.
- **Verification:** 44 focused unit checks pass across recovery, section numbering, continuous flow/geometry and alignment recovery; seven fixtures pass the transitional schemas; production build and license checks pass. The browser recovery regression passes: all-page pixel/geometry equality for four approximations, continued header values, editable healthy control, blocked serialization, expanded issue banner and byte-identical original download. The existing duplex page-limit browser check also passes. Four older reference page-number browser checks fail their body/footer text classification identically on this change and isolated unchanged baseline `62f2fe1d`; these are pre-existing failures, not a claim of a fully green browser suite.
- **Remaining:** implement actual continuous restart semantics using native reference controls, including page ownership and duplex interactions. Other layout guards can still escalate to a document-wide fallback; R01–R06 and L03 remain open.

## Table-cell paragraph-break recovery (2026-09-29)

- **Specification:** ECMA-376 Part 1 (2016), §17.3.1.23 `pageBreakBefore`, §17.4 table content; this is distinct from inline `br` (§17.3.3.1). Existing independently authored native controls in `tests/fixtures/cell-breaks` show the native reference moving the table for a first cell paragraph's break while leaving a later paragraph on the same page. Omitting the break is a disclosed read-only approximation, not full implementation of those native semantics.
- **Failure:** rejecting the property after resolving a cell paragraph previously replaced that entire paragraph with plain preview runs, dropping its picture and inherited heading formatting. An independent rich control reproduces the loss; unaffected pictures elsewhere remain decoded, so aggregate asset counts alone would miss this bug.
- **Recovery:** strict import/editing guards remain. Best-effort import retains the rich paragraph and reports its part and the omitted break. Layout clones only the measured paragraph format when suppressing the break; authored properties, style references, runs, table structure and package bytes remain unchanged. Page-story clearance and painting opt into this specific cell-break approximation without relaxing their other page/height limits. Body paragraph page breaks and disabled cell breaks retain existing behavior. Downloads keep the original package; serialization of read-only imports remains blocked.

Rich body/header cells contain styled text and pictures, and an ordinary body break remains active. Browser comparisons use all rendered pages, including drawing contents, rather than just asset/paragraph counts.

- **Verification:** 38 focused unit checks pass across this recovery, existing cell-break semantics/editing, canvas tables, page-story tables and story-block recovery. All five browser checks pass: four native reference inline-break/edit/export/undo/reopen comparisons and the new all-page pixel/geometry recovery comparisons (body, header and drawing tables), expanded banner and byte-identical original download. Nine fixtures pass schema validation; production build and license checks pass. The first browser attempt hit startup timeouts in two old checks; the complete rerun with a longer startup allowance passed. No hosted CI was used.

## Local bookmark recovery (2026-09-29)

- **Specification:** ECMA-376 Part 1 (2016), §17.13.6.1 `bookmarkEnd` and §17.13.6.2 `bookmarkStart`. Endpoints pair by identifier and document order, independently of overlapping ranges. The cited clauses classify unmatched endpoints as non-conformant. These controls deliberately include semantic errors; passing their XML schemas does not certify valid bookmark semantics or native reference equivalence.
- **Failure:** one unmatched/invalid range caused read-only import to delete every bookmark in the document, removing otherwise valid internal link targets. The independent rich control retains a table, pictures and styles, so render/asset counts alone do not reveal this loss of navigation.
- **Recovery:** an optional validation callback reports known invalid bookmark IDs while returning unaffected ranges. Preview import removes only those IDs from its display model and reports each unavailable ID in `word/document.xml`. Duplicate endpoints discard the whole ambiguous ID; reversed endpoints are not rearranged and missing endpoints are not invented. Column row-range errors are specifically typed; unexpected resolver/conversion errors still propagate. Strict editing validation remains unchanged. Package parts, original download and read-only serialization protection remain intact.
- **Controls:** `tools/bookmark_recovery_fixture.py` creates eight independent packages with point, cell and overlapping valid ranges, a working internal link, and orphan-start/end, reversed, duplicate-start/end, unpaired-column and combined-error variants. Unit controls additionally exercise invalid positions, invalid column row ranges beside valid column selections, callback errors, and unexpected conversion errors. Browser recovery compares bookmarks, all-page pixels and geometry, exercises internal-link navigation to the retained cell target and checks the original download.
- **Remaining:** bookmark syntax errors inside unsupported enclosing structures can still cause broader paragraph/block fallback. Header/footer bookmark identities and safe editing around malformed source ranges remain separate work; R01–R06 are not complete.
- **Verification:** 89 unique focused unit checks pass across recovery, bookmark editing, block/nested tables, active/collapsed columns and native column geometry. The initial run passed 77 and timed out 12 at five seconds; rerunning only those 12 with two workers and a sixty-second limit passed. Two browser checks pass (mixed-error pixel/geometry/navigation/original-download recovery and existing bookmark editing/export/reopen). Eight fixture packages pass schema validation, with the semantic-invalidity caveat above. Build and license checks pass; GitHub Actions remained disabled.

The callback marks the package read-only and identifies failed assets. Markers

still reject failed assets and release healthy allocations on failure. Markers
allocate no bitmap and do not consume the decoded-pixel budget; aggregate source
and preview allocation limits remain in force.

and a failed page background. Paired-source comparisons measure actual geometry

placement structures; §17.3.3 defines retained inline content. Published
WordprocessingShape/WordprocessingGroup schemas cover the retained extensions.

## Low-chroma theme shade arithmetic constraints (2026-09-29)

Two new independently authored full-byte shade sweeps cover 7F8080 and 80817F,
at and just above the HSL midpoint. The native reference exported 512 native colors
on 15 pages; every extracted PDF text color equals the separately saved native
RGB fallback. The source remains byte-identical to a deterministic regeneration.
See `tests/fixtures/theme-low-chroma-sweep/README.md` for source, capture and
verification instructions. Relevant semantics remain Part 1 §17.3.2.6 and
MS-OI29500 §2.1.72; no new normative divergence is claimed.

The new controls rule out arbitrary fixed initial HSL quantization plus exact
shading and a sole fixed-bias output rounding step. For the second base's red
channel, shade bytes 2, 44 and 128 produce 1, 21 and 64. In the dark HSL branch,
`floor(k * shade + bias)` would require both k < 1/2 and k > 1/2. The exact
rational proof, hash validation and dark-branch precondition are implemented in
`tools/check_theme_shade_linearity.py`; its report is retained with the fixture.
Intermediate arithmetic or a modifier-dependent conversion stage remains to
be identified. A proof-check pass is not a renderer conformance pass.

The unchanged renderer matches 68/512 new native colors. Full-precision HSL with
final truncation only matches 427/512, so no conversion candidate was installed.
Provenance/native-witness unit tests and the browser's editable 15-page
preservation/insertion/undo/reopen workflow pass. Native colors remain explicitly
failing under `tools/check-theme-color-boundaries.mjs`. The new large fixture
requires explicit loading readiness waits; its initial five-second open/reopen
assertion timeouts are recorded, without a runtime optimization. The verified
browser workflow took approximately 1.6 minutes including cold setup; no isolated
import benchmark is claimed.

Garamond below 0.18 pt while worsening other families up to 3.04 pt; it is not a
general fix. The 0.2 pt native-origin assertion remains an explicit expected
failure, enabled only after hashes, import and row coverage succeed. Its runner
status is not a rendering pass. The 148 existing script/native-size unit checks
pass unchanged. No application build or schema rerun was needed for these
unchanged sources and diagnostic-only additions. Baseline placement and original
#252 remain partial.


### Native OpenType and application ligature defaults — 2026-09-30

Twelve independently authored packages (324 rows) distinguish absent/empty
`rPrDefault`, omitted/off/on `enableOpenTypeFeatures`, compatibility modes
12/14/15 and an omitted compatibility mode. The installed reference reports
1 pt kerning and standard/contextual ligatures for an absent run-default
category; a present empty category gives zero/none. Explicit properties retain
precedence. ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.7.5.5 permits consumer defaults for an absent
category; §17.3.2.19 defines the kerning threshold.

The native reference diverges from MS-DOCX §2.3.3's unconditional disabled OpenType default:
mode 15 uses the enabled path when the flag is absent, whereas modes 12/14 and
an omitted compatibility mode use the disabled path. Explicit off remains off.
The importer now models these defaults and feeds the existing generic shaping
policies; it adds no font-family or document-specific correction. Source
settings/styles remain untouched through ordinary edits and exact undo.

All 324 new prefix origins match native PDF positions within 0.169 pt. The
older 108-row script control now has prefix errors below 0.191 pt in all nine
faces. Its separate italic paint-offset failure remains explicit; vertical
placement is also still open. Prefix equivalence does not establish full script
equivalence. Controls, native captures and the documented divergence are in
[script-kerning-defaults](../tests/fixtures/script-kerning-defaults/README.md).

Validation: 319 distinct unit checks; 54 ordinary browser passes plus six

All eight #252 pages are RGB-identical before/after. Three alternating timing

Extended the native reduced-size rule to variable fonts whose required MVAR

reject uncertain metadata; present required tags retain the fallback pending

The CSS-loaded Canvas Noto Sans faces now expose their actual asset bytes to
script metadata preparation. An installed namesake cannot override those bytes.
The first browser run exposed this missing connection (10 passed, three size
checks failed); after connecting it, all 13 scenarios passed. Existing permission

The existing three reference EMFs provide 36 native LOGFONT sizes, including regular,

and records script height under the established 600-unit mapping. Both actual

This removes the old unequal 65% X / 60% Y fallback for eligible variable fonts.

## Numbering level structure recovery (2026-09-30)

Best-effort numbering import now contains rejected level/override structure at
its indexed record. Missing or unsupported indexes omit only the unidentifiable
record; duplicate numeric indexes invalidate that level without choosing a first
or last declaration. Invalid overrides cannot silently fall through to the
abstract definition. Healthy levels, counters, formatted body/cell/header
content and pictures survive; original bytes remain protected in read-only mode.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.9.6, 17.9.8, 17.9.26 are the semantic references. This is
recovery, not full support for the rejected declarations. The pre-existing
mismatched override guard remains a spec-support gap: §17.9.8 requires ignoring
the conflicting child ilvl. Native behavior has not been checked, so no reference/spec
divergence is claimed. See `tests/fixtures/numbering-level-recovery/README.md`.

Eight independent failure variants previously erased the healthy level-zero
labels. They now match the complete healthy-control canvas and line geometry.
Source parts and original downloads remain exact. No application sources changed
during live browser verification. No corpus completion is inferred from these
controls; the current corpus scan found no duplicate/missing/out-of-range
numbering indexes. Further late layout recovery remains open under R01–R06.


## Native numbering override investigation (2026-09-30)

Three independent source/PDF pairs now pin 48 native reference marker observations
for conflicting level indexes, full override start values and deeper references.
See `tests/fixtures/numbering-override-index/README.md`. All sources pass the
transitional XSD checks and reproduce from original OOXML generation.

The conflicting-index rejection cannot safely be removed by rebinding child
properties: the native reference normalizes it to an empty replacement level. Matching controls
also expose counter-start and deeper-reference differences, unchanged by explicit
abstract identities. These are unresolved semantics under Part 1 §§17.9.8,
17.9.11, 17.9.25–26. Four required integrity/setup checks and three explicit
expected failures record the current state. No runtime change, editable-support
claim, native geometry equivalence claim or corpus promotion is made by this entry.


## Full numbering override semantics (2026-09-30)

Implemented the native reference behavior recorded for ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.9.8,
17.9.11 and 17.9.25–26. Full level overrides supply formatting while ordinary
first counts use the resolved abstract start. Their own start (zero if omitted)
is retained separately for ancestor-driven resets. An explicit startOverride
activates the child start when present; otherwise its own value applies. These
native initial/restart rules differ from directly applying the declarations'
standalone start values, as shown by the independent controls.

Conflicting valid child indexes produce empty replacement levels without leaking
child formatting or losing counters. Deeper references discard the full override
and its startOverride, unlike deeper references in abstract definitions. Source
XML stays intact on no-op/text edits. User-requested restarts update the explicit
child start or remove the ignored child in the new instance, so the native reference agrees with
the editor. Numerically equal zero-padded indexes do not create duplicate records.

## Nonempty content-control boundary selection (2026-09-30)

ECMA-376 Part 1 fifth edition §§17.5.2.26 (`richText`) and 17.5.2.31
(inline `sdt`) define the wrapper and its inline contents. They do not prescribe
keyboard selection steps. Five independently authored/saved reference controls
establish the native interaction; no normative OOXML divergence is claimed.

From an inside caret at a nonempty persistent rich-text control edge, the first
outward Shift+Arrow selects the boundary without selecting adjacent text. A
continued extension selects that text while retaining the original selection
anchor. Typing after a rightward extension belongs to the control; a leftward
selection starting outside does not. Reversing the boundary-only leftward step
returns to the inside caret. The existing empty-control prompt restoration path
remains separate. Inward/interior and read-only movement retain their behavior.

The implementation reuses control-selection metadata and does not add a layout,
paint, import or font pass. Source XML and unrelated OPC parts remain preserved;
export/reopen and exact undo/redo are checked. See the
[independent native controls](../tests/fixtures/nonempty-control-shift-selection/README.md).
Adjacent/nested control crossings, Shift-click and wider selection interactions
remain open; this is not complete content-control interaction equivalence.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.16.22 permits hyperlink child structures beyond ordinary

`tools/hyperlink_child_recovery_fixture.py` independently creates five original

Unit and browser regressions compare supported content, whole-page pixels and
body/story geometry, including 100% and 75% zoom and original-byte downloads.
This does not implement permission enforcement or revision review. Rich content
inside an unsupported child still has the limited text approximation; errors
inside recognized runs or field envelopes can still escape this boundary.
No reference/spec divergence is claimed, and no corpus entry is promoted.

## Text-clearing-break preview recovery (2026-09-30)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.3.1 (`br`) and 17.18.3 (`ST_BrClear`) define

Strict import still rejects active left/right/all clearance; read-only import
now approximates only that attribute with an ordinary line break, preserving
neighboring text, run formatting, pictures and hyperlinks. The diagnostic names
the source part and warns that text can restart beside the object. It does not
change stored XML, enable unsafe serialization or affect page/column breaks,
for which the specification ignores clear. Malformed values retain their
existing unsupported path. No reference/spec divergence is claimed.

The twelve independently generated [paired controls](../tests/fixtures/clearing-break-recovery/README.md)

clear=none; they establish the declared approximation, not native float-clearing
fidelity. Full float clearance and other recognized-run/field recovery gaps
remain open.

## Top-and-bottom wrapping across paragraphs (2026-09-30)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.4.2.20, 20.4.2.11–12 and 17.3.1.33 describe
wrapping, positioning and paragraph spacing. Nonnegative paragraph-relative
top-and-bottom drawing bands now participate in pagination instead of inflating
the anchor paragraph to the band's bottom. Healthy following text can remain
above a later picture. Intersecting text clears it, with unsuppressed paragraph
before-spacing retained after clearance and the anchor's own spacing excluded
from its drawing origin. Complete body tables stay above the band when they fit;
otherwise they clear it. Paragraph keeps account for clearance, measured lines
remain immutable, page advances expire old bands, and ending regions retain the
remaining occupied band extent.

Independent original DOCX families establish 82 native reference baselines across 27 pages,
all within 0.15 pt. Unit cases cover page cuts, overlapping bands, keepNext,
keepLines, spacing suppression and repeatability. Actual browser checks cover
editing, untouched package parts, exact undo and edited reopening. Local final
checks pass 154 unit tests, seven browser tests (one optional source skipped),
120 schema views and the production/license build. The Project Summary report's
22 matching body lines are within 0.221 pt of the native reference after this change.

This does not establish full wrapping conformance or a reference/spec contradiction.
Existing rejected negative offsets, wrapped-cell/manual-break combinations and
broader mixed-layout interactions remain separate work. Timing measurements are
noisy, with nominal positive report deltas; no speed improvement or universal
absence of slowdown is claimed. See [controls](../tests/fixtures/top-bottom-flow/README.md).

## Negative-offset wrapping recovery (2026-09-30)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.4.2.12/20.4.3.3 define positioning offsets and
§20.4.2.20 defines top-and-bottom wrapping. The latter remains unsupported for
negative paragraph offsets. Best-effort layout now creates a private view that
omits wrapping only on those pictures, retaining signed positions, extents,
stacking and source objects. The disclosed approximation uses §20.4.2.15's
no-wrap behavior; text can overlap and pagination can differ. Strict layout
continues to reject the combination, and original downloads remain intact.

The same view participates in header/footer clearance and painting. It reports
each affected picture in the partial-rendering banner. Healthy wrapping,
paragraphs, tables, styles and decoded assets survive. Unrelated measurement

support or evidence of a standards divergence.

cover 57 unit tests, 11 browser cases, 51 source/export schema views and the

### Image gestures, text hit priority, context menus and printing (2026-09-30)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.4.2.3 (`anchor`, including `behindDoc`, `relativeHeight`,
`locked` and `layoutInCell`), 20.4.2.7–8 (`extent`, `inline`), 20.4.2.10–12
(`positionH`, `positionV`, `posOffset`) and 20.1.7.6 (`xfrm`) describe the
retained placement and frame dimensions. §§17.6.13 (`pgSz`) and 17.6.11
(`pgMar`) describe the physical page geometry used for printing.

Ordinary pointer hits prefer text over behind-text drawings. Alt-click or the
right-click "Select picture behind text" command selects an obscured drawing.
Foreground drawings still receive hits first. Existing content-control
placeholder selection remains intact, including the teacher-card title.

Floating images can be dragged or nudged without changing their anchor paragraph
or reference bases. Explicit movement converts authored alignment/percentage
coordinates to numeric offsets. Unchanged coordinate axes retain their authored
alignment. Inline movement relocates its object run through text. Proportional
corner resizing updates picture frame and transform extents. Each released
gesture is one validated, undoable transaction; Escape cancels its preview.
Right-click arrangement changes the behind/front text layer or orders floating
siblings within their story and layer through `relativeHeight`. Retained drawing
groups can move and change layer as whole objects; their internals and corner
resizing remain unavailable. Relative-size drawings also have no corner handles.
Active unsupported drawing locks and read-only approximations remain protected.

File > Print / Save as PDF, the context menu and Ctrl/Cmd+P capture all physical
pages, including read-only previews, at 192 DPI independently of screen zoom.
Printed pages omit selection/caret/control highlights and table editing guides.
The existing browser print stage assigns each distinct section page size its own
CSS page rule and cleans up after printing or closing the document. PDF output is
raster, without searchable text. Native printer drivers and other browsers are
not covered by the Chromium checks.

Local checks: 98 unit tests, 11 distinct browser cases, 46 final-delivery schema

production build and license policy. The independently authored control and
actual teacher card preserve original package parts after undo. Inspected PDFs

### Required empty paragraphs before continuous sections

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.6.18 places section properties on the terminating paragraph;
§17.6.22 defines continuous transitions. Native reference controls show
that otherwise-empty boundaries retain a body line when they are the section's
sole paragraph, or follow a table in compatibility mode 15 or newer, and the
following section continues on the same paper. Modes 12/14 suppress the
post-table boundary. A retained line keeps its measured height, spacing and
shading; its paragraph border remains suppressed. Source XML is unchanged.

When balancing columns, the required terminal line follows the final table row
below the balanced content. Its height does not redistribute preceding rows;
the next section starts below the complete occupied region. Physical-page
limits still apply. Virtual boundaries continue to terminate keep chains.

The 39 original controls in `tests/fixtures/continuous-boundary` retain native
PDFs, source/reference hashes and every visible text origin. All match within
0.15 pt in the browser. Local checks pass 62 unit tests, 27 browser cases,
295 schema views over 114 source/export packages, and production build/license
policy. The supplied six-page Small Business Quarterly Report remains editable,
with package-preserving export, exact undo and reopening. Its page-5 missing
spacing is corrected; a roughly 2.5 pt font-metric difference and status-symbol
appearance difference remain. This is not full reference equivalence.

## User-selected font files — 2026-09-30

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.26 (`rFonts`) retains the authored font names and
independent character slots. Loading a file is a presentation action, with no
run-format, theme, font-table, package-part or history mutation. See also the
OpenType [name table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/name)
and [fvar table](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/fvar).

The font picker and View → Document fonts accept user-selected TTF/OTF files
without installed-font enumeration or a remote font service. Preferred and
localized typographic/legacy family names, full names and PostScript names
identify the faces; filenames do not. Explicitly loaded files take precedence
over installed/document-embedded faces for matching names in this browser
session. Internal canvas aliases never replace names stored in the DOCX.
Regular/bold/italic companions, static weight/width metadata, and variable
weight/width ranges are retained. Exact full-face aliases bind at normal CSS
weight and retain the existing synthetic-bold handling. Variable ital/slnt
descriptors are parsed, but the native comparison currently covers the four
static styles and real variable weight/width plus separate italic faces.

Complete families validate before publication. Invalid files do not replace
working faces; byte-identical reloads reuse them. Loads are serialized, and
font-dependent probes/layout caches observe a session version. Refresh retries
when the model or font version changes while resources are being prepared.
Current editing, undo, original downloads and protected read-only previews stay
intact. Per-file/session limits are 32/128 MB; resources live until browser reload.
No font bytes are added to exports. TTC/WOFF containers and named variation
instances are not supported by this file picker.

SVG-backed EMF pictures still require usable installed faces; browser FontFaces
cannot be inherited by those images. Fresh decoding determines their warnings,
so a loaded body font does not falsely clear a still-missing metafile font.
This remains an explicit equivalence gap. No commercial fonts or ECMA artwork were
added. The independent renamed-font controls retain both reviewed Adobe OFL
notices, corresponding-source provenance, generator and native reference.

The four-face file-loaded control matches all recorded native reference origins within
0.2 pt vertically, 0.15 pt at line starts and 0.35 pt per glyph.
The cold unit-import
timeout also occurs on unchanged main; the final local run allows 30 seconds
for each test without changing its assertions. Vite development navigation
timing is not a production performance or complete reference-equivalence certification.

sources. Browser image documents cannot inherit the surrounding FontFace set.
Regular/bold/italic descriptors, including registered variation ranges, reuse
the validated file-font registry. Only referenced supplied families are added;
pictures with no supplied matching family retain their exact generated SVG.

Font selection is presentation-only: EMF records, source font names, picture
parts, DOCX embedding declarations and editing history are unchanged. Live font
refresh decodes affected pictures again and clears warnings only for families
now supplied or natively available. OS catalogue and DOCX-embedded font bridging,
and faithful missing-glyph fallback, remain separate work. The existing font
file/session limits apply; self-contained image sources also require transient
base64/SVG storage. No general timing or memory equivalence claim is made.

Independent controls and native observations are documented in
`tests/fixtures/metafile-file-fonts/README.md`. Eight native geometry cases,

pass. The unchanged 1.6pt raster-bound check is not pixel identity; the native reference's italic
Omega fallback still differs. Final local validation: 73 unit checks, eight
distinct browser cases, 66 schema views across 15 packages, build and license
gate. Two first-run browser cases timed out at 30 seconds; all eight passed
with the 180-second scoped limit. A final raster-capture recheck is recorded

### Body PAGEREF recalculation (2026-09-30)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.15.1.90, 17.16.5.45 and 17.16.18 govern the
updateFields setting, bookmark page references and dirty/locked delimiters.

Simple/complex fields and references inside retained TOC results keep their
instructions and envelopes. Direct/enclosing field locks are respected.

refresh failure does not replace the successfully imported document with text.

rolls back results, selection, metadata and history.

the native reference opens dirty/requested references as page 1 before pagination;
Repaginate leaves that cache, while explicit update resolves the bookmark on
page 2. The viewer uses the actual page 2 rather than reproducing the stale
early result. This observation is phase-specific, not complete native equivalence.
The switches control is authored independently from OOXML and tested against
the spec; it has no native capture. TOC/INDEX generation, arbitrary field codes,
instruction expressions, nested PAGEREF result fields, CHARFORMAT and number
formats outside the existing PAGE subset remain gaps. English relative labels
are currently used. Refresh cost on very large reference batches is a profiling
follow-up; no pagination or text-metric optimization was introduced here.

## Editable text-clearing breaks (2026-10-03)

Part 1 §§17.3.3.1 (`br`) and 17.18.3 (`ST_BrClear`) govern interruption and
restart of a text line beside floating objects. Valid `none`, `left`, `right`
and `all` values are retained as individual editable break characters, preserving
rich run/link formatting and preventing clearance metadata from entering typed
text. Page/column breaks ignore clearance as specified; invalid values remain
unsupported. No-op and undo preserve original package parts.

LTR square-float restart follows the requested side and the leftmost-region rule;
`all` waits for full paragraph width. A gap to an outgoing page's float does not
travel onto the next page or column. Native reference controls cover body,
headers, footers and page boundaries at the existing 0.2 pt export tolerance.
Paragraph-relative square floats that fit a fresh writing area reserve placement
capacity in mode 15 without increasing text advancement. Native mode 12 controls
retain its margin-overflow behavior. This mode distinction is observed reference
behavior, not an extra requirement derived from §20.4.2.3 (`anchor`).

Supported inline-only body/cell/story cases keep editing enabled. RTL paragraphs,
wrapped drawings in cells, glossary-placeholder clearing breaks and other guarded
anchor combinations remain unsupported. A separate before-spacing/anchor defect
is recorded rather than treated as fixed. Oversized floats are excluded from the
placement reservation; these controls do not prove their boundary behavior.
See [native controls](../tests/fixtures/clearing-break-wrapping/README.md). No original-template
completion count changes: the 368-file XML scan contains no non-none text-clearing
breaks.

Equivalent full/split cubic controls prove exact geometric identity with rational Bernstein arithmetic and differ only in the SVG media part. Five native API contours change at seven vertices;

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.3 (WordprocessingML paragraphs/runs) and 20.4

govern the retained `wps:txbx/w:txbxContent` and containing shape/group frames.
The application now offers a rich draft editor for plain text frames through

representations, content controls, drawing-local tables, fields, symbols and
pictures inside an edited frame remain guarded. Document style/numbering changes
before drawing text edits and unsupported shape-text decorations remain guarded
as well. Those structures are retained, not flattened or dropped. Existing
overflow clipping and geometry remain active; schema validity is not a full
reference fidelity certification. No corpus counts or verdicts are promoted.

Search occupies a workspace panel instead of obscuring the header and document.

Escape restores the current selection's font size before the field loses focus,

### Option word navigation (2026-10-05)

Option+Left and Option+Right (with or without Shift) now follow native macOS
text fields: moving left stops at the start of each word or punctuation run,

### Triple-click paragraph selection (2026-10-05)

A third click in the document selects the paragraph under the pointer, across
its wrapped lines and up to (not including) its paragraph mark, so typing
replaces the text and keeps the paragraph and its properties. Shift+click keeps
extending the existing selection, and clicks on pictures keep selecting the
picture. Single and double clicks are unchanged. A browser regression covers
wrapped paragraphs, replacement and undo. This is selection only: ECMA-376 Part 1
§17.3.1 paragraphs and DOCX serialization are unchanged.

### Open-failure navigation (2026-10-05)

When a document cannot open (a damaged archive, an unsupported template or text
import, an engine load failure), the message no longer covers the whole window.
The title, save status, back button and menus stay available; the toolbar,
navigation rail and status bar, which have nothing to act on, are hidden. The
message offers Back to documents and New document, plus Download original when
source bytes exist. No save handler is attached, as before. Browser regressions
cover both actions, header placement and the original download. DOCX parsing,
ECMA-376 Part 2 package handling and the read-only/unsupported-content policy are
unchanged.

### Single-row phone toolbar (2026-10-05)

Undo/redo, the five everyday text controls and More formatting tools need 384px
at their 44px touch size. Phones at least that wide (390–430px, the common
sizes) now keep them in one 52px row instead of stacking the text controls into
a 97px block, which returns 45px of document height, most noticeably with the

horizontal scrolling. Browser checks cover 390px and 320px heights, touch-target
sizes and the absence of scrolling. Command placement only; ECMA-376 run
properties and DOCX serialization are unchanged.

### Pointer-opened document menu (2026-10-05)

A right-click or long press on the document opens its menu with no item chosen,
like native context menus. Previously focus moved from the document's text field
to the first item, which Chrome draws with a keyboard focus ring, so Undo looked
selected on every right-click. The menu itself takes focus: Down starts at the
first item and Up at the last, with the usual ring once a key is pressed; hover
keeps its tint. Keyboard-opened menus and every other menu are unchanged. A
browser regression covers both paths, choosing with Enter and Escape returning to
the document. Menu UI only; no OOXML behavior changes.

### Word-level typing undo (2026-10-05)

Typed characters now share one undo step until a new word starts after
whitespace; previously every character was its own
step. A caret move, click, other edit, paragraph break, undo/redo or story switch
also starts a new step, and typing over a selection restores the selection on
undo. Redo restores the same word-sized steps. History snapshots are unchanged;
coalescing only skips recording intermediate keystrokes. Browser regressions cover
word steps, redo, boundaries and selection replacement. DOCX serialization is
unchanged.
