Heading 1–2 (ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.7.4 style definitions: w:style with w:name,
w:basedOn, w:next, w:qFormat, w:pPr keepNext/keepLines/spacing/outlineLvl and
w:rPr b/i/color/sz). The paragraph style list therefore matches the set word
processors offer, and the existing Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+3…6 heading shortcuts, which had
no target in a new document, now apply them; Heading 3–6 carry outline levels 3–6
for navigation. Opened documents keep their own styles, and engine-created test
packages keep the previous minimal set. A browser regression covers the list,
shortcuts, outline, export and reopen; the exported document.xml and styles.xml
pass `npm run check:conformance`.

### Built-in templates (2026-10-05)

Letter, Meeting notes, Report, Résumé and Essay open from the home screen's
Templates menu as new documents instead of failing with "templates will return
in a later iteration". Their blocks are laid out in a new document through the
existing model commands: paragraph styles (Title, Subtitle, Heading 1–3, Normal;
§17.7.4), bullet and numbered lists created with the existing numbering
definitions (§17.9) and a fixed-width table (§17.4). Layout adds no undo step,
leaves the caret at the start and, as before, the template document is unsaved
until its first autosave. Text imports remain unsupported and still show the
open-failure message. Browser regressions open all five templates from the menu,
check styles, lists, the table, editing, autosave, export and reopen; the
exported document.xml, styles.xml and numbering.xml pass
`npm run check:conformance`.

### Plain-text import (2026-10-05)

Importing a .txt file (Import, drag and drop or File → Open) opens it as a new
document with one Normal paragraph per line (§17.3.1), tabs as w:tab runs and
the file's final line ending dropped, instead of the open-failure message.
Decoding, CR/LF normalization and control-character removal reuse the existing
import helpers. Loading the text adds no undo step; the document autosaves as a
new .docx like other imports. Markdown and HTML remain unsupported and still
open the failure message with navigation. A browser regression covers import from
the home screen, autosave, editing, export and reopen; the export passes
`npm run check:conformance`.

### Save as template (2026-10-05)

The documents screen's Templates menu and its "My templates" dialog tell users to
save a document as a template from its File menu, but the canvas editor had no
such command. File → Save as template… now writes the current export to
Documents/Templates/<name>.docx in Puter (asking before replacing a template of
the same name, and signing in first when needed). The open document is unchanged.
New documents started from it open as copies, as before. The command is absent in
the local playground and disabled for read-only previews, whose export would not
preserve unsupported content. Browser regressions cover saving, replacing,
starting a document from the template and the playground menu. Export uses the
existing DOCX serializer; no new OOXML subset.

### Paragraph and document arrow chords (2026-10-05)

Cmd+Up/Down now go to the start/end of the document (macOS), where they moved a
single line. Option+Up/Down move to the start/end of the current paragraph, then
to the neighboring paragraph's (macOS text fields), and Ctrl+Up/Down move to the
previous/next paragraph start (the Windows convention); all three previously moved by
line. Shift extends the selection in each case; plain Up/Down keep line movement
and preferred-column behavior. A browser regression covers each chord, extension
and plain arrows. Caret movement only; ECMA-376 paragraphs and DOCX output are
unchanged.

### PageUp and PageDown (2026-10-05)

PageUp/PageDown scrolled the document view but left the caret behind, so the next
keystroke jumped back, and Shift+PageDown selected nothing. They now move the
caret a screen of lines in its preferred column (stopping at the document's
start or end), scroll the view by the same distance, and extend the
selection with Shift. A browser regression covers movement, scrolling, the
document end and extension. Caret movement only; no OOXML change.

### Formatted copy and paste (2026-10-05)

Copy and cut previously put only plain text on the clipboard, so pasting, even
within the same document, dropped headings, lists and emphasis. A text-only
selection now also carries HTML (headings, lists, bold/italic/underline/strike,
super/subscript, color, highlight, size, font and http(s)/mailto links), which
other applications paste with formatting; the editor's own fragment is embedded
in that HTML for an exact paste back. Paste inserts the text, then applies
paragraph styles (§17.7.4, matched by id then name), alignment, list kind and
level (§17.9) to paragraphs whose marks were copied, and character formatting
(§17.3.2) through the existing commands as one undo step, so that
the final partial paragraph keeps the destination's formatting. HTML from
other applications maps semantic tags and common inline styles; plain values
(not bold, black) leave the destination's formatting. Selections or destinations
with tables, fields, content controls, pictures or notes keep the plain-text
path, as does a plain-text-only clipboard. Unit tests cover HTML conversion and
embedded fragments; browser regressions cover in-document round trips, cut, the
Edit menu, HTML from other web editors, undo, export and the plain fallbacks. The
exported document.xml, styles.xml and numbering.xml pass `npm run check:conformance`.

### Long formatted pastes (2026-10-05)

Pasting long formatted content took a minute for ~1,600 paragraphs: every
formatting command snapshotted the whole document for the model's internal
history (which the editing session already records once per paste), and every
selection re-segmented the whole document into grapheme boundaries and scanned
them linearly. Paste now suspends those redundant snapshots, grapheme boundaries
are cached for unchanged text (a frozen array; no caller mutates it) and
selection clamping uses binary search. The same paste takes under two seconds,
and typing and selection in long documents share the cache. HTML conversion also
no longer turns whitespace between blocks or container blocks (a quotation
around paragraphs) into blank paragraphs, nor adds spaces before table-cell tabs.
Unit and browser suites cover selection, navigation and paste behavior; results
are unchanged apart from speed.

### Markdown and HTML import (2026-10-05)

Markdown (.md, with GitHub tables, task lists and strikethrough) and HTML files
now open as new documents instead of the failure message. Markdown is rendered
with the existing mdast libraries with raw HTML disabled; HTML uses the importer's
existing body cleanup. Both then go through the formatted-paste conversion:
headings become Heading 1–6 (§17.7.4), lists become bullet or numbered paragraphs
with nesting levels (§17.9), and bold, italic, underline, strikethrough,
super/subscript, color and http(s)/mailto links become run properties and
hyperlinks (§17.3.2, §17.16.22). Known limits: tables become tab-separated
paragraphs, code blocks keep their line breaks without a monospace font,
quotations are not indented and pictures are omitted. Loading adds no undo step;
the document autosaves like other imports. Browser regressions cover Markdown and
HTML structure, links, script removal, autosave, export and reopen.

### Link appearance (2026-10-05)

Links created with Insert link (Ctrl/Cmd+K) looked exactly like the text around
them. A new link now takes the document's Hyperlink character style when it has
one (§17.7.4.17 rStyle), and otherwise blue (0563C1) single-underlined direct
formatting (§17.3.2.6 color, §17.3.2.40 u); changing an existing
link's address keeps its look. Text typed straight after a new link continues
with the formatting from before it. Links pasted or imported from HTML or
Markdown without their own color get the same look. The style or formatting is
part of the same undo step as the link. Model-level hyperlink APIs are
unchanged. Browser regressions cover insertion, wrapping a selection, address
changes, continued typing, undo and pasted links; the exported document passes
`npm run check:conformance`.

### Help menu and shortcut reference (2026-10-05)

The editor had no way to show its keyboard shortcuts (the account menu's entry
does not exist in the local playground). A Help menu now offers Keyboard
shortcuts, also opened with Ctrl/Cmd+/. The reference adds the
navigation chords (word, paragraph, document and screen movement, Shift
extension, double- and triple-click) and Heading 1–6. On screens narrower than
360px, where Help would wrap the menu bar and a keyboard is unlikely, the menu is
hidden and the menu bar's arrow-key order skips it. Unit and browser regressions
cover the menu, the chord, the listed entries and narrow-screen keyboard order.
UI only; no OOXML change.

### One "Normal" in the style list (2026-10-05)

The paragraph style list offered "Default paragraph" (no w:pStyle) beside
"Normal". A paragraph without a style takes the document's default paragraph
style (§17.7.4.17 w:default), so both choices looked and behaved the same and the
list showed "Normal" after either. "Default paragraph" is now listed only when a
document defines no default paragraph style, where it is the only way to show
and choose unstyled paragraphs. Choosing Normal writes it explicitly.
Browser regressions cover the list in new documents and the existing
style, outline and reset flows.

### Wrapped toolbar rows (2026-10-05)

Between 701px and about 1190px the formatting toolbar wraps onto a second row,
and the group that ended the first row kept its divider, leaving a stray line at
the row's right edge. A resize observer now marks the groups that end a row and
their divider is transparent, as the last group's always was. Only the divider's
color changes, so the marking cannot alter where the toolbar wraps. A browser
regression checks one and two rows. UI only.

### Mixed font-size placeholder (2026-10-05)

With a selection across two font sizes (a heading and body text, say) the size
box showed a clipped "Mixe", because Chrome keeps room for the size list's picker
inside the 60px field. The toolbar field is now 66px with a 3px right padding and
the phone inspector field 72px, so "Mixed" shows whole while the picker stays
available on hover. A browser regression measures the placeholder against the
field's text area. UI only.

### Document notices as a message bar (2026-10-05)

Notices about the open document (read-only approximation, unsupported features,
fonts unavailable in pictures, approximate script metrics, page references kept)
were plain paragraphs between the toolbar and the page, taking about 100px on
desktop and 140px on phones, with no way to put them away. They now form a
compact tinted message bar with smaller type, a 40% (phones 30%) height limit
with scrolling and a Dismiss button that returns to the document; new notices
show it again. The open-failure message is unchanged and cannot be dismissed.
Browser regressions cover the bar's height, dismissing and the next document's
notices, alongside the existing notice and feature-list checks. UI only.

### Pasting pictures (2026-10-05)

Pasting a screenshot or a picture copied from another application did nothing,
because paste read only text. When the clipboard holds a PNG, JPEG or TIFF and
no text, Ctrl/Cmd+V and Edit → Paste now insert it at the caret through the
existing Insert image path (§20.4.2.8 inline drawing; the same size limits,
validation, undo step and DOCX serialization). Clipboard text beside a picture is
still pasted as text, and read-only previews ignore the paste. A browser
regression covers both paste paths, undo and the text precedence.

### Autocorrect and links as you type (2026-10-05)

The account menu offered "Autocorrect as you type", "Capitalize the first letter
of sentences" and "Link web addresses as you type", all on by default, but the
canvas editor did none of them. Typing now applies the existing correction rules
(typographic quotes and apostrophes, em dashes for two hyphens, ellipses, ©/®/™,
½/¼/¾), capitalizes sentence starts (skipping known abbreviations), and links web
addresses and email addresses when a space or new paragraph ends them, with the
usual link look (§17.16.22 hyperlink). Addresses keep their punctuation. Each
correction or link is its own undo step, so Undo takes it back and leaves what was
typed. The settings are read at each keystroke. Pasted, imported and composed
(IME) text is not changed, and the local playground keeps typing literal. Browser
regressions cover each rule, links on space and Enter, undo, addresses and the
three settings.

### Automatic lists (2026-10-05)

With autocorrect on, typing "* ", "- " or "• " at the start of a paragraph that is
not a list item now makes it a bulleted list item, and "1. " or "1) " a numbered
one (§17.9 numbering through the existing list
command). The marker is removed in the same step, so one Undo restores the typed
characters as plain text. Markers inside a sentence or in list paragraphs stay as
typed. A browser regression covers both kinds, continuation, undo and the
non-list cases.

### Paste without formatting (2026-10-05)

With formatted paste in place, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V and Edit → Paste without
formatting insert only the clipboard's text. Chrome
on macOS sends no paste event for that chord, so the editor cancels the native
action (avoiding a second paste on Windows) and reads the text through the
asynchronous clipboard. The keyboard reference lists it. Browser and unit
regressions cover both entry points against a rich clipboard and the ordinary
paste beside them.

### Replace shortcut (2026-10-05)

Ctrl+H (Windows and Linux) and Cmd+Shift+H (macOS, where Cmd+H hides the
application) now open Find and replace with the
selected text, the same panel as Ctrl/Cmd+F; Chrome otherwise opened its history
page on Ctrl+H. The keyboard reference lists both chords. A browser regression
covers the chord, the prefilled query and the replace field.

### Deletion undo steps (2026-10-05)

Each Backspace or Delete press was its own undo step, so restoring a deleted
word took one Undo per character. A contiguous run of Backspace (or of Delete)
presses is now one step; moving the caret, clicking,
typing, switching direction or any other edit starts a new one. A browser
regression covers both keys, undo and redo.

### Status bar menus (2026-10-05)

The status bar's Zoom (and header/footer Editing) menus used the browser's native
select appearance, with a heavy system chevron set apart from the value and no
hover state, unlike the toolbar's menus. They now share the toolbar's chevron,
hover border and focus border. A browser regression checks the appearance, the
hover response and choosing a zoom. UI only.

### Table commands on right-click (2026-10-05)

Right-clicking in a table offered only the clipboard commands. The document menu
now also lists Insert row below, Insert column right, Delete row, Delete column,
Delete table, Merge cells in row, Split into grid cells and Table properties…,
the same commands and enabled states as Table → Rows & columns (§17.4 table
structure through the existing model commands, so undo and serialization are
unchanged). Pictures and read-only previews keep their own menus. A browser
regression runs each command from the menu and checks the menu outside tables.

### Document menu: plain paste and links (2026-10-05)

The right-click menu now also offers Paste without formatting and Insert link…
(Edit link… inside a link), with their shortcuts.
Both reuse the existing commands. A browser regression opens each from the menu.

### Remove link availability (2026-10-05)

Format → Remove link (and the inspector's Remove link) was enabled for any
selection, even one without a link, where it did nothing. It is now enabled only
when the caret is in a link or the selection overlaps one. A browser regression
covers plain selections, partial overlap and removal at the caret.

### Insert table with a selection (2026-10-05)

Insert table was disabled in the toolbar and menus whenever text was selected,
with no explanation. It is now available, and the table is inserted after the
selection (the selected text is kept), through the existing table command; if
the table cannot be inserted the selection is restored. Pictures keep it
disabled. A browser regression covers the toolbar state, the menu command, the
resulting paragraphs and undo.

### Menu conventions (2026-10-05)

Commands that open a dialog for more input (Indents and tabs, Paragraph borders,
Page setup, Bookmarks, Insert image, the typography, style, table and cell
dialogs, Insert or edit link) now end in an ellipsis, as a few already did; the
ellipsis is decorative, so accessible names are
unchanged. Items that open a dialog popover (Font…, Insert or edit link…) no
longer show a submenu arrow; only real submenus and palettes do. Underline
options no longer shows a stray chevron in the icon column. A browser regression
checks ellipses and arrows in the Format and Insert menus.

### Style dialog layout (2026-10-05)

Edit paragraph style showed about thirty fields in one undifferentiated grid,
each labelled "Style …". The fields are now grouped under Font (size, bold,
italic, underline, color, capitalization, position and spacing), Paragraph
(alignment, line spacing, space before and after, fill, outline level) and
Pagination, followed by the existing borders, in the dialog's fixed order
uses. Visible labels drop the "Style" prefix that the dialog title already
gives; every field keeps its accessible name, so assistive technology and the
existing tests address the same controls. The character style dialog gets the
Font group only. The style patch and §17.7 serialization are unchanged.

### Paragraph borders dialog (2026-10-05)

The dialog repeated its title as a heading inside it, and the Box, All borders,
Bottom only and No borders presets looked like plain text. The presets are now
outlined buttons in a labelled "Presets" group; the inner heading is shown only
inside the style dialog, where it reads "Borders" like the other style groups.
Border reading and §17.3.1.24 pBdr output are unchanged; existing border
browser and unit tests pass.

### Bookmarks dialog spacing (2026-10-05)

The Bookmarks dialog set its hint, Add/Rename buttons and the bookmark list
directly against each other, and on phones its Go to/Delete/Done row ran off the
left edge. The dialog now spaces its two parts with a divider, and right-aligned
button rows in every dialog wrap when they do not fit (no change where they fit).
A browser regression checks the spacing and that every button stays on a 390px
screen; bookmark tests pass unchanged.

### Image properties dialog (2026-10-05)

Picture sizes showed six decimals ("5.333333"), notes ran straight into the next
field's label, and cropping used the browser's raw fieldset. Sizes now show two
decimals; the exact values behind them, including proportional
updates, are still what is applied unless a size is retyped, so wp:extent output
is unchanged. Fields and notes are evenly spaced and cropping is a titled group.
All image-dialog browser tests pass unchanged, and the full unit suite shows no
new failures.

### Inspector menus (2026-10-05)

The formatting inspector's menus (Rows & columns, Line spacing, Character style,
Outline level and others) used the browser's native select look, unlike the
toolbar and status bar. They now share the app's chevron and hover border. UI
only; the controls, their names and their values are unchanged.

### Rulers on phones (2026-10-05)

On phone-width screens (700px and below) the rulers start hidden,
giving the page about 30px more height and 24px more
width at fit-width zoom; View → Ruler shows them. Until the user chooses, the
default follows the window across that width (a phone-sized window that grows
shows them). Ruler editing is unchanged. Browser regressions cover the phone
default, the View toggle, keeping the user's choice and growing windows.

### Text mode explained (2026-10-05)

The status bar's "Text mode" checkbox gave no hint of what it does. Hovering it
now explains that it edits the text in a plain text field without page layout,
for screen readers and other assistive tools. Its name and behavior are
unchanged.

### Fit width on tablets and narrow windows (2026-10-05)

Below 1024px wide (a tablet in portrait, a narrow window) a document opened at
100%, so a Letter or A4 page ran off the right edge. When the widest page does
not fit there at 100%, the document now opens at Fit width, as on phones;
desktop windows keep 100% and scroll, and any zoom
the user picks is kept. A browser regression covers an 800px window and a
1280px one; ruler and page-geometry tests at 100% pass unchanged.

### Touch toolbar scroll cue (2026-10-05)

On touch screens too narrow for the whole toolbar (a tablet in portrait), the
toolbar scrolls sideways, but nothing showed that lists, links, pictures,
tables and More formatting tools were off to the right. The toolbar now fades at
whichever edge has more tools beyond it, updating as it scrolls and resizes. A
browser regression covers both edges at 768px. UI only.

### Focus after menu-bar dialogs (2026-10-05)

A dialog opened from the menu bar (Indents and tabs, Paragraph borders, Page
setup, Kerning, Bookmarks, the style dialogs and others) returned focus to the
menu's title when cancelled or closed, so the next keystrokes were lost. Menu-bar
commands now return the keyboard to the document, keeping the selection, before
they run, so their dialogs close back into the text.
Dialogs opened from toolbar or inspector buttons still return to those buttons.
A browser regression covers Escape and Cancel and continued typing.

### Closing a menu opened with the mouse (2026-10-05)

A menu opened by clicking its title and closed without a command (Escape, or
clicking the title again) left the keyboard on the title, so typing was lost.
Such menus now close back into the document with the selection kept.
Menus opened from the keyboard keep the menu bar pattern and
return to their title, so keyboard navigation along the bar is unchanged.
Browser and unit regressions cover both paths.

### Toolbar pickers and focus (2026-10-05)

Clicking a toolbar picker (text color, highlight, line spacing, insert table,
font, link) moved focus to its button, so closing the picker with Escape or a
second click left the keyboard there and typing was lost. Clicking these
buttons now keeps the document focused, so a mouse-opened picker closes back into
the text with the selection kept; opened from the keyboard, a picker still
returns to its button. Menus and palettes opened right after a pointer press
hold back keyboard focus rings on items and swatches until a key is pressed (the
current choice keeps its tint). A browser regression covers each picker, the
ring and the keyboard path.

## Comments (2026-10-09)

Clauses: ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.13.4 (comments: `comments`, `comment`, `commentRangeStart`,
`commentRangeEnd`, `commentReference`, `annotationRef`) and the w15 `commentsExtended`
companion (`w15:commentEx` `paraId`, `paraIdParent`, `done`) for replies and resolved state.

Supported subset:

- Comment ranges in body paragraphs and table cells, including point comments that have only a
  reference mark, ranges that start or end between paragraphs, overlapping ranges and replies that
  share their parent's range. Anchors are zero-width markers stored with bookmark markers, so every
  edit that moves bookmarks moves comment ranges identically.
- Comment bodies are read as plain paragraphs (tabs and line breaks kept). An unchanged comment
  keeps its source element byte for byte; edited or new comments are written as `CommentText`
  paragraphs with an `annotationRef` run. The last paragraph carries a `w14:paraId` used by
  `commentsExtended`.
- Add, reply, edit, resolve/reopen, delete a thread, delete all (or all resolved) comments, all
  undoable. Creating the first comment adds the comments part, relationship and content type.
  `commentsIds.xml`/`commentsExtensible.xml` entries for removed comments are dropped.
- Untouched documents still save byte for byte.

Gaps: comments in headers, footers, footnotes and drawing text keep the previous read-only
behaviour; rich formatting inside comment bodies is flattened when a comment is edited; people
(`people.xml`) identities and modern-comment mentions are not written. Tests:
`tests/comment-docx.test.js`. The macOS reference application was used to confirm that exported threads, replies
and resolved state reopen as authored.

## Tracked changes (2026-10-09)

Clauses: ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.13.5 (`ins`, `del`, `delText`, `moveFrom`/`moveTo` read as
deletion/insertion, paragraph-mark revisions in `pPr/rPr`) and §17.15.1.90 `trackRevisions`.

Supported subset:

- Inserted and deleted runs, including inside hyperlinks, and inserted or deleted paragraph marks
  in the body and table cells. Deleted text keeps its document positions until accepted.
- Track Changes on/off is read from and written to settings. While it is on, typing, pasting and
  Enter record insertions; Delete/Backspace/selection replacement record deletions; deleting your
  own pending insertion removes it outright.
- Accept/Reject this change, and move to next, all changes, and all changes and stop tracking.
- All Markup (inline colour, underline and strikethrough with left-margin change bars), Simple
  Markup and No Markup (deleted text hidden), and Original (inserted text hidden).
- Unchanged documents save byte for byte; revisions survive untracked edits and round trips.

Formatting revisions (`rPrChange`, `pPrChange`, including in the paragraph mark) are retained, listed with change bars and can be accepted; rejecting them is reported as not supported and keeps them. Gaps: table row/cell revisions, and revisions in
headers, footers and drawing text still open read-only. Moves are not distinguished from
insertions/deletions after an edit. Replace All in Find and Replace is not tracked. Balloons for
deletions are not drawn. Tests: `tests/tracked-changes.test.js`.

## Generated table of contents (2026-10-09)

Clauses: §17.16.5.68 TOC (`\o "1-3" \h \z \u`), §17.16.5.45 PAGEREF (`\h`), §17.13.6 bookmarks,
§17.16.22 hyperlinks. References → Table of Contents builds entries from outline levels 1–3: each
heading receives a `_Toc` bookmark, each entry is an internal hyperlink containing a complex
PAGEREF whose result is refreshed from the current layout, with a right tab and dot leader at the
text width and 0.15″ indent per level (`TOC 1`–`TOC 3` styles are applied when the document defines
them). Update Table rebuilds a TOC whose result fills whole paragraphs; any other TOC keeps its
result and refreshes its page numbers. Remove deletes the field and the title paragraph this editor
adds. The macOS reference application opens the result with working entries and page numbers. Gaps: custom levels,
`\t` style lists, tab leader choice and TC fields are not offered; a TOC inside a content control is
rebuilt only when its result fills whole paragraphs. Tests: `tests/table-of-contents.test.js`.

## Created headers, footers and page numbers (2026-10-09)

Clauses: §17.10.1–§17.10.5 (header/footer parts and `headerReference`/`footerReference`),
§17.16.5.44 PAGE, §17.16.5.40 NUMPAGES. Insert → Header/Footer creates a default header or footer
part (relationship, content type and a reference in the first section, which later sections
inherit) when the document has none. Insert → Page Number places a PAGE field (or Page X of Y) at
the top or bottom of the page, left, centred or right, or at the caret inside a header or footer.
Gaps: first-page and even-page variants are not created; Format Page Numbers and Remove Page
Numbers are not offered. Tests: `tests/page-number-stories.test.js`.

## Footnotes (2026-10-09)

Clauses: ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.11 (`footnoteReference`, `footnoteRef`, `footnotes`/`footnote`,
`separator`/`continuationSeparator`, settings `footnotePr` `numFmt`/`numStart`/`numRestart`).

Supported subset:

- Documents whose body references footnotes now open for editing. Each referenced note is a story
  (`<notes part>#<id>`) laid out at the foot of the page that holds its reference, below a
  two-inch separator rule; pagination reserves that space and repeats until the reservations
  settle. Numbers follow reference order in the document's numbering format and start value.
- Notes are edited in place (click into the note); the body reference is one indivisible mark.
- References → Insert Footnote (Cmd+Option+F / Ctrl+Alt+F) adds a reference at the caret and a new
  note (FootnoteText/FootnoteReference styles when defined, otherwise 10 pt text and a superscript
  mark), creating the footnotes part with separator and continuation-separator notes when the document has none.
- Unchanged documents save byte for byte; a note whose reference is deleted is removed on save.
  The macOS reference application opens new notes with their numbers and separator.

Gaps: notes that do not fit split across pages in the native reference but are kept whole here (the continuation
separator is not drawn); numbering that restarts each page or section, custom reference marks,
endnotes, notes containing tables, bookmarks or comments, and footnotes in headers/footers still
open read-only or display only. Next/Previous Footnote and Show Notes are not offered yet.
Tests: `tests/footnotes.test.js`.

### Footnote restart preview recovery (2026-10-09)

For unsupported global `footnotePr/numRestart` values, strict import still
rejects editing. Best-effort import now records a warning that numbering is
displayed continuously and continues reading the note bodies. Previously the
restart rejection aborted the entire notes-part reader before any note body
was retained. Original package bytes remain available and export remains
blocked on the read-only package.

Tests cover `eachPage` and `eachSect`, non-default start 3, note text, body
references, read-only note stories and preservation of all original OPC parts.
Original mixed-content controls additionally compare full page pixels and line
geometry against a continuous-numbering control at zoom 1 and .75, retaining
two pictures, a table, numbered text and the header. This is fidelity to an
explicit approximation; page/section restart semantics are still unsupported.
The schema checker now includes footnote and endnote parts by content type.
Tests: `tests/footnotes.test.js`, `tests/browser/footnote-recovery.spec.js`.

Unsupported global `footnotePr/numFmt` formats also retain structured previews
with an explicit decimal-numbering warning. Previously the formatter threw a
plain error which bypassed best-effort recovery and prevented the document
from opening. Controls use schema-valid `chicago` and `ordinal`, plus `chicago`
with `eachPage`; both approximation reasons remain visible when combined.
Existing decimal, decimalZero, lowerRoman, upperRoman, lowerLetter and upperLetter
formats remain editable and their unchanged exports preserve all package parts.
This does not implement the missing numbering formats or claim native reference equivalence.

## Retained fields (2026-10-09)

Clause: ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.16.5. Documents containing SEQ (captions), REF/NOTEREF/STYLEREF
(cross-references), DATE/TIME and document-information fields (AUTHOR, TITLE, FILENAME,
DOCPROPERTY…), MERGEFIELD, LISTNUM/AUTONUM, citation add-ins (ADDIN, CITATION, BIBLIOGRAPHY) and
similar fields no longer open read-only. Their instructions are kept as written (add-in
instructions are not tokenized, since they can carry JSON) and their cached results are shown and
editable like any other body field result; they are not re-evaluated. Gaps: Update Field does not
recompute these types yet. Recovery fixtures that used AUTHOR/DATE as their unsupported trigger now
use a locked COMPARE field. Tests: `tests/retained-fields.test.js`.

## Captions, cross-references and Update Fields (2026-10-09)

Clauses: §17.16.5.56 SEQ, §17.16.5.51 REF, §17.16.5.45 PAGEREF. References → Insert Caption adds a
"<Label> <SEQ Label \* ARABIC>" paragraph below or above the selected picture, the table at the
caret, or the current paragraph (Caption style when the document defines it, otherwise 9 pt italic).
Cross-reference inserts a hyperlinked REF (label and number, heading or bookmark text) or PAGEREF
(page number) to a hidden `_Ref` bookmark it creates on the target. Update Fields (F9) recomputes
SEQ results per identifier (`\c`, `\r n`, `\*` ARABIC/ROMAN/ALPHABETIC; `\h` hidden results are
left alone), REF results from their bookmark text, and PAGEREF page numbers. Gaps: chapter
numbering (`\s`), Table of Figures, and REF switches other than `\h` are not evaluated.
Tests: `tests/captions.test.js`.

## Hidden text (2026-10-09)

Clause: §17.3.2.41 `vanish`. Documents with hidden text no longer open read-only. Hidden runs stay in
the text (search, copy and save keep them) and are laid out with no width; `revisionView.showHidden`
lets a Show/Hide ¶ control lay them out. Tests: `tests/hidden-text.test.js`.

## Equations (2026-10-09)

Clause: §22.1 Office Math. `m:oMath` and `m:oMathPara` no longer make a document read-only. Each
equation is one atomic object whose XML is saved unchanged; it is displayed in a linear form
(fractions as `(a)/(b)`, scripts with `^`/`_`, radicals with `√`, delimiters, n-ary operators,
functions, matrices) rather than a two-dimensional layout, and cannot be edited yet.
Tests: `tests/office-math.test.js`.

### Home tab editing commands (2026-10-09)

**Change Case** (Home → Font, and Shift+F3) changes the selection, or the word at
the caret, to Sentence case, lowercase, UPPERCASE, Capitalize Each Word or tOGGLE
cASE; Shift+F3 cycles lowercase → Capitalize Each Word → UPPERCASE → lowercase.
Only the characters of ordinary `w:t` text change (§17.3.3.31); run properties,
character styles, links, fields, pictures and note references are untouched, and
positions do not move. A letter whose conversion changes length (ß → SS) keeps its
original form, so the command is one same-length undo step. Case is not stored as
the `w:caps` property (§17.3.2.5); that remains **All caps** in the Font settings.

**Format Painter** copies the character style (`w:rStyle`, §17.3.2.29) and the
direct character formatting of the selection's first character; with a caret, or
a selection covering whole paragraphs, it also copies the paragraph style
(`w:pStyle`, §17.3.1.27) and direct paragraph formatting. Direct formatting is
taken as the resolved values that differ from the styles alone, so imported
`w:rPr`/`w:pPr` declarations and in-editor edits copy alike. Painting first clears
the target's direct formatting (replacing, not merging), then applies each
property; a property the target cannot take (for example a page break before a
table-cell paragraph) is skipped. One click paints once when the mouse is
released over the pages; a double click keeps painting until Escape or the button
is clicked again. A caret target paints the word under it. Numbering and the
outline level are not copied.

**Sort** reorders whole selected body paragraphs (`w:p`, §17.3.1.22) by Text
(locale collation, optionally case sensitive), Number (the first number in the
paragraph) or Date, ascending or descending; paragraphs without a key go first
when ascending. Each paragraph keeps its properties,
runs and bookmarks. Not supported: sorting table rows, fields or section breaks
within the selection, multiple sort keys and "My list has header row"; these are
refused with a message rather than approximated.

**Show/Hide ¶** (Ctrl/Cmd+8) paints nonprinting marks over the body text on
screen only: · spaces, ° nonbreaking spaces, → tabs, ↵ text-wrapping breaks,
¶ paragraph ends, ¤ cell ends, and labelled dotted rules for page, column and
section breaks (labelled by how the next section starts, §17.6.22). Marks never
reach print, PDF or the saved document. Headers, footers and text boxes do not
show marks yet; hidden text (§17.3.2.14) and optional hyphens are not marked.

The [independent control](../tools/home_editing_fixture.py)
(`public/fixtures/home-editing.docx`) has mixed runs, a character style with
added direct bold, a heading, an unsorted paragraph run, a tab, a nonbreaking
space, a line break, a table and a page break. A browser regression applies all
four commands to it, downloads, reopens and checks the result; the export passes
`npm run check:conformance`. Unit regressions cover each operation, undo and DOCX
round trips.

### Ribbon fitting and focus (2026-10-09)

The Styles gallery now shows whole style tiles and gives up tiles, down to two,
before any ribbon group folds into a drop-down, as a gallery does; at 1280px
the whole Home tab is open. Clipboard folds last among the Home groups. Ribbon
rows use 24px commands spread across a 72px band, in fixed proportions.
Clicking a ribbon button no longer takes focus from the document, so a dialog it
opens returns to the text with the selection kept. On the smallest phones the
title bar hides Search (Find stays on the Home tab) so the document's save status
remains readable; the hidden quick-access Print and All Documents buttons now
stay hidden.

### Font dialog (2026-10-09)

The Font group's launcher and Ctrl/Cmd+D open a Font dialog with two tabs (Font and Advanced).
**Font**: font name (`w:rFonts` ascii/hAnsi, §17.3.2.26), style (`w:b`/`w:i`),
size (`w:sz`/`w:szCs`, §17.3.2.38), font color (`w:color`), underline style and
color (`w:u`, §17.3.2.40), and the effects strikethrough/double strikethrough
(`w:strike`/`w:dstrike`), superscript/subscript (`w:vertAlign`), small caps and
all caps (`w:smallCaps`/`w:caps`). **Advanced**: scale (`w:w`), spacing expanded
or condensed (`w:spacing`), raised or lowered position (`w:position`) and
kerning threshold (`w:kern`). A live preview shows the selection's text.

Fields open from the selection; a mixed value is blank or indeterminate, and only
fields the user changes are applied, in one undo step through the same run
formatting operation as the ribbon. A font that cannot load on the device is
refused with a message. Not included: Hidden (`w:vanish`), Set As Default, Text
Effects, OpenType ligature/number options in this dialog (ligatures remain in the
Formatting Pane), and complex-script font fields. A browser regression applies
style, size, effects and spacing, checks a mixed selection keeps per-run sizes,
undoes, saves and reopens.

### Spelling (2026-10-09)

Body text is checked against the en_US Hunspell dictionary (SCOWL size 60,
2020.12.07), vendored unmodified in `public/dictionaries` with its full notices
and hash-pinned in `npm run check:licenses`; it loads on first use (about 50 ms)
through `nspell` (MIT). Misspelled words get a red wavy line on screen only;
the checker does not author OOXML error markers. Export now invalidates existing
completed `w:proofState` flags when story text changes (see the export-state
entry below). Effective `w:noProof` (§17.3.2.21) declarations suppress checking of
their run contents, including inherited values and explicit false resets. Authored
`w:proofErr` (§17.13.8) annotations now bound automatic checking on initial
load when saved body spelling is complete; flagged words are validated against
the dictionary. Explicit recheck bypasses this cache. Dictionary selection from
`w:lang` (§17.3.2.20) is not yet
implemented: eligible text is checked as US English, as shown in the status bar.

By default, words in UPPERCASE, words containing numbers,
and internet and file addresses are skipped; hyphenated compounds are checked part
by part; curly apostrophes are normalized and a possessive `'s` is ignored. The word
being typed is judged once the caret leaves it. Right-click a marked word for up to
five suggestions (closest first: a swapped letter pair, then a left-out vowel), Ignore
All (for this session) and Add to Dictionary (kept in this browser). Review →
Spelling or F7 opens the Spelling pane at the next misspelling after the caret with
Change, Change All, Ignore Once, Ignore All and Add to Dictionary; each correction is
an ordinary edit and one undo step. The Spelling split button can turn checking as
you type off (remembered) and recheck the document. The status bar's book icon
shows whether errors were found and opens the pane. Not covered: grammar and style,
other languages, headers/footers/text boxes/notes, autocorrect from the menu, and
custom dictionaries beyond the per-browser word list. More than 3,000 errors stop
the marking, as word processors do.

#### Proofing exemptions (2026-10-10)

The supplied Part 1 PDF, page 297 (printed page 287), §17.3.2.21 and §17.17.4,
defines `noProof` as an inherited on/off property that suppresses errors on run
contents. It is not a style toggle. Import and source-preserving serialization
now retain its effective value; model formatting edits can write either value.
The shared ST_OnOff reader accepts XML whitespace around canonical boolean/on/off
tokens, as required by the XML Schema union, while retaining malformed-value guards.
The spelling overlay/pane/menu/corrections use a disposable text projection that
replaces exempt UTF-16 positions with spaces. Source text and layout remain
unchanged. Ordinary text split across ordinary runs remains one word; an
exempt boundary splits proofing, as independently observed in the native reference.

The [handmade control](../tests/fixtures/no-proof/README.md) covers nine native
cases, including repeated inherited true and a derived false. The native reference reports only
`vble` in the mixed `Zzqx`/`vble` case, and the full word when both runs are
ordinary. The app now reports the same five error ranges. No spec/native
divergence is claimed. UTF-16 offsets, typing, property edits, correction,
export/reopen, unrelated-part preservation and exact undo are tested.

The nine checked originals retain exact canvas pixels and caret geometry on
all 50 pages; this is a bounded regression comparison, not full corpus fidelity
or performance certification. Grammar, other-language dictionaries and page
stories/drawing-local proofing remain outside the existing spelling feature.
DrawingML's separate `a:rPr/@noProof` is not implemented by this WML change.

### Paragraph keyboard chords and Go To (2026-10-09)

Added paragraph chords: Ctrl+1/2/5 line spacing (`w:spacing/@w:line`,
`lineRule="auto"`, §17.3.1.33), Ctrl+0 to add or remove 12 pt before, Ctrl+M and
Ctrl+Shift+M to step the left indent by half an inch, Ctrl+T and Ctrl+Shift+T for a
hanging indent (`w:ind`, §17.3.1.12), Ctrl+Q to clear direct paragraph formatting,
Ctrl+Shift+N for Normal, Ctrl+Shift+D/W for double and words-only underline
(`w:u`), Ctrl+Shift+F/P to reach the font name and size, and Alt+Shift+Up/Down to
move the selected paragraphs past a neighbour. On a Mac these use Control where
the browser or system reserves the Cmd chord (Cmd+Q, M, T, N, W, 1–9). Moving
paragraphs reorders `w:p` elements only; it stops at tables, section breaks,
content controls and frames, and keeps the document's final paragraph last.

Ctrl/Cmd+G or F5 opens Go To for Page, Line, Bookmark, Heading, Table and Graphic:
a number goes to that item, +n/−n moves relative to the current one, and Previous
and Next step through them. Lines are layout lines of the body; headers, footers,
notes and comments are not targets. Layout → Breaks gains Column
(`w:br w:type="column"`, §17.3.3.1), already available as Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Enter.
The keyboard reference lists every chord.

### Design → Paragraph Spacing (2026-10-09)

The presets — No Paragraph Space (0/0 pt, single), Compact (after 4 pt, single),
Tight (after 6 pt, 1.15), Open (after 10 pt, 1.15), Relaxed (after 6 pt, 1.5) and
Double (after 8 pt, double) — set `w:spacing` before/after/line (§17.3.1.33) on the
document's default paragraph style, so Normal and every style based on it follow,
in one undo step; the current preset is checked. Style Set Default removes those
declarations so the style inherits the document defaults (`w:pPrDefault`,
§17.7.5.3). The presets are set on Normal, not on the document defaults, so styles
not based on Normal keep their spacing here. Direct paragraph spacing stays
in effect. Not included: Themes, Style Sets, theme Colors/Fonts/Effects,
Set as Default and Watermark.

### Navigation pane (2026-10-09)

View → Navigation Pane (and Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+O) opens the Navigation pane at the left
of the pages. **Headings** lists paragraphs by outline level (§17.3.1.20, through
styles or direct `w:outlineLvl`) as a tree: a heading with lower-level headings
under it collapses and expands, the heading containing the caret is marked, and
choosing one moves the caret there. **Pages** shows a thumbnail of each page drawn
from the screen rendering; choosing one goes to that page's first body text.
**Results** lists every match of the pane's search in its context.

Ctrl/Cmd+F, Home → Find and the title bar's Search open the pane's search, seeded
with a short single-line selection; every match is tinted in the
document, Enter and Shift+Enter step through them, and Escape clears the search,
then closes the pane. The Find and Replace panel stays available as Home → Find →
Advanced Find…, Home → Replace and Ctrl+H (Cmd+Shift+H on a Mac). Find's menu
also offers Go To…. Not included: dragging headings to reorder sections, searching
headers, footers, notes and comments, and searching for objects.

### Table Design: style options and table styles gallery (2026-10-09)

Table Design shows Table Style Options (Header Row, First Column, Total Row,
Last Column, Banded Rows, Banded Columns) and a Table Styles gallery of fourteen
original designs (Plain Grid, Light Grid, Horizontal Rules, Light List, Banded and
Header designs in six accent colors) drawn as live thumbnails. Choosing one formats
the table holding the selection in one undo step: every cell side gets an explicit
`w:tcBorders` side or `nil` (§17.4.66), fills are set or cleared with `w:shd`
(§17.4.33), and header, total and first/last column text gets `w:b` and `w:color`
where the design asks. Changing an option re-applies the current design at once.

These are **direct cell formatting, not a table style**: no `w:tblStyle` (§17.4.63)
or `w:tblStylePr` conditional formatting is written, so the look is identical in any
consumer but the native reference lists the table with its previous (or no) table style, and the
editor does not remember the chosen design after the document is reopened (the
options then apply to the next design chosen). Body-cell text keeps its own bold and
color; only formatting a previous design applied is reset. Repeat Header Rows moves
to Table Layout → Data. Not included: creating or modifying named table
styles, and applying a table style imported with the document to another table.

### Bullet and Numbering libraries (2026-10-09)

The arrows beside Home → Bullets and Numbering open the list libraries: None, seven
bullets (•, ○, ■, ❖, ➢, ✓, –) and seven number formats (1. 1) I. A. a) a. i.).
Choosing one writes a new `w:abstractNum`/`w:num` pair (§17.9.1, §17.9.15) whose
chosen level has the library's `w:numFmt` and `w:lvlText` (§17.9.17, §17.9.11), keeps
the list's other levels and start values, and re-points every paragraph of that list
(`w:numPr`), changing a list rather than only the selection; with no list it
starts one. The current choice is checked. One undo step. Bullets are Unicode
characters in the paragraph font rather than Symbol/Wingdings code points, so no
symbol font is needed. Not included: Define New Bullet/Number Format, picture
bullets, the Multilevel List gallery and the List Styles library.

The Multilevel List button beside them applies one of four complete definitions
(1. 1.1. 1.1.1.; 1) a) i); I. A. 1. a); • ○ ■) to all nine levels of the list holding the
selection, keeping each paragraph's level, or starts a list at level 1.

### Text Effects (2026-10-09)

Home → Font gains a Text Effects menu with outline (none, ¾ pt, 1½ pt, in the
text's color) and outer shadow presets (none; offset bottom right, bottom, right:
3 pt blur, 3 pt distance, black at 60%). They are written as w14 run effects
`w14:textOutline` and `w14:shadow` inside `mc:Ignorable`-declared markup, which
the editor already reads and paints; the current choice is checked. Reflection,
glow, 3-D, gradient text fill, number styles, ligatures and stylistic sets are not
in the menu (imported ones still render and survive editing).

### View → Multiple Pages (2026-10-09)

View → Zoom gains Multiple Pages: pages sit side by side and wrap, zoomed so two
fit across the window (or one page's height). Any other zoom choice —
One Page, Page Width, 100%, the Zoom dialog, the status-bar slider or menu — returns
to one page per row. Pointer hit-testing now prefers the vertically nearest page and,
between pages sharing a row, the horizontally nearest, so clicks land on the page
under the pointer; with one page per row this is the previous behavior. Display
only; nothing is written to the document.

### Insert → Shapes and the Shape Format tab (2026-10-09)

Insert → Shapes offers 22 presets in groups (line; rectangle, rounded
rectangle; oval, triangles, diamond, parallelogram, trapezoid, pentagon, hexagon,
octagon, cross, cloud; right/left/up/down/left-right arrows, chevron, pentagon
arrow; 5- and 4-point stars), drawn as thumbnails from the same geometry the page
uses. A shape is inserted at a default size, floating in front of the text
(`wp:anchor`, §20.4.2.3, relative to the caret's column and paragraph, `wrapNone`,
a fresh `relativeHeight`), as a `wps:wsp` (MS-ODRAWXML wordprocessingShape) with a
preset geometry (`a:prstGeom`, §20.1.9.18), a solid fill (`a:solidFill`) and an
outline (`a:ln`, §20.1.2.2.24) in the default blue. The saved XML is exactly what
the editor read to paint it: the drawing is parsed by the same shape reader as
imported drawings and kept as its source XML.

Selecting a shape shows Shape Format with Shape Fill (palette, custom color, No
Fill), Shape Outline (palette, No Outline) and Weight (¼–6 pt), Height and Width,
Wrap Text, Bring Forward/Send Backward and Delete. Corner handles resize it; the
Move handle and arrow keys move it. Each edit rewrites the shape's DrawingML from
its parameters, previews it, and replaces the drawing in one undo step. Any simple
preset shape qualifies, including those written by other producers: one `wps:wsp`, a supported preset
without adjustments, a solid sRGB or no fill and outline, no text, rotation, flips or
effects. Other drawings keep their existing behavior (move, arrange, drawing text).
A selected shape shows only its frame handles; pictures keep their tint.

The preset reader gains diamond, parallelogram, trapezoid, pentagon, plus,
rightArrow, leftArrow, upArrow, leftRightArrow and star4 from the ECMA-376 preset
definitions, including their adjustment guides and text rectangles, so documents
containing them now render and open for editing instead of being refused. The
[independent control](../tools/preset_geometry_fixture.py)
(`public/fixtures/preset-geometries.docx`) has each with default or explicit
adjustments; it opens editable, its geometry is checked, and an unchanged save is
byte-identical. Not included: drawing a shape by dragging, free resizing (corners
keep the proportions), rotation, text in shapes and text boxes, arrowheads other
than the oval, shape styles/effects, gradients, connectors, curves, freeforms,
callouts, banners, flowchart and equation shapes, Align, Group and the Selection
Pane.

Insert → Text Box adds a simple text box: a 2 × 1 in rectangle with a white
fill and ½ pt black outline, floating in front of the text, whose `wps:txbx`/
`w:txbxContent` (§17.17.1.1) holds one paragraph and whose `wps:bodyPr` uses the default
insets, top anchoring and no autofit. Its text opens in the drawing text editor at
once (and later from Shape Format → Edit Text); the paragraphs are read with the
document's styles and theme. Fill, outline, weight and size edits keep the text box's
paragraphs and body properties as authored, including text boxes written by other producers when they
use sRGB colors. Text boxes are not edited in place on the page, do not link, and do
not autofit or rotate here. The shape code loads with the document engine, so the
app shell downloads nothing more for it.

### Wrap Text, Rotate and Size for pictures (2026-10-09)

Wrap Text (Layout, Picture Format and Shape Format) now offers In Line with
Text, Square, Top and Bottom, Behind Text and In Front of Text for any picture or
shape, plus Bring to Front and Send to Back. In line writes `wp:inline`
(§20.4.2.8); the others write `wp:anchor` (§20.4.2.3) relative to the column and
paragraph with `wrapSquare wrapText="bothSides"` (⅛ in side distances),
`wrapTopAndBottom`, or `wrapNone` with `behindDoc`. A picture leaving the line keeps
its place on the page; a floating one keeps its offsets when they are already
column/paragraph based and otherwise starts at the paragraph. Only the drawing's
frame is rewritten; its graphic, properties and effect extent move across
unchanged, and an untouched drawing is saved byte for byte as before. New pictures
can now float (previously always inline). Not available: Tight and Through
wrapping, Edit Wrap Points, Fix Position on Page, distances from text, and wrapping
for page-relative-size drawings, rotated drawing frames and charts; rotated
pictures or pictures with effect extents can float in front of or behind text only,
as the layout supports.

Picture Format gains Rotate (Rotate Right/Left 90°, Flip Vertical/Horizontal, as
`a:xfrm rot/flipV/flipH`) and Height and Width boxes that keep the picture's
proportions by default. Menus can now show the
ribbon's own icons (previously an unknown icon name showed a generic glyph).

### Typing speed: remembered text measurements (2026-10-09)

Each edit lays the whole story out again, and on a 48-page document a keystroke
made about 22,000 canvas text measurements per 40 paragraphs, nearly all repeats.
The editor now remembers each measurement by style and exact text. A style
object's key is computed once (layout writes only its own output fields onto the
objects it measures with, and measurement reads none of them), callers get a
copy, and the memory is cleared whenever fonts change: font refresh, deferred
script or separator faces, and local font access. Measured on a 400-paragraph,
48-page document under the same machine load, a keystroke in the middle went from
about 910 ms to 380 ms. Layout results are unchanged. Paragraph-level reuse,
which would need relocating document offsets in cached lines, remains future work.

### Arrowheads (2026-10-09)

Line ends of every type now display and open for editing: `triangle`, `stealth`,
`diamond` and `arrow` join `oval` (`a:headEnd`/`a:tailEnd`, §20.1.2.2.15/.37 with
ST_LineEndType §20.1.10.33 and its width/length sizes §20.1.10.34–35). Previously a
drawing with any other arrowhead made the whole document read-only.

The geometry follows native evidence rather than a reading of the schema:
`tests/fixtures/arrowheads` holds two original controls with every type at each
size and 0.5, 1.5 and 6 pt pens, the macOS reference application's own PDF exports of them, and
the marker dimensions read from those PDFs' vector content. With the oval's base
b = max(pen, 2 pt)/2 and sizes sm 2, med 3, lg 5: a triangle is 2b·len long and b·w
half-wide and the line stops b short of its base; a stealth adds a notch b·{2,2,4}
(by length) in front of the base where the line stops; a diamond is centred on the
end like an oval; an arrow is an open V of pen-width arms b·{4,6,9} long and
b·{2.5,3.5,5} half-wide whose outer miter meets the end, the line stopping at its
apex. All 22 measured cases match within 0.02 pt. The line is shortened by erasing
its stroke beyond the stop before the marker is painted, so curved and dashed lines
keep their path. Insert → Shapes gains Line Arrow (a triangle tail end).
Not covered: arrowheads on picture outlines, and choosing arrow styles from Shape
Outline.

### Insert → Cover Page (2026-10-09)

Insert → Pages → Cover Page offers three original designs (Simple, Banded, Lined).
One inserts four Normal-style paragraphs before the first paragraph — title,
subtitle, author and date, seeded with the document's name and today's date — with
direct paragraph and run formatting (spacing, alignment, `w:shd` bands or `w:pBdr`
rules, size, weight and color), the last ending in a page break (`w:br
w:type="page"`, §17.3.3.1), in one undo step with the title selected for typing.
These are plain paragraphs, not content controls from a
building-block gallery (§17.12); replacing or removing a cover page is ordinary
editing. A document that starts with a table is refused.

## Flat axis-line screen coverage (updated 2026-10-10)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.2.2.24 and 20.1.10.31 define DrawingML line
properties and caps. The earlier inferred inclusive-endpoint rule is withdrawn:
it passed threshold-128 JPEG footprint assertions by turning native half-gray
endpoint pixels fully black. Independent coverage checks show that this changes
ink instead of reproducing antialiasing. The extra endpoint extent and tangent
origin adjustment are removed. Authored vectors and physical print projection
are unchanged; the modern arrowhead implementation remains intact.

The two independently authored source families establish all 72 dark-core
bounds at 100%. A fresh 48-line holdout establishes the same cores at 75%.
Flat-cap half-gray pixel checks retain 320 native samples with a maximum
32-channel JPEG allowance, sufficient to reject black/white substitutions.
These are bounded coverage checks, not exact alpha, arbitrary-path, transformed
cap or full native fidelity certification. The old threshold-128 bounds and
assertions remain unchanged as three explicit expected-failure diagnostics.
JPEG values straddle the canvas's half-gray value; exact native endpoint
coverage requires a stronger lossless screen reference.

See `tools/record_axis_line_coverage.py`, the axis-line fixture READMEs and
`tests/browser/axis-line-display.spec.js`. Source-part preservation, editing,
undo/reopen, physical print hashes and dashed controls remain checked. Curve,
fill, cap/dash, high-DPI and resource-ceiling regressions retain their assertions.
Original #88 remains partial; its source geometry and print output are unchanged.

Windows build validation also exposed Git newline conversion of reviewed
spelling dictionary/license assets. Their local bytes were restored exactly
from main, and dictionary Git attributes now preserve those bytes on checkout.
Provenance hashes and license policy are unchanged. No new dependency or
third-party binary is introduced. Existing bundle/dynamic-import optimization
warnings remain notes rather than renderer work.
### Hidden sequence fields (2026-10-09)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.16.5.56 (`SEQ`), printed pages 1241–1243 in the supplied
fifth-edition standard, defines `\h` as hiding the result rather than removing
the field from its sequence. Explicit field refresh now applies the counter
effect of hidden fields (including `\c` repeat and `\r` reset), writes an empty
result, and lets subsequent fields use the correct counter. A general-formatting
switch overrides hiding regardless of switch order. Previously hidden fields
kept stale cached text and were skipped when calculating later numbers.

Independently written OOXML unit controls cover hidden increments, repeats and
resets, `\* roman` and `\* MERGEFORMAT` precedence, export/reopen and idempotent
refresh. Existing caption/cross-reference tests remain controls for visible
sequences. Browser controls exercise F9, undo, export/reopen and idempotent
refresh. Native reference layout controls are still pending; no
full field-formatting or native reference layout equivalence is claimed. Bookmark arguments,
heading restarts and unsupported formatting remain open in S06 of the backlog.
Tests: `tests/sequence-fields.test.js`, `tests/captions.test.js`.

The app's F9 action delegates through the canvas to the existing References
field-update action, which also refreshes page references. Previously the canvas
handled F9 solely as a page-reference refresh and prevented the References
listener from updating SEQ/REF. Standalone canvas users retain the default
page-reference action. Tests: `tests/browser/sequence-hidden.spec.js` and

### Reference field refresh (2026-10-09)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.16.5.51 (`REF`), printed pages 1238–1239, defines the field
value as the bookmarked content and `\p` as the bookmark's relative position.
Explicit refresh now preserves leading/trailing whitespace for plain inline
text bookmarks. `\p` produces `below` before the bookmark and `above` after it.
Previously the updater trimmed all text and ignored switches, replacing every
REF result with plain bookmark text even when it represented a paragraph number.

Unsupported switches, structural/column/object content and self-references
retain their authored caches. They produce localized field-update issues while
supported siblings still refresh; the UI reports deduplicated messages using
its existing notification surface. Existing hyperlink envelopes are preserved,
but `\h` hyperlink creation is not implemented here. `\* MERGEFORMAT` is accepted
without a text transformation. Case, numbering, annotation and other formatting
switches, rich content copying, paragraph formatting propagation and the native reference's
self-reference error result remain incomplete.

Independently authored controls cover exact whitespace, relative position,
unsupported switch retention, structural/self-reference isolation, idempotence,
export/reopen, F9 and one-step undo. Full page pixels and geometry match a
separate expected-cache control at zoom 1 and .75. Native reference layout equivalence
is not claimed. Tests: `tests/reference-fields.test.js` and
`tests/browser/reference-fields.spec.js`.

### Horizontal table grid screen projection (2026-10-10)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.4.38 (`tblBorders`), 17.4.66 (`tcBorders`) and
17.4.80 (`trHeight`) define border declarations and exact row sizing; they do
not prescribe pixel rounding. Live reference controls show horizontal single-border
bands advancing by rounded cumulative row offsets from the rounded frame
origin. Independent absolute rounding displaced internal rules by one pixel.
Minimum-width exposed bottom ink now follows its constrained ending frame;
an exact half-pixel tie survives the layout's 1e-6-pixel coordinate storage.
This is a native screen compatibility rule, not a normative OOXML requirement.

Logical geometry, vertical projection, authored widths and the physical print
branch remain unchanged. Two original six-row/two-column controls establish
63 native bands across uniform/mixed row heights, three pen widths and 100%/75%
zoom. Source geometry, editing, export/reopen and exact undo are checked by
`tests/table-grid-phase.test.js` and `tests/browser/table-grid-phase.spec.js`.
[Fixture provenance and limits](../tests/fixtures/table-grid-phase/README.md).
Older unresolved frame-placement discrepancies remain explicit; this does not
establish arbitrary borders, all zooms or whole-document reference fidelity.

### Picture aspect locks and physical resize corners (2026-10-10)

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.1.2.2.19 `graphicFrameLocks`, 20.1.2.2.31 `picLocks`
(`noChangeAspect`), 20.1.7.6 `xfrm`, 20.4.2.3 `anchor`, 20.4.2.7 `extent`,
20.4.2.8 `inline`, and 20.4.2.10–12 govern picture dimensions and placement.
Either active aspect lock constrains editing. Missing/false locks allow
independent width and height. The reader already retained that distinction;
corner gestures previously forced proportional sizing for every picture.

Ordinary picture corners now resize in the picture's rotated axes. Selection
frames and resize cursors follow those axes. Floating pictures retain the
opposite physical corner, using rounded EMU dimensions and numeric offsets only
when authored placement would no longer yield the required origin. Unaffected
placement axes retain their authored alignment. Inline
picture origins remain governed by paragraph flow. Shift preserves proportions;
Ctrl/Option retains the center. Unlocked corner keyboard arrows adjust the
corresponding physical axis; Shift increases the keyboard step to ten pixels.
Retained drawing scenes and relative-size pictures retain their existing
editing protections, and simple authored preset shapes retain their existing
resize path. Each released gesture is one validated transaction; existing
Escape, revision guards and undo remain in effect. No document-content painter
or initial layout algorithm changes.

The [ten independent controls](../tests/fixtures/image-resize/README.md) cover
missing/false and outer/inner true locks, all corners, rotation, inline placement,
crop/flip preservation, modifiers, authored alignment, export/reopen and exact
package-part undo. An aligned independent control reproduces a 24-pixel
opposite-corner shift before the placement correction.
Four geometry unit checks and the existing image interaction/crop/import checks
pass (14 unit tests total). Ten resize browser cases, three existing interaction
cases and four printing cases pass; the optional external teacher-card case is
not supplied.
The control and 129 final browser-export packages pass 390 standard schema views.
The old interaction module fails the same unlocked-corner check, after its route
is explicitly verified. Schema checks and these editing controls do not certify
complete native reference layout or every original template.

The original scan finds eighteen unlocked main-story pictures in seven sources.
Fourteen ordinary pictures in four sources pass independent-axis resizing and
exact package restoration after undo, including keyboard resizing for authored
corners outside the viewport. Four pictures in three sources remain protected
picture/outline drawing scenes; their hidden handles are checked and their
resizing remains a TODO. All 368 original on-disk hashes are unchanged.

completion is claimed. Native resized effect-padding/perspective fidelity,

error, not an established reference/spec divergence.

ink or complete floating-table equivalence is claimed.

For §§17.5.2.26/31 rich-text/run SDTs, Shift-click and drag preserve an already

ordinary click starts fresh ownership. Selection metadata is not serialized.

the retained native controls record keyboard behavior only. Full native
Shift-click equivalence remains open.

### Footnotes and endnotes (Part 1 §17.11)

| Clause | Supported subset |
| --- | --- |
| §17.11.4 `endnote`, §17.11.6 `endnotePr`, §17.11.7 `endnoteRef`, §17.11.8 `endnoteReference`, §17.11.15 `endnotes` | Body endnote references import as atomic note marks; referenced normal endnotes are editable stories; new documents get an endnotes part with separator and continuation separator notes and its relationship and content type. Unreferenced endnotes are pruned on save as footnotes are. |
| §17.11.14 `@customMarkFollows` | Custom-marked footnote and endnote references import, edit and save; they show no number and take none, the following run holds the mark. |
| §17.11.17 `numFmt` | decimal, lower/upper letter, lower/upper Roman and `chicago` (\*, †, ‡, §, doubled after four) for both kinds. Other formats keep the read-only decimal approximation. |
| §17.11.19 `numRestart` | `continuous`, `eachSect` and (footnotes) `eachPage`. Page restarts renumber after the notes' pages are known and lay out once more. |
| §17.11.20 `numStart` | Digits only, for both kinds. |
| §17.11.21 `pos` | Footnotes: `pageBottom` and `beneathText` (the area starts after the page's last body line). Endnotes: `docEnd`; `sectEnd` is stored and saved but endnotes are still shown after the last section. |
| §17.11.11/§17.11.12 settings | The Footnote and Endnote dialog writes `pos`, `numFmt`, `numStart` and `numRestart` in CT_FtnDocProps/CT_EdnDocProps order, referencing the part's separator notes when the element is new. Section-level `footnotePr`/`endnotePr` are not written ("whole document" only). |

Endnotes lay out after the last body line, behind a short separator, and
continue on added pages; each note stays whole on one page and authored
separator or continuation-notice content is not drawn. Convert swaps reference
kinds and moves note text to the other part (the reference keeps its place).
Note setting changes apply immediately and are saved, but are not part of undo.

### Fields (Part 1 §17.16)

| Field | Clause | Supported subset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TOC` | §17.16.5.68 | Generated from `\o` ranges and `\u` outline levels, `\t` style-to-level lists, `\c`/`\a` caption sequences (tables of figures) and `\f`/`\l` TC entries, scoped by `\b`. `\h` links entries, `\n` omits page numbers (all or a level range), `\p` replaces the tab, `\z` is kept. Unknown switches are retained on rebuild. Leaders and right alignment are paragraph tab stops (§17.3.1.37). Only whole-paragraph results rebuild; others refresh page numbers only. |
| `TC` | §17.16.5.63 | Hidden entry (no separator, no result); text, `\f`, `\l`, `\n` are read for tables of contents. |
| `PAGEREF` | §17.16.5.45 | As before; Update Table can scope the refresh to one table's references. |
| `SEQ` | §17.16.5.56 | Captions write `\* ARABIC|alphabetic|ALPHABETIC|roman|ROMAN`; labels with spaces use underscores in the identifier. Chapter numbers (`\s`) are not evaluated. |
| `REF` | §17.16.5.51 | Cross-references to headings, bookmarks, whole captions, label and number, or caption text, optionally followed by a `\p` above/below reference. |
| `NOTEREF` | §17.16.5.40 | New: evaluates the note number of the note reference inside its bookmark (`\h`, `\f`, `\p`). The formatted variant is inserted as superscript text. |
| `CITATION` | §17.16.5.8 | Inline result generated from the bibliography part: tag, `\m` extra sources, `\p` pages, `\f` prefix, `\s` suffix, `\v` volume, `\n`/`\y`/`\t` suppression, `\l` kept. Style change refreshes every citation. |
| `BIBLIOGRAPHY` | §17.16.5.7 | Block result listing the document's sources (placeholders omitted) in the chosen style, with a hanging indent; `\l` kept. Other switches are not evaluated. |
| `XE` | §17.16.5.72 | Mark Entry writes main/sub/third levels (escaped colons), `\t` cross-references, `\r` page-range bookmarks, `\b`, `\i`, `\f`; new entries are written without a separator. |
| `INDEX` | §17.16.5.29 | Generated with collation, three levels, indented or `\r` run-in, `\h` letter headings, `\e` (tab with right-aligned leader), `\l`, `\g`, `\k`, `\f`, `\b`, `\p`, `\z`; `\c` columns is stored but shown in one column (no section columns are created). |
| `TA` | §17.16.5.62 | Mark Citation writes `\l`, `\s`, `\c` on the first mark and `\s` on later ones, `\b`, `\i`. |
| `TOA` | §17.16.5.67 | One category per field with `\h` heading, `\p` passim (five or more pages), `\f`, `\e`, `\l`; "All" inserts one field per category in use. |

Entry fields (XE, TA, TC) are hidden text: while formatting marks are shown,
their codes are painted above the line without changing layout (an approximation
of hidden-text display, which would reflow the line). Generated results are
written untracked and as one undo step. Index and table-of-authorities page
numbers come from the current layout and settle over up to four passes.

### Bibliography sources (Part 1 §22.6, §22.5)

Sources live in a custom XML item (`b:Sources`) found through the main
document's `customXml` relationship; a new item gets `itemProps` (§22.5.2.1)
with a schema reference to the bibliography namespace. `SelectedStyle` and
`StyleName` record this editor's style identifier and name (no style sheet is
referenced). Source types are all of ST_SourceType; the dialog edits the name
roles and text fields listed in `bibliography.js`. Sources not edited are written
back byte-for-byte; an edited source keeps elements this editor does not edit.
DOI is entered as a URL (the schema has no DOI element). The master list is the
account's own (device storage and Puter KV), not part of the document.

Citation styles are original formatters of the public APA 7, MLA 9, Chicago
author-date, IEEE and Harvard rules for the common source types; style manuals'
long tail (translators in every style, series, multiple editions, legal
citation forms beyond the basic case entry, non-English conventions) is not
covered. A schema pass is not a check of citation correctness.
